topics.name: QA Theory

qs.q: What is software testing?
qs.s: Software ko chala ke check karna ki wo requirement ke hisaab se kaam kar raha hai ya nahi, aur user tak pahunchne se pehle bugs pakadna. Testing quality ke baare me jaankari deti hai aur risk kam karti hai.
qs.b: Software testing is the process of evaluating an application against its requirements to find defects before users do. Its purpose is to reduce risk and give the team the information it needs to decide whether the product is ready to release.
qs.t: 3 kaam: Requirement match karo, Bug pakdo, Risk kam karo. R-B-R.

qs.q: Why is testing important?
qs.s: Bug production me mile to mehnga padta hai: paisa, customer ka trust, kabhi data loss ya security issue. Jitna jaldi bug mile, utna sasta fix.
qs.b: Testing matters because defects found late are expensive. A bug in production can cost money, customer trust and sometimes data or security. Finding it earlier is cheaper and protects the user experience.
qs.t: Late bug = mehnga bug. Early bug = sasta bug.

qs.q: What is the difference between QA, QC and testing?
qs.s: QA (Quality Assurance) process ke baare me hai: bug aaye hi nahi, isliye process sahi banao (preventive). QC (Quality Control) product ke baare me hai: bana hua product check karo (detective). Testing QC ka ek hissa hai: actually app chala ke bugs dhundhna.
qs.b: QA is process-oriented and preventive: it improves the way we build so fewer defects are introduced. QC is product-oriented and detective: it checks the finished product. Testing is one activity inside QC, where we actually execute the application to find defects.
qs.t: QA = Process (rokna). QC = Product (pakadna). Testing = QC ka haath.

qs.q: Error, defect, bug and failure: what is the difference?
qs.s: Error: developer ki galti (insaan ki galti code likhte waqt). Defect/Bug: us galti ki wajah se code me jo kharabi aa gayi. Tester jab defect pakadta hai to use bug bolte hain. Failure: jab wo defect chalte waqt user ko dikh jaye aur system expected kaam na kare.
qs.b: An error is a human mistake made by a developer. That mistake leaves a defect in the code, which we usually call a bug once testing finds it. A failure is what happens when that defect is executed and the system does not behave as expected.
qs.t: Insaan galti kare (Error) → code me kharabi (Defect/Bug) → user ko dikhe (Failure). E-D-F.

qs.q: What is SDLC? Name its phases.
qs.s: Software Development Life Cycle: software banane ke steps. Requirement gathering, Design, Development (coding), Testing, Deployment, Maintenance.
qs.b: SDLC is the life cycle a product goes through from idea to support. The phases are requirement gathering and analysis, design, development, testing, deployment and maintenance.
qs.t: R-D-D-T-D-M: Ram Daily Dal Taste Dekh ke Muskuraata.

qs.q: What is STLC? Name its phases.
qs.s: Software Testing Life Cycle: testing ke steps. 1 Requirement Analysis (kya test karna hai samjho), 2 Test Planning (plan, scope, effort), 3 Test Case Development (cases + test data), 4 Test Environment Setup, 5 Test Execution (cases chalao, bugs report), 6 Test Closure (report, learnings).
qs.b: STLC is the sequence of testing activities: requirement analysis, test planning, test case development, test environment setup, test execution and test closure. Each phase has entry and exit criteria, so testing is planned rather than random.
qs.t: R-P-D-E-E-C: Rahul Pehle Dosa, Eggs, Emli, Chai khata hai.

qs.q: Verification vs validation?
qs.s: Verification: kya hum product sahi tarike se bana rahe hain? (documents, design, code review, bina chalaye). Validation: kya hum sahi product bana rahe hain? (app chala ke dekho ki user ki zaroorat poori hoti hai).
qs.b: Verification asks 'are we building the product right?' It checks documents, designs and code, usually without running the software. Validation asks 'are we building the right product?' It runs the software to confirm it meets the user's actual needs.
qs.t: Verification = Build RIGHT (paper pe). Validation = RIGHT product (chala ke).

qs.q: What are the 7 principles of testing?
qs.s: 1 Testing defects ki presence dikhati hai, absence nahi. 2 Exhaustive testing possible nahi. 3 Early testing paisa bachati hai. 4 Defect clustering: zyada bugs kuch hi modules me. 5 Pesticide paradox: same tests baar baar chalao to naye bug nahi milte, tests badlo. 6 Testing context-dependent hai (bank app aur game alag test). 7 Absence-of-errors fallacy: bug-free par galat cheez bani to bekaar.
qs.b: The seven principles are: testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence; exhaustive testing is impossible; early testing saves cost; defects cluster in a few modules; the pesticide paradox, so tests must be updated; testing depends on context; and the absence-of-errors fallacy, meaning a bug-free product that does not meet user needs is still a failure.
qs.t: Line yaad karo: 'Present, Exhaust, Early, Cluster, Pesticide, Context, Fallacy'. Kahani: Present me Exhaust ho ke Early Cluster me Pesticide dala, Context samjho warna Fallacy.

qs.q: What are the levels of testing?
qs.s: Unit testing: ek function/component (developer karta hai). Integration testing: modules aapas me sahi baat kar rahe hain (jaise PO aur Invoice). System testing: poora app end-to-end. Acceptance testing (UAT): customer/user check karta hai ki business ki zaroorat poori hai.
qs.b: There are four levels: unit testing of individual components, integration testing of how modules work together, system testing of the complete application end to end, and acceptance testing, where the customer confirms it meets business needs.
qs.t: U-I-S-A: Chhota se bada. Ek eent (Unit), deewar (Integration), ghar (System), maalik ki chaabi (Acceptance).

qs.q: Functional vs non-functional testing?
qs.s: Functional: app KYA karta hai, wo sahi hai? (login, payment, search). Non-functional: app KAISE karta hai: speed (performance), load, security, usability, compatibility.
qs.b: Functional testing checks what the system does against requirements, like login or checkout. Non-functional testing checks how well it does it: performance, security, usability, compatibility and reliability.
qs.t: Functional = KYA. Non-functional = KAISE (kitna fast, kitna safe, kitna aasan).

qs.q: Black box, white box and grey box testing?
qs.s: Black box: code nahi dekhte, sirf input-output (the platform me hum yahi karte hain). White box: code ke andar ka logic jaan ke test (unit tests). Grey box: thoda andar ka pata hai (API, database, logs) aur UI se test.
qs.b: Black-box testing checks behaviour through inputs and outputs without looking at the code, which is what crowdtesters do. White-box testing uses knowledge of the internal code. Grey-box combines both, for example testing the UI while checking API responses or logs.
qs.t: Box ka rang = code kitna dikhta hai. Kaala = kuch nahi, Safed = sab, Grey = thoda.

qs.q: Smoke vs sanity testing?
qs.s: Smoke: naya build aaya, sabse important flows chal rahe hain ya nahi (app khulta hai, login hota hai). Wide but shallow. Sanity: kisi chhote change/fix ke baad sirf us area ko jaldi check karna. Narrow but deep.
qs.b: Smoke testing is a quick, broad check of a new build to confirm the critical paths work and the build is stable enough to test. Sanity testing is a narrow, focused check after a small change or fix to confirm that specific area works.
qs.t: Smoke = Dhuan check, poore ghar me aag to nahi (broad). Sanity = sirf ek kamra check (narrow).

qs.q: Regression testing vs retesting?
qs.s: Retesting: jo bug fix hua, wahi bug dobara check karna (same steps). Regression: fix ya naye change ki wajah se purana chalta hua feature toota to nahi, ye check karna.
qs.b: Retesting confirms that a specific reported bug is now fixed, using the same steps. Regression testing checks that the change did not break features that were already working. Retesting is planned for the failed cases; regression covers the surrounding areas.
qs.t: Retest = wahi bug. Regression = baaki sab safe hai na? (Re-GRESS = peeche to nahi gaye).

qs.q: Severity vs priority? Give examples.
qs.s: Severity: bug ka impact kitna bada hai (system pe). Tester decide karta hai. Priority: kitni jaldi fix karna hai (business ke hisaab se). Manager/client decide karta hai. Example 1: homepage pe company ka naam galat spelling: severity low, priority high. Example 2: kabhi kabhi use hone wali purani report pe crash: severity high, priority low.
qs.b: Severity is the technical impact of a defect on the system, usually set by the tester. Priority is how urgently it should be fixed, set by the business. A misspelled company name on the homepage is low severity but high priority, while a crash in a rarely used legacy report is high severity but can be low priority.
qs.t: Severity = Seriousness (kitna dard). Priority = Pehle kaun (kab ilaaj). Logo galat = low-high. Purani report crash = high-low.

qs.q: Explain the bug life cycle.
qs.s: New (report hua) → Assigned (dev ko diya) → Open (dev kaam kar raha) → Fixed → Retest (tester check) → Verified → Closed. Agar fix kaam nahi kiya to Reopened. Side raaste: Rejected (bug nahi hai), Duplicate, Deferred (baad me fix). The platform me: Pending Approval → Approved / Rejected, beech me Info Request.
qs.b: A bug starts as New, is Assigned to a developer, moves to Open while being worked on, then Fixed. The tester retests it; if it passes it is Verified and Closed, otherwise it is Reopened. It can also be Rejected, marked Duplicate, or Deferred to a later release.
qs.t: N-A-O-F-R-V-C: Naya Aadmi Office Fix karke Retest Verify Close. Side doors: Reject, Duplicate, Defer, Reopen.

qs.q: Test plan vs test strategy?
qs.s: Test strategy: company/project level ka high-level approach (kaun se types of testing, tools, risk approach). Usually kam badalta hai. Test plan: ek project/release ka detailed document: scope, in/out of scope, schedule, resources, environment, entry/exit criteria, risks, deliverables.
qs.b: A test strategy is a high-level approach that defines how testing is done across a project or organisation: test types, tools and risk approach. A test plan is a detailed document for a specific release: scope, schedule, resources, environments, entry and exit criteria, risks and deliverables.
qs.t: Strategy = General ka 'kaise ladna hai'. Plan = is ladai ka 'kab, kahan, kaun'.

qs.q: Test scenario vs test case vs test suite?
qs.s: Scenario: kya test karna hai, ek line me ('User login check karo'). Test case: kaise karna hai, detail me: steps, test data, expected result. Suite: test cases ka group (jaise 'Login suite', 'Regression suite').
qs.b: A test scenario is a one-line statement of what to test, such as 'verify login'. A test case is the detailed how: preconditions, steps, test data and expected result. A test suite is a collection of related test cases run together.
qs.t: Scenario = KYA (1 line). Case = KAISE (steps). Suite = cases ki THAILI.

qs.q: What does a good test case contain?
qs.s: Test case ID, title, precondition, steps, test data, expected result, actual result, status (pass/fail), priority, aur requirement link. Steps itne clear ho ki koi bhi naya tester chala sake.
qs.b: A good test case has an ID, a clear title, preconditions, numbered steps, test data, an expected result, and fields for actual result and status. It should be simple enough that any tester can run it and get the same outcome.
qs.t: ID-Title-Pre-Steps-Data-Expected. Rule: koi bhi anjaan tester chala sake.

qs.q: What is an RTM?
qs.s: Requirement Traceability Matrix: ek table jisme har requirement ke saamne uske test cases likhe hote hain. Isse pata chalta hai ki koi requirement bina test ke to nahi chhoot gayi.
qs.b: A Requirement Traceability Matrix maps every requirement to the test cases that cover it. It shows coverage gaps and helps trace a failed test back to the requirement it affects.
qs.t: RTM = Requirement ↔ Test ka rishta. Koi requirement anaath (bina test) na rahe.

qs.q: What is equivalence partitioning?
qs.s: Input ko groups (partitions) me baanto jahan sab values ek jaisa behave karengi, phir har group se ek value test karo. Age 18 se 60 allowed hai: groups hain 17 ya kam (invalid), 18-60 (valid), 61 ya zyada (invalid). Teen values kaafi: 10, 35, 70.
qs.b: Equivalence partitioning divides input into groups that the system should treat the same way, and tests one value from each group. For an age field accepting 18 to 60, I would test one value below 18, one between 18 and 60, and one above 60.
qs.t: Groups banao, har group se ek. 'Ek thali se ek roti'.

qs.q: What is boundary value analysis?
qs.s: Bugs aksar kinaron (boundaries) pe hote hain. Age 18 se 60: test karo 17, 18, 19 aur 59, 60, 61. Developer < aur <= me galti karta hai, wahi pakadna hai.
qs.b: Boundary value analysis tests the edges of input ranges, because defects often occur there. For an age field of 18 to 60, I would test 17, 18, 19 and 59, 60, 61 to catch off-by-one errors.
qs.t: Har kinare pe 3: neeche, upar, beech. 17-18-19 / 59-60-61.

qs.q: Decision table and state transition testing?
qs.s: Decision table: jab output kai conditions ke combination pe depend kare (jaise discount = member hai? + order 1000 se zyada?). Har combination ek row. State transition: jab system ki state badalti hai (jaise ATM: 3 galat PIN ke baad card block). Har state aur transition test karo.
qs.b: Decision table testing covers combinations of conditions and their outcomes, one rule per row, for example discount rules based on membership and order value. State transition testing checks how a system moves between states, such as an account locking after three wrong PIN attempts.
qs.t: Table = combinations ki list. State = 'pehle kya, ab kya'. ATM ka 3 galat PIN yaad rakho.

qs.q: What is exploratory testing? How is it different from ad hoc testing?
qs.s: Exploratory: bina likhe test cases ke, app ko seekhte hue test karna, saath saath sochna aur next test decide karna. Isme ek goal (charter) aur time-box hota hai, notes banate hain. Ad hoc: bilkul random, bina plan aur bina notes. The platform me zyadatar exploratory hota hai.
qs.b: Exploratory testing is simultaneous learning, test design and execution. It is structured by a charter and a time-box, and I take notes as I go. Ad hoc testing is informal and unplanned, with no documentation. In crowdtesting, most bug hunting is exploratory.
qs.t: Exploratory = Goal + Time + Notes. Ad hoc = bas ghoomna.

qs.q: Positive vs negative testing?
qs.s: Positive: sahi input do, app sahi chale (valid email se login). Negative: galat input do, app gracefully handle kare, crash na ho, sahi error message dikhaye (galat email format, khali field).
qs.b: Positive testing uses valid input to confirm the system works as intended. Negative testing uses invalid or unexpected input to confirm the system handles it gracefully with a clear error, without crashing.
qs.t: Positive = 'haan chalega'. Negative = 'galat do, toote nahi'.

qs.q: Static vs dynamic testing?
qs.s: Static: code chalaye bina: review, walkthrough, requirement document padhna. Dynamic: app chala ke test karna.
qs.b: Static testing examines work products without executing code, such as reviews and walkthroughs. Dynamic testing executes the application to observe its behaviour.
qs.t: Static = padh ke. Dynamic = chala ke.

qs.q: Alpha vs beta testing?
qs.s: Alpha: release se pehle company ke andar (internal team) test. Beta: real users ko limited release, wo apne environment me use karke feedback dete hain. Crowdtesting beta jaisa hai: real logon ke real devices.
qs.b: Alpha testing is done internally before release, often in a controlled environment. Beta testing gives a near-final version to real users in their own environments to collect feedback before the full launch.
qs.t: Alpha = ghar ke andar. Beta = bahar ke log.

qs.q: What are entry and exit criteria?
qs.s: Entry: testing shuru karne ke liye kya ready hona chahiye (build deploy, environment ready, test cases ready). Exit: testing kab rokni hai (planned cases chal gaye, critical bugs fix, pass rate ok, deadline).
qs.b: Entry criteria are the conditions that must be met before testing starts, like a stable build and a ready environment. Exit criteria define when testing is complete, such as all planned cases executed and no open critical defects.
qs.t: Entry = darwaza kholne ki shart. Exit = bahar nikalne ki shart.

qs.q: When do you stop testing?
qs.s: Testing kabhi 100% complete nahi hoti (principle 2). Rokte hain jab: exit criteria poore, critical/high bugs fix, deadline ya budget khatam, ya risk acceptable level pe aa gaya.
qs.b: Since exhaustive testing is impossible, I stop when the exit criteria are met: planned coverage is done, no critical defects are open, and the remaining risk is acceptable to the team, or when time and budget limits are reached and the risk is documented.
qs.t: Rokne ke 4 sign: Exit criteria, Critical bug 0, Time/budget, Risk ok.

qs.q: Usability and compatibility testing?
qs.s: Usability: app use karna aasan hai? confusing button, unclear message, zyada steps. Compatibility: alag device, OS, browser, screen size, network pe app sahi chalta hai? Crowdtesting me compatibility bahut important: har tester ka device alag.
qs.b: Usability testing checks how easy and intuitive the product is to use. Compatibility testing checks that it works across devices, operating systems, browsers, screen sizes and networks, which is a major strength of crowdtesting.
qs.t: Usability = aasan hai? Compatibility = har jagah chalta hai?

qs.q: Performance, load and stress testing?
qs.s: Performance: response time kitna hai normal me. Load: expected users ke saath system kaisa chalta hai. Stress: limit se zyada load do, dekho kab tootta hai aur kaise recover karta hai.
qs.b: Performance testing measures speed and responsiveness. Load testing checks behaviour under expected user volume. Stress testing pushes beyond normal limits to find the breaking point and see how the system recovers.
qs.t: Performance = speed. Load = normal bheed. Stress = zyada bheed, kab girega.

qs.q: What is a test environment? Staging vs production?
qs.s: Test environment: jahan testing hoti hai (server, data, config). Staging: production jaisa copy, wahan freely test kar sakte hain. Production: live, real users. Merlin me main staging pe test karta hun aur prod pe read-only check.
qs.b: A test environment is the setup of hardware, software, data and configuration used for testing. Staging mirrors production so we can test safely; production is the live system with real users. At my job I test on staging and do read-only checks on production.
qs.t: Staging = practice ground. Production = asli match (sirf dekho, chhedo mat).

qs.q: What is the role of QA in Agile?
qs.s: Agile me chhote sprints (1-2 hafte). QA shuru se involved: story padhna, acceptance criteria clear karna, sprint me hi test karna, regression, daily standup. Testing end me nahi, saath saath.
qs.b: In Agile, QA is involved from the start of each sprint: clarifying acceptance criteria, testing stories as they are built, running regression, and giving fast feedback in stand-ups. Quality is a shared, continuous activity rather than a phase at the end.
qs.t: Agile QA = Shuru se, Saath me, Sprint ke andar. 3 S.

qs.q: What is defect leakage?
qs.s: Jo bug testing me nahi pakda gaya aur production/customer tak pahunch gaya. Kam leakage = acchi testing.
qs.b: Defect leakage is a defect that escapes testing and is found later, usually in production or by the customer. Tracking it helps a team improve coverage.
qs.t: Leakage = bug ne deewar se chhalang maar di.

topics.intro: Ye har QA interview ka base hai. Course quizzes bhi isi pe hote hain.

topics.name: Crowdtesting Platform

qs.q: What is the platform?
qs.s: The platform duniya ka bada crowdtesting community hai, parent company ka hissa. Testers apne real devices pe real companies ke apps test karte hain, approved bugs aur test cases ke paise milte hain. The Academy free training deta hai.
qs.b: The platform is a global crowdtesting community operated by the company. Testers test real customers' web and mobile apps on their own devices and are paid for approved bugs and completed test cases. It also offers free training through the Academy.
qs.t: Platform = community, company = uske peeche ki firm. Real log, real device, real paisa.

qs.q: What is crowdtesting and why do companies use it?
qs.s: Bahut saare alag testers (alag desh, device, network, language) se ek saath testing. Fayde: real devices aur real conditions, bahut coverage jaldi, location/language testing, internal team ke paas jo nahi hai wo milta hai.
qs.b: Crowdtesting uses a large, distributed group of testers to test a product in real-world conditions. Companies use it for broad device and location coverage, fast turnaround, real networks and languages, and a fresh user perspective their internal team may not have.
qs.t: 4 R: Real device, Real location, Rapid, Real user nazar.

qs.q: Who are the TE and the TTL? Who else is involved?
qs.s: TE (Test Engineer): cycle banata hai, testers ki team chunta hai, poore cycle ka zimmedaar. TTL (Test Team Lead): testers ka main contact, cycle me help karta hai, har bug report pehle review karta hai aur approve/reject ki recommendation deta hai. Upar TSM/TA aur customer ki taraf manager hota hai. Final decision customer ka.
qs.b: The Test Engineer builds the test cycle, selects the testers and owns execution. The Test Team Lead is the testers' main point of contact, answers questions during the cycle and triages every bug report with an approve or reject recommendation. The customer makes the final decision on bugs.
qs.t: TE = Engineer, cycle ka maalik. TTL = Team Lead, testers ka teacher. Customer = judge.

qs.q: What should you read in the test cycle overview before testing?
qs.s: Scope (kya test karna hai, in-scope/out-of-scope), Known issues (jo pehle se pata hain, inhe report mat karo), Environment (kaun sa device/OS/browser), Test focus, Timeline (kab tak), Payout aur bug value rules, bug title format, attachment rules, special instructions. Bina overview padhe bug daloge to reject hoga.
qs.b: Before testing I read the whole overview: the in-scope and out-of-scope areas, the known-issues list, the required environments, the test focus, the timeline, payout and bug value rules, the required title format and any attachment instructions. Most rejections come from skipping this.
qs.t: SKEPT padho: Scope, Known issues, Environment, Payout, Timeline. Plus title format.

qs.q: Walk me through a the platform test cycle from start to finish.
qs.s: Cycle ke 4 status: Pending Activation, Active, Locked, Closed. Cycle aksar 2-3 din chalta. Locked me sirf Info Requested wale items edit ho sakte. Steps: 1 Invitation aata hai (email + app). 2 Overview padh ke accept. 3 Test cases claim (sahi environment pe) ya exploratory bug hunting. 4 Bugs report, existing bugs pehle check. 5 Chat pe TTL ke messages dekhte raho, Info Request ka jawab jaldi do. 6 Cycle lock hota hai. 7 TTL triage, customer final approval. 8 Approved pe payment.
qs.b: I receive an invitation, read the overview and accept. I claim test cases on the correct environment or start exploratory testing in scope, check the existing bugs before reporting, and watch the cycle chat and respond quickly to info requests. After the cycle locks, the TTL triages, the customer approves or rejects, and approved work is paid.
qs.t: I-A-T-R-C-L-P: Invite, Accept, Test, Report, Chat/IR, Lock, Pay.

qs.q: What does in scope and out of scope mean? What if you report an out-of-scope bug?
qs.s: In-scope: jo features/areas customer ne test karne ko bola. Out-of-scope: jo nahi bola (jaise payment page, ya koi aur domain). Out-of-scope bug reject hota hai aur rating pe bura asar padta hai. Shak ho to TTL se chat me poochho.
qs.b: In scope is what the customer has asked us to test; out of scope is everything excluded, such as certain pages or features. Out-of-scope bugs are rejected and can lower your rating, so if I am unsure I ask the TTL in the cycle chat before reporting.
qs.t: Scope ke bahar = paisa bhi nahi, rating bhi kam. Doubt = TTL se poochho.

qs.q: How do you avoid duplicate bugs?
qs.s: Report karne se pehle: cycle ki bug list search karo (keywords se), known issues list dekho (blue bookmark icon wale). Same issue dobara report = DUP rejection; known issue bhi duplicate maana jata hai. Same root cause wale issues bhi duplicate. Agar bug pehle se reported hai to naya report mat banao, us report pe +1 (reproduction, attachment ke saath) do; approved hone pe rating me chhota boost.
qs.b: Before submitting, I search the cycle's bug list with several keywords and check the known-issues list. The first valid report usually wins, so duplicates are rejected. If the same issue appears on another device, I follow the cycle rules instead of filing a new bug.
qs.t: Report se pehle 2 jagah dekho: Bug list + Known issues. 'Pehle aao, pehle paao'.

qs.q: What statuses can a the platform bug report have?
qs.s: Academy (Issue Reports) ke hisaab se: New (submit hua, TTL review baaki), Info Requested (aur jaankari chahiye), Pending (TE ya customer final karega), Approved, Rejected. Edit sirf New aur Info Requested me (Rejected me sirf dispute karne se pehle). Pending aur Approved me edit nahi. Info dene ke baad 'Confirm all requested info is added' click karo, status wapas New. Rejection types: WAD (Working As Designed), DUP (Duplicate ya Known Issue), OOS (Out Of Scope), DNFI (Did Not Follow Instructions), INF (maangi info nahi di), Other. WAD ke alawa har rejection rating giraata hai, DNFI ka double negative. Tester apna report Discard bhi kar sakta hai.
qs.b: A report starts as New, can move to Info Requested, then Pending while the TE or customer finalises it, and ends Approved or Rejected. Rejection types are WAD, DUP, OOS, DNFI, INF and Other. Only WAD does not affect the tester rating, and DNFI has a double negative impact.
qs.t: N-I-P-A-R. Reject: WAD, DUP, OOS, DNFI, INF, Other. WAD = rating safe, DNFI = double maar.

qs.q: What does WAD mean?
qs.s: Working As Designed: jo cheez tumhe bug lagi, wo actually design ke hisaab se sahi hai. Isse bachne ke liye: requirement/overview padho, aur 'mujhe pasand nahi' wali cheez ko bug mat bolo, usability suggestion cycle allow kare tabhi.
qs.b: WAD means 'working as designed': the behaviour reported is intended. To avoid WAD rejections I check the requirements and overview, and I do not report personal preferences as functional bugs.
qs.t: WAD = 'Ye feature hai, bug nahi'.

qs.q: How are bugs valued and paid on the platform?
qs.s: Approved bug ki value: Somewhat Valuable (Won't Fix), Somewhat Valuable, Very Valuable, Exceptionally Valuable. WNF (Won't Fix) = bug valid aur approved hai par customer fix nahi karna chahta. Academy rule: payout bug ki VALUE pe depend karta hai, severity pe nahi. Rating premium: Gold 10%, Silver 5%, Bronze 2.5% approved reports pe. Favourite tester ko us company ke issues pe extra 5% uplift. Isliye core flows ke bade bugs dhundhna best.
qs.b: Approved bugs are rated by value: Somewhat Valuable, Very Valuable or Exceptionally Valuable, and the payout depends on that value. The customer and TTL decide it based on impact, so I focus on core flows where defects have the biggest effect.
qs.t: S-V-E: Somewhat, Very, Exceptionally. Bada impact = bada paisa.

qs.q: What is an Info Request (IR) and how should you respond?
qs.s: TTL ya customer bug pe aur jaankari maangta hai: video, logs, device version, steps clear karna. Jaldi aur exactly wahi do jo maanga, report edit karo, phir 'Confirm all requested info is added' click karo (status Info Requested se New). Issue Quality Review feature ka info request address nahi kiya to cycle close hone pe report auto-reject. Maangi info na dene pe rejection type INF.
qs.b: An info request means the TTL or customer needs more detail, such as a video, logs or clearer steps. I respond quickly with exactly what was asked, update the report, and confirm in the reply. Slow or missing answers can lead to rejection.
qs.t: IR = Ignore mat karo, Respond turant.

qs.q: How does the platform tester rating work?
qs.s: Rating activity aur quality points se banti hai aur baaki testers se compare hoti hai, har raat recalculate. Levels: Unrated (25 points se kam) → Rated (0-49.99%, kam se kam 25 points, aksar 2-3 cycles ke baad) → Proven (top 50-74.99%) → Bronze (75-84.99%) → Silver (85-92.99%) → Gold (top 7%). Badhta: participation, early decline, approved issues/test cases, attachment ke saath +1 reproduction. Girta: participation nahi, rejected kaam, low integrity, TTL/TE ko jawab na dena. WAD rejection rating nahi giraata. Unrated aur Rated testers: ek cycle me max 5 unapproved issues. Rating se paid invitations ke chances badhte hain.
qs.b: The platform rates testers on activity and quality compared with the rest of the community. Levels progress from Unrated and Rated to Proven, Bronze, Silver and Gold. Approved, valuable work raises the rating, while duplicates and out-of-scope reports lower it, and a higher rating leads to more paid invitations.
qs.t: U-R-P-B-S-G: Unrated Rahul Pehle Bronze, Silver, Gold. Quality > quantity.

qs.q: How do you execute a test case on the platform?
qs.s: Slot claim se pehle slot description kholo, requirement (location, device, OS, language) match ho tabhi claim. Steps exactly follow karo. Step status: Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not Executed, Skipped. Naya bug mila to 'Fail & Report Issue' (Source khud Structured ho jata). Bug pehle se reported hai to us report pe +1 do aur uska Issue ID step ke Actual Result/comment me daal ke Fail karo. Slot ka ek bhi test case submit na hua to slot approve nahi hota, koi test case approve nahi. Turnaround time (jaise 6 ghante) claim ke baad gina jata hai. BFV test case 2 ghante me submit na ho to auto-unclaim.
qs.b: I claim the test case only on the environment it requires, follow every step exactly as written, and mark each step pass or fail. Every failed step is linked to a bug report, I attach the evidence requested, and I submit before the deadline.
qs.t: Claim sahi device pe → Steps jaise likhe → Fail = bug link → Time pe submit.

qs.q: What is bug fix verification (BFV)?
qs.s: Customer ne bug fix kar diya, tester dobara check karta hai ki fix hua ya nahi, usually wahi environment pe. Result: fixed ya not fixed, evidence ke saath. Ye retesting hi hai.
qs.b: Bug fix verification is retesting a previously reported bug after the customer fixes it, usually on the same environment, and reporting whether it is fixed with evidence.
qs.t: BFV = Retesting ka the platform naam.

qs.q: What are Academy practice cycles and certifications?
qs.s: Academy me courses aur quiz hote hain. Practice/sandbox cycles unpaid hote hain, inse platform seekhte ho aur rating banana shuru hota hai. Certifications skill dikhate hain aur kuch projects ke liye kaam aate hain. Maine Getting Started aur Testing in the platform Platform complete kiye, aur Introduction to Testing course + quiz.
qs.b: The Academy offers courses, quizzes and certifications. Practice cycles are unpaid and help new testers learn the workflow and start building a rating. I have completed the Getting Started and Testing in the platform Platform tracks and the Introduction to Testing course.
qs.t: Practice = free me seekho. Certification = skill ka certificate.

qs.q: How do you get more invitations on the platform?
qs.s: Profile poora aur sahi (devices, OS, browsers, network, location, languages). Academy complete. Practice cycles me acche bugs. Invitations jaldi accept/reply. Quality bugs, duplicate kam. Rating badhao.
qs.b: Keep the profile complete and accurate, especially devices and environments, finish the Academy, do well in practice cycles, respond quickly to invitations, and submit high-quality, non-duplicate bugs to build the rating.
qs.t: Profile + Academy + Quality + Fast reply = zyada invite.

qs.q: How should you communicate in a test cycle?
qs.s: Cycle chat me professional aur short. Pehle overview padho, phir sawaal. TTL jawab na de to dobara poochho, phir TE ko. Reject se agree nahi to politely reason ke saath baat karo, bahas nahi.
qs.b: I keep communication in the cycle chat short and professional, check the overview before asking, follow up or escalate to the TE if there is no answer, and if I disagree with a rejection I explain my reasoning politely with evidence.
qs.t: Pehle padho, phir poochho. Politely. Evidence ke saath.

qs.q: How and when do testers get paid?
qs.s: Approved kaam ka payment, hourly nahi. Mahine me do baar: 15 tareekh aur mahine ki aakhri tareekh (weekend/US holiday ho to agle business day). Methods: PayPal, Payoneer, Direct To Bank Transfer (Wise). India me SWIFT ki jagah IFSC code maang sakta hai. The platform tax nahi kaatta. Kaam cycle lock ke 15 din ke andar review hota hai; 15 din me check na hua to cycle auto-close aur TTL recommendation ke hisaab se approve/reject. Payout ke sawaal TTL se nahi, TE ya TSM se (TSM payments approve karta hai). Cycle chat me payout ki baat nahi.
qs.b: Testers are paid for approved work, not hourly, twice a month on the 15th and the last day of the month, via PayPal, Payoneer or direct bank transfer through Wise. Work is reviewed within 15 days after the cycle locks, and payout questions go to the TE or TSM, never the cycle chat.
qs.t: 15 aur aakhri tareekh. PayPal, Payoneer, Wise. Paise ki baat TE/TSM se.

topics.intro: Crowdtesting platform pe kaam kaise hota hai: roles, cycle, statuses, rating, payment. Short interview answers; poora content Course Notes section me.

topics.name: Bug Report

qs.q: What is a bug report and why is it important?
qs.s: Bug ka likha hua record jisse developer bina tumse baat kiye bug reproduce kar sake. Clear report = jaldi approve, jaldi fix. Kharab report = reject, chahe bug sahi ho.
qs.b: A bug report is a written record that lets someone who was not there reproduce and understand the defect. A clear report gets approved and fixed faster; an unclear one can be rejected even when the bug is real.
qs.t: Test: kya anjaan aadmi sirf report padh ke bug dekh lega?

qs.q: What fields are in a the platform bug report?
qs.s: Academy ke 12 fields: Issue Title, Issue Type, Frequency, Priority (yahi severity hai), Source (Exploratory ya Structured), Environment (device, browser, OS), Actions Performed (numbered, site/app kholne se shuru), Expected Results, Actual Results, Error Messages, Additional Environment Info (kuch na ho to khali chhodo), Attachments. Report Issue button cycle header me. Submit ke baad check karo attachments khul rahe hain.
qs.b: A the platform issue report has twelve fields: title, issue type, frequency, priority, source, environment, actions performed, expected results, actual results, error messages, additional environment info and attachments.
qs.t: Title, Type, Frequency, Priority, Source, Environment, Actions, Expected, Actual, Error, Additional, Attachments. 3 dropdown (Type, Frequency, Priority) + Source.

qs.q: How do you write a good bug title?
qs.s: Academy rules: title cycle overview ke format se exactly match kare. Area sahi likho (Homepage, My Profile, Cart). Issue accurately describe karo. ALL CAPS nahi. Browser ka naam title me nahi jab tak overview na bole. Har sentence capital letter se. Academy Intro cycle ka format: Device - Area - Description, jaise 'Windows 10 - Homepage - Store Locator link directs to a not found error page'. General tip: jo HO raha hai wo likho, 'not working' nahi.
qs.b: A good title answers where, what and when, so the reader understands the bug without opening it. It describes what actually happens instead of 'not working', and follows the title format given in the cycle overview.
qs.t: Where - What - When. 'Not working' = banned word.

qs.q: How do you write the Action Performed (steps)?
qs.s: Numbered steps, starting point clear (kaun sa page, logged in hai ya nahi). Har step ek action. Test data likho (kaun sa email, kaun sa item). Bas utne steps jitne bug tak jaane ke liye zaroori. Last step wo action jo bug trigger kare.
qs.b: I write short, numbered steps from a clear starting point, one action per step, with the exact test data used. I include only the steps needed to reach the bug, and the last step is the action that triggers it.
qs.t: Start point → ek step ek kaam → data likho → last step = trigger.

qs.q: How do you write expected and actual results?
qs.s: Expected: requirement ya common sense ke hisaab se kya hona chahiye tha, specific. Actual: exactly kya hua, error message word to word, screen pe kya dikha. Actual sirf expected ka ulta nahi hona chahiye aur title copy nahi.
qs.b: The expected result states specifically what should happen according to the requirement or reasonable user expectation. The actual result describes exactly what happened, including any error text. It should add detail, not just negate the expected result or repeat the title.
qs.t: Expected = kya hona tha. Actual = kya hua (exact words). Ulta-pulta copy nahi.

qs.q: What attachments should a bug report have?
qs.s: Academy rules: Screenshot .jpg/.png, red ya yellow rectangle/circle/arrow se mark (haath se drawing nahi), poori screen URL bar ke saath, ek report me 2 se zyada screenshot nahi. Video sirf .mp4, chhota (1 min se kam, zaroori steps), ek report me ek video. Logs .txt me, timestamps ke saath; Charles log .chls/.chlz poora upload. 5 MB se chhota video compress karne ki zarurat nahi. Cloud me store karna Terms of Use violation; PII blur karo. Cycle ke attachment rules sabse upar.
qs.b: I attach a marked-up screenshot for visual issues, a short trimmed video when steps are needed to show the bug, and logs for crashes or errors, always following the attachment rules in the cycle overview.
qs.t: Dikhta hai = screenshot. Steps se aata hai = video. Crash = logs.

qs.q: How do you choose severity on the platform?
qs.s: The platform form me ye field 'Priority' naam se hai, levels Low, Medium, High, Critical (customer overview me apni definition de sakta hai). Payout VALUE pe depend karta hai, severity pe nahi. Impact dekho: kitne users pe, kitna bada, workaround hai ya nahi. Critical (Academy example: app crash ya freeze, privacy breach): crash, data loss, core flow (login/checkout) poora block, security. High: important feature toota, workaround mushkil. Medium: feature partially kaam, workaround hai. Low: cosmetic, chhota UI/content issue. Cycle me apni definition ho to wahi.
qs.b: I judge severity by impact: how many users are affected, how serious it is and whether a workaround exists. Critical means crashes, data loss, security issues or a blocked core flow; high is a major feature broken; medium has a workaround; low is cosmetic. I follow the cycle's own definitions if given.
qs.t: Workaround test: workaround nahi = upar, aasaan workaround = neeche. C-H-M-L.

qs.q: What bug types are there?
qs.s: Academy ke 5 issue types: Functional (feature galat kaam), Visual (layout, alignment, overlap), Content (spelling, translation, galat text), Performance (app 10 second se zyada freeze ya unresponsive), Crash. Cycle me jo types allowed hon wahi chuno. Example: button kuch nahi karta = functional, text overlap = visual, typo = content.
qs.b: The platform uses five issue types: functional, visual, content, performance and crash. A button that does nothing is functional, overlapping text is visual, a typo is content, and a freeze longer than ten seconds is performance.
qs.t: F-V-C-P-C: Functional, Visual, Content, Performance (10 sec), Crash.

qs.q: What is frequency or reproducibility?
qs.s: The platform options: Every time, Occasionally, Hardly ever, Once. Report se pehle 2-3 baar reproduce karo. Kabhi kabhi aane wale bug me Additional Environment Info me likho kitne try me kitni baar aaya (jaise 3/5).
qs.b: Frequency says how often the issue occurs: on the platform the options are every time, occasionally, hardly ever and once. I reproduce it a few times before reporting and note the ratio for intermittent bugs.
qs.t: Every time, Occasionally, Hardly ever, Once.

qs.q: Why only one issue per report?
qs.s: Har bug alag fix, alag status, alag value. Do issue ek report me = confusion, aur aksar reject ya ek hi ka paisa. Alag issue = alag report.
qs.b: Each defect needs its own status, fix and value, so combining issues causes confusion and often leads to rejection. One issue per report keeps it clear and trackable.
qs.t: Ek report, ek bug. 2-in-1 sirf shampoo me.

qs.q: What is a placeholder bug and why is it not allowed?
qs.s: Adhoori report jaldi daal dena taaki pehle tumhara naam aa jaye, baad me details bharoge. Ye rule ke khilaaf hai, reject aur rating down. Report tabhi submit karo jab poori ho.
qs.b: A placeholder is an incomplete report submitted early to claim the bug before others. It is against the rules and is rejected, so I only submit complete reports.
qs.t: Adhoora report = Rejection pakka.

qs.q: What common mistakes get bug reports rejected?
qs.s: Duplicate, out of scope, known issue, WAD, reproduce nahi hua, steps unclear, galat environment chuna, attachment missing, title vague, multiple issues ek me.
qs.b: Common reasons are duplicates, out-of-scope or known issues, working-as-designed behaviour, bugs that cannot be reproduced, unclear steps, the wrong environment, missing attachments, vague titles and several issues in one report.
qs.t: Submit se pehle khud TTL ban ke padho.

qs.q: What is your checklist before submitting a bug?
qs.s: 1 In scope hai? 2 Bug list + known issues me nahi hai? 3 2-3 baar reproduce hua? 4 Title where-what-when? 5 Steps clear, data ke saath? 6 Expected/actual specific? 7 Sahi environment, type, severity, frequency? 8 Screenshot/video/logs attached? 9 Koi personal/customer data screenshot me to nahi?
qs.b: Before submitting I confirm it is in scope, not a duplicate or known issue, reproducible, with a clear title, precise steps and results, the correct environment, type, severity and frequency, the required attachments, and no sensitive data visible.
qs.t: 9 point check: Scope, Dup, Repro, Title, Steps, Results, Fields, Proof, Privacy.

topics.intro: Bug report hi tumhara product hai. Rules Issue Reports course se match kiye gaye. Neeche ek sample bug report bhi hai.

topics.name: Functional Testing

qs.q: What is functional testing?
qs.s: Har feature requirement ke hisaab se sahi kaam karta hai ya nahi, ye check karna. Input do, output dekho, expected se match karo. Black box hota hai.
qs.b: Functional testing verifies that each feature works according to the requirements by giving inputs and comparing the outputs with expected results, without looking at the code.
qs.t: Input → Output → Expected se match.

qs.q: What would you test on a web app?
qs.s: Login/signup/logout/forgot password, forms aur validation, buttons aur links, navigation aur back button, search aur filters, cart/checkout (scope me ho to), error messages, refresh pe data, session timeout, alag screen size.
qs.b: I would cover authentication flows, form validation, buttons and links, navigation including the back button, search and filters, the main transactional flow such as checkout if in scope, error messages, behaviour on refresh and session timeout, and different screen sizes.
qs.t: Ghar ka tour: Darwaza (login), Form, Raasta (nav), Dhundho (search), Kharido (checkout), Galti (errors).

qs.q: What would you test on a mobile app?
qs.s: Install/update/uninstall, permissions (allow/deny), portrait-landscape rotation, interruptions (call, SMS, notification), network badalna (Wi-Fi se mobile data, airplane mode, slow net), background-foreground, battery saver, keyboard aur back button, push notifications, alag screen size.
qs.b: On mobile I test install, update and uninstall, permission handling, rotation, interruptions like calls and notifications, network changes and offline mode, switching between background and foreground, battery saver, keyboard and back-button behaviour, and push notifications.
qs.t: I-P-R-I-N-B: Install, Permission, Rotate, Interrupt, Network, Background.

qs.q: How do you find valuable bugs quickly in a cycle?
qs.s: Pehle test focus aur core flows (jahan paisa ya main kaam hai): login, signup, checkout, search. Phir negative inputs aur edge cases. Normal user jaisa socho aur shaitaan user jaisa bhi. Cosmetic bugs baad me. Bade impact wale bug = Very/Exceptionally valuable.
qs.b: I start with the test focus and the core user flows where defects have the biggest impact, then try negative inputs, edge cases and interruptions. I think like both a normal and a careless user, and leave cosmetic checks for later.
qs.t: Pehle paisa wala raasta, phir kinare, phir sajawat.

qs.q: How do you approach exploratory testing in a cycle?
qs.s: Overview se goal (charter) banao: 'Checkout ko alag payment options aur network changes ke saath explore karo'. Time-box (jaise 45 min). Notes lo: kya kiya, kya mila. Har session ke baad next area chuno.
qs.b: I set a charter from the test focus, time-box the session, take notes on what I tried and found, and then decide the next area based on what I learned.
qs.t: Charter + Timer + Notes.

qs.q: What test ideas do you use for form validation?
qs.s: Khali field, sirf spaces, aage-peeche spaces, max length se zyada, special characters, emoji, galat format (email bina @, phone me letters), copy-paste, number field me negative ya decimal, required field skip karke submit, double submit click.
qs.b: For forms I try empty and whitespace-only values, leading and trailing spaces, input over the maximum length, special characters, wrong formats, pasted text, negative or decimal numbers, skipping required fields and double-clicking submit.
qs.t: Khali, Lamba, Ajeeb, Galat format, Double click.

qs.q: How do you classify a bug as functional, visual or content?
qs.s: Functional: cheez kaam nahi kar rahi ya galat result (button kuch nahi karta, galat total). Visual: dikhne me problem (overlap, cut text, alignment). Content: text galat (spelling, grammar, translation, galat price text). Ek issue me dono hon to main asar dekho.
qs.b: If behaviour or results are wrong it is functional, if it is a layout or display problem it is visual, and if the text itself is wrong, such as a typo or translation, it is content. When it overlaps, I classify by the main impact.
qs.t: Kaam galat = Functional. Shakal galat = Visual. Shabd galat = Content.

qs.q: Do you run a smoke check at the start of a cycle?
qs.s: Haan. 5-10 min me main flows chala ke dekho ki build test karne layak hai. Agar app khul hi nahi raha ya login toota hai, turant report/TTL ko batao, baaki testers ka time bachega.
qs.b: Yes. I spend a few minutes on the main flows to confirm the build is testable, and if something critical like launch or login is broken I report it immediately and inform the TTL.
qs.t: Pehle 10 min = smoke. Block mila = turant batao.

qs.q: How do you use test data and accounts in a cycle?
qs.s: Sirf wo accounts aur data jo cycle ne diya. Apna real data tabhi jab cycle saaf bole. Test data report me likho taaki reproduce ho sake.
qs.b: I use only the accounts and test data provided by the cycle, use personal data only when the cycle explicitly asks for it, and record the test data in my report so the bug can be reproduced.
qs.t: Diya hua data hi use, aur report me likho.

topics.intro: Interview summary aur bug hunting ke practical tarike. Poora Functional Testing course Course Notes section me.

topics.name: Testing Tools

qs.q: How do you take and mark up screenshots?
qs.s: Windows 11: Win+Shift+S (Snipping Tool). Android (Moto): Power + Volume Down. Academy rules: bug ko red ya yellow rectangle/circle/arrow se mark karo, haath se drawing nahi. Poori screen capture karo URL bar ke saath, faltu tabs band. Seedha (upright) orientation. .jpg ya .png. Ek report me max 2 screenshots. PII blur.
qs.b: On Windows I use Win+Shift+S with Snipping Tool and mark the defect with the pen or highlighter; on Android I press Power and Volume Down. I always highlight the problem area and save as PNG or JPG.
qs.t: Win+Shift+S. Power+Vol Down. Hamesha mark karo.

qs.q: How do you record a bug video?
qs.s: Windows 11: Snipping Tool ka record mode, ya Xbox Game Bar (Win+Alt+R). Android: Quick Settings me Screen Record, 'Show taps' on. Academy rules: sirf .mp4, chhota (1 min se kam, sirf zaroori steps), ek report me ek video, sirf local machine pe save (cloud me rakhna Terms of Use violation), the platform platform recording me na dikhe (PII/GDPR), PII blur. 5 MB se bada ho aur upload limit ho to HandBrake se compress.
qs.b: On Windows I record with Snipping Tool's recorder or Xbox Game Bar, and on Android with the built-in screen recorder from Quick Settings, with 'Show taps' enabled. I keep it short, start just before the steps and trim it to the relevant part.
qs.t: Show taps ON. Chhota video. Shuru se bug tak.

qs.q: How do you collect browser logs?
qs.s: F12 se DevTools. Console tab: red errors ka screenshot ya copy. Network tab: failed requests (4xx/5xx status) dekho. Browser version: chrome://version. Ye sab bug me 'Error Code/Message' ya attachment me daalo.
qs.b: I open DevTools with F12, capture red errors from the Console and failed requests with 4xx or 5xx status from the Network tab, and note the browser version from chrome://version. I add these to the error field or as attachments.
qs.t: F12 → Console (laal error) + Network (4xx/5xx).

qs.q: What is a HAR file and what is the risk?
qs.s: Network tab ki poori recording export (.har). Developer ko request/response detail milti hai. Risk: isme cookies, tokens, personal data hota hai. Sirf platform pe, cycle ke kehne pe share karo.
qs.b: A HAR file exports all network activity from the browser, which helps developers debug. It can contain cookies, tokens and personal data, so I only share it through the platform and only when the cycle requests it.
qs.t: HAR = useful par khatarnaak. Sirf maangne pe, platform pe.

qs.q: How do you collect Android logs?
qs.s: Phone me Developer options on (Settings → About phone → Build number 7 baar tap). USB debugging on. Laptop pe Android platform-tools, phir adb logcat > log.txt. Crash ke liye adb logcat -b crash. Bug reproduce karo, phir log save.
qs.b: I enable Developer options and USB debugging, connect the phone, and capture logs with adb logcat into a text file, or the crash buffer for crashes, while reproducing the bug.
qs.t: Build number 7 tap → USB debugging → adb logcat.

qs.q: How do you find device and environment details?
qs.s: Android: Settings → About phone (model, Android version). Windows: winver command. Browser: chrome://version. Network: Wi-Fi ya mobile (carrier). Ye report me sahi environment chunne ke liye.
qs.b: I take Android details from About phone, Windows details from winver, browser details from chrome://version, and note whether I was on Wi-Fi or mobile data, so the environment in the report is accurate.
qs.t: Phone: About. Windows: winver. Browser: chrome://version.

qs.q: How can you test slow network or offline behaviour?
qs.s: Browser: DevTools → Network → throttling (Slow 3G, Offline). Phone: airplane mode beech flow me, Wi-Fi se mobile data switch. Dekho app crash to nahi hota, message sahi dikhta hai, data save hota hai.
qs.b: In the browser I use DevTools network throttling or offline mode; on the phone I toggle airplane mode or switch networks mid-flow, and check that the app shows a clear message, does not crash and does not lose data.
qs.t: Throttle karo, net kaato, dekho girta to nahi.

qs.q: Can you use emulators or DevTools device mode for the platform cycles?
qs.s: The platform rule (the platform Basics): emulators, simulators, remote machines, beta software ya jailbroken devices kabhi use nahi karne. Testing sirf apne real device pe jo profile me hai. DevTools device mode sirf apni samajh ke liye, the platform testing ke liye nahi.
qs.b: No. The platform rules forbid emulators, simulators, remote machines, beta software and jailbroken devices; testing must be done on the real devices listed in my profile.
qs.t: the platform pe emulator = mana. Sirf asli device.

topics.intro: Interview summary, Testing Tools courses ke rules ke saath. Examples tumhare devices ke hisaab se: Windows 11 laptop aur Moto G85. Poore courses Course Notes section me.

topics.name: Data Security

qs.q: Why is data security important in crowdtesting?
qs.s: Hum unreleased apps, customer ke secrets aur kabhi real data dekhte hain. Leak hua to customer ka nuksaan, the platform ka trust khatam, aur tester ka account band ho sakta hai.
qs.b: Crowdtesters see unreleased products and sometimes sensitive data, so any leak can harm the customer and the platform's trust. Following security and confidentiality rules is part of the job.
qs.t: Unreleased + data = trust. Trust toota = account gaya.

qs.q: What does confidentiality or an NDA mean for a tester?
qs.s: Cycle, customer ka naam, features, screenshots, bugs kisi se share nahi: na social media, na forum, na dost, na portfolio. Sirf the platform platform ke andar.
qs.b: Confidentiality means I never share cycle details, the customer's name, features, screenshots or bugs outside the platform, including social media, forums and my portfolio.
qs.t: Cycle ki baat cycle me hi.

qs.q: What is PII and how do you handle it?
qs.s: Personally Identifiable Information: naam, phone, email, address, ID number, card details, location. Report aur screenshot me apna ya kisi aur ka real PII mat dikhao, blur/mask karo. Cycle maange tabhi real data.
qs.b: PII is any information that identifies a person, such as name, phone, email, address or ID numbers. I avoid exposing it in reports and screenshots, mask it when visible, and use real data only when the cycle explicitly requires it.
qs.t: PII dikha = blur karo.

qs.q: How should you handle test accounts and credentials?
qs.s: Jo account diya wahi use, kisi se share nahi, report me password sirf tab jab cycle bole. Apna personal password reuse mat karo. Apna the platform account MFA se secure (maine MFA on kiya hai).
qs.b: I use only the provided test accounts, never share credentials, include them in reports only if instructed, never reuse personal passwords, and keep my own account protected with multi-factor authentication.
qs.t: Diya account, chupa password, MFA on.

qs.q: What are the rules for payment testing?
qs.s: Sirf cycle me diye test cards ya instructions. Real card/real paisa tabhi jab cycle clearly bole aur tum comfortable ho. Card details kabhi screenshot ya report me nahi.
qs.b: For payment testing I use only the test cards or method the cycle provides, use real payment only when explicitly required and I agree to it, and never expose card details in reports or screenshots.
qs.t: Test card hi. Real card = sirf likhit permission pe.

qs.q: What should you do with builds and data after a cycle?
qs.s: Beta builds/apps uninstall karo jab cycle khatam ho ya bola jaye. Download kiye files, screenshots, videos delete karo jo platform pe upload ho chuke. Kuch bhi personal folder ya cloud me mat rakho.
qs.b: After a cycle I uninstall beta builds as instructed and delete local copies of files, screenshots and videos once they are uploaded, so no customer material stays on my devices.
qs.t: Cycle khatam = app hatao, files hatao.

qs.q: How do you keep your device and account secure?
qs.s: OS aur browser updated, antivirus, screen lock, MFA. Unknown link ya fake email (the platform jaisa dikhta) pe click nahi, sender domain check. Public Wi-Fi pe sensitive testing avoid.
qs.b: I keep the OS and browser updated, use a screen lock and MFA, check sender domains to avoid phishing emails that imitate the platform, and avoid sensitive testing on public Wi-Fi.
qs.t: Update, Lock, MFA, Link check.

qs.q: What do you do if you find a security vulnerability?
qs.s: Sirf platform pe report karo (agar scope me security allowed ho, warna TTL se poochho). Aage exploit mat karo, data mat nikalo, kisi ko mat batao.
qs.b: I report it only through the platform, or ask the TTL if security is out of scope. I do not exploit it further, access more data or disclose it to anyone.
qs.t: Report karo, chhedo mat, chup raho.

qs.q: What should you remove from logs and attachments?
qs.s: Tokens, cookies, passwords, personal info. Screenshot me notifications ya doosre tabs me personal cheez na dikhe. Video me personal chats nahi.
qs.b: I remove or mask tokens, cookies, passwords and personal details, and make sure screenshots and videos do not show unrelated notifications, tabs or private messages.
qs.t: Proof me sirf bug dikhe, tumhari zindagi nahi.

topics.intro: General data security practice + PII rules. Poora PII course Course Notes section me.

topics.name: Interview Scripts

qs.q: Tell me about yourself.
qs.s: 60-90 second. Kaun ho → abhi kya karte ho → kya tools → kya seekh rahe ho → kyun ye role. Numbers mat bolo jo defend nahi kar sakte.
qs.b: I'm Ritik, a QA Engineer at Merlin AI, a Y Combinator-backed startup in Bangalore, where I've worked since December 2025. I test our web and mobile app on staging, with read-only checks on production, and I own quality for the purchase order module. I write test cases, run regression, triage production issues and report bugs in Linear. On the automation side I work with Playwright and Python, and I test APIs with Postman. I'm now building my crowdtesting experience on the platform, where I've completed the Academy tracks, because I want exposure to many products and devices.
qs.t: Kaun → Kahan → Kya test → Kya tools → Kyun yahan.

qs.q: Why do you want to do crowdtesting?
qs.s: Alag products, alag devices aur real users ke scenario dekhne ko milte hain, skill fast badhti hai. Apne kaam ke saath extra experience.
qs.b: Crowdtesting exposes me to many different products, devices and user scenarios, which sharpens my bug-finding skills much faster than one product alone. It complements my full-time QA work.
qs.t: Variety → Skill → Experience.

qs.q: How do you test an app with no documentation?
qs.s: Pehle app ko user ki tarah explore karo, main flows samjho. Fir mind map: features aur unke flows. Core flows pe positive/negative, edge cases. Questions note karo, TTL/PM se poochho. Jo seekha uske notes.
qs.b: I start by exploring it as a user to learn the main flows, build a quick map of features, then test the core flows with positive, negative and edge cases. I note open questions and confirm expected behaviour with the team.
qs.t: Explore → Map → Core flows → Edges → Poochho.

qs.q: Tell me about a good bug you found.
qs.s: STAR use karo: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Merlin ka real example: UPB finance verification me Chart of Accounts check kiya aur pata chala ki cost/expense accounts ka poora set do baar bana hua tha, ek copy zero balance wali. Wo pehle se tha, testing ne pakda. Sirf wahi bolo jo tum detail me samjha sako.
qs.b: While verifying a customer's finance fixes on staging, I was checking whether expense categories were grouped correctly. Instead of only looking at the dropdown, I exported the chart of accounts and compared it with a script. I found that a whole set of cost and expense accounts existed twice, one copy with zero balance and one with real balances. I reported it with the evidence list, and it changed how the team planned the clean-up, because the duplicates would have caused wrong postings.
qs.t: STAR. Situation-Task-Action-Result. Ek hi kahani achhi tarah taiyar rakho.

qs.q: How do you handle a rejected bug?
qs.s: Gussa nahi. Reason padho. Galti meri thi (duplicate, scope) to seekho. Agar lagta hai bug sahi hai to politely evidence ke saath explain karo. Next cycle me wahi galti nahi.
qs.b: I read the rejection reason first. If it was my mistake, such as a duplicate or out-of-scope report, I learn from it. If I believe it is valid, I reply politely with extra evidence, and I accept the final decision either way.
qs.t: Padho → Seekho ya Samjhao (politely) → Aage badho.

qs.q: What if you cannot reproduce a bug?
qs.s: Exact steps, data, time, network, device state yaad karo. 5-10 baar try, alag condition me. Video/log hai to wo do. Report me Sometimes/Once aur ratio likho, ya cycle rules ke hisaab se report mat karo.
qs.b: I retrace the exact steps, data and conditions and try several times under different states. If I have a video or logs I include them, and I report it as intermittent with the ratio, or follow the cycle's rule for non-reproducible issues.
qs.t: Retrace, Retry, Record, Ratio.

qs.q: How do you decide severity?
qs.s: Teen sawaal: kitne users pe asar? kitna bada nuksaan (crash, data, paisa)? workaround hai? Fir cycle ki definition se match.
qs.b: I ask three questions: how many users are affected, how serious the damage is, and whether there is a workaround. Then I map that to the cycle's severity definitions.
qs.t: Users, Damage, Workaround.

qs.q: How is crowdtesting different from in-house QA?
qs.s: In-house: ek product deep me jaante ho, team ke saath, requirement access. Crowd: kai products, short cycles, real devices, sirf scope aur overview pe depend, competition (duplicate), report hi tumhari pehchaan.
qs.b: In-house QA means deep knowledge of one product and close work with developers. Crowdtesting means many products, short cycles, real devices and locations, and relying on the overview and the report alone, since the reviewer never talks to you directly.
qs.t: In-house = gehrai. Crowd = chaudai + report quality.

qs.q: What devices and environments can you test on?
qs.s: Jo profile me hai wahi bolo: Windows 11 laptop (Chrome, Edge, Brave) aur Motorola Moto G85 (Android 16, Airtel network). Jhooth mat bolo, cycle me environment match karna padta hai.
qs.b: I have a Windows 11 laptop with Chrome, Edge and Brave, and a Motorola Moto G85 on Android 16 with mobile data on Airtel as well as Wi-Fi.
qs.t: Laptop: Win 11 + 3 browsers. Phone: Moto G85, Android 16.

qs.q: What questions should you ask the interviewer?
qs.s: Interview ke end me 1-2 sawaal: team testing kaise karti hai, kaun se tools, pehle 3 mahine me kya expect, success kaise measure.
qs.b: I would ask how the team plans and tracks testing, which tools they use, what success looks like in the first three months, and how QA works with developers.
qs.t: Process, Tools, 3 mahine, Success.

topics.intro: Ye ready answers hain. Formula yaad rakho: D-E-M = Define (seedha jawab), Example (chhota example), Merlin (apna real kaam). Sirf wahi bolo jo tum defend kar sako.

topics.name: Test Case Writing

qs.q: Write test cases for a login page.
qs.s: Positive: valid email + password se login, Remember me, Enter key se submit. Negative: galat password, galat email, dono khali, sirf ek khali, galat email format, spaces. Boundary: password min/max length. Security: password masked ho, 5 galat try ke baad lock/captcha, back button se logout ke baad wapas andar na jaye, SQL-type input pe crash na ho, HTTPS. UI: labels, error message clear, tab order. Other: forgot password link, session timeout, alag browser/device.
qs.b: I group them. Positive: valid credentials log in and land on the home page, Enter submits the form, Remember me works. Negative: wrong password, unregistered email, empty fields, invalid email format, leading spaces. Boundary: password length limits. Security: password is masked, the account locks or shows a captcha after repeated failures, the back button after logout does not restore the session, and the page uses HTTPS. UI: clear error messages and correct tab order. I would also check forgot password and session timeout.
qs.t: 6 dabbe: Positive, Negative, Boundary, UI, Security, Performance. Har question pe yahi.

qs.q: Write test cases for a search feature.
qs.s: Exact keyword, partial word, case insensitive (Pen/pen/PEN), spaces aage peeche, special characters, khali search, bahut lamba text, koi result nahi wala message, results relevant hain, filter + sort ke saath, pagination, typo suggestion (agar feature hai), speed, search ke baad back button.
qs.b: I would test exact and partial matches, case insensitivity, leading and trailing spaces, special characters, empty and very long input, the no-results message, relevance and ordering of results, combination with filters, sorting and pagination, and response time.
qs.t: Exact, Partial, Case, Khali, Ajeeb, No result, Filter+Sort, Speed.

qs.q: How would you test a pen?
qs.s: Classic question, tumhari sochne ki aadat dekhte hain. Requirement poochho pehle (kaun sa pen, kiske liye). Functional: likhta hai, ink smooth, cap band-khulta, click wala to click. Non-functional: grip comfortable, weight, kitne page chalta hai, alag kagaz pe, garmi/thand me, girne pe tootta hai ya nahi. Negative: ulta pakad ke, gile kagaz pe. Safety: bachche cap nigal na lein (vent hole).
qs.b: First I would ask about requirements: who uses it and for what. Then functional checks such as writing, ink flow, cap or click mechanism; non-functional checks such as grip, weight, how many pages it lasts, behaviour in heat and cold and when dropped; negative checks like writing on wet paper; and safety, such as a vented cap.
qs.t: Pehle sawaal poochho. Phir Kaam, Aaram, Tikau, Galat use, Safety.

qs.q: How would you test a lift (elevator)?
qs.s: Functional: button dabao to sahi floor pe jaye, door khule/band ho, door me koi ho to band na ho (sensor), multiple floor requests ka order. Boundary: max weight pe overload alarm. Safety: emergency button, alarm, power cut pe kya, phone. UI: floor display, button light. Performance: wait time, speed.
qs.b: I would test that it reaches the selected floor, handles multiple requests in a sensible order, and that the doors open, close and reopen when blocked. Then the overload limit and alarm, emergency button, behaviour during a power cut, the floor display and button lights, and travel and waiting times.
qs.t: Jaaye, Khule, Ruke (sensor), Wazan, Emergency, Display.

qs.q: Write test cases for a shopping cart and checkout.
qs.s: Item add/remove, quantity badhana/ghatana (0, negative, max stock se zyada), price aur total sahi (tax, discount, shipping), coupon valid/invalid/expired, cart logout-login ke baad bhi rahe, out of stock item, address add/edit, payment success/fail/cancel, double click pe double order na bane, order confirmation email, back button payment ke baad.
qs.b: I would cover adding and removing items, quantity limits including zero and above stock, correct totals with tax, discounts and shipping, valid and invalid coupons, cart persistence across sessions, out-of-stock handling, address validation, payment success, failure and cancellation, no duplicate orders on double click, and the confirmation email.
qs.t: Add, Qty, Total sahi, Coupon, Persist, Stock, Pay (pass/fail/cancel), Double order.

qs.q: Write test cases for a file upload.
qs.s: Allowed types (pdf, jpg) chalein, not allowed (exe) reject. Max size pe, usse zyada. 0 KB file. Lamba naam, special character naam, same naam dobara. Multiple files. Upload beech me net gaya. Progress bar. Upload ke baad preview/download sahi. Virus/script file name.
qs.b: I would test allowed and blocked file types, size at and above the limit, an empty file, long and special-character file names, duplicate names, multiple uploads, network loss mid-upload, progress indication, and that the uploaded file can be previewed or downloaded correctly.
qs.t: Type, Size, Naam, Multiple, Net cut, Wapas download.

qs.q: Write test cases for forgot password.
qs.s: Registered email pe link aaye, unregistered pe generic message (ye mat batao account hai ya nahi, security). Link ek baar use ho, expire ho time ke baad. Naya password rules follow kare, purana password reject (agar rule hai). Reset ke baad purane sessions logout. Baar baar request pe rate limit.
qs.b: A registered email receives a reset link and an unknown email gets a neutral message that does not reveal whether the account exists. The link works once and expires, the new password follows the rules, old sessions end after reset, and repeated requests are rate limited.
qs.t: Link aaye, Ek baar, Expire, Rules, Purana session out, Spam limit.

qs.q: How do you test a date field or date picker?
qs.s: Valid date, 29 Feb leap year aur non-leap, 31 April (invalid), past/future rules, start date end date se baad na ho, format (DD/MM vs MM/DD), timezone, manual type vs picker, khali.
qs.b: I check valid dates, leap years, invalid dates like 31 April, past and future rules, that a start date cannot be after an end date, date format, timezone handling, typing versus using the picker, and empty values.
qs.t: Leap year, 31 April, Start>End, Format, Timezone.

qs.q: Write test cases for a signup form.
qs.s: Har field ka validation (naam, email, phone, password rules, confirm password match), duplicate email, terms checkbox zaroori, email verification, password strength, captcha, success ke baad kahan jaata hai, back button.
qs.b: I validate each field, including email format, phone format, password rules and password confirmation, block duplicate emails, require the terms checkbox, and check email verification, the success flow and redirect.
qs.t: Har field, Duplicate, Confirm match, Terms, Verify email.

qs.q: How would you test a payment gateway integration?
qs.s: Success, failure, cancel, timeout. Test cards (sandbox). Amount sahi jaaye, currency. Payment success par order bane, fail par na bane, paisa kat gaya par order nahi (pending/refund handling). Double payment nahi. Card details store/screenshot na hon. Bank page se wapas aane pe sahi status.
qs.b: Using sandbox test cards, I test success, failure, cancellation and timeout, correct amount and currency, that an order is created only on success, how a deducted-but-failed payment is handled, no duplicate charges, the return flow from the bank page, and that card data is never stored or shown.
qs.t: Pass, Fail, Cancel, Timeout, Double charge, Card safe.

qs.q: How would you test an ATM?
qs.s: Card insert, sahi/galat PIN, 3 galat pe block, balance check, withdraw (multiple of 100, balance se zyada, daily limit, ATM me cash kam), receipt, card wapas, timeout pe card andar, cash nahi nikla par paisa kata (reversal).
qs.b: I would test card reading, correct and incorrect PINs with blocking after the limit, balance inquiry, withdrawals with valid and invalid amounts, insufficient balance, daily limits and low cash in the machine, receipts, card return and timeout, and reversal when cash is not dispensed.
qs.t: PIN (3 galat), Amount rules, Limit, Cash nahi nikla, Timeout.

qs.q: How do you test a dropdown?
qs.s: Default value, saari options sahi aur sahi order, select karne pe value save ho, keyboard se chale, bahut options pe search/scroll, required ho to khali pe error, dependent dropdown (country → state) sahi badle.
qs.b: I check the default value, the full and correctly ordered list, that the selection is saved, keyboard access, scrolling or search for long lists, required-field validation, and dependent dropdowns updating correctly.
qs.t: Default, Saari options, Save, Keyboard, Dependent.

qs.q: How do you test pagination?
qs.s: Page size sahi, next/prev/first/last, last page pe next disable, total count sahi, page badalne pe filter/sort bana rahe, record repeat ya miss na ho, URL se direct page, 0 results.
qs.b: I verify page size, navigation buttons, disabled states at the edges, total count, that filters and sorting persist across pages, that no records are repeated or skipped, and behaviour with zero results.
qs.t: Size, Next/Prev, Edge disable, Count, Repeat/miss na ho.

qs.q: How would you test a purchase order flow?
qs.s: Tumhara Merlin ka area. Create PO (vendor, items, qty, price), totals (tax, shipping, discount), approval flow, send to vendor, receive (partial/full), receive ke baad inventory badhe, invoice match (PO-receipt-invoice, three-way match), cancel/close, edit after approval rules, permissions (kaun kya kar sakta hai), dusre org ka data na dikhe.
qs.b: In my current role I look after the purchase order module. I test creation with vendor, items, quantities and prices, totals with tax and shipping, the approval flow, sending to the vendor, partial and full receiving and its effect on inventory, matching against invoices, cancel and close, edit rules after approval, role permissions, and data isolation between organisations.
qs.t: Create → Total → Approve → Send → Receive → Inventory → Invoice match → Close. Plus permission.

qs.q: How do you write test cases from a user story?
qs.s: Story padho (As a... I want... so that...), acceptance criteria se har criterion ke liye kam se kam ek positive aur ek negative case. Doubt ho to PM/dev se pehle clear karo. Edge cases khud socho jo AC me nahi likhe.
qs.b: I read the story and its acceptance criteria, write at least one positive and one negative case per criterion, add edge cases the criteria do not mention, and clarify any ambiguity with the product owner before testing.
qs.t: Har AC = 1 positive + 1 negative + edges.

qs.q: How do you prioritise test cases when time is short?
qs.s: Risk based: pehle core business flows aur jo change hua uske aas paas. Phir jahan pehle bugs aaye the. Cosmetic baad me. Team ko batao kya cover nahi hua.
qs.b: I use risk-based prioritisation: core business flows and the areas around the change first, then historically buggy areas, and cosmetic checks last. I tell the team clearly what was not covered.
qs.t: Core + Change + Purane bug areas. Jo chhoota, wo batao.

qs.q: What is error guessing?
qs.s: Experience se andaza lagana ki kahan bug hoga: khali input, zero, negative, special characters, double click, back button, refresh beech me. Experienced tester ki taakat.
qs.b: Error guessing uses experience to predict where defects are likely, such as empty input, zero, negative numbers, double clicks or refreshing mid-flow, and designing tests for those.
qs.t: Experience ka jadoo: Khali, Zero, Double click, Refresh.

qs.q: What is pairwise testing?
qs.s: Jab bahut combinations hon (browser x OS x language), sab test karna mushkil. Pairwise me har do values ka combination kam se kam ek baar cover karte hain, test count bahut kam ho jata hai.
qs.b: Pairwise testing reduces a large number of combinations by ensuring every pair of parameter values is covered at least once, which catches most interaction defects with far fewer tests.
qs.t: Sab combo nahi, har JODI ek baar.

qs.q: What is use case testing?
qs.s: User ka poora kaam shuru se end tak (end-to-end) test: main flow + alternate flows + error flows. Jaise 'user order place karta hai'.
qs.b: Use case testing follows a complete user goal end to end, covering the main flow, alternate flows and error flows.
qs.t: User ki kahani shuru se ant tak.

qs.q: How do you make sure your test coverage is good?
qs.s: Requirement se test case map (RTM), har AC covered, positive+negative+boundary, risky areas pe zyada, review apne lead/dev se, prod bugs se seekh ke naye cases add.
qs.b: I map tests to requirements, cover each acceptance criterion with positive, negative and boundary cases, focus extra effort on risky areas, get my cases reviewed, and add new cases whenever a defect escapes.
qs.t: Map, Har AC, 3 type, Risk, Review, Escape se seekho.

qs.q: How would you test a chat or messaging feature?
qs.s: Message send/receive, order sahi, emoji, lamba message, attachment, offline me bheja to baad me jaaye, read/delivered status, notification, do devices pe sync, block user, delete message.
qs.b: I would test sending and receiving, message order, long text and emoji, attachments, sending while offline, delivery and read status, notifications, sync across devices, and blocking or deleting messages.
qs.t: Send, Order, Offline, Status, Notification, Sync.

qs.q: How would you test a report or export feature?
qs.s: Numbers screen se match karein, filter ke hisaab se data, date range ke kinare, khali data, bahut bada data, export file (CSV/Excel) khule aur columns sahi, timezone, permissions.
qs.b: I check that totals match the screen and the database, filters and date range boundaries apply correctly, empty and large data sets, that the exported file opens with correct columns and formats, timezones and permissions.
qs.t: Number match, Filter, Date kinara, Khali/Bada, File khule.

topics.intro: 1 saal experience pe ye pakka poochha jata hai: 'X ke test cases batao'. Formula: Positive, Negative, Boundary, UI, Security, Performance. Har cheez pe yahi 6 dabbe socho.

topics.name: API Testing

qs.q: What is an API?
qs.s: Application Programming Interface: do software ke beech baat karne ka tarika. Frontend backend se data maangta hai API se. Jaise waiter: tum order do, kitchen se khana laata hai.
qs.b: An API is a contract that lets two software systems communicate. For example, a web app's frontend calls backend APIs to fetch and save data, and the API defines the request and the response format.
qs.t: API = Waiter. Order (request) → Kitchen (server) → Khana (response).

qs.q: Why is API testing important?
qs.s: UI ke neeche ka business logic seedha test hota hai, jaldi aur stable, UI banne se pehle bhi. Security (auth, data leak) bhi yahin pakadte hain.
qs.b: API testing checks business logic directly beneath the UI, so it is faster and more stable than UI tests, can start before the UI is ready, and catches security and data issues early.
qs.t: Fast, Stable, Early, Secure.

qs.q: REST vs SOAP?
qs.s: REST: style, HTTP methods, zyadatar JSON, halka, aaj kal common. SOAP: protocol, sirf XML, strict rules (WSDL), banking/purane systems me.
qs.b: REST is an architectural style using HTTP methods and usually JSON; it is lightweight and most common today. SOAP is a strict protocol using XML with a formal contract, still seen in older enterprise systems.
qs.t: REST = halka JSON. SOAP = bhaari XML.

qs.q: What are the main HTTP methods?
qs.s: GET: data lao. POST: naya banao. PUT: poora replace/update. PATCH: thoda sa update. DELETE: hatao.
qs.b: GET reads data, POST creates a resource, PUT replaces a resource, PATCH partially updates it, and DELETE removes it.
qs.t: CRUD: Create=POST, Read=GET, Update=PUT/PATCH, Delete=DELETE.

qs.q: PUT vs PATCH?
qs.s: PUT poora object bhejta hai aur replace karta hai (jo field nahi bheja wo khali ho sakta hai). PATCH sirf badla hua field bhejta hai.
qs.b: PUT sends the full resource and replaces it, while PATCH sends only the fields to change.
qs.t: PUT = poora kapda badlo. PATCH = sirf button lagao.

qs.q: What do HTTP status code groups mean?
qs.s: 1xx info, 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client ki galti (request galat), 5xx server ki galti.
qs.b: 1xx is informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client errors where the request is wrong, and 5xx server errors.
qs.t: 2 = khush, 3 = idhar jao, 4 = tumhari galti, 5 = meri (server) galti.

qs.q: Explain 200, 201 and 204.
qs.s: 200 OK: request successful, data mila. 201 Created: naya resource bana (POST ke baad). 204 No Content: success par body khali (aksar DELETE).
qs.b: 200 means success with a response body, 201 means a resource was created, usually after POST, and 204 means success with no body, often after DELETE.
qs.t: 200 OK, 201 Bana, 204 Ho gaya par kuch bataunga nahi.

qs.s: 400 Bad Request: request galat format. 401 Unauthorized: login/token nahi ya galat. 403 Forbidden: login hai par permission nahi. 404 Not Found: resource nahi mila. 409 Conflict: duplicate/conflict. 422: format sahi par data validation fail.
qs.b: 400 is a malformed request, 401 means missing or invalid authentication, 403 means authenticated but not allowed, 404 means the resource does not exist, 409 is a conflict such as a duplicate, and 422 means the data failed validation.
