qs.t: 401 = Kaun ho tum? 403 = Pata hai kaun ho, par andar nahi aa sakte. 404 = Hai hi nahi.

qs.q: Explain 500, 502, 503 and 504.
qs.s: 500: server me error (code fata). 502 Bad Gateway: beech wala server ko upstream se galat jawab. 503: service available nahi (down/maintenance/overload). 504: upstream ne time pe jawab nahi diya (timeout).
qs.b: 500 is an internal server error, 502 means a gateway got an invalid response from an upstream server, 503 means the service is unavailable, and 504 means the upstream timed out.
qs.t: 500 fata, 502 galat jawab, 503 band, 504 der.

qs.q: What are the parts of an API request?
qs.s: URL (endpoint), method, headers (Content-Type, Authorization), query/path params, body (POST/PUT me JSON).
qs.b: A request has the endpoint URL, the HTTP method, headers such as Content-Type and Authorization, optional path and query parameters, and a body for methods like POST and PUT.
qs.t: U-M-H-P-B: URL, Method, Headers, Params, Body.

qs.q: Path parameter vs query parameter?
qs.s: Path param: URL ka hissa, ek specific resource (/order/PO-123). Query param: ? ke baad, filter/sort/page (?page=1&size=50). Merlin me: /purchasing/order/:poId path, live?page=1&size=50 query.
qs.b: A path parameter identifies a specific resource within the URL, like an order ID. Query parameters come after the question mark and filter, sort or paginate, like page and size.
qs.t: Path = kaun sa. Query = kaise chhaanto.

qs.q: What should you validate in an API response?
qs.s: Status code, response time, body ka structure (schema), field values aur data types, required fields, headers (Content-Type), error message sahi, data DB/UI se match.
qs.b: I validate the status code, response time, schema and data types, required fields and values, headers, meaningful error messages, and that the data matches the database or UI.
qs.t: Code, Time, Schema, Values, Headers, Error msg.

qs.q: How do you test an API in Postman?
qs.s: Workspace → collection → folders (jaise Purchase Orders) → request. Environment me base_url jaisi variables. Token Postman Vault me (secret). Tests tab me assertions likhte hain, collection runner se sab ek saath. Endpoints DevTools Network (Fetch/XHR) se nikale.
qs.b: At work I set up a Postman workspace with a collection organised by module, an environment holding the base URL, and the auth token stored securely in Postman Vault. I captured real endpoints from the browser's Network tab, then added test scripts for status, response time and response structure, and run them together with the collection runner.
qs.t: Collection → Environment → Vault token → Tests → Runner.

qs.q: What does a Postman test script look like?
qs.s: Tests tab me JavaScript: pm.test('Status is 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200)); response time ke liye pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(2000); JSON ke liye const d = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(d.purchaseOrders).to.be.an('array').
qs.b: Postman tests are JavaScript in the Tests tab using pm.test and pm.expect. I check the status code, that response time is below a threshold, and that fields in the parsed JSON have the right type and values, for example that the purchase orders field is an array.
qs.t: pm.test(naam, function). Andar pm.expect(...).

qs.q: How do you pass data between requests in Postman?
qs.s: Pehli request ke response se value nikal ke variable me save: pm.environment.set('poId', d.id). Agli request me {{poId}} use. Isse chaining kehte hain (create → get → delete).
qs.b: I extract a value from one response and store it with pm.environment.set, then reference it as a variable in the next request. That chains requests, for example create, then fetch, then delete the same record.
qs.t: set karo → {{use}} karo.

qs.q: What negative tests do you run on an API?
qs.s: Token nahi/galat token (401), dusre user ka resource (403/404), required field missing (400/422), galat data type, bahut lamba string, invalid ID, galat method (405), duplicate create (409).
qs.b: I test missing and invalid tokens, accessing another user's or organisation's data, missing required fields, wrong data types, oversized values, invalid IDs, the wrong HTTP method and duplicate creation, and expect the correct error code and message each time.
qs.t: Token, Dusre ka data, Field missing, Type galat, ID galat, Method galat.

qs.q: Authentication vs authorization?
qs.s: Authentication: tum kaun ho (login, token). Authorization: tumhe kya karne ki permission hai (role).
qs.b: Authentication verifies who you are, for example with a login or token. Authorization decides what you are allowed to do, based on roles and permissions.
qs.t: AuthN = Naam. AuthZ = Zaroorat ki permission.

qs.q: What is a bearer token?
qs.s: Login ke baad server token deta hai, har request ke header me Authorization: Bearer <token> bhejte hain. Token ko password jaisa secret rakho, GitHub ya chat me nahi.
qs.b: A bearer token is issued after login and sent in the Authorization header of each request. It must be treated like a password, so I keep it in Postman Vault rather than in shared collections.
qs.t: Bearer = jiske paas token, wahi andar. Chhupa ke rakho.

qs.q: What is IDOR and how do you test for it?
qs.s: Insecure Direct Object Reference: ID badal ke dusre user/org ka data mil jaaye. Test: apne token se dusre org ka ID maango, 403/404 aana chahiye. Merlin me maine ek org ke token se dusre org ka PO maanga, 404 aaya, matlab isolation sahi tha.
qs.b: IDOR is when changing an ID in a request exposes another user's data. I test it by requesting another organisation's record with my token and expecting 403 or 404. When I did this on our purchase order API, it correctly returned 404, confirming data isolation.
qs.t: ID badlo, dusre ka data dikhe = bug.

qs.q: What is idempotency?
qs.s: Same request baar baar bhejo to result ek hi rahe. GET, PUT, DELETE idempotent. POST nahi (har baar naya record). Isliye double click pe double order ek POST bug ho sakta hai.
qs.b: An idempotent request has the same effect no matter how many times it is sent. GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST usually is not, which is why double submissions can create duplicate records.
qs.t: Baar baar dabao, result ek. POST apvaad hai.

qs.q: What is JSON schema validation?
qs.s: Response ka structure check: kaun se fields hone chahiye, unka type (string, number, array). Field naam badla ya type badla to test fail, frontend tootne se pehle pakad lo.
qs.b: Schema validation checks that a response has the expected fields and data types, so a changed or missing field is caught before it breaks the frontend.
qs.t: Schema = response ka naksha.

qs.q: What is rate limiting?
qs.s: Ek time me kitni requests allowed. Zyada bhejo to 429 Too Many Requests. Test: limit tak chale, uske baad 429 aaye, kuch der baad phir chale.
qs.b: Rate limiting caps how many requests a client can make in a period. Beyond the limit the API should return 429 and recover after the window resets.
qs.t: 429 = thoda saans lo.

qs.q: API testing vs UI testing?
qs.s: API: tez, stable, logic directly, UI ke bina. UI: user ka asli experience, layout, flows. Dono chahiye. Bug pakadne ki kosish pehle API level pe, sasta.
qs.b: API tests are faster and more stable and test logic directly, while UI tests confirm the real user experience. A good strategy has more API tests and fewer, focused UI tests.
qs.t: API = andar ka engine. UI = gaadi chala ke dekho.

qs.q: How do you find which APIs a web page calls?
qs.s: DevTools → Network → Fetch/XHR filter → page pe action karo → request pe click: URL, method, headers, payload, response sab dikhta hai. Wahan se Postman me copy (Copy as cURL bhi).
qs.b: I open the Network tab, filter by Fetch/XHR, perform the action, and inspect the request's URL, method, headers, payload and response. Then I recreate it in Postman.
qs.t: F12 → Network → Fetch/XHR → action → click.

qs.q: What is Newman?
qs.s: Postman collection ko command line se chalane ka tool. CI (GitHub Actions) me automatically chala sakte ho. Mere demo repo me Newman CI step hai.
qs.b: Newman is the command-line runner for Postman collections, which lets the same API tests run automatically in a CI pipeline.
qs.t: Newman = Postman bina window ke.

qs.q: What is a pre-request script in Postman?
qs.s: Request bhejne se pehle chalne wala code: token banana, timestamp, random email generate karna, variables set karna.
qs.b: A pre-request script runs before the request is sent, for example to generate test data, set a timestamp or refresh a token.
qs.t: Pre = pehle. Tests = baad me.

qs.q: How do you test pagination in an API?
qs.s: page aur size badal ke: sahi count aaye, totalPages sahi, last page ke baad khali, size 0 ya negative pe error, records repeat na hon.
qs.b: I vary page and size, check counts and total pages, confirm the last page and beyond behave correctly, test invalid sizes, and ensure no records repeat across pages.
qs.t: Count, Total, Aakhri page, Galat size, Repeat nahi.

qs.q: Tell me about a data issue you found while testing an API.
qs.s: Merlin PO detail API me do calculation blocks the: 'calculation' me tax/shipping/discount zero aur 'pricingCalculation' me sahi values jo UI se match karti thi. Aur totalUnits 0 tha jabki items 85. Ye inconsistency report ki. Sirf wahi bolo jo detail me samjha sako.
qs.b: While writing Postman tests for our purchase order detail API, I noticed the response had two calculation blocks: one showed zero tax, shipping and discount, while the other held the correct values matching the UI. A unit total also showed zero while the item count was not. I reported it as a data consistency issue because any consumer reading the wrong block would show wrong totals.
qs.t: Do block, ek zero, ek sahi. Consumer galat padhe = galat total.

topics.intro: Tumhara Postman 6 mahine ka kaam yahan dikhega. Merlin me PO APIs ke liye Postman collection banaya hai, wahi example do.

topics.name: SQL & Database

qs.q: What is a database and an RDBMS?
qs.s: Database: data ko organised tarike se store karne ki jagah. RDBMS: tables (rows-columns) me data, tables aapas me keys se jude. Jaise MySQL, PostgreSQL. Merlin ka error dashboard PostgreSQL pe tha.
qs.b: A database stores data in an organised way. A relational database management system stores it in tables of rows and columns that are linked by keys, for example MySQL or PostgreSQL.
qs.t: Table = Excel sheet. RDBMS = sheets jo keys se judi.

qs.q: SQL vs NoSQL?
qs.s: SQL: fixed tables aur schema, relations, joins (MySQL, PostgreSQL). NoSQL: flexible documents/key-value, schema fixed nahi (MongoDB). MongoDB me data JSON jaise documents me.
qs.b: SQL databases use fixed schemas, tables and joins, like MySQL. NoSQL databases such as MongoDB store flexible, JSON-like documents without a fixed schema and scale horizontally more easily.
qs.t: SQL = register (fixed column). NoSQL = diary (jo marzi likho).

qs.q: Why does a QA engineer need SQL?
qs.s: UI pe jo dikha wo DB me sahi save hua ya nahi, test data banana/dhundhna, bug ka root cause (data galat hai ya code), report numbers verify karna.
qs.b: QA uses SQL to verify that what the UI shows is stored correctly, to find or prepare test data, to check report numbers, and to tell whether a bug is caused by data or code.
qs.t: UI vs DB match, Test data, Root cause.

qs.q: Primary key vs foreign key?
qs.s: Primary key: har row ki unique pehchaan, null nahi (employees.id). Foreign key: dusri table ki primary key ka reference (employees.dept_id → departments.id), relation banata hai.
qs.b: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be null. A foreign key is a column that references another table's primary key, creating a relationship between the tables.
qs.t: Primary = apna Aadhaar. Foreign = papa ka Aadhaar number apne form me.

qs.q: Primary key vs unique key?
qs.s: Dono duplicate allow nahi karte. Primary: table me ek hi, null nahi. Unique: kai ho sakte, ek null allow (DB pe depend).
qs.b: Both prevent duplicates, but a table has only one primary key and it cannot be null, while it can have several unique keys that may allow nulls.
qs.t: Primary = ek raja. Unique = kai sipahi.

qs.q: Write a query to get all orders with status 'FAILED'.
qs.s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'FAILED'; Text single quotes me.
qs.b: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'FAILED';
qs.t: SELECT kya FROM kahan WHERE shart.

qs.q: How do you sort results and limit them?
qs.s: ORDER BY column ASC/DESC, LIMIT n. Latest 10 orders: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;
qs.b: Use ORDER BY with ASC or DESC and LIMIT. For the latest ten orders: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;
qs.t: DESC = bada/naya pehle.

qs.q: What are aggregate functions?
qs.s: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX: bahut rows se ek value. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders; SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE status='PAID';
qs.b: Aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX return one value from many rows, for example the total of paid order amounts.
qs.t: C-S-A-M-M: Count, Sum, Avg, Min, Max.

qs.q: Write a query to count orders by status.
qs.s: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY status; GROUP BY ek jaisi values ko group karta hai.
qs.b: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY status;
qs.t: Jo column SELECT me (bina count), wahi GROUP BY me.

qs.q: WHERE vs HAVING?
qs.s: WHERE: group banne se pehle rows filter. HAVING: GROUP BY ke baad groups filter (aggregate pe). Jaise jin customers ke 5 se zyada orders: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
qs.b: WHERE filters rows before grouping, and HAVING filters groups after aggregation. For customers with more than five orders: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
qs.t: WHERE = pehle (rows). HAVING = baad me (groups).

qs.q: Write a query to find duplicate emails in a users table.
qs.s: SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; Bahut common interview query, aur QA me duplicate data pakadne ke kaam ki.
qs.b: SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
qs.t: Duplicate = GROUP BY + HAVING COUNT > 1.

qs.q: Write a query for the second highest salary.
qs.s: Tarika 1: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees); Tarika 2: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
qs.b: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees); or with DISTINCT, ORDER BY salary DESC, LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1.
qs.t: Sabse bade se chhota sabse bada. Ya OFFSET 1.

qs.q: What are the types of JOIN?
qs.s: INNER JOIN: dono tables me match wali rows. LEFT JOIN: left ki saari + right ka match (na mile to NULL). RIGHT JOIN: ulta. FULL JOIN: dono ki saari. SELF JOIN: table apne aap se.
qs.b: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows, LEFT JOIN returns all left rows plus matches, RIGHT JOIN the reverse, FULL JOIN all rows from both, and a self join joins a table to itself.
qs.t: Inner = beech ka common. Left = left poora + common.

qs.q: Write a query to show employee names with their department names.
qs.s: SELECT e.name, d.name AS dept FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id; e aur d alias hain.
qs.b: SELECT e.name, d.name AS dept FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
qs.t: JOIN ... ON key = key.

qs.q: Write a query to find employees without a department.
qs.s: LEFT JOIN + IS NULL: SELECT e.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE d.id IS NULL; Ye orphan records pakadne ka QA trick hai.
qs.b: SELECT e.name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE d.id IS NULL;
qs.t: Anaath dhundho = LEFT JOIN + IS NULL.

qs.q: DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP?
qs.s: DELETE: kuch ya saari rows, WHERE ke saath, rollback ho sakta (transaction me). TRUNCATE: saari rows tezi se, structure bacha. DROP: poori table hi khatam (structure bhi). Prod pe kabhi nahi!
qs.b: DELETE removes selected rows and can use WHERE and be rolled back in a transaction. TRUNCATE quickly removes all rows but keeps the table. DROP removes the table entirely.
qs.t: DELETE = kuch kapde. TRUNCATE = almaari khali. DROP = almaari hi gayab.

qs.q: What is DISTINCT?
qs.s: Duplicate values hata ke unique dikhata hai. SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders;
qs.b: DISTINCT returns only unique values, for example SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders.
qs.t: DISTINCT = sirf ek ek.

qs.q: How do LIKE and wildcards work?
qs.s: % = kuch bhi (0 ya zyada characters), _ = exactly ek character. Naam 'Ra' se shuru: WHERE name LIKE 'Ra%'. Kahin bhi 'test': LIKE '%test%'.
qs.b: LIKE matches patterns: percent matches any number of characters and underscore matches exactly one. For names starting with Ra: WHERE name LIKE 'Ra%'.
qs.t: % = kuch bhi. _ = ek.

qs.q: How do you handle NULL in SQL?
qs.s: NULL = value hi nahi. = NULL kaam nahi karta, IS NULL / IS NOT NULL use karo. COALESCE(col, 0) se default.
qs.b: NULL means no value, so you compare with IS NULL or IS NOT NULL, not equals. COALESCE replaces NULL with a default.
qs.t: NULL ko = se mat pakdo, IS se pakdo.

qs.q: What is a subquery?
qs.s: Query ke andar query. Average se zyada salary: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
qs.b: A subquery is a query inside another query, for example finding employees whose salary is above the average.
qs.t: Andar wali pehle chalti hai.

qs.q: What is an index?
qs.s: Kitab ka index jaisa: search tez. Par insert/update thoda slow aur jagah leta hai. Slow query ka ek common fix.
qs.b: An index is a data structure that speeds up reads on a column, like a book index, at the cost of extra storage and slightly slower writes.
qs.t: Index = kitab ka index page.

qs.q: UNION vs UNION ALL?
qs.s: Dono do queries ka result jodte hain. UNION duplicate hatata hai (slow). UNION ALL sab rakhta hai (fast).
qs.b: Both combine results of two queries; UNION removes duplicates and UNION ALL keeps them, so it is faster.
qs.t: ALL = sab rakh lo.

qs.q: What are ACID properties?
qs.s: Transaction ke rules: Atomicity (sab ya kuch nahi), Consistency (rules toote nahi), Isolation (ek transaction dusre ko disturb na kare), Durability (save hua to save rahe). Payment me zaroori.
qs.b: ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability: a transaction completes fully or not at all, keeps data valid, does not interfere with others, and persists once committed.
qs.t: A-C-I-D: Sab ya kuch nahi, Rules, Akela, Pakka.

qs.q: How have you used database checks in testing?
qs.s: Seedha DB access nahi to sach bolo. Merlin me data verify ke liye export (Chart of Accounts xlsx) leke script se compare kiya aur duplicates pakde. Error dashboard ka data PostgreSQL me tha. SQL abhi seekh raha hun: basic queries, joins, group by.
qs.b: In my role I mostly verify data through the application and its exports. For example, I exported a customer's chart of accounts and compared it with a script, which revealed duplicated accounts. I am strengthening my SQL with joins, grouping and duplicate-detection queries, which are the checks I use most.
qs.t: Sach bolo: kya kiya + kya seekh rahe ho.

qs.q: What is normalization?
qs.s: Data ko chhoti related tables me baantna taaki duplicate data na ho aur update me galti na ho. 1NF, 2NF, 3NF levels. Interview me ek line kaafi.
qs.b: Normalization organises data into related tables to reduce duplication and update anomalies, typically up to third normal form.
qs.t: Ek baat ek jagah.

qs.q: Basic MongoDB query?
qs.s: db.orders.find({status: 'FAILED'}) = SQL ka WHERE. db.orders.countDocuments({}) = COUNT. find({}, {name:1}) = sirf name column.
qs.b: In MongoDB, db.orders.find with a filter document like status FAILED is the equivalent of a WHERE clause, and countDocuments counts matching documents.
qs.t: find({shart}) = SELECT WHERE.

topics.intro: QA interview me SQL ke 3-4 sawaal aate hi hain, aksar ek query likhwaate hain. Tables ke example: employees(id, name, dept_id, salary), departments(id, name), orders(id, customer_id, status, amount, created_at).

topics.name: Automation (Playwright + pytest)

qs.q: What is test automation?
qs.s: Test cases ko code/tool se chalana, haath se nahi. Repeat hone wale tests (regression) jaldi aur baar baar chal sakte hain.
qs.b: Test automation uses scripts and tools to execute tests and compare results automatically, which makes repetitive checks like regression fast and repeatable.
qs.t: Jo baar baar karna hai, machine ko do.

qs.q: What should you automate and what not?
qs.s: Automate: regression, smoke, stable flows, data-driven tests, API tests. Mat karo: one-time tests, bahut badalti UI, exploratory, usability, visual judgement.
qs.b: I automate stable, repetitive and high-value checks such as smoke, regression, data-driven and API tests. I keep exploratory, usability and one-off tests manual, and avoid automating features whose UI is still changing.
qs.t: Stable + Repeat + Important = automate. Badalta + Ek baar + Feel = manual.

qs.q: What is the test automation pyramid?
qs.s: Neeche bahut saare unit tests (tez, saste), beech me API/integration tests, upar thode UI/E2E tests (slow, tootne wale).
qs.b: The test pyramid recommends many fast unit tests at the base, a solid layer of API and integration tests, and a small number of UI end-to-end tests at the top because they are slower and more brittle.
qs.t: Neeche zyada (unit), upar kam (UI).

qs.q: Why Playwright?
qs.s: Microsoft ka tool. Chromium, Firefox, WebKit. Auto-wait (element ready hone tak khud rukta), fast, Python support, trace viewer, API testing bhi, parallel run, codegen.
qs.b: Playwright supports Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, waits automatically for elements to be ready, which reduces flakiness, has a Python API, built-in tracing for debugging, API testing support and parallel execution.
qs.t: Auto-wait, Teen browser, Trace, API, Fast.

qs.q: Playwright vs Selenium?
qs.s: Selenium purana, bahut languages, WebDriver se, waits khud likhne padte. Playwright naya, auto-wait, fast, trace viewer, network intercept built-in. Selenium ka community bada.
qs.b: Selenium is older and very widely supported but relies on WebDriver and explicit waits. Playwright is newer, faster, auto-waits, and has built-in tracing and network interception. Selenium still has a larger ecosystem.
qs.t: Selenium = purana pakka. Playwright = naya tez, auto-wait.

qs.q: What locators does Playwright offer, and which do you prefer?
qs.s: get_by_role (button, link naam se), get_by_text, get_by_label, get_by_placeholder, get_by_test_id, aur CSS/XPath. Best: role/label/test-id, kyunki user jaisa aur stable. XPath last option.
qs.b: Playwright offers user-facing locators like get_by_role, get_by_label, get_by_text and get_by_placeholder, test IDs, and CSS or XPath. I prefer role, label or test ID locators because they are stable and reflect how users see the page, and use CSS or XPath only as a fallback.
qs.t: Role > Label > Test ID > CSS > XPath.

qs.q: What is auto-waiting in Playwright?
qs.s: Click/fill se pehle Playwright khud check karta hai: element dikh raha, enabled, stable. Isliye time.sleep nahi likhna padta. Assertions bhi retry karte hain (expect).
qs.b: Before actions like click or fill, Playwright waits until the element is visible, enabled and stable, and web-first assertions retry until they pass or time out, so hard sleeps are rarely needed.
qs.t: sleep mat likho, Playwright khud rukta hai.

qs.q: How do you write an assertion in Playwright Python?
qs.s: from playwright.sync_api import expect; expect(page.get_by_text('Products')).to_be_visible(); expect(page).to_have_title('Swag Labs'); expect(locator).to_have_text('...').
qs.b: I use expect from playwright.sync_api, for example expect(page).to_have_title, expect(locator).to_be_visible or to_have_text. These assertions retry automatically.
qs.t: expect(kya).to_have_kuch().

qs.q: Browser vs context vs page?
qs.s: Browser: poora browser. Context: ek alag incognito jaisa session (alag cookies). Page: ek tab. Do users ek saath test karne ho to do contexts.
qs.b: A browser is the browser instance, a context is an isolated session with its own cookies like an incognito window, and a page is a single tab. Separate contexts let me test multiple users at once.
qs.t: Browser = building. Context = flat. Page = kamra.

qs.q: Headless vs headed?
qs.s: Headless: browser window dikhti nahi, fast, CI me. Headed: window dikhti, debug ke liye. pytest --headed.
qs.b: Headless runs without a visible window and is used in CI; headed shows the browser, which is useful for debugging.
qs.t: Headless = bina sar (dikhta nahi).

qs.q: What are pytest basics?
qs.s: File test_*.py, function test_ se shuru, assert se check. Command: pytest. -v detail, -k naam se filter, -m marker se.
qs.b: pytest discovers files and functions starting with test_, uses plain assert statements, and runs from the command line with options like -v for verbose, -k to filter by name and -m to select markers.
qs.t: test_ naam + assert + pytest command.

qs.q: What is a fixture in pytest?
qs.s: Setup/teardown ka reusable code: jaise login karke page dena, test data, API client. Test function ke argument me naam likho, pytest khud de deta hai. yield ke baad cleanup.
qs.b: A fixture provides reusable setup and teardown, such as a logged-in page or an API client. A test requests it by name as an argument, and code after yield runs as cleanup.
qs.t: Fixture = test ke liye pehle se taiyar thaali.

qs.q: What is conftest.py?
qs.s: Shared fixtures ki file. Isme likha fixture saare tests use kar sakte bina import. Mere repo me users aur logged_in_page fixtures yahan hain.
qs.b: conftest.py holds shared fixtures and hooks that every test in that directory can use without importing them.
qs.t: conftest = sabka common kitchen.

qs.q: What does @pytest.mark.parametrize do?
qs.s: Ek test ko alag alag data se kai baar chalana. Jaise invalid logins: locked user, galat password, khali username, ek hi test function me.
qs.b: parametrize runs the same test with multiple data sets, for example several invalid login combinations, without duplicating code.
qs.t: Ek test, kai data.

qs.q: What are pytest markers?
qs.s: Tests pe label: @pytest.mark.smoke, @pytest.mark.api. Phir pytest -m smoke se sirf wahi chalao. pytest.ini me register karo.
qs.b: Markers label tests, such as smoke or api, so I can run a subset with pytest -m. They are registered in the pytest configuration.
qs.t: Marker = test pe sticker.

qs.q: What is the Page Object Model?
qs.s: Har page ki ek class: us page ke locators aur actions (login(), add_to_cart()). Tests sirf in methods ko call karte. UI badla to sirf page class badlo, tests nahi. Maintenance aasaan.
qs.b: The Page Object Model puts each page's locators and actions in its own class, and tests call those methods. When the UI changes, I update one page class instead of many tests, which improves readability and maintenance.
qs.t: Pages = kaise click karna. Tests = kya check karna.

qs.q: What is a flaky test and how do you fix it?
qs.s: Kabhi pass kabhi fail bina code badle. Reasons: timing, test data dependency, network, tests ek dusre pe depend. Fix: hard sleep hatao, sahi wait/expect, independent data, stable locators, retry sirf last option. Mere repo me ek network test flaky tha, wait_for_load_state('networkidle') se fix.
qs.b: A flaky test passes and fails without code changes, usually due to timing, shared data, network or test order. I remove hard sleeps, use proper waits and assertions, isolate test data, improve locators, and only use retries as a last resort.
qs.t: Flaky = timing, data, order, network. Fix = wait sahi, data alag.

qs.q: How do you debug a failing Playwright test?
qs.s: Error message aur screenshot dekho, headed mode me chalao, page.pause(), trace viewer (har step ka DOM aur network), console logs. Locator galat hai ya app me bug, ye decide karo.
qs.b: I read the error and screenshot, rerun headed or with page.pause, and open the trace viewer to see each step's DOM, network and console. Then I decide whether it is a test issue or a real defect.
qs.t: Error → Screenshot → Headed → Trace.

qs.q: How do you handle alerts, dialogs and popups?
qs.s: Browser dialog: page.on('dialog', lambda d: d.accept()). Naya tab/popup: with page.expect_popup() as p: click; new = p.value.
qs.b: For browser dialogs I register a handler with page.on('dialog') to accept or dismiss. For new tabs I wrap the click in page.expect_popup and work with the returned page.
qs.t: Dialog = on('dialog'). Naya tab = expect_popup.

qs.q: How do you handle iframes?
qs.s: page.frame_locator('#frame-id').get_by_role('button', name='Pay').click(). Pehle frame pakdo, phir andar ka element.
qs.b: I use page.frame_locator to target the iframe and then locate elements inside it.
qs.t: Pehle frame, phir andar.

qs.q: How do you upload a file in Playwright?
qs.s: page.set_input_files('input[type=file]', 'path/file.pdf').
qs.b: I use set_input_files on the file input with the path to the file.
qs.t: set_input_files.

qs.q: How can you do API testing in a Python framework?
qs.s: requests library ya Playwright ka request context. Mere repo me api/client.py requests.Session wrapper hai, JSONPlaceholder pe GET/POST/PUT/DELETE aur JSON schema check, marker api.
qs.b: I use the requests library or Playwright's request context. In my demo framework there is an API client wrapper and tests for create, read, update and delete on a public test API, including JSON schema validation.
qs.t: requests.Session + assert status + schema.

qs.q: How do you run tests in CI?
qs.s: GitHub Actions: push pe workflow chalta, Python install, dependencies, playwright install, pytest, HTML report artifact. Mere public repo me CI green hai, API, UI aur Newman alag steps.
qs.b: I use GitHub Actions: on each push the workflow installs Python and dependencies, installs browsers, runs pytest and publishes an HTML report. My public demo repository runs UI tests, API tests and a Postman collection through Newman as separate steps.
qs.t: Push → Install → Run → Report.

qs.q: How do you do data-driven testing?
qs.s: Test data alag file (JSON/CSV) me, parametrize ya fixture se load. Data badlo, code nahi.
qs.b: I keep test data in JSON or CSV files and feed it to tests through parametrize or fixtures, so new cases need data changes rather than code changes.
qs.t: Data file me, code me nahi.

qs.q: How do you avoid logging in before every test?
qs.s: Ek baar login karke storage state (cookies) save: context.storage_state(path='state.json'), phir naye context me storage_state='state.json'. Ya API se login.
qs.b: I log in once, save the storage state to a file, and create new contexts from it, or log in via the API, so tests start already authenticated.
qs.t: Ek baar login, state save.

qs.q: What is your automation framework structure?
qs.s: Sach bolo: Swag Labs (saucedemo) pe public demo. pages/ (page objects), tests/ (UI + api), data/ (JSON), utils/ (config), conftest.py (fixtures), docs/ (test plan, test cases, defect + RCA templates), GitHub Actions CI. AI-assisted banaya, isliye har file khud samjho pehle.
qs.b: My public demo framework uses Playwright with pytest against a demo e-commerce site. It has page objects, UI and API test folders, JSON test data, a config module, shared fixtures in conftest, documentation for the test plan, test cases and defect templates, and a GitHub Actions pipeline with an HTML report. I built it with AI assistance and reviewed each part.
qs.t: Pages, Tests, Data, Utils, Conftest, Docs, CI. (Har folder ka kaam 1 line me bolna aana chahiye.)

qs.q: How do you take screenshots and record traces?
qs.s: page.screenshot(path='x.png'). pytest-playwright options: --screenshot only-on-failure, --tracing retain-on-failure, --video. Trace: playwright show-trace trace.zip.
qs.b: I capture screenshots with page.screenshot, and with pytest-playwright I enable screenshots, video and tracing on failure, then open traces with playwright show-trace.
qs.t: Fail pe screenshot + trace.

qs.q: How do you intercept or mock network calls?
qs.s: page.route('**/*.png', lambda r: r.abort()) images block. Ya route.fulfill se fake response. Backend ke bina UI ke edge cases test.
qs.b: Using page.route, I can block requests or return mocked responses with route.fulfill, which helps test error states and edge cases without depending on the backend.
qs.t: route = beech me khade ho ke request roko ya badlo.

qs.q: Python: list vs tuple vs dict vs set?
qs.s: List [ ]: badal sakte, order. Tuple ( ): badal nahi sakte. Dict { key: value }: key se value. Set { }: unique values, order nahi.
qs.b: A list is ordered and mutable, a tuple is ordered and immutable, a dictionary maps keys to values, and a set holds unique unordered values.
qs.t: List = shopping list. Tuple = pathar pe likha. Dict = dictionary. Set = unique log.

qs.q: How do you handle exceptions in Python?
qs.s: try: risky code; except SpecificError as e: handle; finally: hamesha chale (cleanup). Bina wajah saari exceptions pakad ke chhupana galat.
qs.b: I wrap risky code in try, catch specific exceptions in except, and use finally for cleanup. I avoid catching everything silently because it hides real failures.
qs.t: try, except (specific), finally (cleanup).

qs.q: What is a virtual environment and requirements.txt?
qs.s: venv: project ki alag Python duniya, packages dusre project se mix na hon. requirements.txt: kaun se packages chahiye, pip install -r requirements.txt.
qs.b: A virtual environment isolates a project's packages, and requirements.txt lists the dependencies so anyone can install them with pip install -r.
qs.t: venv = alag kamra. requirements = saamaan ki list.

qs.q: How do you use AI tools in testing?
qs.s: Resume rule: AI-assisted bolo, expertise nahi. Claude se test case draft, failure analysis, code fix ka draft, par har output khud verify, aur code PR developer review karta hai. 'AI drafts, engineer verifies.'
qs.b: I use AI assistants to draft test cases, analyse failures and prototype small fixes, but I verify every output myself, and any code change goes through developer review. My rule is that AI drafts and the engineer verifies.
qs.t: AI drafts, engineer verifies.

topics.intro: SDET ki taraf jaane ke liye sabse important. Dhyaan: apne demo repo (playwright-pytest-framework) ke baare me sirf utna bolo jitna tum code khol ke samjha sako. Walkthrough abhi baaki hai, interview se pehle har file samajh lo.

topics.name: Web & Mobile Basics

qs.q: What happens when you type a URL in the browser?
qs.s: 1 DNS se domain ka IP address. 2 Server se connection (HTTPS me TLS handshake). 3 Browser HTTP request bhejta. 4 Server response (HTML). 5 Browser HTML, CSS, JS load karke page banata (render). 6 JS aur API calls se data aata.
qs.b: The browser resolves the domain to an IP address through DNS, opens a connection with a TLS handshake for HTTPS, sends an HTTP request, receives HTML, then loads CSS, JavaScript and API data and renders the page.
qs.t: DNS → Connect → Request → Response → Render.

qs.q: HTTP vs HTTPS?
qs.s: HTTPS = HTTP + encryption (TLS/SSL). Data beech me koi padh nahi sakta. Login/payment page hamesha HTTPS. Browser me lock icon.
qs.b: HTTPS is HTTP encrypted with TLS, so data cannot be read or altered in transit. Any login or payment page must use HTTPS.
qs.t: S = Secure (taala).

qs.q: Cookies vs session storage vs local storage?
qs.s: Cookie: chhota data, har request ke saath server ko jaata (login session). Local storage: browser me rehta, band karne pe bhi. Session storage: tab band to khatam. DevTools → Application tab me dikhte.
qs.b: Cookies are small values sent with every request, often for sessions. Local storage persists in the browser until cleared, and session storage lasts only for the tab. All are visible in the DevTools Application tab.
qs.t: Cookie = server tak jaata. Local = rehta. Session = tab tak.

qs.q: What is caching and why does a hard refresh matter?
qs.s: Browser purani files save karke rakhta hai taaki page jaldi khule. Naya deploy hua par purana dikh raha = cache. Hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) ya incognito se check karo, bug report me batao ki cache clear kiya.
qs.b: Caching stores files locally to load pages faster. After a deployment, stale cache can show old behaviour, so I verify with a hard refresh or a private window before reporting.
qs.t: Naya deploy, purana dikhe = Ctrl+Shift+R.

qs.q: Frontend vs backend?
qs.s: Frontend: jo user dekhta (HTML, CSS, JS, React). Backend: server, logic, database, APIs. Bug kahan hai: UI me galat dikha par API sahi = frontend; API hi galat = backend.
qs.b: The frontend is what users see and interact with; the backend holds the business logic, APIs and database. Checking the API response tells me whether a bug is in the frontend or backend.
qs.t: API sahi + UI galat = frontend. API galat = backend.

qs.q: What is client-server architecture?
qs.s: Client (browser/app) request bhejta, server process karke response deta. Ek server bahut clients.
qs.b: In client-server architecture, clients such as browsers or apps send requests and a central server processes them and returns responses.
qs.t: Client maange, server de.

qs.q: How do you use browser DevTools as a tester?
qs.s: Elements (HTML/CSS dekho), Console (JS errors), Network (API calls, status, time), Application (cookies, storage), device toolbar (screen size), throttling (slow net).
qs.b: I use Elements to inspect the page, Console for errors, Network for API calls, status codes and timings, Application for cookies and storage, and the device toolbar and throttling for responsive and slow-network checks.
qs.t: E-C-N-A: Elements, Console, Network, Application.

qs.q: What is responsive design testing?
qs.s: Alag screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop) pe layout sahi: text cut na ho, horizontal scroll na aaye, buttons tap karne layak, menu hamburger ban jaye.
qs.b: Responsive testing checks that the layout adapts correctly to phone, tablet and desktop widths without cut text, horizontal scrolling or unusable controls.
qs.t: Chhoti screen pe kuch kate nahi, kuch bahar na bhaage.

qs.q: Native vs hybrid vs web app?
qs.s: Native: platform ki language me (Android Kotlin, iOS Swift), fast. Hybrid: web tech andar app shell me (React Native/Flutter cross-platform bhi). Web app: browser me chalti.
qs.b: Native apps are built for one platform and are fastest. Hybrid or cross-platform apps share code across platforms. Web apps run in the browser.
qs.t: Native = desi. Hybrid = mix. Web = browser me.

qs.q: Android vs iOS testing differences?
qs.s: Android: bahut devices aur versions (fragmentation), back button, APK install. iOS: kam devices, strict guidelines, TestFlight se beta, swipe back gesture. Permissions aur notifications alag behave.
qs.b: Android has many devices and OS versions, a system back button and side-loaded APKs. iOS has fewer devices, stricter guidelines, TestFlight for betas and gesture-based navigation. Permissions and notifications behave differently on each.
qs.t: Android = bheed + back button. iOS = kam device + TestFlight.

qs.q: Emulator vs simulator vs real device?
qs.s: Emulator: hardware + OS ki nakal (Android emulator). Simulator: sirf software behaviour (iOS simulator). Real device: asli battery, network, camera, performance. Final testing real device pe.
qs.b: An emulator mimics hardware and software, a simulator mimics software behaviour only, and a real device shows true performance, sensors, battery and network behaviour, so final verification happens on real devices.
qs.t: Nakal kitni bhi achhi, asli asli hai.

qs.q: How do you test mobile app interruptions?
qs.s: Flow ke beech: call aaye, SMS, alarm, notification, low battery popup, app background me daal ke wapas, lock-unlock. Data bachna chahiye, crash nahi.
qs.b: During a flow I trigger calls, messages, alarms, notifications and low-battery prompts, background and resume the app, and lock the screen, checking that it resumes correctly without losing data or crashing.
qs.t: Beech me chhedo, wapas aao, sab waise ka waisa.

qs.q: What is a deep link?
qs.s: Link jo app ke andar specific screen kholta (email me 'View order' → app me us order ki screen). Test: app installed/not installed, logged in/out.
qs.b: A deep link opens a specific screen inside an app. I test it with the app installed and not installed, and while logged in and logged out.
qs.t: Link → seedha andar wala kamra.

qs.q: How do you test push notifications?
qs.s: Aaye, sahi text, tap pe sahi screen, app band/background/foreground teeno me, permission deny pe na aaye, time zone, duplicate na aaye.
qs.b: I check that notifications arrive with correct content, open the right screen when tapped in killed, background and foreground states, respect permission settings, and are not duplicated.
qs.t: Aaye, Sahi likha, Tap sahi, 3 state, Permission.

qs.q: What is accessibility testing?
qs.s: Disabled users bhi use kar sakein: screen reader (TalkBack), image alt text, color contrast, keyboard se chale, font bada karne pe layout na toote. Standard: WCAG.
qs.b: Accessibility testing checks that people with disabilities can use the product: screen reader support, alt text, colour contrast, keyboard navigation and scalable text, usually against WCAG guidelines.
qs.t: Aankh, Kaan, Haath: screen reader, contrast, keyboard.

qs.q: What is an API error vs a frontend error in a bug report?
qs.s: Network tab me 4xx/5xx dikha to API error, report me endpoint aur status likho. Console me JS error, network sab 200 = frontend error. Dev ka time bachta hai.
qs.b: If the Network tab shows a 4xx or 5xx response, I include the endpoint and status in the report as a likely backend issue. If all calls succeed but the Console shows a JavaScript error, it is likely a frontend issue.
qs.t: Network laal = backend. Console laal = frontend.

qs.q: How do you test on staging vs production safely?
qs.s: Staging pe sab try karo (create, delete). Production pe read-only: dekho, compare karo, kuch create/edit/delete nahi jab tak permission na ho. Merlin me main yahi karta hun.
qs.b: I do all interactive testing on staging, and on production I only do read-only verification such as checking data and comparing with staging, without creating or changing records unless explicitly approved.
qs.t: Staging = khelo. Prod = sirf dekho.

qs.q: What are web session timeouts and how do you test them?
qs.s: Kuch der kuch na karo to logout. Test: time ke baad action pe login page aaye, unsaved data ka kya, multiple tabs me sync.
qs.b: A session timeout logs users out after inactivity. I verify that actions after the timeout redirect to login, check what happens to unsaved data, and check behaviour across tabs.
qs.t: Ruko → action → login page.

topics.intro: Web aur app kaise kaam karte hain, ye samajh ho to bug ka reason bhi bata paoge. Interview me ye bonus points dete hain.

topics.name: Agile, Jira & Defects

qs.q: What is Scrum? Name the roles.
qs.s: Agile ka framework, kaam sprints me (1-4 hafte). Roles: Product Owner (kya banana, backlog priority), Scrum Master (process, rukawat hatana), Development Team (dev + QA).
qs.b: Scrum is an Agile framework that delivers work in short sprints. Its roles are the Product Owner, who owns and prioritises the backlog, the Scrum Master, who facilitates and removes blockers, and the development team, which includes QA.
qs.t: PO = kya. SM = kaise smooth. Team = karo.

qs.q: What are the Scrum ceremonies?
qs.s: Sprint planning (kya karenge), Daily standup (kal kya, aaj kya, rukawat), Sprint review (demo), Retrospective (kya achha, kya sudhaarna).
qs.b: Sprint planning, the daily stand-up, the sprint review where work is demonstrated, and the retrospective where the team discusses what to improve.
qs.t: Plan, Daily, Review, Retro.

qs.q: What is a user story and acceptance criteria?
qs.s: Story: 'As a [user], I want [kaam], so that [fayda]'. Acceptance criteria: kab story done maanenge, testable shartein. Aksar Given-When-Then me.
qs.b: A user story describes a need from the user's view: as a user, I want something, so that I get a benefit. Acceptance criteria are the testable conditions that define when it is done, often written as Given, When, Then.
qs.t: As a / I want / So that. AC = Given / When / Then.

qs.q: What is BDD and Given-When-Then?
qs.s: Behaviour Driven Development: requirement simple English me jo test bhi ban jaye. Given (shuru ki halat), When (action), Then (result). Tools: Cucumber, pytest-bdd.
qs.b: Behaviour-driven development writes requirements as examples in plain language using Given, When, Then, so business, developers and QA share one definition that can also be automated with tools like Cucumber or pytest-bdd.
qs.t: Given halat, When kaam, Then nateeja.

qs.q: What is the Definition of Done?
qs.s: Team ki checklist: code review, tests pass, QA sign-off, docs, deploy staging. Iske bina story done nahi.
qs.b: The Definition of Done is the team's shared checklist, such as code reviewed, tests passing and QA sign-off, that every story must meet before it counts as done.
qs.t: DoD = 'ho gaya' ka sabut.

qs.q: Scrum vs Kanban?
qs.s: Scrum: fixed sprints, roles, ceremonies. Kanban: lagataar flow, board (To do, In progress, Done), WIP limit, sprint nahi.
qs.b: Scrum works in fixed sprints with defined roles and ceremonies. Kanban is a continuous flow on a board with work-in-progress limits and no fixed iterations.
qs.t: Scrum = sprint race. Kanban = conveyor belt.

qs.q: What are story points?
qs.s: Kaam ki mushkil/size ka andaza (ghante nahi). Fibonacci 1,2,3,5,8. Team planning poker se decide.
qs.b: Story points estimate relative effort and complexity rather than hours, often using a Fibonacci scale agreed by the team.
qs.t: Points = mushkil kitna, ghante nahi.

qs.q: What does a good Jira or Linear bug ticket contain?
qs.s: Clear title, environment (staging/prod, browser, build), steps, expected, actual, severity/priority, screenshot/video, logs/API response, affected customer agar hai, related ticket link.
qs.b: A good ticket has a clear title, environment and build, steps, expected and actual results, severity and priority, screenshots or video, logs or API responses, the affected customer if any, and links to related tickets.
qs.t: Bug report wala hi formula + customer + link.

qs.q: What is defect triage?
qs.s: Meeting/process jisme naye bugs dekhte: valid hai?, severity/priority, kisko assign, kab fix. Merlin me on-call me P0/P1 triage karta hun DevRev, PostHog, Linear se.
qs.b: Defect triage reviews new bugs to confirm validity, set severity and priority, assign an owner and decide timing. In my role I triage production issues from customer conversations and monitoring and create prioritised tickets for developers.
qs.t: Valid? Kitna bada? Kiska? Kab?

qs.q: What is RCA?
qs.s: Root Cause Analysis: bug kyun aaya, asli wajah (sirf symptom nahi). 5 Whys technique. Phir fix + prevention (naya test case, process change).
qs.b: Root cause analysis finds the underlying reason a defect occurred, not just its symptom, often with the five whys, and leads to both a fix and a preventive action such as a new test.
qs.t: 5 baar 'kyun?'.

qs.q: What is shift-left testing?
qs.s: Testing jaldi shuru: requirement review me QA, design ke time sawaal, dev ke saath unit/API tests. Bug jaldi = sasta.
qs.b: Shift-left means involving testing earlier, from requirement and design reviews to early API tests, so defects are found when they are cheapest to fix.
qs.t: Testing ko left (shuru) me khiskao.

qs.q: What does QA sign-off mean?
qs.s: QA bolta hai feature release ke liye ready: planned tests chale, critical bugs zero, known issues documented. Merlin me prod re-test ke baad QA signoff hota hai.
qs.b: QA sign-off is a formal confirmation that testing is complete for a release: planned tests were executed, no critical defects are open, and remaining known issues are documented.
qs.t: Sign-off = QA ka thappa, sabut ke saath.

qs.q: How do you estimate testing effort?
qs.s: Feature ka size aur risk, kitne test cases, environment setup, data, regression area, bug fix retest ka buffer. Past similar kaam se compare.
qs.b: I estimate from the feature's scope and risk, the number of test cases, setup and data needs, the regression area and a buffer for retesting fixes, using similar past work as a reference.
qs.t: Size + Cases + Setup + Regression + Buffer.

qs.q: What do you do when a developer says 'it's not a bug'?
qs.s: Bahas nahi. Requirement/AC dikhao, steps aur evidence. Agar requirement me clear nahi to PO/manager se decision. Final decision accept.
qs.b: I refer to the requirement or acceptance criteria and share clear evidence. If the expectation is unclear, I ask the product owner to decide, and I accept the outcome while documenting it.
qs.t: Requirement + Evidence + PO decide.

qs.q: What is a hotfix and how do you test it?
qs.s: Production ka urgent fix, normal release ke bahar. Test: bug fix verify + us area ka focused regression + smoke. Prod pe deploy ke baad read-only verify.
qs.b: A hotfix is an urgent production fix outside the normal release. I verify the fix, run focused regression around the change and a smoke test, then confirm on production after deployment.
qs.t: Fix + Aas-paas + Smoke + Prod check.

qs.q: What QA metrics do you know?
qs.s: Test execution (pass/fail/blocked), defect count by severity, defect leakage, reopen rate, test coverage. Sirf number nahi, unka matlab samjhao.
qs.b: Common metrics are test execution status, defects by severity, defect leakage, reopen rate and requirement coverage. I use them to show risk, not as targets in themselves.
qs.t: Execution, Severity count, Leakage, Reopen.

qs.q: How do you write a test summary report?
qs.s: Scope, environment/build, kitne cases pass/fail/blocked, bugs list severity ke saath, blockers, risks, recommendation (release go/no-go). Merlin me QA reports artifact/sheet me banata hun.
qs.b: A test summary covers scope, environment and build, execution results, defects by severity, blockers and risks, and a clear release recommendation.
qs.t: Scope, Result, Bugs, Risk, Go/No-go.

qs.q: How do you track issues at your current company?
qs.s: Sach: Linear me tickets (dev assign), DevRev se customer issues, PostHog se errors aur session replays, Google Sheets me tracker (jaise Plant Prefab issue tracker). Jira pehle use kiya.
qs.b: Customer-reported issues come in through DevRev, and I use PostHog for errors and session replays to investigate. I log developer tickets in Linear and keep a shared tracker sheet for customer-facing status.
qs.t: DevRev (customer) → PostHog (jaanch) → Linear (ticket) → Sheet (status).

topics.intro: Process ke sawaal. Tumhare tools: JIRA (10 mahine), Linear, DevRev, PostHog. Jo use kiya wahi bolo.

topics.name: Git & CI/CD

qs.q: What is Git?
qs.s: Version control: code ke har change ka history, kaun ne kya badla, purane version pe wapas ja sakte, team saath kaam kar sakti.
qs.b: Git is a distributed version control system that tracks every change to code, lets teams collaborate on branches and lets you return to earlier versions.
qs.t: Git = code ki time machine.

qs.q: Explain clone, pull, add, commit and push.
qs.s: clone: repo ki copy laptop pe. pull: remote ke naye changes lao. add: changes stage karo. commit: snapshot message ke saath. push: remote (GitHub) pe bhejo.
qs.b: clone copies a repository locally, pull fetches and merges remote changes, add stages changes, commit saves a snapshot with a message, and push uploads commits to the remote.
qs.t: clone → pull → add → commit → push.

qs.q: What is a branch?
qs.s: Main code se alag line jahan feature/fix pe kaam, main kharab nahi hota. Kaam ho jaye to merge.
qs.b: A branch is an independent line of development for a feature or fix, merged back into main when it is ready.
qs.t: Branch = alag kamra me kaam.

qs.q: Merge vs rebase?
qs.s: Merge: dono history jod ke ek merge commit. Rebase: apne commits ko latest main ke upar dobara lagata, history seedhi. Shared branch pe rebase se bacho.
qs.b: Merge combines branches and keeps both histories with a merge commit. Rebase replays commits on top of another branch for a linear history, and should be avoided on shared branches.
qs.t: Merge = jodo. Rebase = upar shift karo.

qs.q: What is a pull request?
qs.s: Apne branch ke changes main me daalne ki request. Review hota, CI chalta, approve ke baad merge. Merlin rule: kabhi khud apna PR merge nahi.
qs.b: A pull request proposes merging a branch, triggers CI checks and lets teammates review before merging. At my company we never self-merge.
qs.t: PR = 'please check karke milao'.

qs.q: What is a merge conflict?
qs.s: Do logon ne same file ki same line alag badli. Git khud decide nahi kar pata, manually sahi version choose karke commit.
qs.b: A merge conflict happens when the same lines were changed differently on two branches; you resolve it manually and commit the result.
qs.t: Do log, ek line = conflict.

qs.q: What is .gitignore?
qs.s: File jisme likha kaun si files Git track na kare: .venv, reports, .env (secrets!), __pycache__.
qs.b: .gitignore lists files Git should not track, such as virtual environments, reports and secret files like .env.
qs.t: Secrets kabhi GitHub pe nahi.

qs.q: What is git status, log and diff?
qs.s: status: kya badla, kya staged. log: commit history. diff: exact line changes.
qs.b: git status shows changed and staged files, git log shows commit history, and git diff shows line-by-line changes.
qs.t: status = abhi kya. log = pehle kya. diff = kya badla.

qs.q: What is CI/CD?
qs.s: CI (Continuous Integration): har push pe build + tests automatically. CD (Continuous Delivery/Deployment): pass hone pe staging/prod tak deploy automatically. Merlin dashboard: git push → Vercel auto deploy.
qs.b: Continuous integration builds and tests code automatically on every change. Continuous delivery or deployment then releases passing builds to staging or production automatically.
qs.t: CI = har push pe test. CD = pass to deploy.

qs.q: Why run automated tests in CI?
qs.s: Har change pe turant pata chale kya toota, insaan bhoole nahi, PR merge se pehle green check. Fast feedback.
qs.b: Running tests in CI gives fast, consistent feedback on every change and stops broken code from being merged.
qs.t: Har push = turant feedback.

qs.q: What are dev, staging and production environments?
qs.s: Dev: developers ka. Staging: prod jaisa, QA testing. Production: live users. Merlin me main staging + prod (read-only) pe test karta hun.
qs.b: Development is where developers build, staging mirrors production for testing, and production is the live system. I test on staging and verify on production in read-only mode.
qs.t: Dev → Staging → Prod.

qs.q: What is a feature flag?
qs.s: Code deploy ho gaya par feature on/off switch se control. Kuch users ko dikhao, problem ho to band. Test: flag on aur off dono me.
qs.b: A feature flag turns functionality on or off without redeploying, allowing gradual rollouts. I test both the on and off states and the switch between them.
qs.t: Flag = feature ka switch. Dono state test.

topics.intro: Automation role ke liye Git basic aana zaroori. GitHub tum B.Tech se use kar rahe ho.

topics.name: My Experience Qs

qs.q: Describe your day-to-day work as a QA engineer.
qs.s: Feature testing staging pe (PR aate, test cases, run, bugs), customer issues triage (DevRev, PostHog), Linear tickets, prod pe read-only verification, regression, QA reports, PO module ka ownership, Postman API tests.
qs.b: My day usually combines feature testing and issue triage. I test new features on staging from the pull request and requirements, write and run test cases and log defects in Linear. I also investigate customer-reported issues using PostHog errors and session replays, verify fixes on production in read-only mode, and own quality for the purchase order module.
qs.t: Feature test + Triage + Verify + PO ownership.

qs.q: Walk me through how you test a new feature.
qs.s: 1 Requirement/PR/PRD padhna, doubts poochhna. 2 Test scenarios + cases (positive, negative, edge, permissions). 3 Staging pe data setup. 4 Execute, evidence. 5 Bugs Linear me. 6 Fix retest + regression. 7 QA report + sign-off, prod pe read-only check.
qs.b: I read the requirement and the pull request, clarify doubts with the developer, and write scenarios and cases covering positive, negative, edge and permission paths. I prepare data on staging, execute with evidence, log defects, retest fixes with focused regression, share a test report, and verify on production after release.
qs.t: Padho → Likho → Data → Chalao → Report → Retest → Prod check.

qs.q: Tell me about a production issue you handled.
qs.s: Example: customer ko file kholne pe 'Something went wrong'. Andar reproduce nahi hua. PostHog me exception events dhundhe (React error), session replays dekhe, pata chala sab crash purane code path (old view) pe the. Isse reproduce nahi hone ki wajah mili. Detail tabhi bolo jab yaad ho.
qs.b: A customer saw an error when opening a file, but we could not reproduce it internally. I searched PostHog for the matching exception events and watched the session replays, and found that every crash happened on the older version of the page, which explained why our tests on the new version passed. That gave the developers a precise path to fix.
qs.t: Reproduce nahi hua → Data (PostHog) → Pattern (old path) → Dev ko exact raasta.

qs.q: How do you test safely on production?
qs.s: Read-only: sirf dekhna, compare. Koi create/edit/delete nahi. Interactive testing staging pe (staging me prod data ki copy hoti hai).
qs.b: On production I only perform read-only checks. Anything that changes data I reproduce on staging, which holds a copy of production data.
qs.t: Prod = aankh. Staging = haath.

qs.q: A developer says your bug is not reproducible. What do you do?
qs.s: Exact environment, data, steps dobara share, video/replay, API response, network. Saath baith ke dikha do. Agar intermittent hai to frequency batao.
qs.b: I share the exact environment, data and steps, with a video, session replay or API response, and offer to reproduce it together. If it is intermittent, I document how often and under which conditions it occurs.
qs.t: Evidence + Saath me dikhao.

qs.q: How do you handle a tight deadline?
qs.s: Risk based priority: core flows + change area pehle. Lead ko clearly batao kya cover hoga kya nahi. Quality pe chupke se compromise nahi, risk documented.
qs.b: I prioritise by risk, covering the core flows and changed areas first, and tell my lead clearly what will and will not be covered so the release decision is made with known risk.
qs.t: Priority + Transparent.

qs.q: What do you do when requirements are unclear?
qs.s: Assume nahi. PO/dev/manager se poochho, likh ke confirm (Slack thread). Tab tak jo clear hai wo test.
qs.b: I do not assume. I ask the product owner or developer, confirm the answer in writing, and meanwhile test the parts that are clear.
qs.t: Poochho, likhwao, baaki test karo.

qs.q: Have you ever missed a bug that reached production? What did you learn?
qs.s: Imaandaari se haan bolo (har QA se hota hai). Kya hua, RCA, kya badla (naya test case, checklist). Blame nahi, learning.
qs.b: Yes, it happens to every tester. (Use your own real case here.) When a scenario I had not covered reached production, I helped find the root cause, added the missing scenario to my test cases and checklist, and now plan for that kind of variation explicitly.
qs.t: Haan + Kyun + Kya badla.

qs.q: How do you handle disagreement with a developer?
qs.s: Facts aur requirement pe baat, personal nahi. User impact batao. Agar fir bhi agree nahi to PO/lead decide. Rishta achha rakho.
qs.b: I keep it factual, referring to the requirement and user impact, listen to the developer's view, and if we still disagree, ask the product owner or lead to decide.
qs.t: Fact, Impact, Escalate politely.

qs.q: How do you use PostHog in your work?
qs.s: Exceptions/errors dekhna, session replays se user ne kya kiya, events se kaun sa code path chala, kitne users affected. Isse bug reproduce aur prioritise karna aasaan.
qs.b: I use PostHog to find exception events, watch session replays to see exactly what the user did, check which version or path they were on, and see how many users were affected, which helps reproduce and prioritise issues.
qs.t: Error + Replay + Kitne users.

qs.q: What have you automated so far?
qs.s: Sach: office me Postman API tests (PO endpoints: status, time, structure). Personal public repo: Playwright + pytest framework saucedemo pe (UI + API + CI). Automation ko badha raha hun. Jo nahi kiya, wo mat bolo.
qs.b: At work I have built Postman API tests for our purchase order endpoints, checking status, response time and response structure. Separately, I maintain a public Playwright and pytest demo framework with page objects, API tests and a CI pipeline. I am now working to bring more of our regression under automation.
qs.t: Office = Postman. Personal = Playwright repo. Aage = regression automation.

qs.q: How do you test the mobile app at your company?
qs.s: Phone pe manually, staging app aur prod app, UI level. Code se nahi. Web aur app ki parity bhi check ki (web vs mobile feature audit).
qs.b: I test our mobile app manually on a phone, using both the staging and production builds, at the UI level. I also worked on a parity audit comparing features between the web and mobile app across modules.
qs.t: Manual phone, staging + prod, parity audit.

qs.q: How do you decide what to regression test?
qs.s: Change kahan hua, us module se jude flows, critical business flows (PO → receive → invoice), pehle jahan bug aaye. Poora regression release se pehle.
qs.b: I look at what changed and which flows depend on it, always include critical business flows, add historically fragile areas, and run the broader regression before major releases.
qs.t: Change + Jude flows + Critical + Purane bug.

qs.q: How do you handle multiple tasks at once?
qs.s: Priority: customer impact (P0/P1) pehle, phir deadline wale feature. Tracker me list, manager ko status update. Ek waqt ek kaam.
qs.b: I prioritise by customer impact and deadlines, keep a visible task list, give regular status updates to my manager, and focus on one task at a time.
qs.t: Impact → Deadline → List → Update.

qs.q: What did you learn in your first year?
qs.s: Business domain (purchasing, inventory, finance), customer issues ko data se debug karna, achhi bug report, API testing, automation shuru. Aur poochhna seekha jab clear na ho.
qs.b: I learned the business domain of purchasing, inventory and finance, how to investigate customer issues with data, how to write reports developers can act on, API testing with Postman, and the basics of test automation.
qs.t: Domain, Data se debug, Report, API, Automation.

qs.q: Why do you want to move toward an SDET role?
qs.s: Manual se repetitive regression me time jaata, automation se fast feedback. Coding seekh raha hun (Python, Playwright), API testing kar raha hun. Testing soch + automation dono chahiye.
qs.b: I enjoy finding defects, and I want to scale that with automation so regression is fast and reliable. I am building Python, Playwright and API testing skills so I can combine a tester's thinking with engineering.
qs.t: Tester ka dimaag + Engineer ka haath.

qs.q: What domain knowledge have you gained?
qs.s: Merlin construction/manufacturing businesses ke liye ERP jaisa: purchase orders, receiving, inventory, invoices, AP, journal entries, bank deposits, three-way match. Domain samajh se acche bugs milte.
qs.b: Our product serves construction and manufacturing businesses, so I learned purchasing, receiving, inventory, accounts payable, invoicing and journal entries. Understanding the domain helps me find business-logic defects, not just UI issues.
qs.t: PO → Receive → Inventory → Invoice → AP → GL.

qs.q: Give an example of a business-logic bug you found.
qs.s: Inventory: receive pe 'Allocated' ledger entry duplicate ban rahi thi, aur unreceive pe On Hand kam nahi ho raha tha jabki accounting reversal sahi tha. Ye P1 the. Sirf tab bolo jab detail samjha sako.
qs.b: In inventory, I found that receiving items created duplicate allocation entries in the ledger, and unreceiving did not reduce on-hand quantity even though the accounting entry was reversed correctly. I documented both with steps and evidence and they were treated as high priority.
qs.t: Receive pe double entry, Unreceive pe stock kam nahi.

qs.q: How do you make your bug reports useful for developers?
qs.s: Ek bug ek ticket, exact steps, environment, expected vs actual, screenshot/video, API response ya error, affected customer, aur agar pata ho to suspected area.
qs.b: I keep one issue per ticket with exact steps, environment, expected and actual results, visual evidence, the relevant API response or error, the affected customer, and where possible the suspected area.
qs.t: Dev ko sochna na pade.

qs.q: How do you stay up to date and keep learning?
qs.s: Daily Python practice, Playwright repo, the Academy, SQL practice, real kaam me naye tools (Postman, PostHog).
qs.b: I practise Python regularly, build on my Playwright framework, complete the Academy courses, practise SQL, and learn new tools through real work.
qs.t: Roz thoda: Python, Playwright, SQL, Academy.

qs.q: What is it like doing QA at a startup?
qs.s: Startup (Merlin, YC S24): chhoti team, tez releases, ek QA kai kaam: feature testing, customer triage, prod verification, process banana. Ownership aur seekhna zyada. Bada company me process zyada fixed, role zyada focused.
qs.b: At a startup the team is small and releases are frequent, so I cover feature testing, customer issue triage, production verification and process improvements. It gave me broad ownership early, and I am now ready to go deeper into automation.
qs.t: Chhoti team, tez release, zyada ownership.

topics.intro: 1 saal experience wale interview ka dil yahi hai. Har answer tumhare asli kaam se hai. Koi number ya claim mat jodo jo defend na kar sako.

topics.name: HR Questions

qs.q: What are your strengths?
qs.s: 2-3 strengths + chhota example. Detail pe dhyaan (duplicate accounts pakde), customer issue ko data se debug, jaldi seekhna (Postman, Playwright).
qs.b: I pay close attention to detail, I investigate issues with data rather than guesses, and I learn tools quickly, for example picking up Postman and Playwright while working full time.
qs.t: Detail, Data, Jaldi seekhna. Har ek ka chhota example.

qs.q: What is your weakness?
qs.s: Asli par sudhar wali kamzori. Jaise: shuru me har cheez khud try karta tha, poochhne me der karta tha; ab time-box karta hun aur jaldi poochhta hun. Ya: coding abhi seekh raha hun, roz practice.
qs.b: Early on I spent too long trying to solve things alone before asking for help. Now I time-box investigation and ask earlier, which has made me faster.
qs.t: Kamzori + Ab kya karta hun.

qs.q: Why do you want to leave your current company?
qs.s: Kabhi current company ki burai nahi. Growth: automation/SDET role, bade scale ke products, naya seekhna.
qs.b: I have learned a lot in my current role, and I am now looking for a position with more scope in test automation and larger products, where I can grow toward an SDET role.
qs.t: Burai nahi. Growth ki baat.

qs.q: Why should we hire you?
qs.s: Hands-on QA experience (feature, regression, production triage), domain samajh, API testing, automation seekh raha, sachchi report karne ki aadat.
qs.b: I bring hands-on experience in feature testing, regression and production issue triage, API testing with Postman, a growing automation skill set in Python and Playwright, and a habit of clear, evidence-based reporting.
qs.t: Experience + API + Automation + Clear report.

qs.q: Where do you see yourself in five years?
qs.s: SDET / senior QA engineer, automation framework own karna, juniors ki help. Abroad wali baat interview me tabhi jab company global ho.
qs.b: I see myself as a senior SDET who owns test automation for a product, contributes to quality strategy and mentors newer testers.
qs.t: Senior SDET, framework owner, mentor.

qs.q: How do you handle pressure?
qs.s: Priority list, ek ek kaam, team ko update. Example: on-call me ek saath kai P0/P1, impact ke hisaab se order.
qs.b: I break the work down, prioritise by impact and keep people updated. During on-call periods with several urgent issues, I ordered them by customer impact and worked through them one at a time.
qs.t: List, Priority, Update.

qs.q: Tell me about working in a team.
qs.s: Dev, PM, support ke saath kaam: customer issue se ticket, dev ke saath reproduce, PM se requirement clear. Example ek.
qs.b: I work closely with developers, product and support: I turn customer reports into clear tickets, reproduce issues with developers and clarify requirements with product.
qs.t: Support → QA → Dev → PM, sab ke beech pul.

qs.q: What is your notice period and salary expectation?
qs.s: Notice: apna asli notice period bolo. Salary: pehle research, range bolo, flexible raho. Current CTC sachcha.
qs.b: My notice period is as per my current contract, and I am open to discussing an early release. For salary, I am looking for a fair range based on the role and market, and I am flexible depending on the overall opportunity.
qs.t: Sachcha notice, research ki hui range, flexible.

qs.q: Do you have any questions for us?
qs.s: Hamesha 1-2 sawaal: team structure, automation stack, pehle 3 mahine ki expectations, QA aur dev ka collaboration.
qs.b: Yes: how is the QA team structured, what does your automation stack look like, and what would success look like in my first three months?
qs.t: Team, Stack, 3 mahine.

topics.intro: Last round ke common sawaal. Chhote, sachche, positive jawab.

topics.name: Performance & Security

qs.q: Which tools are used for performance or load testing?
qs.s: JMeter (purana, GUI), k6 (JavaScript scripts, CI friendly), Locust (Python), Gatling. Browser side: Lighthouse, DevTools Performance.
qs.b: Common load testing tools are JMeter, k6, Locust and Gatling. For front-end performance I use Lighthouse and the DevTools Performance panel.
qs.t: JMeter, k6, Locust (Python wala).

qs.q: What metrics do you look at in performance testing?
qs.s: Response time (average, p95), throughput (requests per second), error rate, concurrent users, CPU/memory server ka.
qs.b: Response time including percentiles such as p95, throughput, error rate, the number of concurrent users, and server resource usage.
qs.t: Time, Throughput, Error, Users, Resources.

qs.q: What does p95 response time mean?
qs.s: 95% requests is time ke andar complete hui. Average dhoka de sakta hai, p95 batata hai zyadatar users ka asli experience.
qs.b: p95 is the time within which 95 percent of requests completed. It shows what most users experience better than an average, which slow outliers can hide.
qs.t: 100 me se 95 is se tez.

qs.q: What are soak, spike and volume testing?
qs.s: Soak/endurance: normal load lambe time (memory leak). Spike: achanak bahut load. Volume: bahut bada data (lakhs rows).
qs.b: Soak testing runs a normal load for a long time to find leaks, spike testing applies a sudden surge, and volume testing uses very large data sets.
qs.t: Soak = lamba. Spike = achanak. Volume = bhaari data.

qs.q: What is the OWASP Top 10?
qs.s: Web security ke sabse common risks ki list: broken access control (IDOR jaisa), injection, auth failures, security misconfiguration, sensitive data exposure, etc. QA ko naam aur basic check pata hona chahiye.
qs.b: The OWASP Top 10 lists the most critical web application security risks, such as broken access control, injection, authentication failures, security misconfiguration and cryptographic failures.
qs.t: Number 1 = Broken access control (dusre ka data).

qs.q: What is SQL injection and how would you check for it at a basic level?
qs.s: Input field me SQL jaisa text daal ke database query badalna. Basic check: input me single quote (') daalo, server error (500) ya ajeeb result aaye to report. Exploit mat karo, sirf report.
qs.b: SQL injection is when user input changes a database query. As a basic check, I enter characters like a single quote and watch for server errors or unexpected results, then report it without exploiting further.
qs.t: Quote daalo, 500 aaya = shak.

qs.q: What is XSS?
qs.s: Cross-Site Scripting: input me script daalo jo dusre users ke browser me chal jaye. Check: comment/naam field me test type ka text, agar bold dikhe (render ho) to escaping missing.
qs.b: Cross-site scripting happens when user input is rendered as code in other users' browsers. A simple check is entering harmless HTML formatting; if it renders instead of showing as text, output is not escaped.
qs.t: Input code ban gaya = XSS ka darwaza.

qs.q: What is CSRF?
qs.s: Cross-Site Request Forgery: logged-in user se bina jaane koi action karwa lena (doosri site se). Protection: CSRF token, SameSite cookies.
qs.b: CSRF tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending an unwanted request from another site. Applications defend against it with CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.
qs.t: Tumhare naam pe chupke se request.

qs.q: What basic security checks can a manual tester do?
qs.s: Dusre user/org ka data URL/ID badal ke (IDOR), logout ke baad back button, password masked, session timeout, sensitive data URL me na ho, HTTPS, error message me stack trace na dikhe, role wale permissions.
qs.b: I check access control by changing IDs, session handling after logout and timeout, password masking, no sensitive data in URLs, HTTPS, no technical stack traces in errors, and role-based permissions.
qs.t: ID badlo, Logout back, Mask, URL clean, Error clean, Role.

qs.q: How should passwords be stored?
qs.s: Kabhi plain text nahi. Hash (bcrypt jaisa) + salt. Tester ke liye sign: 'forgot password' pe purana password email me aaye = bada security bug.
qs.b: Passwords should be stored as salted hashes using a slow algorithm like bcrypt. If a system can email you your existing password, that is a serious security defect.
qs.t: Purana password email me aaya = laal jhanda.

qs.q: What is localization and internationalization testing?
qs.s: i18n: app alag language/region ke liye ready (text bahar file me). l10n: specific language me sahi translation, date/currency format, lamba text layout tode nahi, RTL (Arabic).
qs.b: Internationalisation makes an app ready for multiple locales; localisation testing checks a specific locale's translation, date, number and currency formats, text expansion in layouts and right-to-left support.
qs.t: Bhasha, Date, Paisa, Lamba text, Ulta (RTL).

qs.q: What is a compatibility matrix?
qs.s: Table: kaun se browser/OS/device versions support karne hain aur kis par test karenge. Analytics se decide (users kya use karte).
qs.b: A compatibility matrix lists the browsers, operating systems and devices the product supports and which combinations will be tested, usually chosen from usage analytics.
qs.t: Kahan chalna chahiye ki list.

qs.q: What is recovery testing?
qs.s: System crash/network fail/power cut ke baad kaise wapas aata: data safe, transaction complete ya rollback.
qs.b: Recovery testing checks how a system recovers from crashes, network failures or restarts, ensuring data is not lost and transactions complete or roll back cleanly.
qs.t: Gira, utha, kuch khoya nahi.

qs.q: How would you start load testing an API?
qs.s: Pehle normal usage samjho (kitne users, kaun se endpoints). Staging pe hi (prod pe kabhi bina permission nahi). Baseline → dheere dheere load badhao → response time, error rate dekho → bottleneck dev ko.
qs.b: I would agree on realistic usage numbers, run on staging rather than production, establish a baseline, increase load gradually, and monitor response times, percentiles and error rates, then share the bottlenecks with developers.
qs.t: Staging, Baseline, Dheere badhao, Measure.

topics.intro: 1 saal experience pe basic level kaafi hai: terms aur 'kaise check karoge' bata do. Load testing tumhare Merlin API plan me aage aana hai.

topics.name: Introduction to the Platform

qs.q: What is the platform and what is its vision?
qs.s: The platform ek global community hai jisme 1M+ testers hain jo duniya ki sabse badi companies ke products improve karne me help karte hain. Ye online global community hai testers aur technology enthusiasts ki jo world ka digital landscape shape karne ke liye passionate hain. The platform community parent company se powered hai. Vision: tumhe mauka dena ki tum Learn karo (tester kaise bante hain), Earn karo (paise kamao) aur Connect karo (community ke dusre testers se judo). The Academy courses deti hai jo the platform ke baare me foundational knowledge, testing kyun important hai aur tester kaise bante hain, ye sikhate hain. The platform log ko global brands ke paid testing projects se connect karta hai, kahin se bhi kaam kar sakte ho, bas ek device chahiye.
qs.b: The platform is an online global community of over 1 million testers and technology enthusiasts, powered by the company. Its vision is to give members the opportunity to learn how to be a tester, earn money, and connect with other testers. It connects testers with paid testing projects from global brands, and all you need to start is a device.
qs.t: the platform = Learn, Earn, Connect; 1M+ testers; parent company ka engine.

qs.q: What is the company and how is it related to the platform?
qs.s: The company ne 2007 me crowdtesting concept pioneer kiya. Tab se thousands of companies ko positive business outcomes drive karne me help ki: digital quality revolutionize karna, software development accelerate karna, aur customers ko high-quality digital experiences dena. The company the platform community ko use karke custom teams of testers assemble karta hai jo duniya ke kisi bhi device aur operating system combination ko test kar sakein. The platform community parent company se powered hai.
qs.b: The company pioneered the crowdtesting concept in 2007 and helps companies improve digital quality and speed up software development. It uses the platform community to assemble custom teams of testers who can test any device and operating system combination in the world. In short, the platform is the community and the company is the company that powers it.
qs.t: the company = company (2007 se crowdtesting), the platform = uski tester army.

qs.q: What is software testing, why is it important, and who is a software tester?
qs.s: Software testing: product ke features aur functionalities ko evaluate karna, is intent se ki product ke saare defects aur errors locate ho jayein. Important kyun: development phases me jo defects aur errors bane unhe identify karta hai, aur developers ko high quality products banane deta hai jo features, functionalities aur process flows me defect-free hon. Software tester: wo insaan jo product use aur evaluate karta hai taaki uske defects aur errors identify ho sakein.
qs.b: Software testing is the process of evaluating a product's features and functionality with the intent of finding all defects and errors. It matters because it catches the mistakes made during development, so developers can ship high-quality products that are free of defects in features, functionality and process flows. A software tester is the person who uses and evaluates the product to identify those defects.
qs.t: Testing = defect dhoondhna intent ke saath; tester = jo product use karke defects pakde.

qs.q: What is crowdtesting and why is it needed?
