Interactive controls include checkboxes, drop-downs, CTAs such as Subscribe or Watch Now, and captchas that separate humans from bots. Field validation confirms every field holds a correct value before a form is accepted, and the frontend is what users see while the backend handles data storage and processing.
qs.t: Breadcrumb = rasta peeche ka; Hero = top ka bada banner; Hamburger = 3 line hidden menu.

qs.q: List the remaining website and app elements in the platform glossary (Permalink to Overlay), including the parts of a URL.
qs.s: Website/App Elements Terms (part 2): Permalink (Permanent Link) = specific page/blog post ka URL jo content update hone par bhi same rehta hai. PURL (Personal/Personalized URL) = individual ya campaign target ke liye unique web address; social media profile URL ya customized landing page. Pop-up = web page ke upar khulne wali chhoti window. PDP (Product Detail Page) = ek product ki detailed info wala page. PLP (Product Listing Page) = products ki list wala page, aksar sort aur filter ke saath. Push Notification = desktop browser, mobile home screen ya notification center me pop-up jaisa short message. QR (Quick Response) Code = square barcode jo URL, text, location data store karta hai, smartphone/tablet se scan. Radio Button = options ke set me se sirf ek select ho sakta hai. RSS (Really Simple Syndication) = web feed format, XML me hota hai isliye RSS reader chahiye; news, blogs, social media, podcasts me common. Sitemap = website ke important pages/content ki list wala page/file. Tabs = ek window me multiple views. Textbox/Text Field = text enter karne ka object. Toggle Button = setting ko do states ke beech change karna. Tooltip = element par mouse hover ya tooltip icon click par info block. URL (Uniform Resource Locator) = internet par resource ka address; usually parts: Protocol, Domain, Path, Parameters, Fragment. UGC (User Generated Content) = users ka banaya content (text, images, videos, reviews, podcast); trust aur credibility badhata hai. UI (User Interface) = visual aur interactive elements: buttons, icons, text fields, menus etc. Website/App Modal = page ke upar dikhne wala element jo baaki saara page content deactivate kar deta hai. Website/App Overlay = page ke upar content box jo background content ko obscure karta hai.
qs.b: A Product Listing Page lists products with sort and filter, while a Product Detail Page shows one product in detail. A URL usually has five parts: protocol, domain, path, parameters and fragment. A modal sits on top of the page and deactivates all other content, while an overlay obscures the background content. A radio button allows only one choice from a set, whereas a toggle switches a setting between two states.
qs.t: PLP = list, PDP = detail; URL = P-D-P-P-F (Protocol, Domain, Path, Parameters, Fragment).

qs.q: What video and streaming player features appear in the platform website/app elements glossary?
qs.s: Website/App Elements me streaming/video wale terms: Binge = TV show/movie ke end par pop-up jo next episode ya similar content ke trailer par le jaata hai. BYW (Because You Watched) = jo content dekha uske basis par personalized suggestions. Casting/AirPlay = Google Cast ya Apple AirPlay se video/audio supported TV ya sound system par stream karna; same network par device hona chahiye aur player me casting enabled ho. Closed Captions (CC) = audio ka time-synchronized text; mainly un viewers ke liye jo audio sun nahi sakte; usually video ki same language me; turn off ho sakte hain. Continue Watching (CW) = jahan roka tha wahan se video continue karna. Docked View = video window screen ke ek fixed location (corner/bottom) par rehti hai; PiP se farak: docked fixed rehta hai, PiP reposition ho sakta hai. Expanded View = bada/detailed view, zyada options, related content, program guide; playback controls usually hidden jab tak player tap na karo; full-screen se alag (full-screen me video poori screen leta hai). FER (Full Event Replay) = poore event ki complete recording/playback, usually sports/entertainment. IH (Immersive Highlights) = sports jaise highlights jisme user key positions se kya dekhna hai choose kare. Live Window = live stream me content window jisme Live Event ke dauraan player controls use ho sakte hain. MLT (More Like This) = current item jaisa similar items suggest karna. Open Captions = video file me permanently embedded subtitles; off nahi ho sakte. Parental Control = settings jisse parent control kare ki child kya content dekh sakta hai. PiP (Picture in Picture) = floating chhoti window me video dekhte hue device par dusre kaam; multitasking. Playhead = timeline/progress bar par current position ka marker; drag karke navigate. Rail = theme ke hisaab se tiles ka horizontally scroll hone wala collection. Scrub = playhead ko timeline par drag karke aage/peeche jaana. SLE (Single Live Event) = ek live event stream, jaise live sports game ya news event. Subtitles = dialogue/text, mainly un viewers ke liye jo spoken language nahi samajhte; aksar kai languages me available. Thumbnails = bade image/video ko represent karne wali chhoti image; scrubbing ke time timeline ke upar dikhne wali image bhi thumbnail kehlati hai. VST (Video Start Time) = Play click karne se video start hone tak ka time; video streaming testing me common.
qs.b: Closed captions are time-synchronized text of the audio, mainly for viewers who cannot hear, usually in the same language, and can be turned off. Open captions are burned into the video and cannot be turned off, while subtitles help viewers who do not understand the spoken language and often come in several languages. Docked view stays in a fixed position, whereas Picture in Picture can be repositioned. Video Start Time is the time from pressing Play to playback starting, and scrubbing means dragging the playhead along the timeline.
qs.t: CC = sun nahi sakte; Subtitles = bhasha nahi samajhte; Open = band nahi hota. Docked fixed, PiP movable.

qs.q: Explain the Software Development Life Cycle terms in the platform glossary.
qs.s: SDLC Terms: ADB (Android Debug Bridge) = Android devices debug karne ka programming tool. Alpha Build = core functionalities wala pehla working version, test ke liye ready; bahut bugs, kuch features missing ho sakte hain. API = do ya zyada programs/components ke beech communication ka tarika. Azure DevOps = Microsoft product: version control, reporting, requirements management, project management, automated builds, testing, release management. BTS (Bug Tracking System) = application jo database me bugs (aur suggestions) track karta hai. CLI (Command Line Interface) = text-based interface; CMD, Powershell, Terminal. DevOps = cultural philosophies, practices aur tools ka combination jo high velocity par apps deliver karne ki ability badhata hai. Dogfooding = apna banaya software khud use karna ('eating your own dog food'), beta form me test karke development me help. Firebase = Google ki backend cloud computing service (realtime database, cloud filestore); testers ko latest builds distribute karne ke liye Firebase par invite kiya ja sakta hai. InfoSec = digital data ko unauthorized access, use, modification, disclosure, destruction se bachane ke processes/tools; suspicious links se bachna, strong passwords. Jailbreaking = device ke flaws exploit karke manufacturer ke bahar ka software install karna; cracking/rooting bhi kehte hain; rooted/jailbroken device kharidna ya khud root karna suggest nahi kiya jaata, warranty void ho jaati hai aur OS break ho sakta hai. Java = general purpose language, animation wale web pages ke saath; chhote apps = Java applets. JavaScript = public scripting language, web pages par dynamic content/interactivity. JIRA = Atlassian ka product: bug tracking, issue tracking, agile project management. PROD (Production Environment) = public ke liye available, tested aur ready environment. QA (Quality Assurance) = ensure karna ki product contractual aur agreed performance, design, reliability, maintainability meet kare. QA/Stage Environment = public release (Production) se pehle new features/fixes test karne ka build/environment. TestFlight = iOS apps ke beta versions testers ko distribute karne ka tool. UAT (User Acceptance Testing) = intended audience ya business representative real world me software test karte hain.
qs.b: The QA or stage environment is where new features and fixes are tested before release, while production is the public, already tested environment. Builds are often distributed to testers through TestFlight for iOS or Firebase, and Android devices are debugged with ADB. Dogfooding means a team using its own software in beta form, and UAT is testing by the intended audience or business representative. A bug tracking system such as JIRA stores bugs in a database.
qs.t: Stage pe test, Prod pe public; iOS = TestFlight, Android debug = ADB.

qs.q: What are the key streaming terms in the platform glossary, and how do buffering, freezing and stalls differ?
qs.s: Streaming Terms: Buffering = device ko playback speed jitna data fast nahi milta, playback baar baar pause hota hai; streaming start hone se pehle ka delay bhi buffering hai. Internet par har video buffer karta hai, ye zaroori nahi problem ho. CTV (Connected TV) = internet connected TVs jo OTT content access karte hain (Netflix, Amazon Prime Video); Smart TVs aur streaming devices jaise Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, Roku; CD (Connected Devices) ya living room devices bhi kehte hain. DRM (Digital Rights Management) = copy/record na hone dekar copyright protect karna; zyada streaming apps DRM protected. Freezing = playback poori tarah ruk jaata hai aur wait karne par bhi resume nahi hota; usually app restart karna padta hai. HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) = widely used streaming protocol, almost kisi bhi server par; network condition ke hisaab se quality kam/zyada. Linear Channel = scheduled ya live broadcasting. MVPD (Multichannel Video Programming Distributor) = cable, fiber ya satellite se subscription par multiple TV channels aur VOD; mainly TV par; examples Xfinity, DISH Network, DirecTV, Spectrum, Time Warner Cable. NPVR (Network Personal Video Recorder) = recordings provider ke server par save. OTT (Over The Top) = cable/satellite subscription ke bina internet se film/TV content; Netflix, Disney+, Hulu. PVR (Personal Video Recorder) = device jo video ko disk drive, USB, memory card ya network storage me record kare. Stalls = bandwidth kam hone se video continue nahi ho paata (high traffic), loading jab tak issue resolve ya bandwidth available na ho. STB (Set Top Box) = TV ko digital signals receive/decode karne deta hai, home network se connect, OTT video ko TV signals me convert. Upsell = higher-priced/upgraded version kharidne ke liye entice karna; non-subscribed users ko subscribe offer, monthly ke bajaye annual subscription. Video Metadata = description, title, creation date, duration, tags. VOD (Video On Demand) = jab chahe internet device par video dekhna.
qs.b: Buffering happens when the device does not receive data fast enough for playback, so it pauses often; some buffering is normal for every streamed video. Freezing is when playback stops completely and does not resume even after waiting, usually needing an app restart. Stalls happen because there is not enough bandwidth, for example due to high traffic, so the video keeps loading until bandwidth is available. OTT delivers content over the internet without cable, while an MVPD delivers channels via cable, fiber or satellite.
qs.t: Buffer = data slow, Freeze = ruk gaya restart chahiye, Stall = bandwidth kam.

qs.q: Explain the networking terms in the platform glossary.
qs.s: Networking Terms: DNS (Domain Name System) = domain names (jaise www.academybugs.com) ko IP addresses (jaise 192.168.0.1) me translate karta hai. FTP (File Transfer Protocol) = server se client tak files transfer karne ka standard protocol. Firewall = predetermined security rules ke basis par incoming/outgoing traffic monitor aur control karne wala security system. HTTP = web par text, images, sound, video jaise files transfer karne ke rules. HTTPS = HTTP ka secure version jo data encrypt karta hai; login credentials, personal data, payment details bhejte waqt important. IoT (Internet of Things) = sensors, software wale physical objects (devices, vehicles, appliances) ka network jo internet par data exchange karte hain; smart homes, healthcare, transportation. IP address = internet se connected har computer ka unique identifying number. ISP (Internet Service Provider) = internet access/use/manage karne ki services deta hai. Latency = usually milliseconds me; data ko network par destination tak pahunchne ka delay. P2P (Peer to Peer) = decentralized platform, do log bina third party ke directly interact. Proxy = client aur resource dene wale server ke beech intermediary. SMB (Server Message Block) = same network par files share, resources access, communicate karne ka protocol. SSID (Service Set Identifier) = wireless network ka naam. VPN (Virtual Private Network) = device aur remote server ke beech encrypted point-to-point tunnel, IP mask karta hai. Note: Lesson 3 me testers ke liye 'Using a VPN' should-not-do list me hai.
qs.b: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses, latency is the network delay usually measured in milliseconds, and an SSID is the name of a wireless network. HTTPS is the encrypted version of HTTP and matters when sending credentials or payment details. A proxy is an intermediary between client and server, and a VPN creates an encrypted tunnel that masks the device IP, which testers are told not to use on the platform.
qs.t: DNS = naam se number; SSID = WiFi ka naam; VPN = mat use karo the platform pe.

qs.q: What do the HTTP error codes 400, 401, 403, 404, 406, 500, 503 and 504 mean?
qs.s: HTTP Error Codes (notes me 8 codes): 400 Bad Request = apparent client error ki wajah se server process nahi karega (malformed syntax, size too large, invalid framing, deceptive routing). 401 Unauthorized = valid authentication credentials missing (missing/incorrect API keys, expired session tokens, failed login). 403 Forbidden = server request samajhta hai lekin authorize karne se mana karta hai; IP restriction, galat permission ya security measures; URL recheck karo, cache aur cookies clear karo. 404 Not Found = browser server se baat kar paya lekin server ko requested cheez nahi mili; ya server batana nahi chahta ki info hai ya nahi. 406 Not Acceptable = resource sirf aisa content bana sakta hai jo request ke Accept headers ke hisaab se acceptable nahi. 500 Internal Server Error = unexpected condition, koi specific message suitable nahi. 503 Service Unavailable = server overload ya maintenance ki wajah se handle nahi kar sakta; generally temporary. 504 Gateway Timeout = server gateway/proxy tha aur upstream server se timely response nahi mila.
qs.b: 4xx codes point to the request: 400 is a malformed client request, 401 means missing or invalid authentication such as an expired token, 403 means the server understood but refuses to authorize, 404 means the resource was not found, and 406 means the content does not match the Accept headers. 5xx codes are server-side: 500 is an unexpected internal error, 503 means the server is overloaded or under maintenance, usually temporarily, and 504 means a gateway or proxy did not get a timely upstream response.
qs.t: 401 = kaun ho tum? (login nahi), 403 = pata hai kaun ho, phir bhi nahi; 503 = busy/maintenance, 504 = upstream late.

qs.q: What gambling terms should a tester know for betting and casino projects?
qs.s: Gambling Terms (sab 20): 50-50 Split pot = do ya zyada players ke identical hands, pot barabar divide. All-in = player apne saare remaining chips ek bet par lagata hai; call karne wale ke paas full amount cover karne jitne chips chahiye. Bet slip = ticket jo bets, bet amounts aur odds record karta hai. Bet/Wager/Stake = event ke result par risk ki gayi raqam. Call = same betting round me current bet match karna (koi $10 lagaye to $10 match). Cash-out = cash game ya poker tournament chhodte waqt chips ko real money me exchange karna. Check = bet ya raise nahi karna lekin round me rehna; betting next player par. Flop cards = Texas Hold'em aur Omaha me pehla round, face up 3 community cards. Hand = poker me player ke cards ka set. Lobby = online casino ka area jahan games choose karte ho. Odds = outcome ki probability; fractional (3/1), decimal (1.35) ya whole number (+200). Raise = same round me current bet badhana ($10 ko $20 karna = $10 raise). River card = Texas Hold'em/Omaha me 5th aur final community card, turn ke baad. Run it twice = do ya zyada players all-in hone par remaining community cards do alag sequences me deal, pot dono me split. Side Bet = game ke result se directly related nahi outcome par bet; jaise kuch blackjack variants me pehle do cards ka total 13 se upar ya neeche. Sit out = seat chhode bina temporarily game se bahar; chips table par, cards aur betting nahi jab tak wapas na aao. Turn card = 4th community card, flop ke baad aur river se pehle.
qs.b: In poker the flop is the first three community cards, the turn is the fourth and the river is the fifth and final card. Calling matches the current bet, raising increases it, checking stays in without betting, and going all-in bets all remaining chips. A bet slip records the bets, amounts and odds, and odds can be fractional like 3/1, decimal like 1.35 or a whole number like +200. The lobby is where players choose games in an online casino.
qs.t: Flop 3 -> Turn 4th -> River 5th; Call = match, Raise = badhao, Check = pass.

qs.q: What cloud computing and authentication terms are in the platform glossary?
qs.s: Cloud Computing Terms: AWS = Amazon ki subsidiary jo individuals, companies, governments ko on-demand cloud computing platforms aur APIs deti hai. AI = insaan jaise intellectual processes (reason, meaning discover, generalize, past experience se seekhna) wale systems; computer ya robot ka intelligent beings wale tasks karna. ML (Machine Learning) = AI aur computer science ki branch, data aur algorithms se insaan jaise seekhna, accuracy dheere dheere improve. SaaS = cloud based software jo internet par app deliver kare; browser se bina install, usually subscription; examples Slack, Google Workspace, DocuSign. Authentication Terms: Biometric Authentication = fingerprints, face, iris, voice jaise unique traits; traditional method se zyada secure, convenient, personalized, efficient. MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) = login par do ya zyada verification factors. OTP (One-time password) = SMS ya email se temporary numeric/alphanumeric code, sirf ek session ke liye valid, ek hi baar use. SSO (Single Sign On) = ek login se saari digital services access; multiple passwords ki zarurat khatam, centralized authentication se security improve. 2FA (Two-factor Authentication) = login par do alag authentications, jaise password aur registered phone/email par bheja verification code.
qs.b: 2FA requires exactly two different authentications, such as a password plus a code sent to a registered phone or email, while MFA requires two or more factors. An OTP is a temporary code that is valid for only one session and can be used once. SSO lets a user access all services with one login, reducing password management and centralizing authentication. SaaS is cloud software used through a browser, usually on subscription, like Slack or Google Workspace.
qs.t: 2FA = exactly 2, MFA = 2 ya zyada; SSO = ek login sab jagah.

qs.q: Explain the voice testing terms such as ASR, intent, utterance and wake word.
qs.s: Voice Testing Terms: ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) = users typing ke bajaye bol kar input de sakein; computer speech recognition ya speech-to-text. Dictation = words bolna is intent se ki wo likhe jayein; development me dictation ka matlab notes ke hisaab se 'text-to-speech' jahan spoken words machine learning se transcribe hote hain (notes ka wording yahi hai). Intent = task ya action jo user voice application se fulfil karwana chahta hai. NLP (Natural Language Processing) = AI ki branch, computers ko spoken words insaan jaisa samjhana; computational linguistics + statistical, machine learning, deep learning models; text ya voice data ka full meaning, speaker ka intent aur sentiment. Utterance = speech ki chhoti unit; clean breaks before aur after se measure. Voice Assistant = voice recognition, speech synthesis aur NLP se service dene wala digital assistant. Wake word = voice assistant trigger karne wala phrase; detect hone par system request capture, decode aur service karta hai. Related (Other Terms): Smart Assistant = smart device par software jo trigger hone par (aksar Wake word se active listening) tasks perform karta hai. Voice Testing (Testing Terms) = native speakers ke saath voice-enabled products test; functional, dialogue verification, usability aur payment testing combine.
qs.b: The wake word is the phrase that triggers a voice assistant, after which it captures, decodes and services the request. An utterance is a small unit of speech bounded by clean breaks, and the intent is the task the user wants the voice application to fulfil. ASR converts speech to text, and NLP lets computers understand meaning, intent and sentiment. Voice testing on the platform is done with native speakers and combines functional, dialogue verification, usability and payment testing.
qs.t: Wake word jagata hai, Utterance bolte ho, Intent kaam batata hai.

qs.q: What miscellaneous 'Other Terms' does the platform glossary define?
qs.s: Other Terms (sab 22): AEM (Adobe Experience Manager) = enterprise content management system, content aur digital media ki authoring, management, delivery. AOD (Always On Display) = kuch smartphones me screen off hone par bhi time, date, notifications, missed calls dikhe. AR (Augmented Reality) = digital info ko user ke environment ke saath real time me integrate. Compress = file chhoti karna, disk space bachana aur network par fast transfer. D2C (Direct to Customer) = bina retailers/wholesalers/middlemen ke seedha customer ko bechna. DPI (Dots Per Inch) = device resolution ka measure. Emulation = program/device ka dusre program/device ki nakal karna. End User = jo log product/service use karenge, final consumers. FTU (First Time User) = product pehli baar use karne wala; aksar tutorial ya tooltips dikhaye jaate hain. HUD (Heads-up Display) = transparent display, viewpoint se nazar hataye bina data; jaise playback progress bar, sports score card. Hosting = website ko internet par accessible banane ke liye storage aur resources ki service. Incognito = private browsing; history, cookies, temporary data save nahi hota. KYC (Know Your Customer) = user identity identify aur verify karna; financial services me common. OSS (Open Source Software) = source code koi bhi inspect, modify, enhance, distribute kar sake open source license ke under. OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) = dusri organizations se kharide components se devices banane wala. PI (Payment Instrument) = paisa transfer/pay karne ka physical ya virtual tarika. Smart Assistant = smart device par software jo trigger (aksar Wake word) par tasks karta hai. UDID (Unique Device Identifier) = Apple devices (iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, MacBook) ka unique identifier. UXR (User Experience Researcher) = users ko systematically study karke feedback collect/analyze karta hai. VR (Virtual Reality) = computer modeling/simulation se artificial 3D environment me interact. Whitelist (Allowlist) = sirf pre-approved logon ko access; testing me aksar email whitelist: tester apna email bhejta hai aur company whitelist karti hai taaki test site/app/features access ho. WIP (Work in Progress) = kaam abhi complete nahi, chal raha hai.
qs.b: Whitelisting, or allowlisting, restricts access to pre-approved users; in testing, a company often whitelists the tester's email so they can reach the test site or features. A UDID is the unique identifier of an Apple device, KYC is identity verification common in financial services, and an FTU is a first-time user who is often shown tutorials or tooltips. Emulation is one program or device imitating another, and incognito mode does not save history, cookies or temporary data.
qs.t: Whitelist = email bhejo, access milega; UDID = Apple ka ID card.

qs.q: Why is reading instructions so important at the platform, and what should you do when answering an SRS or applying on the Projects Board?
qs.s: Lesson 2: Reading mind, imagination, creativity develop karta hai; critical thinking aur testing skills bhi improve. The platform par requirements aur instructions padhna aur samajhna crucial hai; isse aap professional, hard worker, reliable, motivated, polite, aur expectations se aage dikhte ho. Instructions samajhne se project goals aur aapse kya expected hai pata chalta hai, valuable bugs milte hain, well-written reports banti hain, test case sahi execute hota hai. Testers Projects Board par projects ke liye apply karte hain aur SRS milne par respond karte hain; requirement meet karne par cycle me invite ho sakte hain. SRS rules: question padh ke samjho, phir honestly aur correctly answer karo; answers falsify ya random select mat karo; profile update karne ko kaha jaye to sahi update karo; agar wo profile question already up-to-date hai to next question par ja sakte ho. Projects Board rules: apply karne se pehle project description aur details me requirements dhyan se review karo; meet karte ho tabhi apply karo; project form accurate aur complete info se bharo aur submit se pehle saare fields double check karo. Cycle invitation accept karne ke baad bhi specific tasks se pehle instructions dobara review karna recommended hai.
qs.b: Reading and understanding the instructions tells me the project goals and what is expected, which helps me find valuable bugs, write good reports and execute test cases correctly. For an SRS I read each question, answer honestly and accurately, never pick random answers, and update my profile when asked. Before applying on the Projects Board I check that I meet the requirements, fill the form accurately and double-check every field.
qs.t: SRS me jhooth = khud ka nuksaan; padho, samjho, phir click karo.

qs.q: Which sections of a the platform cycle should you review, and at what point?
qs.s: Lesson 2 ke hisaab se sections aur kab padhne hain: Slot Instructions = slot claim karne se pehle; slotting instructions aur slot description padho, claim se pehle description expand karo. Setup Instructions = testing start, bug submit ya test case execute karne se pehle; environment setup, test environment access, test app install ke instructions. In Scope = bug report karne se pehle; cycle goals samjho aur issue scope me hai ya nahi. Out Of Scope = bug report se pehle; issue OOS areas me to nahi; Known Issues (agar attached) bhi check karo. Issue Reporting Instructions = bug report se pehle; Issue Title format, Required Attachments, Additional environment info (agar required); bug report form ke fields sahi bharo, khaas kar custom fields ya special requirements. Test Case Instructions = Exploratory with Test Cases cycles me dikhta hai; test cases ke specific requirements aur rules. UX Survey Responses = survey ka instruction text poora padho, chahe lamba ho; video recording kab start karni hai ya task se pehle kaunse questions answer karne hain; follow na kiya to poora survey reject ho sakta hai. Cycle Announcements = cycle ke dauraan aate hain (instructions, requirements, advice, warnings, requests); turant padho, follow karo, applicable ho to acknowledge karo. Info Requests & Tester Messenger Messages = submit ke baad message/IR aa sakta hai; dhyan se padho, info do; fix karne ke baad 'Confirm all requested info is added' link click karo taaki TTL, TE ya customer ko pata chale kaam review ke liye ready hai. Other sections bhi padho: Team Contact Information, Special Instructions, Tester Special Requirement, Bonus Instructions, Review questions (agar review hai), aur cycle TE ya the platform ki koi bhi email.
qs.b: Before claiming a slot I read the slotting instructions and the expanded slot description; before testing I read the Setup Instructions; and before reporting I check In Scope, Out of Scope, Known Issues and the Issue Reporting Instructions for title format, required attachments and environment info. During the cycle I read every announcement immediately and acknowledge it if needed. When I get an info request I provide the information and click 'Confirm all requested info is added' so the TTL, TE or customer knows it is ready.
qs.t: Slot -> Setup -> Scope/OOS/KI -> Reporting rules -> Announcements -> IR confirm.

qs.q: What does the platform recommend testers always do regarding instructions?
qs.s: Lesson 2 'What Is Recommended To Do?' poori list (14 points): 1) Extensively, intensively aur thoroughly padho. 2) Instructions aur details par bahut close attention do. 3) Cycle invitation accept karne se pehle aur testing shuru karne se pehle requirements padh ke samjho. 4) Instructions ek se zyada baar padhne ki habit rakho. 5) Test case instructions ke hisaab se hi execute karo. 6) Apna kaam double check karo ki cycle requirements meet ho. 7) Cycle announcements padho, samjho aur zaroori action lo. 8) Cycle, test case ya announcements ke instructions unclear ho to cycle chat room me TTL se poocho. 9) Bug reports aur test cases me info requests aur messages ka turant jawab do. 10) Ensure karo ki issue reports aur test cases cycle requirements meet karte hain aur saare instructions follow hue. 11) Cycle chat room baar baar check karo aur naya sawaal poochne se pehle pehle pooche gaye sawaal dekho. 12) Naya issue report karne se pehle already reported issues aur Known Issues review karo. 13) Saare required attachments sahi collect karke bug report aur test case me upload karo. 14) Tester profile updated rakho aur har baar accurate info do. Aur phir se: extensively, intensively padho aur requirements par close attention do.
qs.b: I read the overview more than once, before accepting the invitation and again before testing, and I double-check my work against the requirements. I ask the TTL in the cycle chat when something is unclear, but first check whether it was already answered. I respond to info requests immediately, review reported and known issues before submitting, attach every required file, and keep my profile accurate.
qs.t: Padho, dobara padho, poocho (chat me), double check karo.

qs.q: What should testers avoid doing when reading instructions and working in a cycle?
qs.s: Lesson 2 'What Should You Avoid?' poori list (11 points): 1) Skim, scan ya quick/speed reading mat karo. 2) Instructions/requirements ki koi chhoti detail skip mat karo. 3) Cycle overview, scope aur expectations jaldi jaldi mat padho. 4) Requirements padhe aur samjhe bina slot claim mat karo. 5) Slot claim karke bina progress ke mat baitho. 6) Test case false information ya galat environment se execute mat karo. 7) Cycle announcements ignore mat karo. 8) Issue reports aur test cases me info requests aur messages ignore mat karo; galtiyon wale reports aur test cases rejection ke risk par hote hain. 9) Jin projects ki requirements meet nahi karte unme apply mat karo. 10) SRS ya project application me false/inaccurate details mat do. 11) Cycle chat me jo sawaal already pooch ke answer ho chuka hai wo baar baar mat poocho.
qs.b: I avoid skimming or speed-reading the overview and never skip small details. I do not claim a slot without understanding its requirements, I do not sit on a slot without progress, and I never execute a test case with false information or the wrong environment. I do not ignore announcements or info requests, I do not apply to projects or answer surveys with inaccurate details, and I do not repeat questions already answered in the chat.
qs.t: Skim nahi, sit nahi, jhooth nahi, ignore nahi, repeat nahi.

qs.q: What are a tester's responsibilities in a the platform test cycle and what should they do?
qs.s: Lesson 3: Testers test cycle ka sabse important role hain; bugs dhundhte hain, test cases execute karte hain, feedback dete hain, product ke issues report karte hain. Responsibilities (7): product ko samajhna; bugs report, test cases execute, reviews submit aur cycle ke dusre testing tasks; info request ka jaldi se jaldi jawab; high-quality issue reports; deadline me test cases finalize; overview review karna aur blocking issues TTL ko report karna; chat room me fellow testers ki help agar answer pata ho. What Testers Should Do (11): the platform Terms of Use aur AI Guidelines follow karo; communication me professional aur polite raho; test cycle instructions follow karo; cycle chat properly use karo; assigned tasks thoroughly aur honestly complete karo; cycle tabhi accept karo jab commitment ho; scope ke andar issues report karo; apne environment se match karne wale slots claim karo; test case execute karne ke baad submit karo; review me thorough feedback do; baaki points ke liye the platform Terms of Use padho.
qs.b: A tester's job is to understand the product, report high-quality bugs, execute test cases and reviews, finish test cases within the deadline and answer info requests as soon as possible. I review the overview, report blocking issues to the TTL and help other testers in chat when I know the answer. I follow the Terms of Use and AI Guidelines, accept a cycle only when I can commit, report only in-scope issues and claim only slots that match my environment.
qs.t: Commit ho tabhi accept; environment match ho tabhi claim.

qs.q: What are testers not allowed to do on the platform?
qs.s: Lesson 3 'What Testers Should Not Do' poori list: the platform Terms of Use aur AI Guidelines violate karna; dishonesty; customer information publicize karna; customers ke saamne payout discuss karna; ek se zyada the platform account banana; koi bhi information falsify karna; VPN use karna; submitted kaam approve karne ke liye kehna; invalid issues report karna (hamesha already reported issues, cycle ki known issues list aur OOS section check karo); maximum allowed limit tak slots claim karna jisse dusre testers claim na kar sakein; slots claim karke bina progress baithe rehna; test cases galat execute karna; test case achanak unclaim karke cycle me idle rehna; report ya test case me invalid attachments; add-ons, scripts etc. intentionally use karke issues dhundhna; rejected bugs ko bina reason dispute karna; rude aur unprofessional hona; attention ke liye All caps use karna. Baaki points the platform Terms of Use aur AI Guidelines me.
qs.b: Testers must not be dishonest, falsify information, create more than one account, use a VPN, publicize customer information or discuss payouts in front of customers. They must not ask for their work to be approved, report invalid issues, hoard slots or sit on them, execute test cases incorrectly, or upload invalid attachments. Using add-ons or scripts to find issues, disputing rejections without reasons, being rude and writing in all caps are also not allowed.
qs.t: Ek account, no VPN, no payout talk, no ALL CAPS.

qs.q: What is the role of a Test Team Lead (TTL) and what can and cannot testers expect from them?
qs.s: Lesson 3: TTLs the platform community ke hand-selected members hain jo TSMs aur TEs ke saath side-by-side kaam karte hain test cycles ka flow aur outcome facilitate karne ke liye. Goal: customer ke liye the platform ki value badhana, output maximize aur noise level minimize karke. TTL testers ka primary contact hai, cycle chat par milta hai; testers ki help, saare bug reports, test cases review aur zarurat ho to problems Test Engineer ko escalate. Duties (8): testers se communicate; issue reports aur test cases timely triage; TE ko assigned duties me support; overview review karke issues TE ko escalate; product ko shortly test karna taaki koi blocker na ho; general cycle progress aur chat monitor; testers ke questions/problems me help; bug disputes review karke recommendations. Testers TTL se expect kar sakte hain: helpful, polite, patient, responsive; bugs aur test cases timely review; cycle ke questions ka answer jo the platform Terms of Use ke andar ho; private chats sirf personal topics ke liye jo general chat me discuss nahi ho sakte. Expect nahi kar sakte: payout ke questions/issues TTL se nahi, TE ya TSM se poocho; testers ke request par bugs/test cases review ya approve nahi honge; TTL se questions sirf cycle chat me; dusre contact methods tabhi jab TE ya TSM allow kare.
qs.b: The TTL is the testers' primary contact through the cycle chat; they triage bug reports and test cases in a timely manner, monitor progress, check the product for blockers, help testers and review bug disputes, escalating to the TE when needed. Testers can expect polite, timely help, but payout questions go to the TE or TSM, not the TTL. Work will not be approved on request, and questions should be asked only in the cycle chat unless the TE or TSM allows another channel.
qs.t: TTL = chat ka dost; payout ka sawaal TTL se nahi, TE/TSM se.

qs.q: What are the responsibilities of the Test Engineer (TE) and the Testing Services Manager (TSM)?
qs.s: Lesson 3: TE = test cycles build aur manage karte hain, testing team assemble karte hain, overall execution ke responsible, customer ke liye best outcome ensure. TE duties (11): test cycles setup; cycle progress monitor; community test teams recruit; testing aur triage schedule ke hisaab se progress ensure; testers ke issues resolve aur zarurat ho to TSM ko escalate; disputed issues resolve; test cases likhna aur adjust karna; SRS likhna; cycle ko track par laane ke liye pre-defined actions; TSM ke saath strategic goals; kuch projects me TTL ki tarah kaam. TSM = client ke saath directly kaam, TTLs aur TEs ki team manage karke client ki testing, feedback, research needs ka solution; test cycle me financial decisions ke responsible. TSM duties (7): TEs ke saath test strategies develop; TEs, TTLs, DTs aur TCWs ki teams manage; account finances monitor aur payouts handle; testing customer expectations meet kare; TEs ko directions; account spending monitor; payments process aur approve.
qs.b: The Test Engineer sets up and monitors cycles, recruits the test team, keeps testing and triage on schedule, resolves disputed issues, writes and adjusts test cases and writes SRS surveys, sometimes acting as TTL. The Testing Services Manager works directly with the client, develops test strategy with TEs, manages TEs, TTLs, DTs and TCWs, and owns the financial side: monitoring spending, handling payouts and approving payments.
qs.t: TE = cycle ka builder + disputes; TSM = client + paisa.

qs.q: What is the escalation path on the platform when you do not get a response?
qs.s: Lesson 3 Scenarios: TTL se time par answer nahi mila (ya overview ke team contact information me diye time frame me nahi) to cycle ke TE ko email karo; TE ka email team contact information section me hai; phir TE ke response ka wait karo. TE ne specified timeframe me reply nahi kiya to TSM ko contact karo; TSM email bhi team contact information section me. TE ya TSM ko email karte waqt clear explanation aur saari zaroori info do: Cycle ID, Cycle name, Tester ID, Bug report ID, Test Case ID, etc. TSM ne bhi respond nahi kiya (rare): pehle recheck karo ki query the platform Terms of Use ke according hai; hai aur phir bhi response nahi to Tester Support: the platform support sitecsp > Request Support > Request Category me 'Test Cycle Issues'. Support ticket me bhi same info (Cycle ID, Cycle name, Tester ID, Bug report ID, Test Case ID etc.). Lesson 6 add karta hai: TSM sirf tab contact karo jab payout issue ho, emergency ho, ya TE se expected reply time me reply na mile (escalation rules ke hisaab se).
qs.b: I first ask the TTL in the cycle chat. If there is no answer within the time frame in the Team Contact Information, I email the cycle's TE, and if the TE does not reply in time I contact the TSM, whose email is also in that section. If even the TSM does not respond and my query follows the Terms of Use, I open a Tester Support ticket under 'Test Cycle Issues'. Every email includes the cycle ID and name, my tester ID and the relevant bug or test case IDs.
qs.t: TTL -> TE -> TSM -> Tester Support (Test Cycle Issues); IDs hamesha saath.

qs.q: How should a tester handle unfair rejections, high-severity bugs approved with low value, and Won't Fix approvals?
qs.s: Lesson 3 scenarios: Customer ne bugs fairly ya unfairly reject kiye: invalid bugs customer reasonably reject karta hai; rejection reason check karo; disagree ho to politely dispute karne ka haq hai. Unfair rejection lage to escalate karne se pehle rejection reasons check karo; confirm hone par screenshots/videos ka evidence collect karo aur TE ko email karke unfair rejection escalate karo; reply na mile to TSM; wo discuss karke solution denge. High-severity issue low value par approve hua: bug kitna valuable hai ye customer decide karta hai, hamare control me nahi. Phir bhi TE ko escalate kar sakte ho; pehle report recheck karo ki wo high severity me categorized hai aur cycle overview ke focus me hai (jaise crash issue); supporting evidence collect karo; attachments ke saath TE ko email; wo action lenge aur feedback denge. Won't Fix (WNF): issue valid hai lekin customer usko fix karne me time/effort nahi lagayega, dusre issues par focus. Agar bahut saare issues WNF accept ho rahe hain jabki wo overview ke testing focus me hain, test case steps se related hain ya blocking issues hain, to TE se confirm karo ki assessment sahi hua ya nahi.
qs.b: If I think a rejection is unfair, I first read the rejection reason, then politely dispute or email the TE with screenshot or video evidence, escalating to the TSM if there is no reply. Bug value is the customer's decision, but if a high-severity in-focus issue such as a crash got low value, I recheck the report and send evidence to the TE. Won't Fix means the issue is valid but the customer will not fix it; if many in-focus or blocking issues get WNF, I ask the TE to confirm the assessment.
qs.t: Reason padho -> evidence lo -> TE ko email; value customer ka faisla.

qs.q: What happens if issues are not reviewed for a long time, or a test case is unclaimed or rejected without a reason?
qs.s: Lesson 3: Issues lambe time tak approve/reject nahi hue: cycle lock hone ke baad up to 15 days wait karo; cycle automatically close hoga aur issues TTL recommendation ke basis par automatically approve ya reject ho jayenge. Ye test case par bhi apply hota hai. Reviews: cycle close hone tak check nahi hue to sab accept ho jayenge. Cycle lock ke baad bhi issues check nahi hue ya New status me hain to TE ko batao, koi unforeseen issue ho sakta hai. Test case bina reason unclaim/reject hua jabki progress ki thi ya instructions ke hisaab se sahi complete kiya: TE ko email karo. Possible reasons (4): slot allotted time me submit nahi hua to automatically unclaim; galti se unclaim ya reject; test case poorly executed tha lekin team reason dalna bhool gayi; test case me updates aaye aur TE/TSM ne saare test cases unclaim kar diye bina clear reason; is par announcement expect karo, naya claim karne ko kaha ja sakta hai.
qs.b: After a cycle locks, I can wait up to 15 days; the cycle then closes automatically and pending issues and test cases are approved or rejected based on the TTL's recommendation, while unchecked reviews are all accepted. If issues are still in New status after the lock, I let the TE know. If a test case is unclaimed or rejected without a reason, I email the TE; common causes are missing the allotted submission time, a mistake, a missing rejection note, or a test case update that unclaimed everyone.
qs.t: Lock ke baad 15 din; TTL recommendation se auto approve/reject; reviews sab accept.

qs.q: How should a tester handle blocking issues, one-time issues, issues that fix themselves, and being asked to discard a reproducible bug?
qs.s: Lesson 3 scenarios: Product problem se testing block: TTL ko batao, wo TE/TSM ko escalate karenge; workaround dhundhne ki koshish karo aur team ko batao. One-time issues: proof (video aur logs) collect ho gaya to report kar sakte ho chahe dobara reproduce karna mushkil ho; example: recording karte hue reproduce kar rahe the aur app achanak crash ho gayi, video aur logs hain to report karo. Pehle check karo ki one-time/non-reproducible issues OOS section me listed nahi hain, TTL se confirm kar sakte ho. Issue apne aap fix ho gaya ya temporary tha: agar issue review hone se pehle notice kiya to discard kar sakte ho; reproduction maangne ke baad notice kiya to issue ke Messages tab se TTL ko batao ki ab reproducible nahi. Reproducible tha lekin discard karne ko kaha gaya: report karte waqt valid aur reproducible tha to TE ko reconsider karne ko bolo. Lekin report reject ho sakta hai kyunki temporary website/app issue ya aapke device/browser se related ho sakta hai; confident ho ki aisa nahi hai to evidence collect karke TE ko investigate ke liye report karo. Customer ne galat build diya ya new build test karne ko kaha aur purane reported bugs new build me reproducible nahi: ye aapki galti nahi, TE ko inform karo, aur reject hone par dispute kar sakte ho.
qs.b: When the product blocks testing, I inform the TTL, who escalates to the TE or TSM, and I look for a workaround. A one-time issue can be reported if I captured a video and logs, provided non-reproducible issues are not out of scope, which I can confirm with the TTL. If an issue disappears before review I discard it; if I notice after a reproduction request, I tell the TTL through the Messages tab. If bugs were rejected because the customer supplied a wrong or new build, I can inform the TE and dispute.
qs.t: One-time bug = video + logs ho to report; khud theek hua = discard ya Messages tab.

qs.q: How can you verify that an email really comes from the platform, and how do you report a suspicious one?
qs.s: Lesson 3: Email legit hai ya nahi check karne ke liye sender ka email address dekho: email kholo aur name ke paas sender email dekho, ya down arrow icon click karke detailed info me 'from' line check karo. The platform sirf in domains se email bhejta hai: the platform's own official domains (listed in the course). Example: us@the platform website ka domain the platform website hai, to legit. Domain in me se nahi hai to pakka legit nahi. Report karne ke liye: the platform support sitecsp > Request Support > Request Category > Potential Cheating/Fraud/Misbehaviour > form bharo. Aur info ke liye Tester Security Course. Useful Courses to Review (Lesson 3 end): the platform Basics, Testing Basics, the platform Cycle Process, Slots, Test Cases and Reviews, Bug Reports.
qs.b: I check the sender address next to the name or in the 'from' line. The platform sends email only from the platform website, m.the platform website, the company's domain and the company's email domain, so anything else is not legitimate. I report suspicious emails through the support portal under Request Support, category 'Potential Cheating/Fraud/Misbehaviour', and the Tester Security Course has more detail.
qs.t: Sirf 4 domain: platform, platform mail, company, company mail.

qs.q: How do you build a positive reputation as a tester on the platform?
qs.s: Lesson 4: Positive reputation tester ki success ka important part hai. Projects setup aur manage karne wale Test Engineers un testers par rely karte hain jo bugs report, test cases complete aur project chat room me participate karte hain. Consistently contribute karne wale testers reliable maane jaate hain aur baar baar projects me invite hote hain. Shuruaat aise karo: project overview ke instructions follow karo; quality bug reports likho; test cases sahi aur time par complete karo; TTL ya TE ke messages ka jaldi jawab do. 3 specific cheezein: Pay attention to details, Be reliable, Submit quality work. Pay attention to details = project overview ke saare instructions padho aur follow karo; project announcements aur chat room messages padh ke updates/changes se aware raho. Be reliable = accept kiye projects me actively participate karo; kaam sahi aur time par complete karo. Submit quality work = project requirements follow karne wali high value bug reports; project ki time limit me useful information ke saath test cases aur reviews complete karo. Har project invitation reputation build karne ka mauka hai.
qs.b: Test Engineers keep inviting testers who contribute consistently. I build reputation in three ways: paying attention to details by following the overview and reading announcements and chat updates, being reliable by actively participating and finishing work correctly and on time, and submitting quality work through high-value bug reports and useful test cases and reviews within the time limit. Responding quickly to the TTL or TE also helps.
qs.t: Reputation = Details + Reliable + Quality (DRQ).

qs.q: What are the common bug title mistakes in Academy cycles and how do you avoid them?
qs.s: Lesson 5 (Most Common Mistakes In Academy Practice Cycles) ka aim: valid, error-free bug reports aur cycle instructions follow karna sikhana. Title wali galtiyan: 1) Issue title me galat area: browser tab me page name check karo; breadcrumb (agar hai) se area pehchano; Common Website Elements and Pages lesson dekho; common areas ke examples: Login, Register, Profile or Account, Cart, Blog, Checkout, Help, Settings; app me current area ke liye navigation menu ya tabs check karo. 2) Title me inadequate/vague description: issue aise samjhao ki report khole bina sirf padh ke samajh aaye; clarity brevity se zyada important; link, video ya item ho to naam likho, example: An error page opens after clicking on the 'T-Shirt' link in the product description. 3) Issue type galat identify karna: bug types review karo; functionality se related ya affect karta hai to 'Functional' select karo.
qs.b: For the title area I check the page name in the browser tab, the breadcrumb, or the app's navigation menu and tabs, using common areas such as Login, Register, Cart, Checkout or Settings. The description must be clear enough to understand without opening the report, with clarity taking precedence over brevity, and naming the specific link or item, for example 'An error page opens after clicking on the T-Shirt link in the product description'. If the issue affects functionality, the type should be Functional.
qs.t: Area tab/breadcrumb se, naam quote karo, clarity > brevity.

qs.q: What mistakes do testers make in the Action Performed steps and how should they be written?
qs.s: Lesson 5 Action Performed wali galtiyan: 1) Ek step me ek se zyada action: har step me sirf ek action, clear aur follow karne me easy; swipe/scroll down aur tap/click ko do steps me divide karna better; step me extra info chahiye to parentheses ya brackets, example: Open the 'Casual Jacket' item (it's located in the second row of the results). 2) Invalid URL: overview me diya test URL copy karo; URL ko kisi symbol me enclose mat karo. 3) Preconditions use nahi karna: issue reproduce karne ki conditions step 1 se pehle precondition ke roop me; example: 'Precondition: The user has logged in. 1. Open the platform app.'; saare steps preconditions me mat daalo, sirf zarurat par. Academy Challenge tip: Action Performed me step numbers sahi order me hon.
qs.b: Each step should contain exactly one action, so scrolling and tapping become two steps, and extra detail goes in parentheses. The first step uses the test URL copied from the overview without wrapping it in any symbol. Conditions needed to reproduce, such as 'The user has logged in', go in a precondition before step 1, but not every step should become a precondition, and step numbers must be in the correct order.
qs.t: Ek step = ek action; URL nanga copy karo; precondition sirf zaroori.

qs.q: What are the common mistakes with actual/expected results and attachments, and what formats are required in Academy?
qs.s: Lesson 5: Unclear actual aur expected results: reproduction steps ke baad kya expect karna hai aur kya hota hai clearly samjhao; 'Not working properly' avoid karo, kyunki ye issue explain nahi karta; test case step se report kar rahe ho to template hata kar cycle ke Issue Reporting Instructions ke hisaab se khud results likho. Required attachments missing: report karne se pehle hamesha Issue Reporting Instructions section check karo; submit se pehle saare required attachments do; doubt ho to cycle chat me TTL se poocho; doosron se pehle report karne ke liye jaanbujh kar incomplete/galat attachments dena the platform Terms of Use ke against hai, DNFI rejection aur current aur upcoming cycles se removal ho sakta hai. Wrong format (e.g. log, m4v): format requirements Issue Reporting Instructions me check karo. Academy me: Screenshots .jpg ya .png; Screen recording .mp4; Console/device logs .txt. Galat format upload hua to jaldi fix karo; uploaded attachments open hone me error to nahi, recheck karo; upload me error aaye to dusra browser try karo aur cache, cookies clear karo.
qs.b: Actual and expected results must clearly describe what should happen and what actually happens; phrases like 'not working properly' are not acceptable, and test case templates must be replaced with my own wording. I always check the Issue Reporting Instructions and attach everything required, because deliberately submitting incomplete attachments to report faster violates the Terms of Use and can lead to a DNFI rejection and removal from cycles. In the Academy, screenshots must be .jpg or .png, screen recordings .mp4 and logs .txt.
qs.t: Academy formats: photo jpg/png, video mp4, log txt.

qs.q: What are the rules for screen recordings in the platform bug reports?
qs.s: Lesson 5 'Screen recording not starting from the homepage or not matching the action performed' ke tips: Issue Reporting Instructions ke andar screen recording ke instructions padho. Agar poore reproduction steps dikhana required hai to homepage se start karo aur action performed se match karo. Recording me unnecessary steps mat karo. The platform platform recording me mat dikhao, GDPR violation se bachne ke liye, kyunki usme PII ho sakta hai. Cycle ke testing scope se unrelated dusre projects ya products mat dikhao. Background noise hatane ke liye microphone mute rakho (jab tak narrate nahi karna). Academy Challenge tip (logs): logs reproduce karte waqt collect karna shuru karo aur homepage se start karo; Charles logs sirf required ho tab upload karo.
qs.b: I follow the recording instructions in the Issue Reporting Instructions; when the full reproduction is required I start from the homepage and match the action performed steps without extra steps. I never show the platform platform, because it may contain PII and would violate GDPR, and I never show unrelated projects or products. The microphone stays muted unless I am narrating.
qs.t: Homepage se shuru, the platform screen nahi (GDPR), mic mute.

qs.q: What extra tips help avoid rejection in Academy Challenge cycles?
qs.s: Lesson 5 'Academy Challenge Practice Cycles' (note: Academy Challenge cycles me galtiyon wale bug reports reject hote hain): Action Performed: step numbers sahi order me. Source: test case steps se related issue ho to test case se report karo; test case flow se report nahi kiya to source option me 'Structured' select karo. Logs: Charles logs sirf required ho tab upload; zarurat na ho to mat daalo. Logs: issue reproduce karte waqt logs collect karna start karo aur homepage se start karo. Custom Fields: diye instructions aur specified format ke hisaab se bharo. Duplicates and Known issues: hamesha already reported aur known issues check karo; cycle me known issues file attached hai ya nahi dekho. Duplicates: same root cause wale issues duplicate maane jaate hain; example: keyword search ke baad incorrect results, alag keywords se bhi ho to same issue. Out Of Scope: OOS section dhyan se review karo; har cycle ki apni requirements, testing start se pehle check karo.
qs.b: In Academy Challenge cycles any mistake in the report leads to rejection, so I keep step numbers in order, report test-case-related issues from the test case, and otherwise choose 'Structured' as the source. I upload Charles logs only when required, start logs from the homepage while reproducing, and fill custom fields in the specified format. I check reported and known issues, remembering that issues with the same root cause are duplicates, and review the Out of Scope section before testing.
qs.t: Same root cause = duplicate; test case flow nahi to Source = Structured.

qs.q: How should a tester control anger when facing a frustrating rejection or decision?
qs.s: Lesson 6: Achha tester calm aur collected rehta hai, lekin mistreat hone par upset hona allowed hai. Course ka goal: anger trigger karne wali situations handle karna taaki the platform Terms of Use violate na ho (jisse account suspension ya termination ho sakta hai). Examples: issue WAD ki jagah 'Other' se reject hua jo rating affect karta hai; test case par bahut time lagaya aur bina clear reason reject/unclaim hua. Avoid Doing Anything When Angry: anger me turant kuch karne ka mann karta hai jo regret dega aur doosron ko hurt karega; keyboard se haath hatao aur khade ho jao. Take a Timeout: break lo jab tak better feel na ho; physical activity, deep breaths, chehra dhona. Identify and Understand the Issue: sochke dekho cause kya hai: TTL ya TE ka response dekh ke gussa aaya? TE decision se agree nahi? Instruction galat samjha aur recheck karke irritate hue? Negative thoughts hatao; 'It should or must be like this' wali soch chhodo; khud se poocho jo kehne wale ho wo true, valid, relevant, fundamental hai ya nahi. Koi bhi outcome accept karne ko ready raho. Cycle overview, test case, slot instructions dobara padh ke reevaluate karo. Ye bhi samjho (5 points): har cycle/project ki apni requirements; galti se instructions galat execute kiye to redo zaroori; galti se galat slot claim kiya to unclaim zaroori kyunki invalid results; the platform Terms of Use follow karna must, violation se account termination; sabke saath respect, hamesha professional aur polite.
qs.b: When something frustrates me, I avoid acting while angry, step away from the keyboard and take a break until I am calm. Then I identify the real cause and re-read the overview, test case and slot instructions to see the decision from the other side. I remember that each cycle has its own requirements, that I must redo wrongly executed tests or unclaim a wrong slot, and that violating the Terms of Use can end in account termination.
qs.t: Ruko -> break lo -> overview dobara padho -> phir bolo.

qs.q: After calming down, how should a tester dispute or escalate, and what should they avoid?
qs.s: Lesson 6: Avoid: apni concerns/disagreement cycle chat room, issue report ke messages tab, test cases ya reviews me discuss mat karo; community me doosron ka agreement mat dhundho; bina samjhe seedha TSM ya usse upar escalate mat karo. Ye situation complicate karta hai aur heated discussion me Terms of Use violate ho sakta hai. Key: achha communication, jo tabhi possible jab anger control me ho. Possible Issues and Solutions: message/decision instructions se aligned nahi lage to: issue report se related ho to report dispute karo; dusri problem ho (test cases ya reviews bina clear reason reject/unclaim, TTL misconduct etc.) to TE ko escalate. Rejection reason check karo, sirf rejection type nahi. Escalation Team Contact Information ke escalation rules ke hisaab se pehle TE ko; escalation tab tak avoid karo jab tak urgent na ho ya higher-up ki help na chahiye. Taiyari: supporting info aur screenshots gather karo; testing website/app, documentation check karo. TE email cycle overview me milega; dusre cycles ke TE emails use mat karo. Email rules (6): subject me cycle ID; polite aur professional; concern clearly, issue par focus; bina point ke lamba mat khincho; recheck karo ki clear hai; dusre TEs ya TSMs ko CC ya BCC mat karo. TSM sirf tab: payout issue, emergency, ya TE se expected reply time me reply nahi mila. Feedback email me share kar sakte ho, processes improve karne me help karta hai.
qs.b: I never argue in the cycle chat, the issue Messages tab or reviews, and I don't rally other testers or jump straight to the TSM. If I disagree with a rejection reason, not just its type, I dispute the report; for other problems such as unexplained test case rejections or TTL misconduct, I email the cycle's TE with evidence. The email has the cycle ID in the subject, is polite, clear and focused, and is not CC'd or BCC'd to other TEs or TSMs. The TSM is contacted only for payout issues, emergencies or when the TE has not replied in time.
qs.t: Report = dispute; baaki = TE email (subject me Cycle ID, no CC/BCC).

qs.q: What are the possible outcomes of a dispute or escalation, and how should a tester respond?
qs.s: Lesson 6 Possible Outcomes: outcome teen tarah ka: accepted, rejected, ya future consideration and improvement. Sab points accept nahi honge aur kuch feedback apply hone me time lagega. Calm aur rational raho; 'I am always right' wali soch nahi. Overcome na ho to pehle aur doosre point par wapas jao ya yahin ruk jao kyunki mental health affect ho sakti hai. Dispute rejected: rejection reason dhyan se padho; dispute ke baad zyada detailed reason milna expected hai; reason reasonable hai to accept karke move on; isse better tester bante ho aur customer ke liye similar issue report karne se bachte ho. Email: TE ka response dhyan se padho; aapki taraf se kuch karna hai aur willing ho to help karo; unki end par resolve hoga to cycle duration me ya future me (agar consider hua) wait karo. Hamesha professional communication; temper aaye to reply se pehle cool down; communication ek hi thread me rakho, TE ke message ka jawab dene ke liye naya email thread mat banao. Note: emergency hai aur TE ya TSM se expected time me reply nahi mila to Tester Support: Tester Support Portal > Request Support > request category me Test Cycle Issues > form complete. Be Proud of Yourself: anger appropriately handle karna bada accomplishment hai; professional bante ho aur community better banti hai.
qs.b: A dispute or escalation can end in acceptance, rejection, or future consideration and improvement. If a dispute is rejected, I read the more detailed reason and, if it is reasonable, accept it and move on, which helps me avoid similar reports. I reply to the TE in the same email thread, stay professional, and use Tester Support under 'Test Cycle Issues' only for an emergency when neither the TE nor the TSM replied in time.
qs.t: 3 outcomes: Accept, Reject, Future; same thread me reply.

qs.q: How do you keep written communication concise and clear in bug reports and messages?
qs.s: Lesson 7 (Effective Written Communication): kaam customer aur project team dono ko easily samajh aana chahiye. Concise aur clear likho: point jaldi pahunche, confusion na ho, reader ka attention rahe. Avoid: uncommon abbreviations; vague words jaise 'Can't, unable, or not working'; sentence lamba karne ke liye irrelevant info. Example 1: galat: 'After filtering the results, some products are not displayed even though the filter shows that there are 25 results but there are only 23 products on the page' (lagta hai aur results hain jo dikh nahi rahe, user confuse). Sahi: 'There are only 23 products after filtering the search results using the Black color filter option even though it shows 25 beside the filter option.' Example 2: galat: 'Can't register an account'; 'Unable to checkout'; 'Search is not working'. Sahi (kya ho raha hai batao): 'An error page opens after tapping on the sign-up button'; 'An infinite loading occurs after tapping on the checkout button'; 'The homepage is reloaded after clicking on the search suggestions'. Note: iska matlab har message ko jitna ho sake chhota karna nahi; issue clearly samjhao bina unnecessary info aur redundancy ke. Customer ko kaam accept karne ya jaldi fix karne ke liye convince/push mat karo.
qs.b: Clear writing describes exactly what happens instead of using vague words like 'can't', 'unable' or 'not working'. For example, instead of 'Unable to checkout' I write 'An infinite loading occurs after tapping on the checkout button'. I avoid uncommon abbreviations and irrelevant details, but concise does not mean as short as possible; it means clear without redundancy, and without pushing the customer to accept or fix the issue.
qs.t: 'Not working' mat likho; jo dikh raha hai wahi likho.

qs.q: How should a written message be structured, and what does a professional tone look like?
qs.s: Lesson 7: Structure and Organization: logical sequence; introduction, phir supporting details, phir conclusion ya actionable suggestions. Galat: 'I noticed that the performance was not good at all as it took a lot of time to make an account. Moreover, the app crashed during the process which can frustrate the user.' Sahi: registration me slowdown; sign-up page fully load hone me around 1 minute; fields bhar ke sign-up tap kiya to infinite loading; loading ke dauraan screen tap ki to app crash; app reopen karke login ho gaya. Step by step sequential batane se reader pehli baar me samajhta hai. Professional Tone: topic, audience aur situation ke hisaab se sahi tone; professional tone = respectful, polite, objective; tense situation me bhi overly emotional ya aggressive nahi; galat tone se misinterpretation ya impolite lag sakta hai; offensive language kabhi nahi. Positive atmosphere, collaboration, trust aur respect. Example 1: galat: 'I can't open the test app at all. What do you expect me to test this way?' Sahi: 'I would like to inform you that the test app can't be opened. I already tried opening it on other devices but nothing worked. It would be helpful if you could take a look at it and provide another app file. Thanks'. Example 2: galat: 'The app performance seems like a joke...' Sahi: performance expected se slow tha, section kholne me around a minute wait; performance improvement ko main focus banana helpful hoga smoother user experience ke liye.
qs.b: I structure messages with an introduction, supporting details in sequence, and a conclusion or suggestion, for example describing a slow sign-up page, the infinite loading and then the crash in order. My tone stays respectful, polite and objective even in tense situations, and I never use offensive language. Instead of 'What do you expect me to test this way?', I write that the app cannot be opened on other devices either and politely ask for another app file.
qs.t: Intro -> details -> conclusion; tone = respectful, polite, objective.

qs.q: Why is proofreading important for testers, and what should you check?
qs.s: Lesson 7 Proofreading: final step; message clear aur mistakes-free ho. Check karo: spelling, grammar, punctuation, formatting; message wahi kehta hai jo kehna chahte the; padh ke khud se poocho reader samjhega ya nahi. Time lagta hai lekin message clear aur professional banta hai, reader ke time ki respect, miscommunication kam, credibility badhti hai. Example 1: galat: 'I couldnt find the feature mention in the test case step1 and 3. I have restrasted and reinstall the app but still the same'. Sahi: 'I couldn't find the feature mentioned in the test case steps 1 and 3. I have restarted and reinstalled the app but I still couldn't find it. Could you please confirm if the feature is available?' Example 2: galat: 'The app version attach in the cycle overview is wrong. I can't perform test case steps this way.' Sahi: 'I would like to inform you that the app version attached in the cycle overview does not match the version mentioned in the test case step. Could you please check if the attached app is correct?' Note: achha likha message bhi kabhi misinterpret ho sakta hai, lekin clear likhkar reader ke time ki respect karte hain. Ye skills customers aur the company team ke saath trust banati hain aur future projects ke opportunities badhati hain.
qs.b: Before sending, I proofread for spelling, grammar, punctuation and formatting, and I check that the message says what I intend from the reader's point of view. For example, 'I couldnt find the feature mention in step1' becomes 'I couldn't find the feature mentioned in steps 1 and 3; could you please confirm if it is available?' Proofreading shows respect for the reader's time, reduces miscommunication and builds credibility with customers and the company team.
qs.t: Bhejne se pehle ek baar reader ban ke padho.

qs.q: What is a true review on the platform, and how can using AI to write feedback hurt a tester?
qs.s: Lesson 8 (The impact of AI on testers): AI sabke liye free hai, reviews, usability studies, feedback, survey answers me use karne ka temptation hota hai. True Review / Opinion / Feedback / Usability Study = honest, personal, aapke genuine experience par based; tester ne app, website, platform ya hardware product use karte waqt kya dekha, mehsoos kiya aur socha. Customers isi liye services use karte hain; real human insights chahiye jo surface-level se aage jaayein. Authentic feedback real improvement laata hai; AI-written ya personal engagement ke bina feedback apna purpose fail karta hai. Consequences (3): Damaged Credibility = TE, TTL ya customer ko feedback vague, AI-written, generic, robotic ya test environment se disconnected lage to trust kho dete hain; negative reputation se kam project invitations. Reduced Opportunities = high-quality insightful feedback top testers ko alag karta hai; AI responses se aapki value ghatti hai; customer ko AI feedback chahiye to wo khud AI use kar lenge, aap par kyun rely karein? Terms and Conditions = sab testers ko the platform Terms of Use aur AI Guidelines follow karni hain; violation se account termination ho sakta hai; the platform par generative AI ki acceptable use policy review karo.
qs.b: A true review is honest, personal and based on my genuine experience of what I saw, felt and thought while using the product, which is exactly what customers pay for. If feedback looks vague, generic or AI-written, the TE, TTL or customer loses trust, which damages my reputation and reduces invitations. It also makes me replaceable, since the customer could use AI directly, and violating the Terms of Use and AI Guidelines can lead to account termination.
qs.t: Customer ko AI chahiye hota to tumhe kyun bulata?

qs.q: Why shouldn't testers rely on AI tools like ChatGPT to write reviews or survey answers?
qs.s: Lesson 8: the platform authentic, insightful feedback deliver karta hai, lekin trend aaya hai ki users AI se reviews aur open-ended survey answers likhwa rahe hain. ChatGPT jaise tools daily life me useful, lekin tester ki insights replace karna dangerous shortcut hai. Why so? It's Not Personal = AI overly polished text banata hai, aapka actual experience replicate nahi kar sakta; customers jaanna chahte hain aapko kya confusing, delightful ya frustrating laga, machine ka generic response nahi. It Can Mislead Customers = AI feedback real issues miss kar sakta hai ya functionality ki galat taareef kar sakta hai; customer galat direction me jaata hai, time aur resources waste, the platform platform par bura asar. Why Honest Feedback Matters = har usability survey/review ka end goal customers ko aise products banane me help karna jo users love karein; actual experience wala feedback value add karta hai, jo sirf real human kar sakta hai. AI button kaam na karne ya page loading par frustration feel nahi kar sakta, feature smooth chalne par joy nahi, aur interface overwhelmed ya empowered kaise feel karata hai ye subtle baatein explain nahi kar sakta. Isliye honest feedback irreplaceable hai.
qs.b: AI-written feedback is not personal; it produces polished generic text and cannot describe what I actually found confusing, delightful or frustrating. It can also mislead customers by missing real issues or falsely praising functionality, wasting their time and reflecting poorly on the platform. Honest feedback from real experience is irreplaceable because only a human feels the frustration of a broken button or the subtle way an interface makes them feel.
qs.t: AI ko gussa ya khushi feel nahi hoti; tumhe hoti hai, wahi likho.

topics.intro: platform platform par smart tester banne ke tips: glossary, instructions padhna, team roles, escalation, common mistakes, communication aur AI rules.

topics.name: Screenshots

qs.q: What is a screenshot and why does it matter in a bug report?
qs.s: Screenshot (screen capture) computer ya mobile screen par dikh rahe data ki image hoti hai. Bug report me tester ko jo essential attachments lagane hote hain, unme screenshot sabse important me se ek hai. Aage ke lessons me alag OS par screenshot lena sikhaya gaya hai, par pehle rules samajhne hain.
qs.b: A screenshot, or screen capture, is an image of what is displayed on a computer or mobile screen. It is one of the essential attachments a tester must add to a bug report because it shows the defect visually.
qs.t: Screenshot = bug ka photo saboot.

qs.q: What rules must a screenshot follow on the platform?
qs.s: 6 rules: (1) Highlight: hamesha bug ko red ya yellow rectangle, circle ya arrow se mark karo. (2) JPG or PNG format: sirf .jpg ya .png me save karo. (3) Hand drawing tool mat use karo: mouse/hand drawing se highlight nahi, proper shape (rectangle/circle) use karo. (4) Complete screen capture karo: sirf bug ya portion nahi, poori device screen chahiye, website test kar rahe ho to browser URL bar bhi. (5) Unnecessary tabs close karo: testing website se unrelated browser tabs hide/close karo (yeh rule sirf computer browser testing par lagta hai). (6) Upright orientation: har screenshot upright hona chahiye. Note: ek bug report me 2 se zyada screenshots upload mat karo.
qs.b: A screenshot must highlight the bug with a red or yellow rectangle, circle or arrow, be saved as .jpg or .png, avoid freehand drawing, capture the entire screen including the URL bar for websites, hide unrelated browser tabs on desktop, and be in upright orientation. Also, no more than two screenshots should be uploaded in one bug report.
qs.t: H-J-H-C-C-U: Highlight, JPG/PNG, no Hand-draw, Complete screen, Close tabs, Upright; max 2.

qs.q: How do you take and highlight a screenshot on Windows using Windows + PrintScreen or PrintScreen with Paint?
qs.s: Windows + PrintScreen ek saath dabao to screenshot file ban jaati hai, default location Pictures ke andar Screenshots folder. Fast tarika (5 steps): 1) sirf PrintScreen dabao, screenshot clipboard me copy hota hai (nayi file nahi banti). 2) Paint kholo, Ctrl+V. 3) Rectangle ya circle shape chuno, color red ya yellow. 4) Bug ke around shape draw karo. 5) Ctrl+S ya File > Save se save karo.
qs.b: Pressing Windows + PrintScreen saves a full-screen capture to Pictures > Screenshots. A faster way is to press PrintScreen to copy it to the clipboard, paste it into Paint with Ctrl+V, draw a red or yellow rectangle or circle around the bug, and save with Ctrl+S.
qs.t: PrtSc -> Paint -> Ctrl+V -> red box -> Ctrl+S.

qs.q: How do you use Windows + Shift + S (Snipping Tool) to capture a bug screenshot?
qs.s: Windows + Shift + S file save nahi karta, clipboard me copy karta hai, isliye Paint jaise editor me paste karna padta hai. Steps: 1) Windows+Shift+S dabao. 2) Upar snipping mode chuno: Window Snip (3rd icon) agar taskbar exclude karna hai, Fullscreen Snip (4th icon) agar poori screen chahiye. 3) Window Snip chuna hai to us window par click karo. 4) Paint kholo, CTRL+V. 5) Rectangle/circle, red ya yellow. 6) Issue mark karo. 7) CTRL+S ya File > Save. 8) File rename karo. 9) Location select karke Save.
qs.b: Windows + Shift + S copies a snip to the clipboard rather than saving a file. I choose Window Snip, the third icon, to exclude the taskbar or Fullscreen Snip, the fourth icon, for the whole screen, then paste into Paint, highlight the bug with a red or yellow shape, and save and rename the file.
qs.t: Win+Shift+S: 3rd = Window, 4th = Fullscreen, phir Paint.

qs.q: How do you capture and annotate screenshots with ShareX on Windows?
qs.s: ShareX special software hai capture + annotate ke liye. Steps: 1) ShareX download aur install karo. 2) ShareX kholo, After capture tasks me jao: Upload image to host deselect karo aur Open in image editor select karo. 3) Screenshot lo: Capture > Fullscreen click karo, ya PrintScreen key dabao. 4) Image editor apne aap khulega, rectangle/circle draw karo aur Enter dabake save karo. Default location: Documents ke andar ShareX\Screenshots folder. Note: Upload image to host option off hona hi chahiye.
qs.b: In ShareX I open After capture tasks, turn off Upload image to host and turn on Open in image editor. Then I capture with Capture > Fullscreen or the PrintScreen key, draw a rectangle or circle in the editor and press Enter to save; files go to Documents > ShareX > Screenshots.
qs.t: ShareX: upload OFF, editor ON.

qs.q: How do you take a screenshot with the Xbox Game Bar on Windows?
qs.s: Pehle enable karo: Windows+S se search me Xbox Game Bar likho, Enable Xbox Game Bar select karke enable karo; ya Settings > Gaming > Xbox Game Bar toggle on. Yeh method file save karta hai aur taskbar exclude karta hai. Use: 1) Windows+G se Game Bar kholo. 2) Camera icon par click (ya seedha Windows+Alt+PrintScreen bina Game Bar khole). 3) Notification aayega, click karke screenshot dekho. 4) Open file location, phir Continue. 5) File rename aur move karo. 6) Paint jaise editor me kholo. 7) Rectangle/circle, red ya yellow. 8) Issue mark karo. 9) CTRL+S ya File > Save.
qs.b: After enabling Xbox Game Bar from search or Settings > Gaming, I press Windows + G and click the Camera icon, or press Windows + Alt + PrintScreen directly. It saves a file without the taskbar; I then open it in Paint, highlight the issue in red or yellow and save.
qs.t: Win+G camera ya Win+Alt+PrtSc, taskbar gayab.

qs.q: How do you take and highlight a screenshot on macOS?
qs.s: macOS ke built-in tools kaafi hain. Steps: 1) Shift + Command + 3 ek saath press and hold. 2) Screenshot corner me dikhega, edit ke liye click karo. 3) Rectangle ya circle shape chuno. 4) Sahi se highlight karke Done par click karke save. Default location: Desktop. Apple ki references: Take a screenshot on your Mac, Annotate an image.
qs.b: On macOS I press Shift + Command + 3, click the thumbnail that appears in the corner, add a rectangle or circle around the bug and click Done. Screenshots are saved to the desktop by default.
qs.t: Mac: Shift+Cmd+3, Desktop par milega.

qs.q: How do you capture and highlight screenshots on Linux?
qs.s: Notes me suggested tool Flameshot hai. Steps: 1) Terminal me install: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install flameshot. 2) Flameshot normal app ki tarah kholo. 3) Taskbar me Flameshot icon par click. 4) Mouse se complete screen select karo. 5) Neeche tools aayenge, rectangle ya circle chuno. 6) Bug ke around shape draw karo. 7) Save button. Install me problem ho to official installation instructions follow karo.
qs.b: On Linux I use Flameshot, installed with sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install flameshot. I click its taskbar icon, select the complete screen, draw a rectangle or circle around the bug and click Save.
qs.t: Linux = Flameshot (flame se bug jalao).

qs.q: How do you take a screenshot on an Android device?
qs.s: Steps: 1) Jo screen capture karni hai woh kholo. 2) Phone ke hisaab se: Power + Volume Down kuch seconds press and hold; agar na chale to Power button kuch seconds hold karke Screenshot tap karo; dono na chale to manufacturer support site dekho ya google karo. 3) Screenshot gallery ke screenshots folder me milega.
