qs.s: Ye technique input ranges ke edges test karti hai, kyunki coding errors wahin sabse zyada hote hain. Minimum aur maximum valid values, aur unke just inside aur just outside values test karo. Example: valid range 1 to 100. Lower Boundary: 0, 1, 2 (minimum ke just below, exactly at, just above). Upper Boundary: 99, 100, 101 (maximum ke just below, exactly at, just above).
qs.b: Boundary value analysis tests the edges of input ranges, where coding errors are most likely. For a valid range of 1 to 100, I test 0, 1 and 2 at the lower boundary and 99, 100 and 101 at the upper boundary, covering just below, exactly at and just above each limit.
qs.t: Kinare pe bug: 0-1-2 aur 99-100-101.

qs.q: What is Decision Table Testing?
qs.s: Isse Decision-Based Testing bhi kehte hain. Table me alag input combinations aur unke expected outcomes organize karte hain. Ensure karta hai ki saare logic paths aur business rules test ho. Inputs, conditions aur outputs ka clear visualization na ho to important combinations miss ho sakte hain; table se mistakes kam aur complex conditions me system behavior clear. Example: streaming website do conditions pe discount deti hai: subscription duration (1-month, 3-month, 12-month) aur user new hai ya existing member. Table se har combination explicitly test hota hai, jaise New User 3-month plan pe sahi discount paaye, aur Existing User 12-month plan pe galat promotion na paaye.
qs.b: Decision table testing, also called decision-based testing, maps input combinations and their expected outcomes in a table so every logic path and business rule is tested. For example, with discounts based on plan duration of 1, 3 or 12 months and on new versus existing users, the table ensures every combination is checked, such as a new user on a 3-month plan getting the correct discount.
qs.t: Conditions ka table = koi combo miss nahi.

qs.q: What is State Transition Testing?
qs.s: Ye check karta hai ki system ek state se doosri state me specific inputs ya events ke basis pe kaise transition karta hai. Attempts ki ginti ya past actions bhi consider karta hai, taaki specific sequence of events ke baad system sahi respond kare. Aksar state transition diagram banaya jata hai jisme saari possible states, inputs aur transitions map hoti hain. Example: ATM login sirf do failed PIN attempts allow karta hai; teesre consecutive failed attempt pe card block. Test ensure karta hai ki system Active State se Warning State (1 ya 2 fails ke baad) aur finally Blocked State (3 fails ke baad) me sahi jaaye, sirf user actions ke sequence ke basis pe.
qs.b: State transition testing checks how a system moves between states based on inputs, events and the sequence or count of past actions, often using a state transition diagram. For an ATM that allows two failed PIN attempts, I verify it goes from Active to Warning after one or two failures and to Blocked after the third consecutive failure.
qs.t: ATM: Active, Warning (1-2 fail), Blocked (3 fail).

qs.q: What is functional testing focused on, compared to non-functional testing?
qs.s: Software testing broadly do types: Functional aur Non-Functional. Functional Testing har function aur feature ko specified requirements ke hisaab se verify karta hai. Main purpose: software kya karta hai (what). Requirements, user actions aur results ki accuracy se directly related. Typical questions: Does this button work as expected? Can a user successfully log in with valid credentials? Does the search function return the correct results based on the input? Is the data correctly saved after an action? Functional testing types: Unit, Component, Smoke, Sanity, Regression, Ad-hoc, Integration, System, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), Interface, aur Localization Testing (jab functional aspects pe focus ho). Functional testing mainly Black Box techniques pe rely karta hai, yaani testers ko internal code ya system architecture ka knowledge typically nahi chahiye.
qs.b: Functional testing verifies that each function and feature works according to requirements, so it answers what the software does, for example whether a button works, a user can log in or data is saved correctly. It includes unit, component, smoke, sanity, regression, ad-hoc, integration, system, UAT, interface and functional localization testing, and it mainly uses black box techniques that need no knowledge of the internal code.
qs.t: Functional = KYA karta hai, black box.

qs.q: What is non-functional testing and what types does it include?
qs.s: Non-Functional Testing software ki overall quality aur system behavior verify karta hai. Focus: system kaise perform, behave aur operate karta hai alag conditions me (how). Specific functional requirements se directly tied nahi, lekin user experience aur product reliability ke liye crucial. Questions: How fast does the application load? Can the system efficiently handle a large number of concurrent users (e.g., 1,000) without any slowdown? Is the data secure from unauthorized access and cyber threats? How easy is the application to learn and navigate for a brand new user? Key types: Performance Testing (sub-types: Load, Stress, Spike, Endurance), Security Testing, Usability Testing, Reliability Testing, Scalability Testing, Compatibility Testing, aur Localization Testing. Localization ke functional aspects bhi hain, par cultural fit aur linguistic correctness pe focus ki wajah se ye non-functional quality attributes me bhi aata hai, taaki product specific region ya locale ke liye suitable ho.
qs.b: Non-functional testing verifies the overall quality and behavior of the system, meaning how it performs, such as load speed, handling 1,000 concurrent users, security and ease of learning. Key types are performance testing with load, stress, spike and endurance, plus security, usability, reliability, scalability, compatibility and localization. Localization sits in both categories because it also checks cultural fit and linguistic correctness.
qs.t: Non-functional = KAISE chalta hai; Localization dono me.

qs.q: Why is functional testing the foundation of other testing types?
qs.s: 5 benefits: 1) Enables Meaningful Non-Functional Testing: speed ya security test karne se pehle core features kaam karne chahiye; functional stability performance, security aur baaki non-functional tests ka reliable baseline. 2) Identifies Blocker Bugs Early: primary features verify karke critical defects pakadta hai jo aage testing ya deployment rok dete, time aur resources bachte hain. 3) Ensures Basic Usability: functionally correct app basic pathways deti hai, jisse Usability Testing refinement aur experience pe focus kar sake, broken features pe nahi. 4) Provides a Stable Environment for Automation: automated regression tests stable functional requirements pe bante hain; functionality baar-baar toote to automation mushkil aur ineffective. 5) Validates Product Requirements: product apna intended purpose deliver kare aur user needs meet kare, performance ya security se pehle ye primary value hai. Conclusion: functional ensure karta hai software wo kare jo karna chahiye; non-functional ensure karta hai ki wo efficiently, securely aur reliably kare. High-quality product dono me excel karta hai.
qs.b: Functional testing is the foundation because non-functional tests like performance and security only make sense once core features work. It catches blocker bugs early, gives usability testing working pathways to refine, provides the stable base automated regression needs and validates that the product meets its intended purpose. Functional testing ensures the software does the right thing, and non-functional testing ensures it does so efficiently, securely and reliably.
qs.t: Pehle chale, phir tez/safe chale.

topics.intro: Functional testing ke types, SDLC, manual vs automation, scripted vs exploratory, testing techniques aur functional vs non-functional.

topics.name: Introduction to Testing

qs.q: What are the Academy practice test cycles?
qs.s: The Academy practice test cycles (6): 1) Introduction to Testing 2) Computer Testing 3) Mobile Device Testing 4) Charles Proxy Testing 5) Academy Challenge 6) Academy All Stars.
qs.b: The Academy practice cycles are Introduction to Testing, Computer Testing, Mobile Device Testing, Charles Proxy Testing, Academy Challenge and Academy All Stars.
qs.t: Intro, Computer, Mobile, Charles, Challenge, All Stars.

qs.q: What are the benefits of participating in the Academy practice test cycles?
qs.s: 4 benefits: 1) Testers real the platform test cycle ke processes experience aur samajhte hain. 2) Academy courses me seekhi skills apply karte hain: testing, issues report karna, test cases complete karna aur reviews submit karna practice. 3) the Academy team feedback aur suggestions deti hai skills improve karne ke liye. 4) Practice cycles me approved work se time ke saath tester rating badhti hai. Higher tester rating wale testers ko paid test cycles milne ke zyada chances.
qs.b: Practice cycles let testers experience a real the platform cycle and apply what they learned by testing, reporting issues, completing test cases and submitting reviews. The Academy team gives feedback, and approved work raises the tester rating over time, which increases the chances of getting paid cycles.
qs.t: Practice = real cycle ka swaad + feedback + rating badhe.

qs.q: What are the sign-up rules for Academy practice test cycles?
qs.s: Rules: 1) Practice cycle me sign up se pehle pichhle the Academy courses complete karne honge. 2) Pichhla practice cycle pass nahi kiya to agle me sign up nahi. 3) Jo cycle already complete kar liya usme dobara sign up nahi. 4) Quiz pass karne pe blue sign up button activate hota hai. 5) Pichhla practice cycle pass nahi kiya to sign up button locked rehta hai. 6) Academy All Stars cycle me sign up nahi kar sakte; Academy team qualifying testers ko select aur invite karti hai. 7) All Stars qualify karne ke liye pehle saare 5 prior Academy practice cycles pass karne honge, aur submitted issue reports valuable, well-written aur nearly error-free hone chahiye.
qs.b: Testers must complete the previous Academy courses, pass the preceding practice cycle and cannot repeat a cycle they already completed. The blue sign up button activates after passing the quiz and stays locked if the previous cycle was not passed. All Stars has no sign up; the Academy team invites testers who passed all five prior cycles with valuable, well-written, nearly error-free reports.
qs.t: Quiz pass = blue button; All Stars = sirf invite, 5 pass + saaf reports.

qs.q: When are testers added to an active versus a pending Academy cycle after signing up?
qs.s: Sign Up button click karne pe practice cycle ka invitation milta hai. Sign up ke din pe depend karta hai ki active ya pending cycle me add honge: Monday - Wednesday: current cycle me add. Thursday - Sunday: pending cycles me add, jo agle hafte ke Monday ko activate hote hain.
qs.b: Testers get an invitation once they click Sign Up. If they sign up Monday to Wednesday they are added to the current cycle, and from Thursday to Sunday they are added to a pending cycle that activates the following Monday.
qs.t: Som-Budh = abhi; Guru-Ravi = agle Monday.

qs.q: How does the Academy grades system work?
qs.s: 1) Har practice cycle ki ek requirement hai; pass ke liye fulfill karni hai. 2) Requirement fulfill nahi ki to pass nahi; same cycle me dobara sign up karna hoga. 3) Requirement poori ki to Passed. 4) Pichhla cycle pass nahi to agle me sign up nahi; example: Introduction to Testing pass aur complete nahi kiya to Computers Testing me sign up nahi. 5) Grades do tarike se: (a) Active aur locked academy cycles ke dauran, Pass grade tabhi milega jab tester ka approved issue aur approved test case dono ho. Pass grade issue aur test case approve hone ke 12 se 24 hours ke andar milta hai. Uske baad agle practice cycle me sign up kar sakte ho, cycle close hone ka wait nahi karna. (b) Cycle close hone pe baaki testers ko Pass aur Fail grades assign hote hain. 6) Pass hone wale agle Academy level me sign up kar sakte hain. 7) Fail hone wale same level me dobara sign up kar sakte hain. 8) Pass hone pe email aata hai ki level successfully pass hua. 9) Saare paanch Academy practice cycles complete hone pe Academy graduation ka email aata hai.
qs.b: Each practice cycle has a requirement, and testers who meet it pass while others must sign up for the same cycle again. During active and locked cycles, a tester gets a Pass within 12 to 24 hours once both an issue and a test case are approved, so they can move on without waiting for the cycle to close; remaining testers get Pass or Fail grades when the cycle closes. Passing a level triggers an email, and completing all five practice cycles triggers an Academy graduation email.
qs.t: Approved issue + approved test case = Pass, 12-24 ghante me.

qs.q: What are the requirements to participate in the Introduction to Testing cycle, and what do testers practice there?
qs.s: Participate karne ki requirements: 1) Saare pichhle the Academy courses pass 2) Computer ya mobile device hona 3) Computer aur mobile device pe screenshots bana sakna. Testers practice karenge: 1) Live cycles me testing 2) Test cycle chat me communicate karna 3) Issue report submit karna 4) Slot claim karna 5) Test case complete karna 6) Screenshots banana.
qs.b: To join Introduction to Testing, a tester must pass all previous Academy courses, have a computer or mobile device and be able to take screenshots on both. In the cycle they practice testing in a live cycle, communicating in the cycle chat, submitting an issue report, claiming a slot, completing a test case and creating screenshots.
qs.t: Practice: test, chat, issue, slot, test case, screenshot.

qs.q: What rules are specific to the Introduction to Testing Academy cycle?
qs.s: 1) Computers aur mobile devices dono testing ke liye allowed. 2) Issue report ki mistakes fix karne ke liye info request aayega. 3) Jo issue reports tester fix nahi karte wo reject honge. 4) Sirf ek issue report allowed. 5) Invalid issue reports discard karne ko kaha jayega; discard ke baad tester doosra valid issue report kar sakta hai. 6) Doosre testers ke reported issues hidden hain; duplicates ki chinta nahi.
qs.b: Both computers and mobile devices are allowed. Testers get an info request to fix mistakes, and reports not fixed are rejected. Only one issue report is allowed, invalid reports must be discarded before reporting another valid one, and other testers' issues are hidden so duplicates are not a concern.
qs.t: Ek hi issue; info request fix karo warna reject; duplicate ki tension nahi.

qs.q: What is required to pass the Introduction to Testing cycle, and what should testers do next?
qs.s: Pass ke liye: 1) Ek approved issue report 2) Ek approved test case. What to do next: pehle FAQ padho aur pichhle courses review karo; quiz complete karo; help ke liye Reference Links dekho; cycle me sign up karo; overview padho aur cycle instructions follow karke practice cycle complete karo; complete karne ke baad agle test cycle pe jao. Grades note: active aur locked cycles me approved issue aur approved test case dono hone pe 12 se 24 hours me Pass grade; phir agle cycle me sign up bina close ka wait kiye; cycle close pe baaki testers ko Pass/Fail. Pass wale agle level me, fail wale same level me dobara sign up.
qs.b: Passing requires one approved issue report and one approved test case. The steps are to read the FAQ and review earlier courses, complete the quiz, use the Reference Links, sign up, follow the cycle overview and then move on to the next cycle. The Pass grade arrives within 12 to 24 hours of both being approved.
qs.t: 1 approved issue + 1 approved test case = pass.

qs.q: Why might a tester not receive an invitation after signing up for Introduction to Testing?
qs.s: FAQ Q-1: Agar tumne Introduction to Testing cycle pehle kabhi pass kiya hai, to same course dobara join nahi kar sakte; agle course pe jao. Agar sure ho ki pass nahi kiya aur phir bhi invitation nahi mil raha, to support team se contact karo aur request category drop down me Academy (on-boarding & training) select karo.
qs.b: If the tester already passed Introduction to Testing before, they cannot join it again and should continue to the next course. If they are sure they have not passed it and still get no invitation, they should contact support and choose Academy (on-boarding & training) as the request category.
qs.t: Pehle pass = dobara nahi; warna support > Academy (on-boarding & training).

qs.q: What should a tester do after receiving an Introduction to Testing cycle invitation?
qs.s: FAQ Q-2 steps: 1) Academy page kholo aur saare the Academy courses review karo. 2) Cycle overview dhyan se padho, pass karne ke saare instructions wahan hain. 3) Ek chhota test case complete karke submit karo, aur overview me di gayi testing website test karke valid issue dhoondho; mile to saare instructions follow karke submit karo. 4) Academy team issue aur test case review karegi aur zarurat ho to more information maangegi.
qs.b: The tester should review all Academy courses, read the cycle overview carefully, complete and submit the short test case and test the website in the overview to find and submit one valid issue following all instructions. The Academy team then reviews the issue and test case and may request more information.
qs.t: Courses, overview, test case, ek valid bug, phir review.

qs.q: What should a tester do if they cannot find a bug in the Introduction to Testing cycle?
qs.s: FAQ Q-3: Ummeed mat chhodo, testing jaari rakho. Gehraai me jao aur har feature try karo. Site ko bug hunter ki tarah nahi, real user ki tarah browse karo. Focused raho, bugs khud saamne aayenge. FAQ Q-9: Cycle lock hone se pehle test case complete aur valid bug report karne ki koshish karo. Agar nahi ho paya, Introduction to Testing cycle me dobara sign up karo.
qs.b: Keep testing, go deeper and try every feature, browsing like a real user rather than a bug hunter, and the bugs will show up. If you still cannot complete the test case and report a valid bug before the cycle locks, you can sign up for the Introduction to Testing cycle again.
qs.t: Real user bano; lock tak na mila to dobara sign up.

qs.q: How do duplicates work in the Introduction to Testing cycle?
qs.s: FAQ Q-4: Is cycle me doosre testers ke reported issues dekh nahi sakte, kyunki saare hidden hain. Isliye duplicates ki chinta nahi; jo bhi valid issue mile freely report karo.
qs.b: In this cycle, all issues reported by other testers are hidden, so testers do not need to worry about duplicates and can report any valid issue they find.
qs.t: Intro cycle me sab issues chhupe, duplicate ka darr nahi.

qs.q: What should you do if your issue report has status Info Requested or has not been checked yet?
qs.s: FAQ Q-5: Report correct karne ka email aaye to How to edit a bug report? course review karo. FAQ Q-6: Issue report khol ke status check karo. Agar status Info Requested hai: matlab report me mistakes theek karni hain, ya fix ke baad Confirm all request is added link click karna bhool gaye. Mistakes theek karo (agar nahi kiya) aur Confirm all request is added link pe click karo. Isse status Info Requested se New ho jayega aur Academy team ko pata chalega ki report dobara check ke liye ready hai. Agar status pehle se New hai, to Academy team ke check ka wait karo; volume ki wajah se delay possible, par saare reports jaldi check honge.
qs.b: If the status is Info Requested, I fix the mistakes and click the Confirm all request is added link, which changes the status from Info Requested back to New so the Academy team knows it is ready for review. If the status is already New, I simply wait, since reviews can be delayed by volume.
qs.t: Fix karo + Confirm all request is added = Info Requested se New.

qs.q: Can you attach a video to your issue in the Introduction to Testing cycle?
qs.s: FAQ Q-7: Haan, video upload kar sakte ho. Lekin labeled screenshot bhi upload karna zaroori hai. Is test cycle me labeled screenshot mandatory hai taaki tum screenshot capture aur highlight karna seekho. High quality video ke liye Screen Recordings course dekho.
qs.b: Yes, a video can be added, but a labeled screenshot is still mandatory in this cycle so the tester learns how to capture and highlight a screenshot. The Screen Recordings course explains how to capture a good video.
qs.t: Video chalega, par labeled screenshot zaroori.

qs.q: What should be written in the area section of a bug title?
qs.s: FAQ Q-8: Bug title ka area section website/app pe bug ki location batata hai. Bas wo page name likho jahan issue hota hai. Example 1: Homepage pe broken link. Area = Homepage, redirect hone wala error page nahi. Sahi: Windows 10 - Homepage - Store Locator link directs to a not found error page. Galat: Windows 10 - Store Locator - Store Locator link directs to an error page. Example 2: category page pe filter option kaam nahi karta. Area = Product Listing Page (ya PLP), Filter nahi. Filter function ka naam hai, area nahi. Sahi: iPhone 6S - PLP - Selecting Free Shipping filter doesn't display all the products with free shipping. Galat: iPhone 6S - Filter - Free Shipping doesn't work correctly.
qs.b: The area is the location where the bug happens, which is simply the page name. For a broken link on the homepage, the area is Homepage, as in Windows 10 - Homepage - Store Locator link directs to a not found error page, not the error page it leads to. For a broken filter on a category page, the area is the Product Listing Page or PLP, not Filter, because Filter is the function name.
qs.t: Area = page jahan bug hua, function ka naam nahi.

qs.q: What happens once your test case and issue report are both approved in Introduction to Testing?
qs.s: FAQ Q-10: Badhai, tum Introduction to Testing cycle pass kar gaye. Passing grade issue aur test case approve hone ke 12 se 24 hours me milega. Passing grade milne pe agle practice cycle me sign up kar sakte ho. Agle course Computer cycle ka content review karo, quiz do, aur sign up button unlock hone pe Computer Testing practice cycle join karo. Aur sawal ho to test cycle chat me post karo, jo Academy team monitor karti hai.
qs.b: It means the tester has passed, and the passing grade arrives within 12 to 24 hours of both approvals. They can then review the Computer cycle course, take its quiz and join the Computer Testing practice cycle once the sign up button unlocks. Other questions can be posted in the test cycle chat, which the Academy team monitors.
qs.t: Dono approve = pass; 12-24 ghante; agla Computer Testing.

qs.q: How does the Introduction to Testing quiz and its Reference Links course work?
qs.s: Cycle me sign up se pehle quiz pass karna hai, 10 questions sahi answer karke. Reference Links course quiz me madad ke liye hai. Use kaise karein: 1) Course naye tab me kholo 2) Take the Quiz button se quiz shuru karo 3) Kisi question ka answer na pata ho to step 1 wala tab kholo 4) Neeche table se us quiz question ka corresponding course dhoondho aur kholo 5) Course review karke sahi answer do. Question-course map: 1 = Accepting an Invitation; 2 = Testing Websites and App; 3 = Communication; 4 = Basics of Screenshots; 5 = How to Edit an Issue; 6 = How to Write an Issue Report; 7 = How to Write an Issue Report; 8 = How to Edit an Issue Report; 9 = Introduction to Testing; 10 = Practice Test Cycles.
qs.b: Testers must answer 10 quiz questions correctly before they can sign up for the cycle. The Reference Links course is opened in a separate tab and maps each question to a course, for example question 1 to Accepting an Invitation, 4 to Basics of Screenshots, 6 and 7 to How to Write an Issue Report and 10 to Practice Test Cycles, so testers can review the right course when unsure.
qs.t: 10 me 10 sahi, tab sign up; Reference Links tab khula rakho.

topics.intro: Academy practice cycles, sign up rules, grades system, Introduction to Testing cycle ke rules aur FAQs.

topics.name: Localization Testing
topics.intro: L10N, T9N, I18N, G11N ka farq, har type ke bug examples, aur platform pe Localization cycle kaise kaam karta hai.

qs.q: What is localization testing?
qs.s: Notes ke hisaab se localization testing ka matlab hai internationalized software ko adapt karna by adding locale-specific components and translating text. Ye wo tareeka hai jisse software alag languages aur regional differences ke hisaab se adapt hota hai. Isme content ko translate aur adapt kiya jata hai taaki target audience ki linguistic, cultural aur baaki requirements meet ho sakein.
qs.b: Localization testing verifies that internationalized software has been correctly adapted for a specific locale by adding locale-specific components and translating text. It checks that the product meets the linguistic, cultural and other requirements of the target audience in that region.
qs.t: Pehle I18N ready software, phir L10N usko local banata hai.

qs.q: Why is localization important?
qs.s: Localization ensure karta hai ki product ya content target market ke liye culturally aur linguistically appropriate ho. Isse user experience aur engagement dono better hote hain.
qs.b: Localization makes a product culturally and linguistically appropriate for the target market. That directly improves user experience and engagement in that market.
qs.t: Local feel = zyada engagement.

qs.q: What are the four localization-related types (L10N, T9N, I18N, G11N)?
qs.s: Chaar types: (1) L10N = Localization: product/content ko specific local market ke liye adapt karna; text translate karna, date and time formats adjust karna, images aur symbols ko local culture ke hisaab se modify karna. (2) T9N = Translation: text ko ek language se doosri language me convert karna; localization ka part hai par sirf linguistic aspect pe focus. (3) I18N = Internationalization: product/content ko aise design aur develop karna ki alag languages aur cultures ke liye localize karna easy ho. (4) G11N = Globalization: product/content ko globally use hone ke liye design aur develop karna, cultural aur linguistic differences ko shuru se dhyan me rakhte hue.
qs.b: L10N is localization, adapting a product to a specific local market including text, date/time formats, images and symbols. T9N is translation, converting text between languages, which is only the linguistic part. I18N is internationalization, designing the product so it is easy to localize. G11N is globalization, designing the product for global use while considering cultural and linguistic differences from the start.
qs.t: Number = beech ke letters ki ginti: L-10-N, T-9-N, I-18-N, G-11-N.

qs.q: What is the one-line difference between internationalization and localization?
qs.s: Notes ki line: Internationalization is preparing products for potential use everywhere, whereas localization is adding features for use in a specific locale. Matlab I18N = har jagah use ke liye taiyari, L10N = ek specific locale ke liye features add karna.
qs.b: Internationalization prepares a product for potential use everywhere, while localization adds the features needed for use in one specific locale.
qs.t: I18N = everywhere ready, L10N = ek jagah ke liye fit.

qs.q: How do internationalization, localization and globalization differ according to the course?
qs.s: Internationalization: software applications ko aise design karna ki unhe duniya ki alag languages aur regions ke liye bina engineering changes ke adapt kiya ja sake. Localization (L10n): internationalized software ko adapt karna by adding locale-specific components and translating text. Globalization (G11N): ye term Microsoft, IBM aur Sun Microsystems ne banaya taaki Internationalization aur Localization dono ko ek saath combine kiya ja sake; isko often NLS bhi kehte hain (National Language Support ya Native Language Support). Ye part book ".NET Internationalization" (ISBN 0321341384, Addison-Wesley, 2006) se excerpt kiya gaya hai.
qs.b: Internationalization designs software so it can be adapted to different languages and regions without engineering changes. Localization adapts that internationalized software by adding locale-specific components and translated text. Globalization is the umbrella term, coined by Microsoft, IBM and Sun Microsystems, that combines internationalization and localization and is often called NLS, National or Native Language Support.
qs.t: G11N = I18N + L10N, aka NLS; teen companies ne naam diya: Microsoft, IBM, Sun.

qs.q: What does NLS stand for and how is it related to globalization?
qs.s: Globalization (G11N) ko often NLS kaha jata hai, jiska full form National Language Support ya Native Language Support hai. G11N term Microsoft, IBM aur Sun Microsystems ne banaya tha Internationalization aur Localization ko combine karne ke liye.
qs.b: NLS stands for National Language Support or Native Language Support. It is another name often used for globalization, the term that combines internationalization and localization.
qs.t: NLS = National/Native Language Support = G11N ka doosra naam.

qs.q: Why do we need localization testing?
qs.s: Business aur customer bases usually global hote hain. Jin countries me software sell hoga, unke criteria meet karne ki demand hoti hai. Isliye localization testing zaroori hai.
qs.b: Businesses and customer bases are usually global, so software has to meet the criteria of every country it is sold in. Localization testing checks that those country-specific requirements are actually met.
qs.t: Global customers = global criteria = L10N testing.

qs.q: What is the commercial benefit of localization and what is its downside?
qs.s: Commercially benefit hai zyada se zyada markets tak access. Downfall hai management ki taraf se budgetary commitments, kyunki main focus usually native language (English) pe hota hai aur doosri languages ko kam emphasis milta hai.
qs.b: The commercial benefit is access to more and more markets. The downside is the budget commitment it needs from management, because the focus is usually on the native language, English, and other languages get less emphasis.
qs.t: Fayda = naye markets, nuksaan = budget aur English-first mindset.

qs.q: What are the three key areas of localization and internationalization efforts?
qs.s: Notes me key points teen groups me hain: (1) Language, (2) Culture, (3) Writing conventions. Har group ke andar detailed items hain (alag cards me).
qs.b: Localization and internationalization efforts focus on three key areas: language, culture and writing conventions.
qs.t: LCW: Language, Culture, Writing conventions.

qs.q: What language-related points must localization and internationalization efforts cover?
qs.s: Language ke 6 points: (1) Computer-encoded text: product localize hone ke liye ready hai ya nahi, iska ek common sign hai Unicode ka use; isse system wide range of character encoding issues support kar pata hai. (2) Different number systems: kuch countries counting ka alag method use karti hain, English wale 1, 2, 3 system se alag. (3) Writing direction: kuch left to right (German, English, French), kuch right to left (Arabic aur doosre Middle Eastern countries). (4) Spelling variants jahan same language boli jati hai (tomato vs tomatoe, Localization vs Localisation, colour vs color). (5) Capitalization rules aur sorting rules bhi alag ho sakte hain. (6) Input keyboard shortcuts aur keyboard layouts alag ho sakte hain.
qs.b: The language points are computer-encoded text, where Unicode use is a common sign the product is ready to localize; different number systems; writing direction, left-to-right versus right-to-left; spelling variants within the same language such as colour versus color; different capitalization and sorting rules; and different keyboard shortcuts and layouts.
qs.t: Language ke 6: Unicode, Numbers, Direction, Spelling, Caps/Sort, Keyboard.

qs.q: What is one of the most common ways to know if a product is ready to be localized?
qs.s: Notes: computer-encoded text ke under, ek common tareeka hai Unicode ka use dekhna. Unicode system ko wide range of character encoding issues support karne deta hai.
qs.b: One of the most common signs that a product is ready to be localized is its use of Unicode, because Unicode lets the system support a wide range of character encodings.
qs.t: Unicode dikha = localization-ready.

qs.q: Give examples of left-to-right and right-to-left languages from the course.
qs.s: Left to right: German, English, French. Right to left: Arabic aur doosre Middle Eastern countries ki languages.
qs.b: German, English and French are written left to right, while Arabic and other Middle Eastern languages are written right to left.
qs.t: Arabic ulta chalti hai: RTL.

qs.q: What culture-related points must localization efforts cover?
qs.s: Culture ke 7 points: (1) Images aur colors: comprehensibility aur cultural acceptance ke issues. (2) Names and titles. (3) Government-assigned numbers (USA me Social Security number, Canada me SIN) aur passports. (4) Telephone numbers, addresses, postal codes. (5) Currencies (symbols, currency markers ki position). (6) Weights and measures. (7) Paper sizes (note: ye bahut common nahi hai).
qs.b: The culture points are images and colors and whether they are understood and culturally acceptable; names and titles; government-assigned numbers such as the US Social Security number or Canadian SIN, and passports; telephone numbers, addresses and postal codes; currencies, including symbols and marker position; weights and measures; and paper sizes, which are less common.
qs.t: Culture ke 7: Image, Name, Govt ID, Phone/Address, Currency, Weight, Paper.

qs.q: What writing-convention points must localization efforts cover?
qs.s: Writing conventions ke 3 points: (1) Date and time formats, calendar uses (Gregorian vs Lunar, etc). (2) Time Zones: usually internationalized products UTC time use karte hain. (3) Number format: decimal separators aur digit groupings.
qs.b: Writing conventions cover date and time formats and calendar systems such as Gregorian versus Lunar, time zones, where internationalized products usually use UTC, and number formats such as decimal separators and digit grouping.
qs.t: Writing ke 3: Date, Zone (UTC), Number.

qs.q: Which time standard do internationalized products usually use?
qs.s: Notes: Time Zones point me likha hai ki internationalized products usually UTC time use karte hain.
qs.b: Internationalized products usually store and work with UTC time, then handle local time zones on top of it.
qs.t: Global product = UTC ghadi.

qs.q: What are the possible difficulties with localization testing?
qs.s: Longer development cycle paper pe simple lagta hai par hota nahi. Larger software maintain karna mushkil hota hai. Product ki poori life me text ke parallel versions maintain karna bahut bada challenge hai. Example: user ko dikhne wali har nayi text line ke liye, appropriate translated text bhi system me hona chahiye. Product me nayi language add karna usually testers ke liye bugs ki gold mine hota hai.
qs.b: Localization lengthens the development cycle and makes large software harder to maintain. The biggest challenge is keeping parallel versions of every text string for the whole life of the product, since each new user-facing line needs its translation too. Adding a new language is usually a gold mine of bugs for testers.
qs.t: Nayi language = bugs ki gold mine.

qs.q: What is L10N and what does it look like on a website?
qs.s: Localization (L10N) ka matlab product ya content ko specific locale ya market ke liye adapt karna; content ko translate aur adapt karna taaki region ki cultural, linguistic aur baaki requirements fit ho. Website example: text ko local language me translate karna, region-specific images aur currency use karna, aur date and time formats ko local conventions ke hisaab se adjust karna.
qs.b: L10N is adapting a product or content to a specific locale so it fits that region's cultural and linguistic requirements. On a website that means translating text into the local language, using region-specific images and currency, and adjusting date and time formats to local conventions.
qs.t: L10N website = Language + Images + Currency + Date.

qs.q: What are typical L10N bugs listed in the course?
qs.s: 9 examples: (1) Incorrect Date Formats: jahan DD/MM/YYYY standard hai wahan MM/DD/YYYY dikhana. (2) Wrong Currency Symbols: European countries me prices ke liye euro ki jagah $ use karna. (3) Language Mismatches: galat language me text, jaise Portuguese-speaking audience ko Spanish content. (4) Cultural Insensitivity: kuch cultures me inappropriate ya offensive images/icons. (5) Improper Text Direction: Arabic jaisi languages ke liye RTL ki jagah LTR text. (6) Non-translated Content: website ke parts untranslated chhod dena, jaise buttons, labels, error messages. (7) Incorrect Units of Measurement: jahan metric standard hai wahan imperial units (feet, inches) instead of metric (meters, centimeters). (8) Inconsistent Terminology: localized site ke alag pages pe same concept ke liye alag terms. (9) Font Issues: aise fonts jo kuch languages ke special characters ya diacritics support nahi karte.
qs.b: Typical L10N bugs are incorrect date formats, wrong currency symbols, language mismatches, culturally insensitive images or icons, wrong text direction for RTL languages, untranslated buttons, labels or error messages, wrong measurement units, inconsistent terminology across pages, and fonts that cannot show special characters or diacritics.
qs.t: L10N ke 9: Date, Currency, Language, Culture, Direction, Untranslated, Units, Terms, Font.

qs.q: Give an example of a date format and a currency L10N bug.
qs.s: Date: jin regions me DD/MM/YYYY standard hai wahan MM/DD/YYYY format me date dikhana. Currency: European countries me prices ke liye euro ki jagah $ dikhana.
qs.b: A date bug is showing MM/DD/YYYY in a region where DD/MM/YYYY is the standard. A currency bug is showing prices in dollars instead of euros in European countries.
qs.t: Europe me $ dikha = L10N bug.

qs.q: What is an incorrect units of measurement bug?
qs.s: Jahan metric system standard hai un regions me imperial units (feet, inches) use karna instead of metric units (meters, centimeters).
qs.b: It is showing imperial units such as feet and inches in a region where the metric system, meters and centimeters, is the standard.
qs.t: Metric desh me feet-inch = galat.

qs.q: What is T9N and what would a tester check for it?
qs.s: T9N bhi product ko specific market ke liye adapt karta hai par primarily translation pe focus karta hai: text ko ek language se doosri me convert karna, ye ensure karte hue ki translated content culturally appropriate ho aur intended meaning sahi convey kare. Example: tester check karta hai ki website content English se Spanish me translate hua hai, including headings, paragraphs, buttons aur navigation menus.
qs.b: T9N focuses on translation, converting text from one language to another while keeping it culturally appropriate and accurate in meaning. For example, a tester checks that a website's headings, paragraphs, buttons and navigation menus have all been translated from English to Spanish.
qs.t: T9N check = heading, paragraph, button, menu sab translate hua?

qs.q: What are typical T9N bugs listed in the course?
qs.s: 7 examples: (1) Inaccurate Translations: sahi meaning convey nahi karte ya grammatically incorrect hain. (2) Missing Translations: website ke parts original language me reh gaye. (3) Over-localization: aisa content translate kar dena jo original language me rehna chahiye, jaise brand names ya technical terms. (4) Inconsistent Terminology: website pe same term ke liye alag translations. (5) Cultural Insensitivity: culturally inappropriate ya offensive translations. (6) Truncated Text: translated text bahut lamba hai aur cut off ho jata hai ya design me fit nahi hota. (7) Unlocalized Images: images jisme text hai wo translate nahi hua.
qs.b: Typical T9N bugs are inaccurate or ungrammatical translations, missing translations, over-localization of brand names or technical terms, inconsistent terminology, culturally insensitive translations, truncated text that no longer fits the design, and images whose embedded text was not translated.
qs.t: T9N ke 7: Inaccurate, Missing, Over, Inconsistent, Culture, Truncated, Image.

qs.q: What is over-localization?
qs.s: Over-localization ek T9N bug hai: aisa content translate kar dena jo original language me hi rehna chahiye tha, jaise brand names ya technical terms.
qs.b: Over-localization is translating content that should stay in the original language, such as brand names or technical terms.
qs.t: Brand name translate kiya = over-localization.

qs.q: What are truncated text and unlocalized image bugs?
qs.s: Truncated Text: translated text bahut lamba ho jata hai aur cut off ho jata hai ya design me fit nahi hota. Unlocalized Images: images jinke andar text hai, wo translate nahi kiya gaya.
qs.b: Truncated text is translated text that is too long and gets cut off or does not fit the design. Unlocalized images are images that contain text which was never translated.
qs.t: Lamba text kata = truncation; image ka text English hi raha = unlocalized image.

qs.q: What is I18N and what is a real example of it?
qs.s: I18N (internationalization) ka matlab product ya content ko aise design aur develop karna ki usse alag languages aur regions ke liye code ya structure me significant changes ke bina adapt kiya ja sake. Isme flexible framework banaya jata hai jo multiple languages, date formats, currencies aur doosre locale-specific elements support kare. I18N specifically technical aspects pe focus karta hai. Real example: website/app ko flexible template ke saath design karna jisme languages ke beech easy switching ho, right-to-left (RTL) languages ka support ho, aur various character sets handle karne ke liye Unicode use ho.
qs.b: I18N is designing and developing a product so it can be adapted to different languages and regions without significant code or structure changes. It is the technical side: a flexible framework that supports multiple languages, date formats and currencies. A real example is a site or app with a flexible template that switches languages easily, supports RTL languages and uses Unicode for different character sets.
qs.t: I18N = technical taiyari: template, RTL, Unicode.

qs.q: What are typical I18N bugs listed in the course?
qs.s: 9 examples: (1) Incorrect Encoding: galat character encoding, jisse garbled text aata hai. (2) Inflexible Layouts: layouts jo alag text lengths ke saath adapt nahi hote, text overflow ya misalignment. (3) Unicode Support Issues: special characters ya diacritics ko properly handle na karna, display errors. (4) Hard-coded Text: text code me directly embedded hai instead of external resource files me store hone ke (taaki translation easy ho). (5) Currency and Number Format Problems: locale-specific currency symbols aur number formats support na karna. (6) Broken RTL Support: right-to-left languages ka support sahi na hona, galat text alignment aur layout issues. (7) Date and Time Format Issues: locale-specific date/time formats support na karna, users confuse hote hain. (8) Non-scalable Images: translation se text length badalne pe images properly resize nahi hoti. (9) Inconsistent Language Detection: user ki preferred language sahi detect na karna, content galat language me dikhna.
qs.b: Typical I18N bugs are incorrect encoding causing garbled text, inflexible layouts that overflow or misalign, Unicode support issues with special characters, hard-coded text not stored in resource files, unsupported currency and number formats, broken RTL support, unsupported date and time formats, non-scalable images, and inconsistent detection of the user's preferred language.
qs.t: I18N ke 9: Encoding, Layout, Unicode, Hard-code, Currency, RTL, Date, Image, Detection.

qs.q: What is hard-coded text and why is it an I18N bug?
qs.s: Hard-coded Text: text jo directly code me embedded hai instead of external resource files me store hone ke, jahan se translation easy hoti. Isliye wo translate nahi ho pata. Lesson 9 example: mobile app Spanish me switch karne ke baad bhi "Submit" English me dikhata hai.
qs.b: Hard-coded text is text embedded directly in the code instead of in external resource files, so it cannot be translated easily. For example, a mobile app still shows Submit in English after the user switches to Spanish.
qs.t: Code me chipka text = translate nahi hoga.

qs.q: What is the difference between an incorrect encoding bug and a Unicode support issue?
qs.s: Incorrect Encoding: galat character encoding use karna, result garbled text. Unicode Support Issues: special characters ya diacritics ko properly handle na karna, jisse display errors aate hain. Dono I18N bugs hain.
qs.b: An incorrect encoding bug uses the wrong character encoding, so text appears garbled. A Unicode support issue is failing to handle special characters or diacritics properly, which causes display errors. Both are I18N bugs.
qs.t: Garbled = encoding; diacritic tuta = Unicode.

qs.q: What is G11N?
qs.s: Globalization (G11N) ka matlab product ya content ko aise design aur develop karna ki wo alag languages aur regions ke liye easily adapt ho sake. Isme flexible infrastructure banta hai jo multiple locales support kare, taaki product ko alag markets ke liye efficiently localize kiya ja sake bina extensive changes ke. G11N overall process hai aur isme internationalization aur localization dono efforts include hote hain.
qs.b: G11N is the overall process of designing and developing a product so it can easily be adapted to various languages and regions, with infrastructure that supports multiple locales. It includes both internationalization and localization efforts.
qs.t: G11N = poora global plan, andar I18N + L10N.

qs.q: What are typical G11N bugs listed in the course?
qs.s: 8 examples: (1) Inconsistent Localization: website ke kuch parts localized hain, kuch nahi, disjointed user experience. (2) Incorrect Locale Detection: user ka locale sahi detect na karna, galat language ya region-specific content. (3) Non-translatable Content: hard-coded text ya special characters ka support na hone ki wajah se content translate nahi ho pata. (4) Inadequate Resource Management: localized resources ka poor management, jaise missing ya incomplete translation files. (5) Inflexible Design: design jo alag languages me text expansion ya contraction accommodate nahi karta, layout issues. (6) Poor Performance: resources ki inefficient handling se localized content slow load hota hai. (7) Cultural Insensitivity: images, icons ya text jo kuch cultures me inappropriate ya offensive hain. (8) Incorrect Formatting: dates, times, numbers aur currencies ko regional standards ke hisaab se format na karna.
qs.b: Typical G11N bugs are inconsistent localization across the site, incorrect locale detection, non-translatable content, poor management of localized resources such as missing translation files, inflexible design that cannot handle text expansion or contraction, slow loading of localized content, culturally insensitive images or text, and incorrect formatting of dates, times, numbers and currencies.
qs.t: G11N ke 8: Inconsistent, Locale, Non-translatable, Resources, Design, Performance, Culture, Format.

qs.q: Which G11N bug relates to performance and which to translation files?
qs.s: Poor Performance: resources ki inefficient handling ki wajah se localized content ka slow loading. Inadequate Resource Management: localized resources ka poor management, jaise missing ya incomplete translation files.
qs.b: Poor performance is slow loading of localized content caused by inefficient resource handling. Inadequate resource management is poor handling of localized resources, such as missing or incomplete translation files.
qs.t: Slow = performance; file missing = resource management.

qs.q: How does G11N differ from I18N?
qs.s: G11N me I18N aur localization (L10N) dono aate hain, jabki I18N G11N ka subset hai jo technical preparation pe focus karta hai. I18N multiple locales ke liye technical readiness deal karta hai, jabki G11N me product ko globally accessible aur relevant banane ki broader strategy shamil hai. Summary: dono closely related hain, par G11N broader concept hai jisme I18N uske process ka part hai.
qs.b: G11N is the broader concept that includes both I18N and L10N. I18N is a subset of G11N focused on technical readiness for multiple locales, while G11N covers the wider strategy of making the product globally accessible and relevant.
qs.t: G11N bada umbrella, I18N uske neeche technical hissa.

qs.q: Summarize L10N, T9N, I18N and G11N using the course's differences table.
qs.s: Table (Type / Definition / Process requires / Example): L10N (Localization): product ko specific region ke liye adapt karna / Translation + Cultural Adaptation / "Thanksgiving" references ko global audience ke liye convert karna. T9N (Translation): text ko ek language se doosri me convert karna / Language-specific / "Welcome" ko "Bienvenue" (French) me translate karna. I18N (Internationalization): product ko localize karna easy banana / Technical (Unicode, externalized text, UI adaptability) / UTF-8 encoding aur text ke liye resource files use karna. G11N (Globalization): product ko worldwide usable banana / I18N + L10N / aisa app design karna jo multiple languages support kare.
qs.b: L10N adapts a product for a specific region through translation plus cultural adaptation, for example converting Thanksgiving references for a global audience. T9N converts text between languages, like Welcome to Bienvenue in French. I18N makes a product easy to localize through technical work such as Unicode, externalized text and UI adaptability, for example UTF-8 and resource files. G11N makes a product usable worldwide and equals I18N plus L10N, for example an app that supports multiple languages.
qs.t: Thanksgiving = L10N, Bienvenue = T9N, UTF-8 = I18N, multi-language app = G11N.

qs.q: What does each type require as a process according to the summary table?
qs.s: L10N requires Translation + Cultural Adaptation. T9N requires Language-specific work. I18N requires Technical work (Unicode, externalized text, UI adaptability). G11N requires I18N + L10N.
qs.b: L10N requires translation plus cultural adaptation, T9N is purely language-specific, I18N is technical work such as Unicode, externalized text and UI adaptability, and G11N requires both I18N and L10N.
qs.t: L10N culture+text, T9N sirf text, I18N tech, G11N dono.

qs.q: What is the one-line takeaway for each of L10N, T9N, G11N and I18N?
qs.s: Takeaway: L10N = Customizing content/UI for a specific audience. T9N = Pure text translation. G11N = Big-picture global readiness. I18N = Technical preparation for multiple languages.
qs.b: L10N is customizing content and UI for a specific audience, T9N is pure text translation, G11N is big-picture global readiness, and I18N is technical preparation for multiple languages.
qs.t: Customize, Translate, Big-picture, Tech-prep.

qs.q: How can you recognize a localization test cycle on the platform?
qs.s: Jab aapko platform pe Localization cycle me invite kiya jata hai, test cycle ID ke paas 'Lc' icon dikhta hai jo testing type denote karta hai. Ye course explain karta hai ki invite milne pe Localization test cycles me kaise participate karna hai.
qs.b: A localization cycle shows an Lc icon next to the test cycle ID, which denotes the testing type.
qs.t: Lc icon = Localization cycle.

qs.q: What is the first thing you notice in a localization cycle and what are its issue types?
qs.s: Localization cycle me enter karte hi sabse pehle overview section me payout table dikhti hai. Localization cycles me 6 issue types hain aur har ek ka payout alag ho sakta hai, isliye accept aur report karne se pehle inhe dekh lena. 6 types: (1) Corrupted Characters, (2) Missing Translation, (3) Poor Translation, (4) Truncation and Overlap, (5) Currency and Number Format, (6) Other/General.
qs.b: The first thing you see is the payout table in the overview section. Localization cycles have six issue types, Corrupted Characters, Missing Translation, Poor Translation, Truncation and Overlap, Currency and Number Format, and Other/General, and each can have a different payout, so review them before accepting and reporting.
qs.t: 6 types: Corrupt, Missing, Poor, Truncate, Currency, Other.

qs.q: What kinds of issues fall under the Other/General issue type in a localization cycle?
qs.s: Other/General examples: Shipping Options, Form Entry, Foreign OS Issue, Foreign Input Method Issue (foreign character keyboard), 3rd Party Software issues, Disputed borders map, Images and colors (comprehensibility aur cultural appropriateness ke issues), Culture, Subtitling of film and video, Spoken (Audio).
qs.b: Other/General covers shipping options, form entry, foreign OS issues, foreign input method issues such as a foreign character keyboard, third-party software issues, disputed borders on maps, images and colors that are hard to understand or culturally inappropriate, culture, subtitling of film and video, and spoken audio.
qs.t: Baaki sab (shipping, keyboard, map border, audio, subtitles) = Other/General.

qs.q: What happens when you accept a localization cycle?
qs.s: Accept button click karte hi ek Specified Language popup window khulti hai, jisme aap cycle me test hone wali language select karte ho. Note: wo language aapke tester profile me added honi chahiye, warna aap cycle join nahi kar paoge.
qs.b: Clicking Accept opens a Specified Language popup where you select the language being tested. That language must already be in your tester profile, otherwise you cannot join the cycle.
qs.t: Accept = language chuno; profile me nahi to entry nahi.

qs.q: How does the Type drop-down work when reporting a localization issue?
qs.s: Report Issue pe Type drop-down hota hai. Neeche ke fields bharne se pehle report ko classify karo (Type select karo). Jo Type select karoge uske hisaab se report fields badal jaate hain. Example: Missing ya Poor Translation select karne pe Recommended String aur Actual String fields add ho jaate hain.
qs.b: In the report form you choose the Type first, before filling any other field, because the fields change based on the type. For example, choosing Missing or Poor Translation adds Recommended String and Actual String fields.
qs.t: Pehle Type, phir fields; Translation type = Recommended + Actual String.

qs.q: Which extra fields appear when you select Missing or Poor Translation?
qs.s: Missing Translation ya Poor Translation select karne pe report me Recommended String aur Actual String fields add hote hain.
qs.b: Selecting Missing Translation or Poor Translation adds two fields, Recommended String and Actual String.
qs.t: Translation bug = kya hona chahiye (Recommended) vs kya hai (Actual).

qs.q: What should you notice in the Issues tab of a localization cycle?
qs.s: Issues Tab me Bug Type field me 6 nayi additions hain (localization issue types), jinhe re-order bhi kiya ja sakta hai. Agar cycle me multiple languages hain, to far right pe language column check karna mat bhoolo.
qs.b: In the Issues tab, the Bug Type field includes the six localization types and can be re-ordered. If the cycle has several languages, check the language column on the far right.
qs.t: Issues tab: Bug Type 6, language column right side.

qs.q: How are localization bug reports submitted and reviewed?
qs.s: Bug report complete hone ke baad usse Functional cycle ki tarah hi Submit Issue button click karke submit karo. Phir cycle ka LNE (Localization Expert) bugs review karta hai aur unhe approve karta hai (Somewhat, Very, ya Exceptional ke roop me) ya invalid bug hone pe reject karta hai.
qs.b: You submit with the Submit Issue button, the same as in a functional cycle. The cycle's LNE, the Localization Expert, reviews each bug and either approves it as Somewhat, Very or Exceptional, or rejects it if it is invalid.
qs.t: LNE judge: Somewhat, Very, Exceptional ya Reject.

qs.q: Who reviews bugs in a localization cycle?
qs.s: Cycle ka LNE (Localization Expert) bugs review karta hai.
qs.b: Bugs in a localization cycle are reviewed by the cycle's LNE, the Localization Expert.
qs.t: LNE = Localization Expert.

qs.q: What are the important points to follow in localization cycles?
qs.s: 7 points: (1) Saare bug reports English me likho, jab tak test cycle ke scope me kuch aur specify na ho. (2) Jo languages aap jaante ho aur familiar ho unhe tester profile me specify karo taaki platform ke Localization testing projects ke liye eligible bano. (3) Jo languages aap nahi jaante unhe profile me add mat karo. (4) Test cycle ka overview padho aur samjho; usme important information hoti hai jo testers ko follow karni hai. (5) Overview me "Issue Reporting Instructions" milenge; bug report karne se pehle hamesha ye padho aur follow karo. (6) Di gayi information accurate honi chahiye: no guessing, koi translator app nahi, Google Translate bhi nahi. (7) Kuch unclear ho to cycle chat se testing team ko contact karo; agar question platform ke Terms of Use violate kar sakta hai to cycle ke TE ko email karo.
qs.b: Write bug reports in English unless the cycle scope says otherwise. Add only languages you know to your profile so you are eligible, and never add unfamiliar ones. Read the cycle overview and its Issue Reporting Instructions before reporting. Be accurate, with no guessing and no translator apps including Google Translate. Ask the team in cycle chat if something is unclear, and email the TE if the question might violate the Terms of Use.
qs.t: English report, sachchi languages, overview padho, no Google Translate, doubt to chat/TE.

qs.q: In which language should localization bug reports be written?
qs.s: English sabhi bug reports ke liye use honi chahiye, jab tak test cycle ke scope me kuch aur specify na kiya gaya ho.
qs.b: Bug reports should be written in English unless the test cycle's scope specifies otherwise.
qs.t: Bug kisi bhi language ka ho, report English me.

qs.q: Can you use translation tools when reporting localization bugs?
qs.s: Nahi. Di gayi information accurate honi chahiye: no guessing ya kisi translator app ka use, including Google Translate.
qs.b: No. The information must be accurate, so you must not guess or use any translator app, including Google Translate.
qs.t: Google Translate = no.

qs.q: Whom should you contact when something is unclear in a localization cycle?
qs.s: Kuch unclear ho to cycle chat ke through testing team se baat karo. Agar question platform ke Terms of Use ko violate kar sakta hai, to cycle ke TE ko email karo.
qs.b: Reach out to the testing team through the cycle chat. If the question might violate the platform's Terms of Use, email the cycle's TE instead.
qs.t: Normal doubt = chat; sensitive doubt = TE ko email.

qs.q: Where do you find the Issue Reporting Instructions for a localization cycle?
qs.s: "Issue Reporting Instructions" test cycle ke overview me milte hain. Bug report karne se pehle hamesha inhe padho aur follow karo.
qs.b: The Issue Reporting Instructions are in the cycle overview, and you should always read and follow them before reporting a bug.
qs.t: Instructions overview me, report se pehle padho.

qs.q: Give examples of L10N bugs from the test scenarios lesson.
qs.s: L10N Bug: Incorrect cultural references. Examples: (1) Japan me food delivery app rice bowl ki jagah burger emoji dikhata hai, jabki rice bowl zyada common hai. (2) French website pe GDPR compliance message English me aata hai. (3) Checkout form state field require karta hai, par UK me states exist nahi karte.
qs.b: L10N scenario bugs are incorrect cultural references, such as a Japanese food delivery app showing a burger emoji instead of a rice bowl, a GDPR compliance message appearing in English on a French site, and a checkout form requiring a state field for the UK, which has no states.
qs.t: Japan burger, France GDPR English, UK state field.

qs.q: Give examples of T9N bugs from the test scenarios lesson.
qs.s: T9N Bug: Incorrect or misleading translations. Examples: (1) Hotel booking app me "Check Out" ko "Verificación" translate kiya (iska matlab Verification hai, hotel chhodna nahi). (2) Website ke French version me form ab bhi "Enter your name" English me dikhata hai. (3) Website translate karne ke liye Google Translate use hua, unnatural phrases aaye (jaise "File Not Found" ko kuch Spanish locales me "Archivo no hallado" ki jagah "Archivo no encontrado" translate kiya).
qs.b: T9N scenario bugs are incorrect or misleading translations, such as Check Out translated as Verificación in a hotel app, a French form still showing Enter your name in English, and machine translation producing unnatural phrases, like File Not Found rendered as Archivo no encontrado instead of Archivo no hallado in some Spanish locales.
qs.t: Check Out = Verificación? Galat T9N.

qs.q: Give examples of I18N bugs from the test scenarios lesson.
qs.s: I18N Bug: Hardcoded text that cannot be translated. Examples: (1) Mobile app Spanish me switch karne ke baad bhi "Submit" English me dikhata hai. (2) Website ke German version me "Login" expand hokar "Anmelden" ho jata hai, par button size same rehta hai, text cut off ho jata hai. (3) Banking app Arabic users ke liye layout properly mirror nahi karta, text galat direction me dikhta hai.
qs.b: I18N scenario bugs include hard-coded text, such as Submit staying in English after switching to Spanish; a German Anmelden label cut off because the Login button did not resize; and a banking app that does not mirror its layout for Arabic users, so text runs the wrong way.
qs.t: Submit English, Anmelden kata, Arabic mirror nahi.

qs.q: Give examples of G11N bugs from the test scenarios lesson.
qs.s: G11N Bug: Currency not converting properly for different regions. Examples: (1) E-commerce site France ke users ko bhi product prices USD me dikhata hai, EUR me convert nahi karta. (2) Flight booking website UK user ko "12/06/2025" dikhati hai par system isse June 12 ki jagah December 6 interpret karta hai.
qs.b: G11N scenario bugs include currency not converting by region, such as prices shown in USD to users in France instead of EUR, and date interpretation errors, such as a UK user seeing 12/06/2025 but the system reading it as December 6 instead of June 12.
qs.t: France me USD, UK me 12/06 = December? G11N bug.

qs.q: A German Login button shows Anmelden cut off. Which type of bug is it per the course?
qs.s: Lesson 9 me ye example I18N Bugs ke under hai: German version me "Login" expand hokar "Anmelden" ho jata hai par button size same rehta hai, isliye text cut off hota hai. (Text expansion ko layout handle nahi kar paya.)
qs.b: The course classifies it as an I18N bug: the label expands from Login to Anmelden in German but the button size stays the same, so the text is cut off.
qs.t: Button nahi bada = I18N.

topics.name: Payment Testing
topics.intro: Payment instruments (card, wallet, bank) se real purchase karke test karna - types, targets, in-store tips, evidence, open banking aur FAQs sab yahan.

qs.q: What is Payment Testing and what is a payment instrument (PI)?
qs.s: Payment Testing matlab koi bhi test jisko complete karne ke liye payment instrument (PI) use karna padta hai. Common PIs: Credit Card, Debit Card, PayPal. Global level pe local payment methods bhi test hote hain jo specific country ke unique hote hain - jaise Klarna (Sweden), PayTM (India), Alipay (China).
qs.b: Payment testing is any test that requires a payment instrument to complete. Common payment instruments are credit cards, debit cards and PayPal. Globally we also test local payment methods unique to a country, such as Klarna in Sweden, PayTM in India and Alipay in China.
qs.t: PI = jis cheez se paisa diya jaye; Klarna-Sweden, PayTM-India, Alipay-China.

qs.q: How do you add your payment methods to your tester profile, and what data is collected?
qs.s: Payment methods profile me add karne se platform team sahi testers ko projects ke liye source kar paati hai. Steps: 1) Platform website kholo aur log in karo. 2) Apne naam aur Tester ID ke paas wale arrow pe click karo - profile menu options dikhenge. 3) Tester Profile pe click karo aur Payment Testing tab pe jao. 4) Har section me jao aur apne available payment methods add karo. 5) Save button dabao. Note: Tester Profile me payment methods ka koi confidential data collect nahi hota - sirf identifying items jaise issuing country aur bank names.
qs.b: I log in, click the arrow next to my name and Tester ID, open Tester Profile and go to the Payment Testing tab. I go through every section, add my available payment methods and click Save. No confidential payment data is collected, only identifying items like the issuing country and bank name.
qs.t: Login - Arrow - Tester Profile - Payment Testing tab - Save; sirf country aur bank name.

qs.q: What are the three payment testing types?
qs.s: Teen types: Active Testing, Split Testing, Passive Testing. Active = tester khud flow follow karke purchase karta hai. Split = active ka live variation, conference call pe purchase. Passive = tester purchase nahi karta, apna PI data customer ko deta hai aur account monitor karta hai.
qs.b: There are three payment testing types: active testing, split testing and passive testing. In active testing I complete the purchase myself, in split testing I complete it live on a call, and in passive testing I provide my PI data and monitor my account while the customer makes the purchases.
qs.t: A-S-P: Active khud, Split call pe, Passive bas dekho.

qs.q: What is Active payment testing?
qs.s: Active test me tester ek test case ya flow follow karke purchase complete karta hai. Example: Credit Card se website pe shoes kharidna. Typically isme: purchase ko screenshot ya video me capture karna, failures aur issues report karna, aur purchase totals track karna.
qs.b: An active test requires the tester to go through a test case or flow and complete a purchase, for example buying a pair of shoes with a credit card on a website. Typically I capture the purchase in a screenshot or video, report failures and issues and track the purchase totals.
qs.t: Active = khud shoes kharido, proof lo, total likho.

qs.q: What is Split payment testing?
qs.s: Split test active test ka live variation hai. Testers ko conference call pe invite kiya jata hai aur call pe rehte hue payment complete karni hoti hai. Isme screen share karne, questions ka answer dene aur issues report karne ko kaha ja sakta hai.
qs.b: A split test is a live variation of an active test. Testers are invited to a conference call and complete the payment while on the call. They may be asked to share their screen during the purchase, answer questions and report issues.
qs.t: Split = call pe live, screen share ke saath.

qs.q: What is Passive payment testing?
qs.s: Passive test me tester khud purchase nahi karta. Tester ko apna PI data securely customer ko ek specific period ke liye dena hota hai, aur apne PI accounts monitor karne hote hain taaki saari purchases aur refunds sahi tarah ho rahe hon.
qs.b: In a passive test the tester does not make the purchase. The tester securely provides their payment instrument data to the customer for a specific period and monitors their accounts to make sure all purchases and refunds are made correctly.
qs.t: Passive = data do, account pe nazar rakho - purchase aur refund dono.

qs.q: What are the three common payment testing targets?
qs.s: 1) Point-Of-Sale ya In-Store Testing: stores, restaurants, hotels jaise point of sale pe jaakar credit/debit card ya mobile wallet test karna. 2) ATM Testing: specific ATMs pe jaakar paisa nikalna ya test cycle ke diye card se operations karna. 3) Online ya E-commerce: specific retail website pe credit/debit card, mobile wallet ya PayPal jaise online payment system se purchase karna.
qs.b: The three common targets are point-of-sale or in-store testing, where I pay at stores, restaurants or hotels with a card or mobile wallet; ATM testing, where I withdraw money or run operations at specific ATMs with the card provided by the cycle; and online or e-commerce testing, where I buy on a specific retail website using a card, mobile wallet or a system like PayPal.
qs.t: Store, ATM, Online - teen jagah paisa chalta hai.

qs.q: What is the difference between a credit card and a debit card by definition?
qs.s: Credit card: cardholder ko issue hota hai taaki woh merchant ko pay kar sake, is promise pe ki woh card issuer ko amount plus other agreed charges wapas dega. Debit card: merchant ko pay karne ke liye payment card, credit jaisa hi, lekin transaction karte hi paisa seedha cardholder ke bank account se transfer ho jata hai.
qs.b: A credit card lets the cardholder pay a merchant based on a promise to repay the card issuer the amount plus other agreed charges. A debit card is similar, but the money is transferred immediately and directly from the cardholder's bank account when the transaction is made.
qs.t: Credit = baad me chukao (promise), Debit = abhi account se kato.

qs.q: How do credit and debit cards work, and how are they authenticated?
qs.s: How it works: Credit card se pay karte waqt aap essentially short-term loan lete ho. Debit card bank account se linked hota hai, to aap seedha account se paisa nikaal rahe ho. Authentication: Credit - currently sirf PIN-based; historically signature-based tha; kuch merchants ke paas abhi bhi purane un-updated devices hain jinme receipt pe signature lagta hai. Debit - transactions 4-digit PIN pe based hain.
qs.b: Paying with a credit card is essentially a short-term loan, while a debit card withdraws money directly from the linked bank account. Credit transactions are currently PIN-based, though historically they were signature-based and some old terminals still need a signed receipt. Debit transactions use a 4-digit PIN.
qs.t: Credit = loan + purana signature; Debit = account + 4-digit PIN.

qs.q: How do transaction timing and interest charges differ between credit and debit cards?
qs.s: Transaction: Credit me funds tab deduct hote hain jab merchant credit card processor ke saath purchase settle karta hai, aur account balance me dikhne me typically 2-3 din lagte hain. Debit me transaction real-time complete hota hai, paisa turant katta hai. Interest: Credit me billing cycle (lagbhag 30 din) ki purchases ke liye due date se pehle small grace period milta hai; due date tak poora balance se kam pay kiya to average daily balance pe interest lagta hai. Debit me koi interest charge nahi.
qs.b: Credit card funds are deducted after the merchant settles with the processor, typically taking 2-3 days to show, while debit transactions are real-time and deducted instantly. Credit cards have a billing cycle of around 30 days with a small grace period, and paying less than the full balance by the due date accrues interest on the average daily balance. Debit cards have no interest charges.
qs.t: Credit: 2-3 din, 30 din cycle, interest; Debit: turant, zero interest.

qs.q: How does a magnetic stripe card work and how do you pay with it in store?
qs.s: Magnetic stripe card ke back side pe stripe hoti hai, jo modified iron-based magnetic particles se stripe aur receiving terminal ke beech data communicate karti hai. Steps: 1) Card terminal me swipe karo. 2) Kuch terminals poochte hain debit hai ya credit. 3) PIN enter karo. 4) Transaction complete, receipt issue. 5) Agar credit card hai (ya debit card jo credit jaisa act kar raha ho) to receipt sign karo - signed receipt merchant rakhta hai, second receipt aap lete ho.
qs.b: A magnetic stripe card has a stripe on the back that uses modified iron-based magnetic particles to send data to the terminal. I swipe the card, choose debit or credit if asked, enter the PIN, and the transaction completes with a receipt. For a credit card, or a debit card acting like one, I sign the receipt; the merchant keeps the signed copy and I take the second one.
qs.t: Swipe - type - PIN - receipt - sign (credit ho to).

qs.q: How does a chip card differ and how do you pay with it?
qs.s: Chip card ke front pe EMV chip hoti hai. Isse terminal me insert karna padta hai. Dikhne me magnetic stripe card jaisa hi, lekin bahut zyada secure. Steps: 1) Card terminal me insert karo (chip upar ki taraf). 2) Baaki steps magnetic stripe card ke step 2-5 jaise hi.
qs.b: A chip card has an EMV chip on the front and is inserted into the terminal rather than swiped. It looks like a magnetic stripe card but is much more secure. I insert it with the chip facing up and then follow the same steps 2 to 5 as for a magnetic stripe card.
qs.t: EMV chip = insert, chip upar, baaki stripe jaisa.

qs.q: How does a contactless card work and how do you pay with it?
qs.s: Contactless cards NFC (near field communication) technology use karte hain. Card terminal pe tap ya hover karo, PIN nahi chahiye. Small-value transactions ke liye use hote hain aur usually per day limited hote hain. Steps: 1) Card terminal pe tap/wave/hover karo (do baar tap ho jaye to tension nahi). 2) PIN ya sign nahi chahiye, sirf limit exceed hone pe PIN dalna padta hai. 3) Terminal success ya failure batata hai aur receipt issue hoti hai.
qs.b: Contactless cards use NFC, so I tap or hover the card over the terminal without entering a PIN. They are for small-value transactions and are usually limited per day. I tap the card, no PIN or signature is needed unless the limit is exceeded, and the terminal shows success or failure and issues a receipt.
qs.t: NFC tap = no PIN, chhota amount; limit cross to PIN.

qs.q: What is a mobile e-wallet and how do you set it up on iOS and Android?
qs.s: Mobile E-wallets jaise Google Pay ya Apple Pay contactless payment method hain jo contactless cards wali same NFC technology use karte hain. Pay karne se pehle setup karna padta hai, kuch minute lagte hain. iOS: iPhone pe Wallet function me jao, Add Credit or Debit Card tap karo, card info Apple Pay app me dalo, card issuer verify karega. Android: pre-loaded app kholo; Android Pay interface me button hai jisse card number aur CVC (card verification code - teen ya chaar digit number, usually card ke back pe) daal ke debit/credit card add karte ho. Agar tablet ya dusre device pe Android Pay pehle se setup hai, to phone pe app download karke login karne pe cards automatically sync ho jate hain.
qs.b: Mobile e-wallets like Google Pay and Apple Pay are contactless methods that use the same NFC technology as contactless cards, and they must be set up first. On iOS I open Wallet, tap Add Credit or Debit Card and enter the card details for the issuer to verify. On Android I open the pre-loaded app and add the card number and CVC; if Android Pay is already set up on another device, the cards sync automatically after login.
qs.t: Wallet = NFC; iOS Wallet me add, Android me number + CVC, sync auto.

qs.q: How do you pay in store with a mobile e-wallet?
qs.s: Steps: 1) Mobile device ko NFC enabled terminal pe hover karo. 2) Device ke authentication method se khud ko authenticate karo (Fingerprint, FaceID, device password, etc.). 3) Terminal success ya failure notify karta hai aur receipt issue hoti hai. 4) Kuch countries/regions me amount ek limit se zyada hone pe PIN dalna ya receipt sign karna pad sakta hai - isliye badi purchase pe PIN yaad rakho.
qs.b: I hover the phone over the NFC-enabled terminal, authenticate with my device method such as fingerprint, Face ID or passcode, and the terminal shows success or failure and issues a receipt. In some countries, if the amount exceeds a certain limit, I may need to enter the PIN or sign the receipt, so I remember my PIN for big purchases.
qs.t: Hover - Face/Finger - receipt; bada amount = PIN yaad rakho.

qs.q: Which receipt must you take when testing a card or mobile e-wallet in store?
qs.s: Important rule: card ya Mobile E-wallet test kar rahe ho to terminal receipt (jisme card information ho) zaroor lo - sirf product receipt nahi. Har case me lena hai: transaction accepted ho, declined ho, ya error aaye.
qs.b: When testing a card or mobile e-wallet, I always take the terminal receipt that contains the card information, not only the product receipt. I take it in every case, whether the transaction is accepted, declined or ends in an error.
qs.t: Terminal receipt hamesha - pass, fail, error teeno me.

qs.q: What are the most common payment methods used on e-commerce platforms?
qs.s: E-commerce sites electronic payment use karti hain - matlab paperless monetary transactions. Common methods (4): 1) Credit and debit cards. 2) Bank payment system online ya Internet Banking. 3) E-commerce payment system online (PayPal jaisa). 4) Mobile wallet online.
qs.b: E-commerce sites use electronic, paperless payments. The most common methods are credit and debit cards, online bank payment or internet banking, online e-commerce payment systems such as PayPal, and online mobile wallets.
qs.t: Card, Bank, PayPal-type, Wallet - online ke chaar raste.

qs.q: How do you pay online with a credit or debit card?
qs.s: Credit/debit cards popular online method hain. Steps: 1) Checkout page pe card option select karo. 2) Card ki saari details dalo (zaroorat ho to screenshot lo) aur proceed karo. 3) Zaroorat ho to OTP dal ke authenticate karo aur payment complete karo.
qs.b: On the checkout page I select the card option, enter all the card details, taking a screenshot if needed, and proceed. If required, I authenticate with an OTP and complete the payment.
qs.t: Card select - details - OTP - done.

qs.q: How do you pay online using internet banking?
qs.s: Bank payment systems me koi physical card nahi hota; ye Internet banking account wale customers use karte hain. Steps: 1) Checkout page pe card details ki jagah batao kis bank se pay karna hai. 2) Bank ki website pe redirect hoge. 3) Login/password ya two-factor authentication se authenticate karke payment complete karo.
qs.b: Internet banking involves no physical card and is used by customers with online banking accounts. On checkout I choose my bank instead of entering card details, I am redirected to the bank's website, and I authenticate with login and password or two-factor authentication to complete the payment.
qs.t: Bank chuno - bank site pe jao - login/2FA.

qs.q: What is an online e-commerce payment system and how do you pay with it?
qs.s: PayPal, PayTm, Google Wallet jaise systems me apne account se multiple cards ya bank accounts attach kar sakte ho aur alag purchases ke liye alag select kar sakte ho. Ye fee charge karte hain, badle me benefits jaise one-click transactions aur password memory. Steps: 1) Checkout pe PayPal jaisa option select karo (ya koi alternative). 2) Payment website (PayPal, etc.) pe redirect hoge. 3) Login/password ya two-factor authentication se authenticate karke transaction complete karo.
qs.b: Systems like PayPal, PayTm and Google Wallet let you attach multiple cards or bank accounts and choose one per purchase; they charge a fee in exchange for benefits like one-click transactions and password memory. I select the option at checkout, get redirected to the payment site, and authenticate with login and password or two-factor authentication to complete it.
qs.t: PayPal = kai cards ek jagah, fee ke badle one-click.

qs.q: How do you pay online with a mobile wallet?
qs.s: Agar smartphone se online shopping kar rahe ho aur mobile payment app (Apple Pay ya Android Pay) pehle se setup hai, to phone se jaldi purchase ho jata hai - card nikaal ke number punch nahi karna. Steps: 1) Checkout pe Apple Pay ya Android Pay option select karo (agar hai). 2) Khule window me apni info check karo ya suitable card select karo. 3) Device ke authentication method se authenticate karke transaction complete karo.
