qs.b: If my mobile payment app like Apple Pay or Android Pay is set up, I can buy without typing card numbers. At checkout I select Apple Pay or Android Pay, check my information or choose a card in the window that opens, and authenticate with my device method to complete the transaction.
qs.t: Online wallet = select, card chuno, Face/Finger.

qs.q: What evidence should you capture when paying online or on an e-commerce platform?
qs.s: Teen cheezein: 1) Jab website/app success ya error message details ke saath dikhaye, uska screenshot. 2) Website/app ki order details wali email ka screenshot. 3) Zaroorat ho to apne attached card/bank/e-wallet ke corresponding page pe transaction check karo.
qs.b: I take a screenshot of the success or error message with its details, a screenshot of the order details email from the website or app, and if necessary I check the transaction on the page of the attached card, bank or e-wallet.
qs.t: Message ka SS, email ka SS, bank me check.

qs.q: What is an in-store testing cycle?
qs.s: In-store cycle me testers point of sale wali specific jagah visit karte hain - stores, restaurants, hotels, travel companies, hospitals, taxi services, etc. Payment method test karne ke liye purchase complete karni hoti hai (Tester ka card, customer ka diya card, mobile-wallets, etc.).
qs.b: In an in-store cycle, testers visit specific places with a point of sale, such as stores, restaurants, hotels, travel companies, hospitals or taxi services, and complete a purchase to test a payment method, which may be their own card, a card provided by the customer or a mobile wallet.
qs.t: In-store = dukaan, hotel, taxi - jahan POS ho.

qs.q: How should you get ready for an in-store testing trip?
qs.s: 4 tips: 1) Trip plan karo - ghar se nikalne se pehle route map karo, khas kar multiple locations ho to. 2) Store ki details pehle check karo (accepted cards, timings, restrictions, Google pe check karo ki store exist karta hai aur band nahi hai) taaki visit waste na ho. 3) Locations ke beech paidal chalna hai to achhe shoes pehno. 4) Multiple items kharidne hain to backpack le jao.
qs.b: I plan the trip and map my route before leaving, especially for multiple locations. I check store details in advance, such as accepted cards, timings, restrictions and whether it still exists, so the visit is not wasted. I wear good shoes if walking and bring a backpack if buying multiple items.
qs.t: Map, store check, shoes, backpack.

qs.q: What are the rules for contacting the TTL during in-store testing?
qs.s: 1) Testing tabhi shuru karo jab TTL ne plan pe concur kiya ho (store address, payment card, device, etc.). 2) Mobile payments ke liye environment prepare karo aur TTL se concurrence lo (app ka sahi version install karna, logs capture enable karna). 3) Plan me koi change ho to turant TTL ko batao taaki schedule affect na ho aur zaroorat ho to dusre mobilize kiye ja sakein. 4) PM/TTL ki consent ke bina bank ya store customer care ko contact mat karo - customer care ko naye store process ka pata nahi hota, aur issue customer tak escalate ho sakta hai.
qs.b: I start only after the TTL agrees with my plan, including store address, card and device. For mobile payments I prepare the environment, like the correct app version and log capture, and get TTL approval. I inform the TTL immediately of any change of plans, and I never contact bank or store customer care without PM or TTL consent, because they may not know the new process and the issue could escalate to the customer.
qs.t: TTL ka haan pehle, change turant batao, customer care ko kabhi khud nahi.

qs.q: Why communicate with fellow testers and read all cycle instructions before an in-store test?
qs.s: TTL project ke start me Slack ya Skype jaise communication channel me add karega - wahan ke fellow testers se connect karo; unki info aur experiences kaam bahut aasan bana dete hain. Test cycle ki saari instructions padho - store pahunchne se pehle payment flow achhe se samjho, jaise payment fail ho to kya karna hai.
qs.b: The TTL adds testers to a channel like Slack or Skype at the start of the project, and connecting with fellow testers there helps because they share useful information and experiences. I also read all cycle instructions so I understand the payment flow before arriving, including what to do if a payment fails.
qs.t: Slack pe doston se seekho, store se pehle flow ratt lo.

qs.q: What should you do if a store employee asks about your purpose during an in-store test?
qs.s: Store me jaane se pehle imaginative hoke alag scenarios socho. Agar employee pooche to believable aur realistic reason dena hai. Merchant ko mat batao ki aap platform ke project ke liye testing kar rahe ho - zyada tar in-store tests confidential hote hain. Exception sirf tab jab customer ya TTL/PM ne specifically store staff se interact karne ko kaha ho.
qs.b: I prepare realistic scenarios beforehand so I can give a believable reason if an employee asks what I am doing. I do not tell the merchant that I am testing for a platform project, because most in-store tests are confidential, unless the customer, TTL or PM has specifically asked me to interact with the staff.
qs.t: Kahani ready rakho, testing ka naam mat lo.

qs.q: How should you collect evidence and behave with merchants during in-store testing?
qs.s: Evidence: notebook le jao aur raste me sab document karo; bahut saari photos ya videos lo. Polite raho: agar photos li aur staff ne object karke delete karne ko kaha, to maan lo aur unki instruction follow karo, aur incident TE/TTL ko report karo. Conflicts avoid karo - situation bane to bas 'Thank you for your time' bolo, test abort karo, calmly store se niklo aur TTL ko inform karo.
qs.b: I bring a notebook to document everything and take lots of pictures or videos. If staff object to my photos and ask me to delete them, I comply and report the incident to the TE or TTL. If a conflict arises, I say thank you for your time, abort the test, leave calmly and inform my TTL.
qs.t: Notebook + photos; staff bole delete to delete, jhagda nahi - thank you bolo, niklo.

qs.q: What should you do if your card keeps getting declined across planned store visits?
qs.s: Agar trip me kai store visits planned hain aur lagatar failures aa rahe hain to testing rok do. Example: 5 store visits planned hain aur pehle 2 fail ho gaye, to ruk jao aur aage badhne se pehle TTL se check karo issue kya ho sakta hai. Ye bhi ensure karo ki jo payment card use karna hai woh blocked na ho.
qs.b: If I see continuous failures, I pause testing. For example, if five store visits are planned and the first two fail, I stop and check with the TTL about the possible issue before continuing. I also make sure the card I intend to use is not blocked.
qs.t: 5 me se pehle 2 fail = ruko, TTL se poocho.

qs.q: What are the timing and spending rules for in-store testing?
qs.s: Kaam time pe complete karo: results jaldi se jaldi submit karo, khas kar issues ho to - late results aur issue reports ki value nahi rehti. Ideally store visit ke 2 se 3 ghante ke andar report karo. Peak hours me test mat karo (jab tak instruct na kiya ho) - multiple tries me line hold ho sakti hai aur line me time waste hota hai. Spending limit: purchase amount exceed mat karo - hamesha lowest priced items lo.
qs.b: I submit results as soon as possible, ideally within 2 to 3 hours of the store visit, because delayed results and issue reports may lose value. I avoid peak hours unless instructed, since multiple attempts can hold up the line and waste time. I stay within the spending limit and always choose the lowest-priced items.
qs.t: 2-3 ghante me report, rush hour nahi, sabse sasta item.

qs.q: What data should you gather from the card terminal receipt during in-store testing?
qs.s: Har card terminal receipt (error, declined, accepted) ki photo deni hai - error aur refusal receipts ignore mat karo, customer ke liye important hain. Receipt se data: 1) STAN/RRN - cardholder bank ka generate kiya number jisse transaction identify hota hai. 2) Authentication/Approval number - confirm karta hai ki debit/credit transaction approve hua. 3) Merchant ID/MID - payment processor ka merchant ko diya unique code. 4) Acquirer - financial institution (basically bank) jo transaction process kar raha hai. 5) Transaction ya sale amount - account se charge hua amount. Note: har data receipt pe hona mandatory nahi, kuch missing ho to fine hai.
qs.b: I photograph every terminal receipt, whether error, declined or accepted, because refusals matter to the customer. From the receipt I capture the STAN or RRN that identifies the transaction, the authentication or approval number, the merchant ID, the acquirer bank processing the transaction and the transaction amount. Not every field is always present, and that is acceptable.
qs.t: S-A-M-A-A: STAN, Approval, MID, Acquirer, Amount.

qs.q: Besides the receipt, what other evidence is commonly required in in-store testing?
qs.s: 1) Terminal Photo: transaction wale terminal device ki image (model aur version ke saath) - mandatory nahi, kabhi possible nahi hota. 2) GPS Image: Google Maps se tester ki point-of-sale ya ATM pe location ki GPS image. 3) Storefront Page: storefront ki photo. 4) Signage Image: door ya cashier area pe accepted cards ka signage ho to uski photo. Important: jagah pe jo bhi experience hua sab note karo, kyunki payment decline ka reason ya real-life factors likhne pad sakte hain jo test me interfere hue.
qs.b: Common evidence also includes a photo of the terminal with its model and version when possible, a GPS image from Google Maps showing me at the point of sale or ATM, a storefront photo, and a photo of the accepted-cards signage if present. I also note my whole experience, since I may need to explain why a payment was declined or what real-life factors interfered.
qs.t: Terminal, GPS, Storefront, Signage + diary of experience.

qs.q: What is Open Banking? Give examples.
qs.s: Open Banking ek system hai jisme customers apna financial data securely third-party apps aur services ke saath share kar sakte hain. Pehle banks ye info apne systems me lock rakhte the. Ab customers real time me data access karke decisions le sakte hain; banks ke liye naye services aur revenue sources; customers money better manage karte hain. Examples: 1) App jo saare savings accounts collate karke high-yield savings option recommend kare. 2) Lender jo loan eligibility se pehle multiple banks ke financials ka clear view chahe. 3) App jo credit cards aur bank transactions ka spending track karke insights de aur budget banane me help kare.
qs.b: Open banking is a system that lets customers securely share their financial data with third-party apps and services, instead of banks keeping it locked in their own systems. Examples are an app that collates savings accounts to recommend a high-yield option, a lender viewing finances across banks before approving a loan, and an app that tracks spending across cards and accounts to help with budgeting.
qs.t: Open Banking = bank ka data, tumhari permission se, dusre app me.

qs.q: What are the two main aspects of Open Banking?
qs.s: 1) Data sharing: customers apna financial data (account balances, transaction history, etc.) authorized third-party services ko access de sakte hain, secure APIs ke through electronically. Access kabhi bhi revoke kar sakte hain. 2) Third-party services: is data se naye financial apps banti hain. Benefits: Financial management tools (saare accounts ka data ek jagah - budgeting, saving, spending tracking), Tailored financial products (data ke basis pe loans, credit cards ke personalized recommendations), Payment innovation (faster aur more secure online payments). Open banking competition aur innovation promote karta hai, lekin security risks ka dhyan rakho aur sirf authorized providers ke saath data share karo.
qs.b: The two aspects are data sharing and third-party services. Customers grant authorized services access to data like balances and transaction history through secure APIs and can revoke it at any time. With that data, new services offer financial management tools, tailored financial products and payment innovation, though users should share data only with authorized providers because of security risks.
qs.t: Share (API, revoke) + Services (Manage, Tailor, Pay fast).

qs.q: What are the most common types of open banking testing on the platform?
qs.s: Open banking me sensitive info handle hoti hai, testers clients ko security aur quality standards meet karne me help karte hain. Common types (5): 1) Payment testing - transactions test karke ensure ki saari APIs kaam kar rahi hain. 2) Functional testing - app ki core functionalities expected kaam karein. 3) Usability testing - interface aur UX confusing ya frustrating na ho. 4) Regression testing - app updates se existing functionality me unexpected changes na hon. 5) Accessibility testing - products accessibility standards meet karein, sab log seamlessly use kar sakein.
qs.b: The most common open banking testing types are payment testing to confirm all APIs work through real transactions, functional testing of core features, usability testing so the interface is not confusing, regression testing so updates do not break existing functionality, and accessibility testing so everyone can use the app.
qs.t: P-F-U-R-A: Payment, Functional, Usability, Regression, Accessibility.

qs.q: How is a tester's personal banking information kept safe in open banking projects?
qs.s: Tester info care se handle hoti hai, GDPR aur Information Security policies follow karke - personal details store aur share karne ke methods pe strict guidelines. Customers ko bhi security policies aur Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) follow karne padte hain, tabhi testing start hoti hai. Banking aur payment instrument projects pe TTL/TE/TSM team specialists aur highly experienced hoti hai. Tester ko bhi cycle instructions closely follow karne hain, kuch unclear ho to poochna hai.
qs.b: Tester data is handled under GDPR and information security policies with strict rules on how personal details are stored and shared. Customers must also follow security policies and sign NDAs before such testing begins, and the TTL, TE and TSM team on these projects are experienced specialists. As a tester I follow cycle instructions closely and ask when something is unclear.
qs.t: GDPR + InfoSec + NDA + expert TTL/TE/TSM.

qs.q: What advice is given for getting into and preparing for open banking test cycles?
qs.s: 1) Invitations ke liye Tester Profile me Payment Testing fields bharo; Projects Board pe banking projects ke liye apply karte raho. 2) Invite milne pe overview dhyan se padho, phir dobara padho, aur attached documentation bhi; slotting instructions aur claimed slot ki specific instructions pe dhyan do; test cases follow karo, doubt ho to TTL/TE se poocho. 3) Apne bank ke products ki conditions study karo, test team se baat karo ki value hai ya nahi aur cost/fees reimburse hogi ya nahi; feasible ho to bank ke unusual products dhundo - aisa test kar paoge jo koi aur nahi kar sakta (bugs easier to find, more valuable bugs, specific Test Cases ka access). 4) Payment Method kaise kaam karta hai samjho - kaunsi info chahiye aur apni info kaise protect karni hai; jaise slot specific bank maange to experienced tester ko flow aur bank app se request approve karna pata hota hai; zyada tar screen recording chahiye (hamesha nahi), flow pata ho to clean video banta hai jisme kam editing. 5) Test devices pe screen recording ka achha setup rakho - fast turnaround aur high-quality evidence.
qs.b: I fill in the Payment Testing fields in my profile and watch the Projects Board for banking projects. Once invited, I read the overview twice plus all attached documents, follow slotting and slot-specific instructions, and ask the TTL or TE when unsure. I study my bank's products and ask whether they add value and if fees are reimbursable, understand how the payment method flow works so I can record a clean video, and keep a good screen-recording setup for fast, high-quality evidence.
qs.t: Profile bharo, overview do baar, bank ke unique products, flow samjho, recorder ready.

qs.q: What data-protection rules apply to evidence in open banking testing?
qs.s: 1) Personal aur payment info hamesha blur/redact karo; video/screenshot attach karne se pehle double-check karo ki sab sensitive info redact hai. 2) Private Attachment: cycle me enabled ho to use karo - jo attachments publicly visible nahi hone chahiye ya sensitive info rakhte hain unhe hide karne ke liye. 3) Full bank card number kabhi screenshot ya recording me share mat karo. Pehle 6 digits 'BIN' number kehlate hain - ye share karna ok hai. Card ke back pe CVV usually 3 digits ka hota hai aur expiry date share nahi karni. 4) Test me customer product ko consent dena pade to testing ke baad revoke karo. 5) Projects pe hamesha Terms of Use aur Privacy Policy follow karo.
qs.b: I always blur or redact personal and payment information and double-check before attaching. I use Private Attachment when enabled for sensitive files. I never show the full card number; only the first 6 digits, the BIN, are fine to share, while the CVV and expiry date must not be shared. I revoke any consent given to the customer product after testing and always follow the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
qs.t: BIN 6 ok, baaki number/CVV/expiry nahi; consent wapas lo.

qs.q: Which Academy courses are recommended before open banking testing?
qs.s: Smooth, secure aur successful open banking testing ke liye ye 5 Academy courses padhne recommend kiye gaye: 1) Issue Reports. 2) Slots and Test Cases. 3) Screenshots. 4) Screen Recordings. 5) Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
qs.b: The recommended Academy courses are Issue Reports, Slots and Test Cases, Screenshots, Screen Recordings, and Personally Identifiable Information.
qs.t: Issue, Slot, SS, Recording, PII - paanch course.

qs.q: What are the best practices about payment instruments and slots in payment testing?
qs.s: 1) Specify all PIs: apne saare payment instruments tester profile me specify karo taaki zyada payment testing projects ke liye eligible bano. 2) Correct PI rakho aur usi se test karo: kai testers slot/test case claim karte hain aur phir report karte hain ki required PI nahi hai. Slot/test case tabhi claim karo jab required PI ho, aur usi se test karo.
qs.b: I list all my payment instruments in my tester profile to be eligible for more payment projects. I only claim a slot or test case if I actually have the required payment instrument, and I test with that exact instrument, since many testers claim slots and then report they do not have it.
qs.t: Saare PI profile me; jo PI nahi, woh slot nahi.

qs.q: What best practices apply to recording evidence and keeping records in payment testing?
qs.s: 1) High quality, editable video capture program use karo - ScreenPal (pehle ScreenCast-O-Matic) Pro long time se recommended hai (sab testing ke liye great investment) kyunki editing me blurring allow karta hai. 2) Confidential data blur karo - naam, address, card number, CVV, OTP etc. 3) Saari transactions ke emails aur receipts rakho; dates, amounts, PIs aur cycles track karne ke liye spreadsheet banana achha hai.
qs.b: I use a high-quality editable recorder; ScreenPal Pro, formerly ScreenCast-O-Matic, is recommended because it allows blurring while editing. I blur confidential data like name, address, card number, CVV and OTP. I keep all emails and receipts and track dates, amounts, payment instruments and cycles in a spreadsheet.
qs.t: ScreenPal se blur, spreadsheet me hisaab.

qs.q: What should you review in a payment test cycle and how do you clear doubts?
qs.s: Test cycle ka overview padho aur samjho - isme refund policy, required PIs, required proofs aur testers ko jo bhi pata hona chahiye sab hota hai. Kuch bhi skip mat karo. Kuch unclear ho to testing team se cycle chat pe poocho. Agar question Terms of Use violate kar sakta hai ya personal hai, to cycle ke TE ko email karo.
qs.b: I read and understand the whole cycle overview, which includes the refund policy, required payment instruments and required proofs, without skipping anything. If something is unclear, I ask the testing team in the cycle chat; if the question is personal or might violate the Terms of Use, I email the cycle's TE.
qs.t: Overview = refund + PI + proof; general doubt chat pe, personal TE ko email.

qs.q: How can you tell whether a card is a debit or a credit card?
qs.s: Pakka karne ke liye apne bank se poocho ki card credit hai ya debit. Aur jab card tester profile me add karte ho, card type automatically select ho jata hai.
qs.b: To be sure, I ask my bank whether the card is credit or debit. Also, when I add the card to my tester profile, the card type is selected automatically.
qs.t: Doubt = bank se poocho; profile khud bata deta hai.

qs.q: Why do you sign the back of a credit card?
qs.s: 1) Identity Verification - merchant card pe signature aur receipt pe signature compare kar sakta hai; match na ho to credit card thief pakadne ka ek tareeka. 2) Protection - purchase dispute hone pe sab parties (aap, merchant, credit card company) protect hote hain. Example: statement me aisa transaction dikhe jo aapne nahi kiya, to credit card company merchant se signed receipt maang sakti hai ye prove karne ke liye ki card aapne hi swipe kiya.
qs.b: Signing a credit card supports identity verification, since the merchant can compare the card signature with the receipt signature to catch a thief. It also protects the cardholder, merchant and card company in disputes, because the card company can demand the signed receipt from the merchant to prove who swiped the card.
qs.t: Sign = pehchaan + dispute me saboot.

qs.q: Why do some merchants avoid accepting credit card payments?
qs.s: 1) Processing costs - card payments accept karne pe businesses zyada fees dete hain, typically har transaction pe around 2-3% ya zyada, aur merchant account ke part ke roop me flat monthly charges bhi ho sakte hain. 2) Complexity - business merchant account me paisa available hone me kai din lag sakte hain (especially credit card). Upar se charges kuch mahine me reverse ho sakte hain - card fraudulently use hua ya customer product/service se unhappy hai to card issuers jaldi chargeback issue karte hain.
qs.b: Merchants may avoid credit cards because of processing costs, typically around 2-3% or more per transaction plus possible flat monthly charges, and because of complexity: funds can take several days to arrive, and charges can be reversed months later through chargebacks for fraud or customer complaints.
qs.t: 2-3% fee + late paisa + chargeback ka dar.

qs.q: Why might some stores not accept American Express and Discover cards?
qs.s: Zyada tar merchants Visa aur MasterCard lete hain, lekin kabhi kabhi American Express aur Discover nahi lete. Reasons: 1) In cards ko accept karne ki fees plain Visa aur MasterCard se zyada hoti hai. 2) In issuers ke saath customers ke liye charges dispute aur reverse karna aasaan ho sakta hai.
qs.b: Most merchants accept Visa and MasterCard, but some decline American Express and Discover because their acceptance fees tend to be higher and it may be easier for customers to dispute and reverse charges with those issuers.
qs.t: AmEx/Discover = mehenga fee + aasaan dispute.

qs.q: Why should you pay with the testing card beforehand when ordering in a restaurant?
qs.s: In-store FAQs pehle se padh lo kyunki real life me sochne ka time nahi milta; TTLs answer dete hain lekin ye knowledge dono ka time bachata hai. Restaurant me: jo card test kar rahe ho woh terminal pe acceptable na ho ya refuse ho jaye, aur aap khana order kar chuke ho, to apne cash se pay karna padega. Isliye paisa bachane ke liye, agar test cycle recommend kare to sabse sasta khana order karo.
qs.b: The testing card might not be accepted or might be refused by the restaurant terminal, and if I have already ordered I would have to pay in cash myself. So I pay with the testing card beforehand and, if the cycle recommends it, order the cheapest food to save money in case I have to pay.
qs.t: Pehle card try, phir khana - aur sabse sasta.

qs.q: Do you get the same reward if the testing card is declined or errors out in store?
qs.s: Zyada tar cases me haan - agar testing card test hua (swipe, insert ya tap) aur terminal se koi bhi response (approval, not accepted, rejection ya error) receipt ke saath mila, aur tester ne same effort lagaya, to reward same milna chahiye. Lekin har case me (approval, not accepted, rejection, error) merchant se receipt lena zaroori hai - test case ke transaction ka proof. Lekin agar store me terminal hi nahi hai aur sirf cash accept hota hai, to lower reward wala dusra test case claim karne ko kaha ja sakta hai kyunki card test nahi hua.
qs.b: In most cases yes: if the card was swiped, inserted or tapped and any terminal response with a receipt was received, whether approval, not accepted, rejection or error, the same effort should earn the same reward. I must take the receipt in every case as proof. If the store has no terminal and only takes cash, I may be asked to claim another test case with a lower reward because the card was not tested.
qs.t: Card chala + receipt mili = same reward; terminal hi nahi = kam reward.

qs.q: What should you say if a merchant questions your honesty while you test cards?
qs.s: Merchant ko mat batao ki aap card test kar rahe ho - trouble aur explain karne me time waste se bacho. Agar card pe zaroori information nahi hai to merchant ko bolo ki ye business card hai.
qs.b: I do not reveal that I am testing the card, to avoid trouble and wasted time. If the card lacks the usual information, I tell the merchant it is a business card.
qs.t: Sawal ho to: business card hai.

qs.q: Can merchants refuse certain types of cards, and what should you do?
qs.s: Haan, ye merchant ki marzi hai. Kuch merchants high fees ki wajah se specific cards nahi lete, ya testing cards pe suspicious ho jate hain, khas kar jab card pe koi inscription ya cardholder name nahi hota. Aisa ho to calm raho aur politely walk away karo.
qs.b: Yes, merchants can refuse. Some do not accept specific cards because of high fees, and some get suspicious of testing cards, especially cards without an inscription or cardholder name. In that case I stay calm and walk away politely.
qs.t: Mana kare to shanti se nikal lo.

qs.q: Is the full card number shown on a terminal receipt?
qs.s: Nahi, sirf last 4 ya 5 digits. Receipts pe card number ke last five digits se zyada aur expiration date nahi dikhni chahiye. Poora credit card number receipt pe ho aur receipt kho jaye ya chori ho to security risk hai - koi bhi fraud kar sakta hai.
qs.b: No. Receipts show only the last 4 or 5 digits and must reveal no more than the last five digits and no expiration date, because a full card number on a lost or stolen receipt could easily be used for fraud.
qs.t: Receipt pe max last 5 digit, expiry kabhi nahi.

qs.q: What do you do if a store you must test is permanently closed?
qs.s: Kabhi Google Maps pe store working dikhta hai lekin jaane pe pata chalta hai store exist hi nahi karta. Test cycle me probably iske liye test case hoga, kyunki wahan jaane ki mehnat ka pay karna sense banata hai. Evidence dena hoga: 1) Us jagah ke paas aapki GPS image. 2) Store ki jagah jo place hai uski photo.
qs.b: If a store shown as open on Google Maps turns out not to exist, the cycle will probably have a test case for that so the effort is paid. I provide a GPS image of myself near the location and a photo of the place where the store should be.
qs.t: Store gayab = GPS + jagah ki photo.

qs.q: Should you sign a testing card provided by the test cycle?
qs.s: Nahi, sign nahi karna, kyunki ye cards aapke baad dusre testers bhi test ke liye use kar sakte hain. Agar test cycle overview isko warn karta hai to kisi bhi circumstance me sign mat karo.
qs.b: No. Cycle-provided testing cards may be used by other testers after me, so I do not sign them, and if the overview warns about it I never sign under any circumstances.
qs.t: Cycle ka card = sabka card, sign nahi.

qs.q: Is there a payment limit on testing cards given by test cycles?
qs.s: Team ka paisa bachane ke liye payment amount pe limit lagana sense banata hai. Overview dhyan se padho aur koi limit ho to note karo. Lekin kuch stores me products/services card limit se mehenge ho sakte hain - isliye hamesha TTL se poocho ki agar price thoda zyada hai to limit cross karna allowed hai ya nahi.
qs.b: Usually yes, to save money for the team, so I read the overview carefully and note any limit. If a store's items cost slightly more than the limit, I always ask the TTL whether going over is allowed.
qs.t: Limit overview me; thoda upar jaana ho to TTL se poocho.

qs.q: Can you be charged twice if a contactless card is tapped more than once?
qs.s: Nahi. Contactless terminal card ko kitni bhi baar read kare, charge sirf ek baar hi hoga.
qs.b: No. No matter how many times a contactless terminal reads the card, the charge occurs only once.
qs.t: Do tap, ek charge.

topics.name: Usability Testing
topics.intro: Usability Testing course: real users se UI, usability aur UX ka feedback lena, surveys, video recordings, GDPR aur best practices.

qs.q: What is usability testing?
qs.s: Usability Testing matlab product ya application ke user interface ko aise logon se test karwana jo us app ke user population ka representative sample hain. Participants check karte hain ki UI user-friendly hai ya nahi, aur kya user intended tasks successfully aur aasani se complete kar pata hai. Ye design, usability aur experience par feedback collect karne ka effective tareeka hai. Clients testers ki honest aur real opinions ko value karte hain taaki target audience ke liye sabse user-centric experience design kar sakein.
qs.b: Usability testing is testing a product's user interface with people who are a representative sample of its real users. Participants evaluate whether the interface is user-friendly and whether they can complete the intended tasks successfully and with ease. It is an effective way to collect honest feedback on design, usability and experience so the client can build a more user-centric product.
qs.t: Real users + real tasks + aasani = usability testing.

qs.q: What are the three things usability studies focus on?
qs.s: Teen focus areas: 1) User Interface (UI): pages, screens aur visual elements ki series jisse user service ke saath interact karta hai. UI me colors, font size, layout, images, menus, pages ke beech navigation, content aur content ka organization aata hai. 2) Usability: website ya app ka ease of use, yaani user kitni aasani aur effectively app use kar pata hai. Example: shopping site ki usability high hai agar user bina unnecessary ya unintuitive steps ke item basket me add kar le. 3) User Experience (UX): user website ko kaise experience karta hai, use karne se pehle, dauran aur baad ke positive aur negative thoughts aur feelings. UX baaki dono se zyada subjective hai kyunki ye emotional response measure karta hai.
qs.b: Usability studies focus on three things. The UI, meaning the screens and visual elements such as colors, font size, layout, images, menus, navigation and content organization. Usability, meaning how easily and effectively a user can use the product, for example adding an item to a basket without unnecessary steps. And UX, the range of thoughts and feelings before, during and after use, which is the most subjective because it measures emotional response.
qs.t: U-U-UX: dikhta kya hai (UI), chalta kaise hai (Usability), lagta kaisa hai (UX).

qs.q: Which of UI, usability and UX is the most subjective, and why?
qs.s: Notes ke hisaab se UX sabse zyada subjective hai, UI aur Usability factors se bhi zyada, kyunki UX emotional response measure karta hai. UX me before, during aur after use ke positive aur negative thoughts aur feelings ki range count hoti hai.
qs.b: UX is the most subjective of the three, because it measures the user's emotional response to the website or application. It covers the positive and negative thoughts and feelings that arise before, during and after use, rather than visual elements or task efficiency.
qs.t: UX = dil ki baat, isliye sabse subjective.

qs.q: Why is usability testing needed?
qs.s: Companies software aur products consumer ke use ke liye banati hain. Successful end-user product ke liye wo end user ke liye easy to use hona chahiye. Agar user-friendly nahi hai to users use karne, khareedne ya refer karne ke liye kam inclined honge. User-friendly product market me laane ka ek tareeka usability testing hai. Notes ye bhi kehte hain ki companies ko product creation phase me UI design ke liye usability expert bhi lana chahiye.
qs.b: Products are built for end users, so a successful product must be easy for them to use. If it is not user-friendly, people are less likely to use, buy or refer it. Usability testing is one way companies make sure they bring user-friendly products to market, ideally alongside a usability expert who helps design the interface during product creation.
qs.t: Use nahi kar paaya = khareedega nahi, refer bhi nahi karega.

qs.q: When should usability testing be done in the development cycle?
qs.s: Perfect world me usability testing poore development cycle me hoti hai. Shuru me simple prototype se, ya agar implementation available nahi hai to paper prototypes (wireframes aur sketches) se bhi test ho sakta hai. Minimum: completed application available hone ke baad lekin paid customers ko bechne aur use hone se pehle. Kyunki usability testing current implementation me issues nikalti hai, cycle me itna time chhodo ki kam se kam small aur obvious issues (low-hanging fruit) fix ho jaayein; complex issues first maintenance release tak defer ho sakte hain.
qs.b: Ideally usability testing runs throughout the development cycle, starting early with simple or even paper prototypes such as wireframes and sketches. At minimum it should happen once the completed application is available but before paying customers use it. Enough time should be left to fix the small, obvious issues, the low-hanging fruit, while more complex issues can be deferred to a first maintenance release.
qs.t: Paper se shuru, launch se pehle zaroor; chhote fix abhi, bade maintenance release me.

qs.q: Who needs usability testing?
qs.s: Notes ke mutabik har company jo user-facing products banati hai, use usability testing chahiye taaki product user-friendly ho.
qs.b: Every company that makes user-facing products needs usability testing to make sure the product is user-friendly.
qs.t: User dekhta hai? To usability test chahiye.

qs.q: What are the different ways usability testing can be executed?
qs.s: 1) In-house usability testing: participants test in-person usi building me jahan test moderator hai. 2) Remote usability testing: participant aur moderator same location par nahi. Remote do tarah ka: Moderated (synchronous): moderator aur participant real-time communicate karte hain, phone ya screen sharing se. Unmoderated (asynchronous): real-time communication nahi; participant moderator ka banaya survey task plan use karke apne schedule par testing complete karta hai.
qs.b: Usability testing can be in-house, where participants test in person in the same building as the moderator, or remote, where they are in different locations. Remote testing can be moderated, also called synchronous, where moderator and participant talk in real time by phone or screen sharing, or unmoderated, also called asynchronous, where the participant follows a survey task plan created by the moderator on their own schedule.
qs.t: Moderated = Synchronous = saath me live; Unmoderated = Asynchronous = apne time pe.

qs.q: Which type of usability testing does the platform mostly focus on, and how does that process work?
qs.s: Platform mostly remote unmoderated usability testing par focus karta hai. Process: 1) Usability expert existing product/app review karta hai aur client se baat karke unke pain points samajhta hai. 2) Expert ek survey compile karta hai jisme task plan hota hai jo har test participant execute karega. 3) Expert app ka expert review bhi karta hai. 4) Participants ke surveys complete hone ke baad expert data analyze karta hai aur results report banata hai jisme surveys ke aggregated results aur enhancements/changes ke suggestions hote hain.
qs.b: The platform mostly focuses on remote unmoderated usability testing. A usability expert reviews the product, talks to the client about pain points, and compiles a survey with a task plan that each participant executes, while also doing an expert review. After participants finish, the expert analyzes the data and produces a results report with aggregated survey results and suggestions for enhancements.
qs.t: Expert: samjho, survey banao, khud review karo, report do.

qs.q: What questions should you ask yourself to give useful UX feedback?
qs.s: Companies apni websites aur apps apne customers ke liye design karti hain. Relevant, honest aur useful feedback dene ke liye customer mindset me switch karo aur khud se poochho: 1) How does it make you feel? 2) Can you navigate the pages with ease? 3) Do you get stuck somewhere? 4) What recommendations would you give to improve it? Notes ye bhi kehte hain ki hamari individual preferences aur prior experiences decide karte hain ki hum kisi offering ko kaise respond karte hain, aur usability aur UX aksar subconsciously decide karte hain ki website pasand aayi ya nahi.
qs.b: I switch to the customer mindset and ask four questions: how does it make me feel, can I navigate the pages with ease, do I get stuck anywhere, and what would I recommend to improve it. Usability and UX often shape subconsciously whether we like a site, so these questions help me give relevant, honest and useful feedback.
qs.t: Feel, Navigate, Stuck, Recommend - FNSR.

qs.q: Why do companies do usability testing, and what scenarios do they want to avoid?
qs.s: Companies usability testing karti hain taaki superior user experience dekar customers ko apne page par rakhein aur competitors se door rakhein. Jo scenarios avoid karne hain: 1) Website use karte hue aapko doosron se poochna pade ki basket me item kaise add karein. 2) Checkout process complete karne me 30 minutes lag jaayein.
qs.b: Companies run usability tests to keep customers on their site and away from competitors by offering a superior user experience. They want to avoid situations like a user having to ask someone how to add an item to the basket, or the checkout process taking 30 minutes.
qs.t: Basket ke liye help maangna aur 30 min checkout = customer gaya competitor ke paas.

qs.q: What is the goal of desktop usability?
qs.s: Desktop usability ki definitions alag hain, depending kisse baat kar rahe ho: customers, developers ya test engineers. Lekin goal same hai: 1) user ko easy to use interface dena; 2) user apna goal/task shortest time me accomplish kar sake; 3) support calls kam hon.
qs.b: Definitions differ between customers, developers and test engineers, but the goal of desktop usability is the same: give the user an interface that is easy to use, lets them accomplish their task in the shortest time, and reduces support calls.
qs.t: Easy, Fast, Kam support calls.

qs.q: How were desktop applications designed in the early days?
qs.s: Early days me user ko ordered screens ki series se guide kiya jaata tha, kyunki development paradigm tha 'one entry point into a function and one exit point out of a function'. Isse application 'one size fits all' categorize hoti thi. Installation manual thi: install karo, phir specific configuration files manually modify karo. Customization minimal ya aksar non-existent tha.
qs.b: Early desktop applications guided users through a fixed series of ordered screens, because the paradigm was one entry point into a function and one exit point out of it, making them one size fits all. Installation was manual, with users editing configuration files, and customization was minimal or non-existent.
qs.t: Purana zamana: ek darwaza andar, ek bahar, sabke liye ek size.

qs.q: What was the most important usability innovation for desktop applications today, and how does it work?
qs.s: Aaj desktop usability design karte waqt sabse pehla factor audience hai; public use ke liye app ho to har experience/knowledge level ke users consider karne padte hain. Sabse important innovation: installation ko jitna ho sake painless banana. Aaj installation screens ki series hoti hai jise Wizard kehte hain, jo user ko specific information aur choices deti hai ki app kaise aur kahan install ho. User selection ke basis par software behind the scenes zaroori program changes kar deta hai. Wizard concept OS ke dusre functions par bhi apply hua: new hardware add karna, network configure karna, aur aise areas jahan pehle bada installation guide ya manual padhna padta tha jo average user ke liye foreign terminology me hota tha. Wo guide samajh nahi aata tha to tech support call hi option tha. Wizards se novice user bhi successfully install karke turant chal sakta hai. Ye 'usability' hai.
qs.b: The audience comes first, and for public applications you must cater to every experience level. The most important usability innovation was making installation painless through Wizards, a series of screens that give the user information and choices about how and where to install, while the software makes the changes behind the scenes. The same concept is used for adding hardware or configuring a network, replacing hard-to-read manuals and support calls, so even novices can get up and running immediately.
qs.t: Wizard = manual + support call ka replacement.

qs.q: How do customizable toolbars and menus support usability in desktop applications?
qs.s: Desktop apps me simplest se most complex tasks ke liye bahut functions hote hain. User customizable toolbars aur menu bars se configure kar sakta hai ki app kaise perform kare, apne task set ke hisaab se functions choose karke. Most common functions ek mouse click door hon to menus/folders scan karne ka time bachta hai aur task jaldi complete hota hai. Example: jo user MS Word me constantly documents edit karta hai, use Web, Web Tools, Frames ya Database functions ki zaroorat nahi, to wo ye toolbars hide kar sakta hai, aur editing toolbars document ke upar visible rakh sakta hai. Toolbars visual impact ke liye bhi customize hote hain: kuch log small icons, kuch larger icons, kuch icons ke saath function text form me dekhna pasand karte hain. Ye 'usability' hai.
qs.b: Users can choose which functions appear on their toolbars and menus based on their tasks, keeping the most common ones a click away so they do not waste time searching through menus. For example, someone editing documents in Word can hide Web, Web Tools, Frames or Database toolbars and keep editing tools visible. Toolbars can also be customized visually, with small icons, large icons, or icons with text.
qs.t: Jo roz chahiye wo ek click pe; baaki chhupa do.

qs.q: What are themes or skins, and why do they count as usability?
qs.s: Users ko aksar apni applications ko 'skin' karne ki ability milti hai aesthetic appeal ke liye. Bahut apps me standard 'themes' hote hain: coordinated backgrounds, typefaces, button styles, cursors, etc. ke sets, jo user favorite color ya background ke hisaab se choose kar sakta hai, ya apna personal theme bana sakta hai. Isse user ko satisfaction milta hai kyunki ye unhe pleasing lagta hai aur wo use apna keh sakte hain. Ye 'usability' hai.
qs.b: Themes are coordinated sets of backgrounds, typefaces, button styles and cursors that users can select or customize to create their own. They count as usability because they give the user satisfaction, the application feels pleasing and like something they can call their own.
qs.t: Apna theme = apnapan = satisfaction.

qs.q: How has Help improved desktop usability?
qs.s: Saalon me usability improve karne ka ek sabse bada change Help ke area me hua. Help files se user apna subject matter aur zaroori information aasani se dhoondh pata hai, aur Help aise context me likha gaya jo most users samajh sakein. Help Files ka coverage bhi badha: jo information application ke andar nahi hai wo online available hai, saath me forums jahan users questions pooch kar dusre users se answers le sakte hain. Ye 'usability' hai.
qs.b: Help is one of the biggest usability improvements. Help files make it easier to find information, are written in language most users understand, and their coverage has grown, with extra information available online along with forums where users can ask questions and get answers from other users.
qs.t: Help = samajh aane wali bhasha + online + forums.

qs.q: How does desktop usability differ for private industry (corporate) applications?
qs.s: Private industry apps ki audience bahut narrower hoti hai kyunki users ke specific job functions ya skill sets hote hain. Desktop customization corporate policies se limited ho sakti hai. Company aesthetic changes allow na kare ya sirf kuch appearance changes allow kare taaki company me uniformity bani rahe. Companies aksar app ya OS desktop ko customize karti hain, kuch functions hide ya disable karke (jo user ke tasks/role ke liye zaroori nahi), phir available karti hain. Employee kuch customization kar sakta hai lekin sirf company policy ke andar. Ye corporate 'usability' hai.
qs.b: Corporate applications have a narrower audience of users with specific job functions or skills. Customization is often limited by company policy to keep uniformity, and companies may hide or disable functions not needed for a role before rollout. Employees can still customize, but only within the policy, which is corporate usability.
qs.t: Corporate = narrow audience + policy ki boundary.

qs.q: What are software suites, and how do they relate to usability?
qs.s: Pichhle kuch saalon me desktop usability ka role 'software suites' tak expand hua, jahan kai applications ek dusre ke saath interact karti hain aur sabka same look and feel hota hai, taaki user ka learning curve minimum ho aur apps ke beech interaction seamless ho. Saath hi suite ki har application independently customize ho sakti hai. Desktop apps ab web applications ke saath bhi interface kar rahi hain, jisse desktop aur apps ka appearance aur customization badal raha hai, taaki dono apps usable aur seamless hon minimal learning curve ke saath.
qs.b: Software suites are groups of applications that interact with each other and share the same look and feel, which minimizes the learning curve and makes moving between them seamless, while each app can still be customized independently. Desktop apps are also starting to interface with web apps, again aiming for seamless use with a minimal learning curve.
qs.t: Suite = same look and feel = kam seekhna padta hai.

qs.q: How do the notes summarize usability in one sentence?
qs.s: Notes ka one-sentence summary: 'Usability is empowering the user to be able to perform their task with minimal effort.'
qs.b: Usability is empowering the user to perform their task with minimal effort.
qs.t: Minimum mehnat, task poora = usability.

qs.q: What is web usability, and what are its broad goals?
qs.s: Web usability ek approach hai websites ko end-user ke liye easy to use banane ki, bina kisi specialized training ke. User web page par actions ko general life ke interactions se intuitively relate kar sake (jaise button dabao to result action ho). Broad goals: 1) Information clear aur concise tareeke se present karo. 2) Users ko correct choices bahut obvious tareeke se do. 3) Kisi action ke consequences ke baare me ambiguity hatao (jaise delete/remove/purchase click karna). 4) Sabse important cheez web page ya web app par sahi jagah rakho.
qs.b: Web usability means making websites easy to use without any special training, so users can intuitively relate actions on a page to everyday interactions, like pressing a button to cause an action. Its goals are to present information clearly and concisely, give the correct choices in an obvious way, remove ambiguity about the consequences of actions such as delete or purchase, and put the most important thing in the right place.
qs.t: Clear info, Obvious choice, No ambiguity, Right place.

qs.q: What are the four broad areas of web usability?
qs.s: Notes ke mutabik web usability ke broad areas: 1) Ease of Access (accessibility), 2) Clarity of Communication, 3) Content, 4) Navigation.
qs.b: Web usability can be divided into four broad areas: ease of access, clarity of communication, content, and navigation.
qs.t: ACCN: Access, Communication, Content, Navigation.

qs.q: Why is ease of access the most important aspect of web usability?
qs.s: Web usability ka sabse important aspect 'Accessibility' hai: kya site aasani se accessible hai? Website har group ke users ke liye accessible honi chahiye. Agar ye aspect handle nahi hua to content kitna bhi achha ho, koi dekhna nahi chahega. Agar access karna pain hai to user ke wapas aane ka chance kam. Website ka feel aur look design aur end-user dono perspective se dhyan me rakhna chahiye; design business ke hisaab se alag ho sakta hai lekin purpose same: ease of access. Website people with disabilities ke liye bhi accessible honi chahiye W3C standards follow karne ke liye. Example: images ke liye ALT tags, jo disabilities wale users ko samajhne me help karte hain ki wo portion kis liye hai, aur low internet par bhi help karte hain. Color schema mostly dedicated design team decide karti hai, lekin hum ensure karke value add kar sakte hain ki end-user ke liye sab achha dikhe.
qs.b: Accessibility is the most important aspect, because if a site is hard to access no one will look at its content, however good, and users are less likely to return. The site should be accessible to every group of users, including people with disabilities, following W3C standards, for example ALT tags on images, which help users with disabilities and users on slow internet. Testers can also add value by checking that the design team's color scheme looks good for end users.
qs.t: ALT tag = disability wale user + slow internet dono ka dost.

qs.q: What does clarity of communication mean in web usability?
qs.s: Har website ka ek purpose hai aur user ko uske baare me informed hona chahiye: business ke baare me aur saari relevant info jo user ko trust karne ke liye entice kare. User ko website ka purpose samajh aana chahiye zyada info ke liye access karne se pehle. Agar info sahi tareeke se convey nahi hui to user missing information ki complain karega. Proper information proper jagah par, bina hassle ke. Example: 'About Us' jaise basic info links, aur query ke liye 'Contact Us' link sahi jagah hona chahiye. Website ka brand uska logo hai jo vital info hai; logo relevant industry ke saath sync me hona chahiye.
qs.b: Clarity of communication means the user should understand the site's purpose and the business behind it, with enough relevant information to trust it. The right information should be in the right place without hassle, such as clear About Us and Contact Us links, otherwise users complain about missing information. The logo is the brand and should be in sync with the industry.
qs.t: Purpose clear, About Us + Contact Us ready, logo industry se match.

qs.q: What makes good website content from a usability perspective?
qs.s: Content kisi bhi website ka important portion hai. Content clear aur easy to understand ho, aur target users ke level ke hisaab se baat kare. Home page par content aur design elements ka balance ho, aur required info ya links ho. Kisi bhi underlying page se user jaldi main page par wapas ja sake. Agar info files ke form me hai to users download kar sakein aur unme appropriate contents milein. Reading interactive ho business objectives dhyan me rakhte hue. Example: URLs ya links descriptive hon taaki user samjhe kis liye hain, aur saath me concise bhi. Content me proper heading ho aur 'bold' aur 'italic' ka appropriate jagah use ho jo users ko attract kare.
qs.b: Content should be clear, easy to understand and pitched at the level of the target users. The home page should balance content and design, users should be able to get back to the main page quickly from any page, downloadable files should contain what they promise, and links and URLs should be descriptive yet concise. Proper headings and appropriate use of bold and italic help draw users in.
qs.t: Clear content, descriptive-but-short links, sahi jagah bold/italic.

qs.q: What should be checked about website navigation?
qs.s: Navigation ka type matter nahi karta, one-tier, two-tier ya three-tier, lekin easily accessible hona chahiye. Site ke kisi bhi part se home page par wapas jaane ka raasta hamesha ho. Links poori website me consistent hon, same style aur color schema. Navigation aisa ho ki naya visitor kahin lost na ho. Example: company logo home page se linked ho taaki user aasani se home par wapas jaa sake. Agar site 'Site Search' feature deti hai (jo aajkal quick access ke liye vital hai) to uska proper implementation aur location site ke design element ko dhyan me rakh kar ho.
qs.b: Whatever the navigation type, one, two or three tier, it should be easily accessible, with a way back to the home page from anywhere, for example by linking the logo to the home page. Links should be consistent in style and color so new visitors never get lost, and if there is a site search it should be properly implemented and placed in line with the design.
qs.t: Logo click = ghar wapsi; links ek jaise; search sahi jagah.

qs.q: Why is web usability a continuous process, and what is the aim of usability testing?
qs.s: Web usability continuous process hai kyunki site ka design aur dusre elements badalte rehte hain. Target audience ke representatives se surveys karwana bahut important hai, isse naye ideas milte hain aur pata chalta hai ki kuch badalna hai ya nahi. Usability testing ka aim: samajhna ki log site kaise use karte hain aur errors note karna, saath hi kuch parts me improvement ke areas.
qs.b: Web usability is continuous because the design and elements of a site keep changing, so surveys with representatives of the target audience are needed to learn what should change. The aim of usability testing is to understand how people use the site and to note errors as well as areas of improvement.
qs.t: Site badlegi, test chalta rahega.

qs.q: Where can you find the study requirements in a usability cycle?
qs.s: Usability cycles me study requirements in sections me ho sakti hain: 1) Overview, 2) Slots tab under slotting rules, 3) Slot description of each slot.
qs.b: Study requirements can be found in the cycle Overview, in the Slots tab under the slotting rules, and in the slot description of each individual slot.
qs.t: Overview, Slotting rules, Slot description - teeno jagah dekho.

qs.q: When is UX feedback acceptable?
qs.s: Usability testing customers ke liye tabhi valuable hai jab feedback un users se aaye jo certain criteria meet karte hain. Customers ye criteria define karte hain, aur mandatory hai ki sirf wahi log cycle accept karein jo criteria meet karte hain. Jo testers study requirements meet nahi karte unke results accept nahi honge. Agar aap study requirements match nahi karte to cycle accept mat karo aur slot claim mat karo.
qs.b: UX feedback is only valuable if it comes from users who meet the criteria the customer defines, so it is mandatory that only testers who meet those criteria accept the cycle. Results from testers who do not meet the study requirements are not accepted, so I never accept a cycle or claim a slot I do not match.
qs.t: Criteria match nahi = cycle accept nahi, slot claim nahi.

qs.q: What are the reasons a usability survey may be rejected or a slot unclaimed?
qs.s: Saare 7 reasons: 1) SRS me diye answers survey ke andar ke answers se alag hain. 2) Survey ke answers claimed slot ki study requirements se match nahi karte. 3) Survey questions ke invalid aur incoherent responses. 4) Tester ki inactivity ya unsatisfactory progress. 5) Video slots ke liye koi video upload nahi hua ya tester video me bol nahi raha. 6) Survey instructions follow nahi kiye. 7) Wrong slot claim kiya (jaise invalid geolocation). Note: jo testers baar baar wrong slots claim karte hain ya study requirements match nahi karte, unhe saare usability test cycles se exclude kiya ja sakta hai.
qs.b: A survey can be rejected or a slot unclaimed if the SRS answers differ from the survey answers, if the survey answers do not match the claimed slot's requirements, if responses are invalid or incoherent, if the tester is inactive or progress is unsatisfactory, if a video slot has no video or the tester is not speaking, if survey instructions are not followed, or if the wrong slot was claimed, such as an invalid geolocation. Testers who repeatedly claim wrong slots or do not match requirements may be excluded from all usability cycles.
qs.t: SRS mismatch, slot mismatch, bakwas jawab, inactive, video/awaaz nahi, instructions ignore, galat slot - 7.

qs.q: What can happen to testers who keep claiming wrong slots?
qs.s: Notes ka note: testers jo wrong slots claim karte rehte hain ya study requirements match nahi karte, unhe saare usability test cycles se exclude kiya ja sakta hai.
qs.b: Testers who keep claiming the wrong slots or not matching the study requirements may be excluded from all usability test cycles.
qs.t: Baar baar galat slot = saare UX cycles se bahar.

qs.q: How can you recognize a usability cycle on the platform?
qs.s: Jab aapko platform par Usability cycle ka invite milta hai, to test cycle ID ke bagal me 'Ux' icon dikhta hai jo testing type denote karta hai.
qs.b: A usability cycle is marked by a Ux icon next to the test cycle ID, which denotes the testing type.
qs.t: Cycle ID ke paas Ux = usability cycle.

qs.q: What are the steps to start and complete a usability survey?
qs.s: Steps: 1) Test cycle accept karne ke baad upper navigation menu me 'Slots' tab par click karo aur apne profile se match karta slot claim karo. 2) 'Take Survey' tab par click karo aur 'Start Survey' click karo. 3) Phir 'Survey Direct Link' par click karo taaki survey new browser tab me khule aur aapka platform profile visible na ho. 4) Survey finish hote hi 'Study Complete' button click karke survey submit karo. 5) Agar screenshots ya videos chahiye, to 'Uploads' tab par click karke attachments upload karo; upload aur submit ke baad aap done ho.
qs.b: After accepting the cycle, I open the Slots tab and claim a slot matching my profile. Then I go to the Take Survey tab, click Start Survey, and open the Survey Direct Link so the survey runs in a new tab without my profile visible. When finished I click Study Complete to submit, and if screenshots or videos are required I upload them in the Uploads tab.
qs.t: Slots, Take Survey, Start, Direct Link, Study Complete, Uploads.

qs.q: Why is it important to read survey instructions thoroughly?
qs.s: Survey ke instruction text ko thoroughly padhna extremely important hai, chahe (aur khaas kar jab) wo lambe hon. Unme ho sakta hai video recording kab start karni hai ya kisi task se pehle kaun se questions answer karne hain. Instructions follow nahi kiye to poora survey reject hone ka risk hai kyunki answers valid nahi rehte.
qs.b: Survey instructions must be read thoroughly, especially when long, because they may say when to start recording or which questions to answer before a task. Not following them risks the whole survey being rejected because the answers are no longer valid.
qs.t: Lambi instruction = zyada dhyan se padho.

qs.q: What should you avoid in survey responses?
qs.s: Chaar cheezein avoid karo: 1) One liners: clients ko report karne ke liye sirf aapke survey answers hote hain, isliye open-ended questions me detailed answer do. 'I didn't like the design' ya 'the website looks good' jaise answers help nahi karte. Khud se 'Why?' poochho; agar kuch pasand nahi to explain karo kyun aur kya chahiye. Usability study me koi wrong answer nahi; honest real feedback chahiye jo sirf aapke personal experience par based ho, na ki dusre kya feel karenge. 2) Question se unrelated answers: answers question se relate karein; jaise checkout experience poocha hai to login ki problems mat batao. 3) Poor language: agar survey language me comfortable nahi ho to pooch sakte ho ki native language me answer kar sakte ho; aksar translate karne wale log hote hain. Survey language me confusing answer se native language me clear answer behtar. 4) Estimated survey duration ke comparison me impossible response time: har cycle se pehle UX engineer ya TTL survey karke dekhta hai, aur wo time expected duration ka reference hota hai. Bahut tez response signal deta hai ki care aur attention-to-detail nahi tha, aur results invalidate ho sakte hain.
qs.b: I avoid four things: one-liner answers, since my answers are the only data reported to the client, so I explain why I like or dislike something; answers that do not relate to the question, like describing login problems when asked about checkout; poor language, since I can ask to answer in my native language and a clear native answer beats a confusing one; and an impossibly fast completion time compared to the reference time set by the UX engineer or TTL, which may invalidate my results.
qs.t: One-liner, off-topic, poor language, too fast - chaaron se bacho.

qs.q: How is the expected survey duration estimated?
qs.s: Har usability test cycle se pehle UX engineer ya TTL survey khud karke dekhta hai. Survey complete karne me jo time laga wo reference time hota hai jisse testers ka expected duration estimate hota hai. Unreasonably fast response se lagta hai ki care aur attention-to-detail skip hua, aur results invalid ho sakte hain.
qs.b: Before each usability cycle, either the UX engineer or the TTL goes through the survey, and the time they take is used as the reference for the expected duration. An unreasonably fast response suggests a lack of care and attention to detail and may invalidate the results.
qs.t: UX engineer/TTL ka time = benchmark; usse bahut tez = shak.

qs.q: Are there wrong answers in a usability study?
qs.s: Notes kehte hain usability study me koi wrong answers nahi hote. Honest, real feedback chahiye jo sirf aapke personal experience par based ho, na ki ye ki dusre log kaise feel kar sakte hain.
qs.b: There are no wrong answers in a usability study. The client wants honest, real feedback based only on my personal experience, not on how I think others might feel.
qs.t: Apni feeling batao, dusron ki nahi.

qs.q: When should you claim a video slot?
qs.s: Video slot sirf tab claim karo jab 100% sure ho ki video time par de paoge. Bina video ke submissions reject ho jaate hain.
qs.b: Only claim a video slot if you are 100% sure you can provide the video in time, because submissions without a video are rejected.
qs.t: 100% sure ho tabhi video slot.

qs.q: Why are video recordings valuable in usability testing, and what should they capture?
qs.s: Videos se customer wahi dekh aur sun pata hai jo aap dekh aur experience kar rahe ho; prototype ya app use karte waqt testers ke mind me kya chal raha hai uski valuable insights milti hain, aur website ke improvement wale areas detect karne me help hoti hai. Most usability tests me start-to-finish real time video chahiye taaki customer dekhe: 1) Where you get stuck, 2) What you liked, 3) How you felt about the experience. Examples: task me online shopping cart me products add karke checkout complete karna; agar kisi action se blocked ho to recording continue rakho, issue capture karo aur clearly explain karo. Blocker issues customer ke liye extremely valuable hain.
qs.b: Videos let the customer see and hear what I experience, giving insight into my mind and showing which areas need improvement. Most tests need a real-time, start-to-finish recording showing where I get stuck, what I liked and how I felt. If I am blocked, I keep recording, capture the issue and explain it clearly, because blocker issues are extremely valuable to the customer.
qs.t: Stuck, Liked, Felt - aur blocker aaye to recording band mat karo.

qs.q: What should you avoid in usability video recordings?
qs.s: 1) Sirf actions explain karna bina thoughts ya feelings ke. Jaise 'I'm scrolling down, I clicked this, I added this to my cart' visible actions hain, lekin client jaanna chahta hai aap poore process me kya soch aur feel kar rahe ho; client primarily aapke thoughts aur feelings me interested hai. 2) Khud ko video me record mat karo kyunki ye GDPR violation hai.
qs.b: I avoid only narrating visible actions like scrolling or clicking without sharing my thoughts and feelings, because the client is mainly interested in what I think and feel. I also never record myself on camera, since that is a GDPR violation.
qs.t: Click-click commentary nahi, dil ki baat; apna chehra nahi.

qs.q: Which recording tool should you use, and what is not allowed?
qs.s: Screen recording tool use karo. Test cycle overview me aapke device ke liye suggested screen recording software list hota hai. Pehle device ki screen ko record karne ke liye second device use mat karo; aise videos inferior quality ki wajah se reject ho jaate hain.
qs.b: Use a screen recording tool, as suggested in the test cycle overview for your device. Do not use a second device to film your first device's screen, because such videos are rejected for inferior quality.
qs.t: Screen recorder haan, doosre phone se shooting na.

qs.q: How should you follow video instructions in a usability survey?
qs.s: Survey me instructions hoti hain ki video me kaun se steps record karne hain. Video recording instructions non-video slots me bhi dikhte hain, jinhe ignore kar sakte ho. Agar video slot claim kiya hai to video instructions bahut dhyan se padho, aur agar task permit nahi karta to test website par kahin bhi click mat karo. Sirf tab click karo jab kaha jaaye, aur sirf wahi record karo jo kaha gaya hai. Example: instructions checkout process record karne ko kehti hain to website ke dusre sections me navigate karte hue khud ko record mat karo.
qs.b: I read the video instructions carefully, click only when the task asks me to, and record only what is asked, for example only the checkout process and not other sections of the site. Video instructions also appear in non-video slots, where they can be ignored.
qs.t: Jo kaha wahi record, jo kaha tabhi click.

qs.q: What does speaking your thoughts out loud in a video involve?
qs.s: Har action se pehle aur baad apne thoughts out loud bolo. Customer aapka honest verbal feedback chahta hai aur aapke thoughts, feelings aur actions ke peeche motivations jaanna chahta hai. Har task me jo mind me aaye consistently bolo, browsing aur navigating ke dauran bhi, app/website par action se pehle aur baad, positive ho ya negative: what you did, why you did it, what you expected to happen, what you didn't expect, what you like, what you dislike, what is clear, what is unclear, etc. Improvement ya feature add karne ke suggestions bhi de sakte ho. Video record karte waqt explore aur sochne ka time lo.
qs.b: I speak my thoughts aloud consistently before and after every action, including while browsing and navigating, whether positive or negative. I explain what I did, why, what I expected, what surprised me, what I like and dislike, and what is clear or unclear, and I can suggest improvements or new features. I take my time to explore and think while recording.
qs.t: Kiya, kyun, expect, surprise, like, dislike, clear, unclear - sab bolo.

qs.q: What four things must you account for regarding sound quality in a video recording?
qs.s: Sound quality critical hai. Chaar cheezein: 1) Recording start karne se pehle voice recording on hai ye check karo, ki aapki awaaz clearly suni aur samjhi ja sake. 2) Quiet environment me raho, distracting background noise na ho. 3) Loudly aur clearly bolo. 4) Jis website/app ko test kar rahe ho uski sounds record mat karo; jaise video play hone lage to hum aapko sunna chahte hain, video ko nahi.
qs.b: Sound quality is critical. Before recording I check that my voice is recorded and can be clearly understood, I work in a quiet place without background noise, I speak loudly and clearly, and I avoid recording sounds from the site or app, so if a video plays the customer hears me, not the video.
qs.t: Mic check, shanti, zor se bolo, site ki awaaz nahi.

qs.q: Why does first impression matter in usability video recordings?
qs.s: Aapka first impression hi count karta hai. Kabhi surveys kehte hain ki kahin click karne se pehle kuch questions ke answers do. Agar task website open karne ko kehta hai to wo pehli baar hona chahiye jab aap website kholte ho aur recording start karte ho. Ye instructions important hain kyunki website ke kisi element se bahut jaldi predisposed hone se experience ke baare me aapke thoughts aur feelings badal sakte hain.
qs.b: Your first impression is what counts. When the task asks you to open the website, it should be the first time you open it, with recording started, and some surveys ask questions before you click anything. Seeing elements too early can alter your thoughts and feelings about the experience.
qs.t: Pehli nazar ka feedback - pehle se site mat dekho.

qs.q: What guidelines help avoid GDPR violations in usability video recordings?
qs.s: GDPR kya hai ye samajhne ke liye GDPR course padho. Video record karte waqt khaas dhyan: 1) 'Start survey' click karne ke baad tabs ke neeche survey direct link par click karo; isse survey alag new window me khulta hai bina platform visible hue. 2) Video me sirf testing website dikhe jaisa survey me instructed hai (kuch rare cases me, aur sirf jab survey me specifically likha ho, survey ke tasks bhi record kar sakte ho). 3) Khud ko survey questions answer ya fill karte hue record mat karo. 4) Recording me sirf apna first name bolo, last name mention mat karo.
qs.b: To avoid GDPR violations I open the survey via the survey direct link so the platform is not visible, I make sure the video shows only the testing website as instructed, recording survey tasks only if the survey explicitly says so, I do not record myself filling out survey questions, and I only say my first name aloud, never my last name.
qs.t: Direct link, sirf site, survey filling nahi, sirf first name.

qs.q: How can you improve as a usability tester?
qs.s: Har cheez ki tarah, usability testing skills improve karne ke liye experience aur practice chahiye: 1) Different websites visit karo aur observe karo ki wo dusron se kya alag karti hain. 2) Out loud bolo ki kya pasand hai, kya nahi, kya badloge, etc.
qs.b: Improvement comes from experience and practice: visit different websites and observe what they do differently, and practise speaking aloud what you like, what you do not like and what you would change.
qs.t: Websites dekho, bolkar practice karo.

qs.q: What do usability testing cycles provide to the customer, and what should you review first?
qs.s: Usability testing cycles customer ko valuable, actionable feedback dete hain ki unka mobile app ya website intuitive, consistent, accessible ya easy-to-use hai ya nahi. Note: Usability project me participate karte waqt project-specific guidance aur instructions ke liye overview review karna important hai.
qs.b: Usability cycles give the customer valuable, actionable feedback on whether their app or website is intuitive, consistent, accessible and easy to use. Before participating, I always review the overview for project-specific guidance and instructions.
qs.t: Intuitive, Consistent, Accessible, Easy - aur pehle overview.

qs.q: What is the Think Aloud Protocol?
qs.s: Usability sessions me feedback dene ki common technique. Moderated aur unmoderated dono testing par apply hoti hai. Isme task perform karte hue apne thoughts, actions aur feelings verbalize karte ho, jaise apne words me stream-of-consciousness narration. Multi-step process (jaise retail app/website ka purchase process) me 'state the obvious' important hai; moderated ya recorded unmoderated session me viewer dekh sakta hai ki aapne button click kiya lekin click ke peeche thoughts ya feelings nahi jaanta. Har task me bolte raho; normal hai ki tester shuru me bahut bole aur session ke saath narration slow ya band ho jaaye, isliye consistent flow rakho. Usability sessions aapko as a person test nahi karte, app ya website ko test karte hain, isliye negative feedback samet saara feedback collected data ka critical part hai.
qs.b: The Think Aloud Protocol is a common technique, used in both moderated and unmoderated testing, where you verbalize your thoughts, actions and feelings as a stream-of-consciousness narration while doing a task. You should state the obvious, because viewers can see a click but not why you clicked, and keep the narration consistent instead of slowing down as the session goes on. The session tests the product, not you, so negative feedback is a critical part of the data.
qs.t: Bolte raho, obvious bhi bolo, product test ho raha hai tum nahi.

qs.q: What are the first impression and value proposition validation exercises?
qs.s: App home screen ya website homepage par pehli baar aate hi test case first impressions describe karne ko keh sakta hai. Ye exercise aksar gateway pages par hoti hai jinpar bahut traffic aata hai (jaise homepage) ya jin pages par important message ya theme ho. Goal: koi aur task start karne se pehle page dekh kar initial impression dena. First impression ke baad value proposition validation exercise ho sakti hai jisme poocha jaata hai ki aapke hisaab se app ya website kis liye use hoti hai aur kya uska purpose clear hai.
qs.b: The first impression exercise asks you to look at a page, usually a high-traffic gateway page like the homepage or one with an important message, and give your initial impression before doing any other task. It may be followed by a value proposition validation exercise, where you describe what you think the app or website is for and whether its purpose is clear.
qs.t: Pehle dekho-batao, phir batao ye kis kaam ka hai.

qs.q: What should you look for in look and feel, and in layout and content, while moving through the UI?
qs.s: Look and feel: feedback aksar colors aur color schemes, font size aur font style par hota hai. Questions: Is the design too dark or too light? Are there too many colors or not enough colors? Is it readable? Layout and content: page/screen par content ka layout. Questions: Is the content easy to read and understand? Is the content informative? Are the images too big or small, placement aur size kaisa hai, kya images aapke goal me block banti hain? Is it clear when there is a link versus regular text?
qs.b: For look and feel I comment on colors, color schemes, font size and style: is the design too dark or light, are there too many or too few colors, is it readable. For layout and content I check whether content is easy to read, understand and informative, whether images are the right size and placement or get in the way, and whether links are clearly distinguishable from regular text.
qs.t: Look-feel = rang aur font; Layout = padhna, images, link vs text.

qs.q: What should you look for in content flow and information architecture?
qs.s: Content flow: app/website me andar jaate hue dekho ki screens ya pages ke beech connection sense banata hai ya nahi. Questions: Does the content on one page relate to the next page? Does the next click make sense? Does the terminology match, jaise ek page par 'contract' aur dusre par 'documents' same cheez refer kar rahe hain? Information architecture (IA): navigation mobile apps aur websites dono ka important aspect; visitors lost na hon, isliye dead ends ya confusing paths note karo. Questions: Does the way the site is organized make sense? Can you find the functionality you're looking for? Is it easy to return to the home screen or homepage?
qs.b: For content flow I check whether each page relates to the next, whether the next click makes sense, and whether terminology is consistent, for example contract on one page and documents on another for the same thing. For information architecture I note dead ends or confusing paths, and check whether the organization makes sense, whether I can find the functionality I need, and whether it is easy to return home.
qs.t: Flow = page se page ka rishta; IA = raasta, dead end, ghar wapsi.

qs.q: What should you check when you encounter an error message during a usability session?
qs.s: Error message aaye to message window aur uske contents ko dhyan se dekho. Questions: Do you understand the error message? Is it clear what went wrong and how to fix it? Kya app/website aapko poora required process karwa ke baad wo batati hai jo shuru me pata hona chahiye tha, jaise password rules?
qs.b: I look closely at the message and check whether I understand it, whether it is clear what went wrong and how to fix it, and whether the product made me go through a required step only to tell me something I needed at the start, such as password rules.
qs.t: Samjha? Fix pata? Password rules pehle bataye?

qs.q: What are the tips for UX session capture?
qs.s: 1) Web ya desktop Usability cycles ke video submissions typically webcam aur/ya capture program se record hote hain, jaisa Screen Recordings Academy course me discuss hua. 2) Mobile Usability cycles ke video kai methods se record hote hain, kuch platform-specific. Project details review karo ki session capture requirements hain ya nahi. Agar specific requirements nahi hain to options webcam se lekar iOS devices ke liye mirroring software jaise Reflector, ya Android ke liye bahut saare screencast tools tak hain. 3) Tool koi bhi ho, kisi dusre app ya website par recording test karo taaki settings sahi hon aur audio/video capture properly kaam kare. 4) Session capture karte waqt koi aur customer information display mat karo jaise Test Cycle Chat; ye platform ke Terms of Use ka violation maana jaata hai.
qs.b: Web and desktop sessions are usually captured with a webcam and/or capture program, while mobile sessions use various platform-specific methods, from a webcam to mirroring software like Reflector for iOS or screencast tools for Android, unless the project specifies requirements. Whatever the tool, I do a test recording on a different app or site to confirm audio and video work. I never show other customer information such as the Test Cycle Chat, which violates the platform's Terms of Use.
qs.t: Test recording dusri site pe; Reflector iOS; Test Cycle Chat kabhi screen pe nahi.

qs.q: How is a usability study different from a functional cycle?
qs.s: Usability cycles customer ko feedback dete hain ki unke app ka interface aur general flow kitna intuitive hai. Consistency aur general ease-of-use actionable feedback me hamesha key players hain. Usability cycles primarily survey-based hote hain, jabki Functional cycles bug-based hote hain.
qs.b: Usability cycles give feedback on how intuitive an app's interface and general flow are, with consistency and ease of use as key factors. They are primarily survey-based, whereas functional cycles are bug-based.
qs.t: Usability = survey; Functional = bug.

qs.q: How are participants selected for a usability study?
qs.s: Usability studies me participants invite karte waqt demographics, psychographics aur dusre factors heavily consider hote hain. Isse study specific group ke liye tailored hoti hai aur zyada accurate insights milti hain. Bias minimize hota hai aur results relevant aur larger audience par applicable hote hain. Apna tester profile accurate aur up to date rakho; agar cycle ki requirements meet karte ho to Usability cycle ka invite mil sakta hai.
