qs.b: Participants are invited based heavily on demographics, psychographics and other factors, so the study is tailored to a specific group, gives more accurate insights, minimizes bias and produces relevant results. To be invited, I keep my tester profile accurate and up to date so I can be matched when I meet a cycle's requirements.
qs.t: Profile updated = invite ka chance.

qs.q: How are testers compensated for a usability study?
qs.s: Usability studies test cases jaise hain: successful completion ke liye one flat rate. Survey payouts test cycle ke hisaab se vary karte hain.
qs.b: Usability studies pay one flat rate for successful completion, similar to test cases, and the survey payout varies by test cycle.
qs.t: Survey poora = flat rate; rate cycle pe depend.

qs.q: Why can a tester not participate in the same UX test cycle twice?
qs.s: Example: aap website owner ho aur jaanna chahte ho ki users blue ya red login button prefer karte hain. Ek user se poocha jo blue prefer karta hai. Usi user se 30 baar poochoge to likely same answer milega aur data suggest karega ki users blue button prefer karte hain. Ye good practice nahi; testers ka pool diversify karna behtar hai taaki opinions ki range mile.
qs.b: Participating twice would skew the data. If you asked the same user who prefers a blue login button 30 times, the data would wrongly suggest all users prefer blue. It is better to diversify the pool of testers to get a range of opinions.
qs.t: Ek banda 30 baar = 30 log nahi.

qs.q: Why is redoing a survey not allowed in usability tests?
qs.s: Redos aksar allowed nahi hote kyunki client aapka first impression chahta hai. Agar aap pehle website ya application dekh chuke ho to honest feedback collect karna impossible hai.
qs.b: Redos are usually not allowed because the client wants your first impression, and honest feedback cannot be collected once you have already been exposed to the website or application.
qs.t: Redo = first impression khatam.

topics.name: Voice Testing
topics.intro: Voice Testing course: utterances, wake words, in-home aur on-site moderated collections, ML feedback loop aur best practices.

qs.q: What is Voice Testing on the testing platform?
qs.s: Voice Testing ek real-world testing hai jiska goal end users ko flawless voice experience dena hai. Testers se utterances collect ki jaati hain taaki real logon par based ek voice algorithm banaya ja sake, jo voice assistant me use hoga. Utterances submit karne ke liye testers ko scripts milti hain jinme instructions hoti hain ki utterances kaise complete karni hain.
qs.b: Voice Testing is real-world testing aimed at delivering flawless voice experiences to end users. Testers record utterances, and those are used to build a voice algorithm based on real people for a voice assistant. Testers follow scripts that tell them exactly how to complete each utterance.
qs.t: Real log bolte hain, algorithm seekhta hai, script raasta dikhati hai.

qs.q: What market numbers does the Academy give to show why voice testing matters?
qs.s: Notes ke numbers: US Voice and Speech Recognition Technology market 2018 me $1.8 billion ka tha aur 2030 tak lagbhag $60 billion tak pahunchne ki ummeed hai. Global Natural Language Processing (NLP) market 2021 me $20.98 billion tha aur 2028 tak $127.26 billion forecast hai. Matlab business me huge competition, emerging technologies me improvements aur consumers ke liye zyada offerings.
qs.b: The US voice and speech recognition market was valued at 1.8 billion dollars in 2018 and is expected to reach about 60 billion dollars by 2030. The global NLP market reached 20.98 billion dollars in 2021 and is forecast to reach 127.26 billion dollars by 2028. That growth means strong competition and a big need for quality voice testing.

qs.q: Why is voice a challenging area to test?
qs.s: Voice ek natural interaction hai jo consumers ko 'zero click' experience deta hai. Devices me voice technologies ab common hain, lekin inke saamne bahut obstacles hain. Platform par bhi text based test cycles hi norm hain. Voice testing user input se shape hoti hai jo varying languages, user intent, dialects aur jargon ki wajah se complicated ho jaata hai.
qs.b: Voice gives users a natural, zero-click experience, but voice technology faces many obstacles. Most test cycles are text based, while voice input is complicated by different languages, user intent, dialects and jargon. That variety makes voice much harder to test than typed input.
qs.t: Zero click, par 4 mushkilein: Language, Intent, Dialect, Jargon.

qs.q: What value do the platform's voice collections provide to clients?
qs.s: Voice collections ek large volume ka diverse audio data deti hain jo voice applications ko train aur test karne me use hota hai. Is data se development aur testing phases me potential issues identify kiye ja sakte hain, aur voice application ki performance ko alag alag types ke audio inputs ke against benchmark kiya ja sakta hai.
qs.b: Voice collections give clients a large volume of diverse audio data to train and test voice applications. The data helps find potential issues during development and testing, and it lets clients benchmark their application's performance against many kinds of audio input.
qs.t: Collection ke 3 kaam: Train, Find issues, Benchmark.

qs.q: What is the purpose of Voice Testing within the platform?
qs.s: Purpose hai voice ke challenges ke solutions ko champion karna aur is badhte (surging) market ko improve karna. 'Lead digital quality' mission ke saath platform voice collection challenges accept karta hai, broad client bases ke saath partner karta hai aur data collection me successful methods laata hai. Vetted testers is tarah consumers tak pahunchne wali technologies me viability daalte hain.
qs.b: The purpose is to champion solutions to voice challenges and improve this fast-growing market. Under a mission to lead digital quality, the platform partners with many clients and brings proven methods to data collection. Vetted testers help make sure the technology that reaches consumers actually works.
qs.t: Mission: lead digital quality, vetted testers se.

qs.q: Where does voice testing fit in the SDLC?
qs.s: Beta testing SDLC ke final steps me se ek hai. Ise user testing ya customer validation bhi kehte hain. Beta testing ka aim hai ki client ka software market me aane se pehle end users satisfied hon. Platform ke on-site aur in-home testing offerings voice testing practitioners ko woh environments aur devices dete hain jo controlled aur specifically designed voice collections gather karne ke liye chahiye.
qs.b: Voice testing is closely tied to beta testing, which is one of the final steps of the SDLC and is also called user testing or customer validation. Its goal is to make sure end users are satisfied before the product hits the market. On-site and in-home testing provide the environments and devices needed for controlled, purpose-built voice collections.
qs.t: Beta = User testing = Customer validation, SDLC ka last stop.

qs.q: Walk through the history of voice recognition technology covered in the Academy.
qs.s: Timeline: 1950 - Bell Laboratories ne 'Audrey' banaya, toll operators ki productivity ke liye; room jitna bada system, 9 numerical digits (1-9) 90% accuracy se recognize karta tha. 1962 - IBM ne World's Fair me Shoebox introduce kiya; 16 spoken words recognize karta tha, phonemes ki sound aur pitch sun kar. Late 70s / Early 80s - DARPA (Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency) ne speech recognition research fund kiya; Carnegie Mellon ka Harpy program 1000 se zyada words interpret kar sakta tha. 1990 - pehla consumer based computer software Dragon Dictate, Windows aur Mac ke liye. 2011 - Apple ne Siri release kiya. 2012 - Google ne Google Now. 2013 - Microsoft ne Cortana. 2014 - Amazon ne Alexa, Amazon Echo par. 2017 - Samsung ne Bixby, Galaxy S8 par. 2022 - Meta ne CAIRaoke.
qs.b: Voice recognition started in 1950 with Bell Labs' Audrey, which recognized digits 1 to 9 with 90 percent accuracy, followed by IBM's Shoebox in 1962 with 16 words. DARPA-funded research led to Carnegie Mellon's Harpy, which handled over 1000 words, and Dragon Dictate became the first consumer software in 1990. Then came Siri in 2011, Google Now in 2012, Cortana in 2013, Alexa on Echo in 2014, Bixby on the Galaxy S8 in 2017 and Meta's CAIRaoke in 2022.
qs.t: Audrey 9 digit, Shoebox 16 word, Harpy 1000+; phir S-G-C-A-B-C (Siri, Google Now, Cortana, Alexa, Bixby, CAIRaoke) 2011 se 2022.

qs.q: Which industries, products and tester communities does the platform's voice testing cover?
qs.s: Industries (partnerships): retail, media/entertainment, financial services, travel/hospitality, healthcare aur automotive. Products ka scope: SmartHome devices, AR/VR, in-car infotainment systems aur wearables. Platform ek global community use karta hai jisme native languages, dialogs, dialects, genders aur age groups ka mix hai. Market badhega to voice testing portfolio bhi badhega.
qs.b: Voice testing partnerships cover retail, media and entertainment, financial services, travel and hospitality, healthcare and automotive. Products in scope include smart home devices, AR/VR, in-car infotainment systems and wearables. The platform draws on a global community with diverse native languages, dialects, genders and age groups.
qs.t: 6 industries, 4 product types (Home, AR/VR, Car, Wearable).

qs.q: List the voice testing lexicon terms taught in the Academy.
qs.s: Lesson 2 me 14 industry standard terms hain: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Beta Testing, Dictation, Dogfooding, Latency, Machine Learning (ML), Moderator, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Smart Assistant, Intent, Utterance, Voice Assistant, Wake word.
qs.b: The lexicon covers 14 terms: AI, ASR, beta testing, dictation, dogfooding, latency, machine learning, moderator, NLP, smart assistant, intent, utterance, voice assistant and wake word. These are the industry-standard words used in voice testing projects.
qs.t: 14 shabd: AI-ASR-Beta-Dictation-Dogfood-Latency-ML-Moderator-NLP-Smart-Intent-Utterance-Voice-Wake.

qs.q: How does the Academy define Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning?
qs.s: AI: aise systems jinme insaan jaise intellectual processes hon, jaise reason karna, meaning discover karna, generalize karna ya past experience se seekhna. AI ek digital computer ya computer-controlled robot ki ability hai woh tasks karne ki jo intelligent beings se associate hote hain. ML: AI aur computer science ki ek branch jo data aur algorithms use karke insaan ke seekhne ke tareeke ko imitate karti hai, aur dheere dheere accuracy improve karti hai.
qs.b: AI refers to systems with human-like intellectual processes such as reasoning, finding meaning, generalizing and learning from experience, letting a computer or robot do tasks associated with intelligent beings. Machine learning is a branch of AI and computer science that uses data and algorithms to imitate how humans learn, gradually improving its accuracy.
qs.t: AI = sochna; ML = data se dheere dheere seekhna.

qs.q: What is Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)?
qs.s: ASR woh technology hai jo information systems ke users ko input type karne ki jagah bol kar dene deti hai. Ise computer speech recognition ya speech-to-text bhi kehte hain.
qs.b: Automatic Speech Recognition is technology that lets users speak their input instead of typing it. It is also known as computer speech recognition or speech-to-text.
qs.t: ASR = bolo, type mat karo (speech-to-text).

qs.q: What are beta testing and dogfooding?
qs.s: Beta Testing: public release se pehle real products par real environments me testing; aim hai usability ya functional problems ek controlled reporting environment me dhoondhna. Dogfooding: software development me apna banaya software khud use karna. 'Eating your own dog food' matlab apne software ko beta form me khud test karna taaki development me madad mile.
qs.b: Beta testing is testing real products in real environments before public release to find usability or functional problems in a controlled reporting setup. Dogfooding, or eating your own dog food, means a team uses and tests its own software in beta form to help development.
qs.t: Beta = bahar walon se pehle real test; Dogfood = apna khana khud khao.

qs.q: How does the Academy define dictation?
qs.s: Speech dictation matlab words is intent se bolna ki woh likhe jayenge. Development me dictation ko notes 'text-to-speech' kehte hain, jisme bole gaye words machine learning se transcribe kiye jaate hain. Utterance stage example: 'Send a direct message to a friend requesting to reschedule your plans together.'
qs.b: Dictation means speaking words with the intent that they will be written down. In development, the notes describe it as spoken words being transcribed by machine learning. A sample dictation prompt is sending a direct message to a friend asking to reschedule plans.
qs.t: Dictation = bolo aur likha jaaye.

qs.q: What is latency in voice testing?
qs.s: Latency delay ka measure hai, yaani data ko network ke across destination tak pahunchne me kitna time lagta hai. Usually milliseconds me measure hoti hai. Latency testing example: Wake word use karke device se weather poochho, aur jab device jawab de raha ho tab Wake word se follow up command do ki ek application khole.
qs.b: Latency is the delay, usually measured in milliseconds, for data to reach its destination across a network. In voice testing, a latency test might ask the device about the weather and then interrupt with a follow-up wake-word command to open an app while it is still responding.
qs.t: Latency = milliseconds ka intezaar.

qs.q: What is a moderator in software testing?
qs.s: Moderator ek live instructor hota hai. Moderators ka kaam hai individuals ko product criteria ke hisaab se use karwana, questions ke answers dena, issues resolve karna aur feedback gather karna.
qs.b: In software testing, a moderator is a live instructor who guides participants to use the product according to the test criteria. Moderators answer questions, resolve issues and gather feedback.
qs.t: Moderator = live guide: guide, answer, resolve, gather.

qs.q: What is Natural Language Processing (NLP)?
qs.s: NLP AI ki ek branch hai jiska maksad computers ko spoken word ki utni hi samajh dena hai jitni insaan ko hoti hai. NLP computational linguistics ko statistical, machine learning aur deep learning models ke saath combine karta hai. In technologies se computers human language ko text ya voice data ke form me process karke uska poora meaning 'samajh' paate hain, including speaker ya writer ka intent aur sentiment.
qs.b: NLP is a branch of AI that aims to give computers a human-like understanding of language. It combines computational linguistics with statistical, machine learning and deep learning models so computers can process text or voice and understand its full meaning, including intent and sentiment.
qs.t: NLP = Linguistics + Stats + ML + Deep Learning = meaning, intent, sentiment.

qs.q: What is the difference between a smart assistant and a voice assistant?
qs.s: Smart Assistant: software jo usually smart device par installed hota hai aur trigger hone par services deta hai (aksar built-in active listening jo Wake word se trigger hoti hai), tasks activate aur perform karta hai. Voice Assistant: ek digital assistant jo voice recognition, speech synthesis aur NLP use karke kisi particular application ke through service deta hai.
qs.b: A smart assistant is software on a smart device that provides services when triggered, often by active listening for a wake word. A voice assistant is a digital assistant that uses voice recognition, speech synthesis and NLP to deliver a service through a particular application.
qs.t: Smart = device par jaagta hai; Voice = recognition + synthesis + NLP.

qs.q: What are intent, utterance and wake word?
qs.s: Intent: ek task ya action jo user voice application se fulfil karwana chahta hai. Utterance (lexicon): speech ki ek chhoti unit, jiski length aage aur peeche clean breaks se measure hoti hai. Lesson 4 ke hisaab se utterance ek spoken phrase ya statement hai, ek word se zyada, lekin complete sentence hona zaroori nahi, e.g. 'My name is Roger.' Wake word: woh phrase jo voice assistant ko trigger karta hai; detect hone par system request ko capture, decode aur service karta hai. Example: 'Hey Google'.
qs.b: An intent is the task or action a user wants a voice application to fulfill. An utterance is a small unit of speech bounded by clean breaks, more than one word but not necessarily a full sentence. A wake word, such as Hey Google, triggers the assistant, which then captures, decodes and services the request.
qs.t: Wake word jagata hai, utterance bolta hai, intent kaam batata hai.

qs.q: What do testers do in general voice testing projects?
qs.s: Voice Testing me testers AI/ML devices ko curated phrases provide karte hain taaki product improve ho. Scripts testers ko digital ya printed form me milti hain, jinme direct instructions aur guidance hoti hai ki utterances kaise complete karni hain.
qs.b: In voice testing projects, testers provide curated phrases to AI and ML devices to improve the product. They receive digital or printed scripts with direct instructions on how to complete each utterance.
qs.t: Curated phrase + script = voice project.

qs.q: What are the four types of utterances?
qs.s: Chaar types: 1) Free-form - 'Today I am feeling great because the sun is shining and everyone is being friendly.' 2) Prompted - prompt: friend ko event suggest karne ka message bhejo - 'Hey Charles, have you ever been to the downtown farmers market? It is worth checking out.' 3) Structured - prompt: camera application band karo - 'Close camera.' 4) Nonsensical - 'Yada, yada, rammalamma shoosh.'
qs.b: There are four utterance types: free-form, where the tester speaks freely; prompted, where the tester responds to a scenario such as messaging a friend about an event; structured, a specific command like Close camera; and nonsensical, meaningless speech like Yada, yada, rammalamma shoosh.
qs.t: FPSN: Free, Prompted, Structured, Nonsense.

qs.q: What background sound options exist for utterances?
qs.s: Do options: 1) Clean - koi background noise nahi. 2) With background noise - controlled environment ke andar real world environments simulate karna (intellectual property, environmental factors, specific goal statistics ki wajah se); aise situations jahan users background noise ke saath virtual assistant se baat karte hain; noise itni loud ho ki sound recording me perceive ho, lekin utterance recording disrupt na kare; typical decibel range 50-60; example: Coffee Shop - People Talking.
qs.b: Utterances are recorded either clean, with no background noise, or with background noise. Noise recordings simulate real-world settings inside a controlled environment, loud enough to be heard but not to disrupt the utterance, typically 50 to 60 decibels, for example people talking in a coffee shop.
qs.t: Clean ya Coffee shop, 50-60 dB.

qs.q: What are the three speech volumes used in voice collections?
qs.s: Teen volumes: Low - perceptible hona chahiye, whisper nahi, jaise library me dheere bol rahe ho. Normal - normal speaking voice. Loud - boisterous, projecting voice, jaise audience se baat kar rahe ho.
qs.b: There are three speech volumes: low, which is quiet like speaking in a library but never a whisper; normal, your regular speaking voice; and loud, a projecting voice as if addressing an audience.
qs.t: Library, Normal, Audience.

qs.q: What utterance stages are given as examples in voice scripts?
qs.s: Utterance stages: Dogfooding - 'Using the Wake word, instruct the device to close all applications.' Dictation - 'Send a direct message to a friend requesting to reschedule your plans together.' Functional Testing - 'Instruct the device to open the camera application and capture a picture.' Latency Testing - 'Using the Wake word, ask the device about the weather, as the device is responding, trigger a follow up command using the Wake word by asking the device to open an application.' During exercise - testers se aise utterances maange ja sakte hain jo transcribe honge jab user fitness device par installed smart assistant se baat kare; labored breathing aur badhi heart rate bolne ke tareeke ko affect karti hai, isliye yeh criterion un unique utterance types ko capture aur improve karne ke liye hai.
qs.b: Script stages include dogfooding, such as telling the device to close all apps; dictation, such as messaging a friend to reschedule; functional testing, such as opening the camera and taking a picture; and latency testing, where a follow-up wake-word command interrupts the device mid-response. There is also during-exercise collection on fitness devices, since heavy breathing and a raised heart rate change how people speak.
qs.t: D-D-F-L-E: Dogfood, Dictation, Functional, Latency, Exercise.

qs.q: Why are high quality utterances critical?
qs.s: Voice testers ke liye high quality utterances dena critical hai kyunki yeh utterances seedha AI engine ko steer karti hain. Testers ko saare test criteria consider karke intent match karne wali utterances deni chahiye. Use se pehle utterances QA hoti hain, jahan quality aur viability check hoti hai. Isliye sirf high quality utterances deliver karo taaki saare resources maximize hon.
qs.b: High quality utterances matter because they directly steer the AI engine. Every utterance is QA'd for quality and viability before use, so testers should consider all criteria, match the intent and deliver only high-quality recordings to avoid wasting resources.
qs.t: Utterance = AI ka steering wheel; QA pehle hi check karega.

qs.q: What guidelines help a tester deliver high quality voice responses?
qs.s: Guidelines: Speak clearly and confidently. Enunciate words and phrases, har word/phrase ki sound delivery ensure karo. Read each prompt carefully. Prepare prior to recording. Utterances ke beech clear pauses rakho. Recordings start/stop accurately aur efficiently karo. Delivery har section/environment/script ke saath align ho; criteria (section/environment/script) changeovers note aur prepare karo. Difficult scenarios me pehle kuch examples practice karo. Progress track karne aur on task rehne ke liye jo bhi chahiye use karo. Structured utterance prompts me words ke semantics ya intended meaning me mat kho jao; aksar response natural sound kare to personal perspective se aana zaroori nahi. Interruption se bachne ke liye controlled environment dhoondho ya banao.
qs.b: Speak clearly and confidently, enunciate every word, read each prompt carefully and prepare before recording. Leave clear pauses, start and stop recordings accurately, keep delivery aligned with each section, environment and script, and practice difficult scenarios first. Track your progress, do not overthink the semantics of structured prompts as long as the response sounds natural, and record in a controlled environment without interruptions.
qs.t: Clear bolo, prompt padho, pause do, script follow karo, shant jagah chuno.

qs.q: What recording rhythm does the Academy recommend between utterances?
qs.s: Clear pauses ki good practice, jab tak precise rhythm establish na ho: Start Recording > Pause for 3 seconds > Deliver first Utterance > Pause for 3 seconds > Finish recording.
qs.b: Until you have a steady rhythm, start the recording, pause for 3 seconds, deliver the utterance, pause another 3 seconds and then finish the recording. The clear pauses give clean breaks around each utterance.
qs.t: Start, 3 sec, bolo, 3 sec, stop.

qs.q: How should testers use creativity in utterances?
qs.s: Do tareeke: Variance - responses mix up karo, wide range of vocabulary daalo; socho ki AI machine ko great data feed kar rahe ho. Natural Utterances - wahi words aur phrases use karo jo aap rozana virtual assistant ko instruct karte waqt bolte ho.
qs.b: Use variance by mixing up responses and using a wide range of vocabulary so the AI gets rich data. Keep utterances natural, using the words and phrases you would really use with a virtual assistant every day.
qs.t: Variety + Natural = great AI data.

qs.q: What must testers always avoid while recording utterances?
qs.s: Hamesha avoid: Mumbling; utterances dete waqt eating, drinking ya chewing gum; hate speech/profanity/personally identifiable information use karna; examples me di gayi phraseology use karna.
qs.b: Testers must always avoid mumbling, eating, drinking or chewing gum while recording, using hate speech, profanity or personally identifiable information, and copying the phrasing from the examples.
qs.t: No Mumble, No Munch, No PII/Profanity, No Copy.

qs.q: Which sounds should be avoided unless they are part of the test criteria?
qs.s: Jab tak test criteria me specify na ho, yeh avoid karo: Hesitating, Smacking lips, Throat clearing noises, Laughing, Heavy breathing, Whispering, Cross-talk, Long pauses. Total 8.
qs.b: Unless the criteria ask for them, avoid hesitating, lip smacking, throat clearing, laughing, heavy breathing, whispering, cross-talk and long pauses. Some of these, like heavy breathing, can be valid when the criteria call for them, for example during-exercise collections.
qs.t: 8 noise: Hesitate, Smack, Throat, Laugh, Breath, Whisper, Cross-talk, Long pause.

qs.q: What is In-Home Voice Testing and what is its cycle process?
qs.s: In-Home Voice Testing ek powerful global community of freelance testers use karta hai; yeh tight knit community hai jisme shared resources hain, aur testers trained aur queued hote hain paid test cycles deliver karne ke liye. Process: Selection > Commitment > Shipping/Receiving > Testing (Tester) > Testing (Referrals) > Test Case Submittal > Device Return.
qs.b: In-home voice testing uses a global community of trained freelance testers on paid cycles. The cycle runs selection, commitment, shipping and receiving, testing by the tester, testing by referrals, test case submittal and finally device return.
qs.t: Select, Commit, Ship, Test, Refer, Submit, Return.

qs.q: Which documents are important for voice testing?
qs.s: Paanch documents: NDA, Covid Consent, Referral Submission Form, Mileage Reimbursement Form, Device FAQ Document.
qs.b: The key documents are the NDA, the Covid consent form, the referral submission form, the mileage reimbursement form and the device FAQ document.
qs.t: N-C-R-M-D: NDA, Covid, Referral, Mileage, Device FAQ.

qs.q: What might a tester have to do when receiving a device?
qs.s: Device receive karte waqt: recipient ke roop me aapke signatures required honge; local receiving instructions ke liye test cycle criteria check karo; multiple failed delivery attempts ke baad carrier device ko local hub par hold kar sakta hai.
qs.b: When receiving a device, the tester will need to sign for it and should check the test cycle criteria for local receiving instructions. After multiple failed delivery attempts, the carrier may hold the device at a local hub.
qs.t: Sign karo, criteria padho, warna hub par atkega.

qs.q: What device instructions are typically provided to in-home participants?
qs.s: Das instructions: Identifying the device model; Putting on/taking off/adjusting wearables; Basic device function instructions; Device care instructions; Device use safety instructions; New user device-walkthrough guide; Power instructions; Network connection instructions; Login instructions; Basic troubleshooting instructions.
qs.b: Participants usually get instructions on identifying the device model, wearing and adjusting wearables, basic functions, device care, safe use, a new-user walkthrough, power, network connection, login and basic troubleshooting. These help them prepare and run the project safely.
qs.t: Model se troubleshooting tak 10 instructions.

qs.q: What device skills should an in-home voice tester have?
qs.s: Device skills: device par pichhli utterances ka transcription dhoondhna; Debug Menus; device factory reset karna (device return karne se pehle yeh to-do hai); Device Care Basics.
qs.b: A tester should know how to find the device's transcription of previous utterances, use debug menus, factory reset the device before returning it and follow device care basics.
qs.t: Transcript, Debug, Reset (return se pehle), Care.

qs.q: What are the rules for returning a device?
qs.s: Device return karte waqt prepaid return label hona chahiye. FedEx and Affiliated Sites - Ok. Drop boxes, pick-ups - Not Ok. Proof of return ke liye receipt lena aur rakhna zaroori hai. Return se pehle factory reset bhi to-do hai.
qs.b: Return the device with the prepaid return label through FedEx or its affiliated sites, never through drop boxes or pick-ups. Always get and keep the receipt as proof of return, and factory reset the device beforehand.
qs.t: FedEx counter haan, drop box naa, receipt sambhaal.

qs.q: How does the referral opportunity work in in-home voice testing?
qs.s: Agar applicable ho to tester kisi ko required testing complete karne ke liye refer kar sakta hai. Referral woh insaan hai jise aap directly supervise karte ho jab woh additional test case(s) complete kare jo aapke platform account se submit hote hain; unhe apna platform account nahi chahiye. Saare referrals apni script aapke device par aapke ghar me complete karte hain (notes me 'using their own account' bhi likha hai). Sirf unhe refer kar sakte ho jo aapki guidance me aapke ghar me test complete kar sakein. 18 ya usse zyada umar ka koi bhi participate kar sakta hai, agar referral form par submit hua ho aur NDA aur Consent forms bhare hon. Refer karne ke liye platform par 'Referral' test case claim karo, jisme NDA aur Consent forms ka link aur test case script hoti hai.
qs.b: Where allowed, a tester can refer someone they directly supervise in their own home, on their own device, and the referral's test cases are submitted from the tester's account, so the referral does not need a separate account. Referrals must be 18 or older, listed on the referral form and have signed the NDA and consent forms. To add one, the tester claims a Referral test case, which contains the form links and the script.
qs.t: Referral: 18+, ghar me, aapke device par, aapki supervision, Referral test case claim.

qs.q: What soft skills does a voice tester need?
qs.s: Paanch soft skills: Naturally inquisitive, Attention to detail, Responsiveness, Problem-solving, Responsible.
qs.b: A good voice tester is naturally inquisitive, pays attention to detail, is responsive, solves problems and is responsible.
qs.t: I-A-R-P-R: Inquisitive, Attention, Responsive, Problem-solving, Responsible.

qs.q: What statistics are given for the in-home voice collection team?
qs.s: In-home team stats: June 2021 se March 2022 ke beech 1866 voice devices ship hue; 7,940 unique test participants; 6.7 million utterances.
qs.b: The in-home team shipped 1866 voice devices between June 2021 and March 2022, worked with 7,940 unique participants and collected 6.7 million utterances.
qs.t: 1866 devices, 7940 log, 6.7 million utterances.

qs.q: What are the features of the platform's on-site moderated testing sites?
qs.s: On-site testing sites: centrally located (commute easy); accessible aur diverse testing pool outreach ke liye ideal; adaptable office spaces; tried testing methodologies; agile ability - condensed timeline me pop up, set up aur projects start; secure device storage; local troubleshooting.
qs.b: On-site testing facilities are central and accessible, which helps reach a diverse testing pool. They have adaptable office space, proven methods, the ability to pop up and start projects on short timelines, secure device storage and local troubleshooting.
qs.t: Central, Accessible, Adaptable, Tried, Agile, Secure, Troubleshoot.

qs.q: What is the on-site troubleshooting escalation path and what guides exist?
qs.s: Escalation: Moderator > Tech Moderator > On-Site Lead > Client POC. Troubleshooting guides ke examples: Wifi connected ensure karna: Settings > Connectivity > Wi-Fi > Wi-Fi toggled on ho aur Network SSID present ho. Location settings enable karna: Settings > Privacy > Permissions Manager > Location > 'use location' ON aur 'use find my device' ON.
qs.b: On site, issues escalate from Moderator to Tech Moderator to On-Site Lead and finally to the Client POC. Sites also keep troubleshooting guides, for example checking that Wi-Fi is on and the network SSID is present, or turning on use location and find my device under Privacy permissions.
qs.t: M > TM > Lead > Client.

qs.q: What project-specific staffing roles exist for on-site voice testing?
qs.s: Paanch roles: Director of Operations Voice; TPM/Onsite Lead; Moderator; Loss Prevention Moderator; Technical Moderator.
qs.b: On-site projects are staffed with a Director of Operations for voice, a TPM or On-site Lead, moderators, loss prevention moderators and technical moderators.
qs.t: Director, TPM/Lead, Moderator, Loss Prevention, Tech.

qs.q: Describe the streamlined process of an on-site test session.
qs.s: Process: 1) Intake - projected participants check in: Match ID, Project Confirmation, Security Badge, Vaccination Card (if required). 2) Har participant forms complete aur submit karta hai: Covid Consent, Non-Disclosure Agreements, Demographics Form. 3) Moderators test instructions aur coaching dete hain (subject matter expert se direct guidance). 4) Testers quality assured collections complete karte hain. 5) Follow up surveys se valuable feedback. 6) Device data extract karke client ko export. 7) Device accountability secured. 8) Test session feedback ka review, issues discuss. 9) Moderators, rooms aur devices next test session ke liye prepare.
qs.b: Participants check in with ID match, project confirmation, a security badge and a vaccination card if required, then complete the Covid consent, NDA and demographics forms. Moderators coach them through quality-assured collections, followed by surveys, data export to the client, device accountability checks, a feedback review and preparation for the next session.
qs.t: Check-in, Forms, Coaching, Collect, Survey, Export, Secure, Review, Reset.

qs.q: What is a moderator's role and training in on-site voice testing?
qs.s: Moderators ko testers ko accommodate karne, test kiye ja rahe device ke baare me knowledgeable banne aur risky situations rokne ki training milti hai. Purpose: participant ko device introduce karna, test kaise karna hai instruct karna, issues ke liye monitor karna, test complete hone par tester ko dismiss karna, phir device ko safe keeping aur data transfer ke liye device bank me return karna. Responsible: onsite testers ki security aur well being, onsite devices, aur operation me apna role smoothly chalana. Training kai dino me: structured training agenda, 1:1 instruction, group instruction, experienced moderators ko shadow karna.
qs.b: A moderator introduces the participant to the device, explains the test, monitors for issues, dismisses the tester at the end and returns the device to the device bank for safekeeping and data transfer. They are responsible for tester and device security and wellbeing. Moderators train over several days through a structured agenda, one-on-one and group instruction, and shadowing experienced moderators.
qs.t: Introduce, Instruct, Monitor, Dismiss, Device bank.

qs.q: What testing environments are used in on-site moderated voice testing?
qs.s: On-site testing real world aur exploratory hai. Indoor: individually controlled testing rooms jo audio interference kam karte hain; room ke andar criteria aur environments 'simulate' kar sakte hain. Outdoor: valuable outdoor 'ambient' noise capture karne ke liye; testers itni doori par hote hain ki audio interference ya overlap kam ho; controlled, structured aur secured.
qs.b: On-site testing is real-world and exploratory and uses two environments. Indoor rooms are individually controlled to cut audio interference and can simulate conditions, while outdoor sessions capture ambient noise with testers spaced apart in a controlled, structured and secure setup.
qs.t: Indoor = simulate; Outdoor = ambient, doori rakho.

qs.q: What statistics are given for on-site moderated voice collections?
qs.s: Ek single client account ke stats: 10.8 million utterances delivered; 54 moderated voice projects globally; 35,800 unique test participants.
qs.b: For a single client account, on-site work delivered 10.8 million utterances across 54 moderated voice projects worldwide with 35,800 unique participants.
qs.t: 10.8M, 54 projects, 35.8K log.

qs.q: Describe the historical voice collection client examples.
qs.s: Client 1: Testing Type - Voice/Functional/Smart Speakers; Intent - client team (limited scope, education, resources) ke saath frictionless voice experience jo lives save kar sake; Delivery - community ne Alexa enabled devices par test kiya, First Aid aur Blood Drive Scheduling skills improve kiye, structured test cycles me utterance responses validate kiye aur dono Amazon skills launch hue. Client 2: Testing Type - Voice/Utterance Collection/Client Devices; Intent - targeted utterances/demographics ka collection structured criteria ke saath scale karna, conversation enhancing headphones ke algorithms ke liye; Delivery - multiple locations me real world testing, qualified audio files gather, algorithm performance improve. Client 3: Testing Type - Voice/UX/Smart Speakers; Intent - younger demographic ke liye cool aur innovative in-car experience; Delivery - Alexa aur Google Assistant enabled devices par 19 countries me local dialects ke saath test, dialog verification construct aur perform kiya, issues aur failures uncover kiye.
qs.b: One client used structured cycles on Alexa devices to validate First Aid and Blood Drive Scheduling skills, helping launch both. Another scaled targeted utterance collection across multiple locations to train algorithms for conversation-enhancing headphones. A third tested an in-car experience for younger users on Alexa and Google Assistant devices in 19 countries, using dialog verification to uncover failures.
qs.t: Client 1 First Aid, Client 2 Headphones, Client 3 Car 19 countries.

qs.q: Who is the Machine Learning and Implementing Voice Collections lesson meant for?
qs.s: Note: yeh course un testers ke liye hai jinhone pichhle saare courses complete kar liye hain aur voice testing ke baare me aur seekhna chahte hain, future projects kaise construct hote hain, aur bada AI/ML picture samajhna chahte hain.
qs.b: This lesson is for testers who have finished all the earlier courses and want to go deeper into voice testing, understand how future projects are built and see the bigger AI and ML picture.
qs.t: Advanced level: pehle sab courses, phir bada picture.

qs.q: What are the three phases of a machine learning project?
qs.s: Teen phases: Collection - subject ke baare me jitni ho sake information gather karo; poochho: kya data collect karna hai? kitna data collect karna hai? data store aur access karne ka sabse efficient tareeka kya hai? Training - ML data me patterns dhoondhna hai, supervised ya unsupervised learning; mathematical ya business knowledge laga kar algorithm ko given input par predictions ke liye train karo; voice perspective se: kya AI engine user ko samajhta hai? Deploy - ML model ko production environment me daalna taaki data-driven decisions zyada automated tareeke se hon.
qs.b: An ML project has three phases. Collection gathers data and decides what to collect, how much and how to store it; training finds patterns through supervised or unsupervised learning so the model can make predictions, which for voice means checking whether the AI understands the user; and deployment puts the model into production for automated, data-driven decisions.
qs.t: Collect, Train, Deploy.

qs.q: What iterative principles are used to implement voice collection, and what happens in Plan?
qs.s: Voice testing iterative principles: Plan > Design > Model > Test Feedback. Plan me poochho aur action lo: Voice objective kya hai? - intended voice strategy design, detail aur forecast karo, business needs aur goals ke hisaab se prioritize karo. Deliverable kitna useful hai? - voice hi solution kyun hai? kya koi alternative method zyada feasible hai? Success kaise measure hogi? Planning stage me engineers, AI researchers, developers aur testers ko include karo.
qs.b: Voice collection follows an iterative cycle of plan, design, model and test feedback. In planning, define the voice objective and prioritize by business goals, question whether voice is truly the right solution, decide how success will be measured and include engineers, AI researchers, developers and testers from the start.
qs.t: Plan: Objective, Usefulness, Measure, Sabko shamil karo.

qs.q: What happens in the Design stage of voice collection?
qs.s: Design: dhyan rakho ki UX ke liye voice design unique hai; AI ka type decide karo (e.g. health inquiries ke liye responsive, sales situations ke liye); user context aur bot ki capabilities samajh kar sample dialogues aur scenarios banao; happy path layout karo; assistant ko organization aur intent ke hisaab se brand karo; goal ke liye testing type decide karo: Utterance Collections, Payment Testing, Usability testing and Feedback, Functional Testing, Dialog Verification; user feedback gather karo.
qs.b: Design recognizes that voice UX is unique. Teams choose the type of AI, build sample dialogues from user context and bot capabilities, lay out the happy path, brand the assistant and pick the testing needed, such as utterance collections, payment, usability, functional testing or dialog verification, then gather user feedback.
qs.t: Design ke 5 test: Utterance, Payment, Usability, Functional, Dialog.

qs.q: What principles guide the Model stage?
qs.s: Data models utne hi achhe hain jitna data unme jaata hai. Real-world testing leverage karo (lab ke bahar test, AI human input/data se banta hai, real aur direct interactions ka raw data). Real-world testing ke gains cement karne aur changes par regression rokne ke liye automated testing use karo. Mobile aur web se aage socho - AI jo bhi affect karta hai samjho (platforms, channels, applications, finance systems). Biases actively identify aur rectify karo - diverse data pools (gender, dialect, age, education), globally socho, biases avoid karo. Agile, iterative model use karo taaki system continuously improve aur extend ho; feedback loop build karo - direct client feedback request karo aur adjust karo.
qs.b: A model is only as good as its data, so use real-world testing outside the lab and lock in gains with automated regression testing. Think beyond mobile and web to everything the AI touches, actively remove bias with diverse data pools across gender, dialect, age and education, and run an agile, iterative feedback loop with the client.
qs.t: Garbage in, garbage out: real data, automation, beyond web, no bias, feedback loop.

qs.q: What are the stages of the voice testing feedback loop?
qs.s: Saat stages: 1) Data Collection - collection design, implement aur utterances gather. 2) Define Quality Metrics - Linguistic Engineers (LE) guidelines aur quality criteria set karte hain. 3) Audio Sampling - kaun se files query/examine karni hain uska method aur type decide. 4) Data Quality Analyst (DQA) Review - LEs aur DQAs predetermined schedule par datasets analyze karte hain. 5) Quality Analysis - data mila? demographics match? recordings playable? intelligible? domain match? script content match? etc. 6) Data Quality Report - generated report review aur action items discussion ke liye present hoti hai. 7) Vendor Quality Remediation - corrections ki koshish aur client ko completed remediations review ke liye iteratively invite karna.
qs.b: The feedback loop runs from data collection to quality metrics defined by Linguistic Engineers, then audio sampling and a scheduled review by LEs and Data Quality Analysts. Quality analysis checks whether data arrived, matches demographics, domain and script, and is playable and intelligible. A data quality report drives action items, and vendor quality remediation fixes issues and brings the client back to review them.
qs.t: Collect, Metrics (LE), Sample, DQA, Analyze, Report, Remediate.

qs.q: What actions and checks belong to the Test stage?
qs.s: AI systems ko real time feed of information chahiye, monitor aur update ke liye iterative. Actions: delivered utterances ko new intents se map karo; jo areas attention maangte hain unhe mitigate, retest, update karo; testing ko target goals se match karo. Har testing type ka check: Utterance Collections - kya AI engine user ki speech samajhne ke liye adequately trained hai? Payment Testing - kya users voice se transaction complete kar sakte hain? process seamless hai? Usability Testing and Feedback - kya users experience enjoy kar rahe hain? intuitive hai? Functional Testing - kya experience expected tarah kaam karta hai? Dialog Verification - kya saare users samjhe jaate hain aur proper response milta hai?
qs.b: AI systems need a real-time, iterative feed of information, so testing maps delivered utterances to new intents, fixes and retests weak areas and aligns with target goals. Each test type has a key question: is the engine trained to understand speech, can users pay by voice seamlessly, is the experience enjoyable and intuitive, does it work as expected, and are all users understood and answered properly.
qs.t: Har test ka ek sawaal: Samjha? Pay hua? Maza aaya? Chala? Jawab mila?

qs.q: What best practices help a tester complete voice testing successfully?
qs.s: Best practices: testing shuru karne se pehle goal establish karo (criteria/environments match, highest quality utterances, delivered utterances QA expectation se match). Big picture socho - jis virtual assistant me contribute kar rahe ho uska intent conceptualize karo. Jab tak test criteria samajh na aaye questions poochho - moderator ho to uski help lo, Community aur Test Engineers se doubts clear karo. Test ki length aur timeline consider karo. Test, product aur voice commands ki responsibility lo. Delivery enhance karne aur realistic feedback dene ke liye creativity use karo. Khud ko current aur future projects ke liye asset banao.
qs.b: Set a goal before starting: match the criteria and environment, deliver top-quality utterances and meet QA expectations. Think about the assistant's intent, ask questions through moderators, the community or Test Engineers until the criteria are clear, plan for the test length and timeline, take ownership, use creativity and aim to be an asset for future projects.
qs.t: Goal, Big picture, Poochho, Time, Ownership, Creativity, Asset.

qs.q: What are the goal, the do's and the don'ts of a voice test?
qs.s: Set the goal: Test Completion - saare boxes check karo, test script completion. Do: rules poore padho; description poori padho; jo bhi supplementary material diya ho padho; instructions follow karo; zaroorat ho to assistance maango; timeline requirements meet karne ke liye pace set karo. Don't: parts skip karna; responses overthink karna; off script jaana (criteria ke bahar responses banana).
qs.b: The goal is full test completion, ticking every box and finishing the script. Read all the rules, the description and any supplementary material, follow instructions, ask for help when needed and keep a pace that meets the timeline. Do not skip parts, overthink responses or go off script.
qs.t: Sab padho, script pe raho, skip mat karo.

topics.name: API Testing (Course)
topics.intro: API kya hai, HTTP basics, Postman me CRUD aur auth, API me kya test karna hai, aur SOAP/WADL/JSON jaise API types ka course.

qs.q: What is an API, and how does the course explain it?
qs.s: API ka full form hai Application Programming Interface. Ye ek computing interface hai jo do applications ke beech communication allow karta hai. Academy ke hisaab se API testing platform ki sabse challenging testing categories me se ek hai, isliye pehle API ko samajhna zaroori hai, phir uski testing.
qs.b: API stands for Application Programming Interface. It is a computing interface that allows two applications to communicate with each other.
qs.t: API = do apps ke beech ka 'translator-cum-messenger'.

qs.q: How does an API work between a device and a server? Explain with an example.
qs.s: API device aur server ke beech intermediary ka kaam karta hai. Flow: user ka device kuch data request karta hai, wo request API ke through server tak jaati hai. Server data retrieve karta hai, use interpret karta hai, zaroori actions perform karta hai, aur result wapas API ke through device ko bhejta hai. Restaurant example: waiter customer ka order (request) leta hai aur kitchen ko deta hai; khana ready hone par waiter hi customer ko serve karta hai. Waiter = customer aur kitchen ke beech intermediary. API bhi bilkul waiter jaisa hai, bas device aur server ke beech.
qs.b: An API acts as an intermediary between a device and a server. The device sends a request through the API, the server retrieves and interprets the data, performs the necessary actions and sends the response back through the API. It is like a waiter in a restaurant who carries the customer's order to the kitchen and brings the food back.
qs.t: Customer = device, kitchen = server, waiter = API.

qs.q: How is API testing different from regular testing or bug hunts?
qs.s: Notes ke do points: (1) API testing me aap web browser ya mobile device use nahi karte. (2) Aap specialized client applications jaise Postman use karte ho, jahan customer ke server ko saari requests aap khud directly bhejte ho, kisi web page se nahi. Course me aage ke topics: API test karne ke concepts, API me kya test karna hai, aur Postman.
qs.b: API testing does not use a web browser or a mobile device. Instead, you use a specialized client application such as Postman and send every request to the customer's server directly yourself, not through a web page.
qs.t: No browser, no phone; sirf Postman aur direct request.

qs.q: What is HTTP and how does it work?
qs.s: HTTP = Hypertext Transfer Protocol. Ye World Wide Web pe data communication ki foundation hai, isliye Internet ka sabse popular application protocol hai. Ye ek stateless, asymmetric request-response protocol hai: HTTP client server ko HTTP request message bhejta hai, server client ko response message return karta hai.
qs.b: HTTP, the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web and the most popular application protocol on the Internet. It is a stateless, asymmetric request-response protocol: the client sends a request message and the server returns a response message.
qs.t: HTTP = Stateless + Asymmetric + Request-Response (SAR).

qs.q: What is a URL and what is its syntax?
qs.s: HTTP resources ko uniquely identify karte hain URLs (Uniform Resource Locators), jo http aur https URIs (Uniform Resource Identifiers) ke form me hote hain. Syntax: protocol://hostname:port/path-and-resource-name. Protocol = application protocol, Web APIs me usually https ya http. Hostname = domain name jo host computer (web server) ko identify karta hai. Port = TCP port number jis par host client requests sun raha hai. Path and resource name = forward slash (/) se separated path segments ka sequence plus requested resource ka naam, file-extension bhi ho sakta hai.
qs.b: HTTP resources are identified by URLs, Uniform Resource Locators, in the form of http and https URIs. The syntax is protocol://hostname:port/path-and-resource-name, where protocol is usually http or https, hostname is the domain of the web server, port is the TCP port the host listens on, and the path is a sequence of slash-separated segments ending in the resource name.
qs.t: P-H-P-P: Protocol, Hostname, Port, Path.

qs.q: What are the default ports for HTTP and HTTPS, and how do you break down a URL that has no port?
qs.s: Agar URL me port omit kiya gaya hai to default https requests ke liye 443 aur http requests ke liye 80 hota hai. Notes ka example: https://www.<platform-domain>/academy/tracks/1. Isme https = protocol, www.<domain> = domain, /academy/tracks/1 = path and resource name component. Port explicitly nahi likha, isliye client (yaani web browser) is case me default 443 set karta hai.
qs.b: If the port is omitted, the client uses 443 for HTTPS and 80 for HTTP. For example, in a URL like https://www.example-domain.com/academy/tracks/1, https is the protocol, the domain is the hostname, /academy/tracks/1 is the path and resource name, and the browser defaults the port to 443.
qs.t: S wala secure, bada number 443; plain http, 80.

qs.q: What does the request line of an HTTP request contain?
qs.s: HTTP Request aur HTTP Response messages ka basic structure same hota hai. Request line specify karti hai: (1) HTTP method, (2) Resource (example me "/"), (3) HTTP-version (example me "1.1").
qs.b: HTTP requests and responses share the same basic structure. The request line specifies the HTTP method, the resource being requested, for example "/", and the HTTP version, for example 1.1.
qs.t: Request line = Method + Resource + Version (MRV).

qs.q: What are the common HTTP methods and what does each do?
qs.s: Notes ke common methods: GET = specific resource request karne ke liye. POST = server par content post karne ke liye. HEAD = sirf HTTP headers request karna, response message body omit hoti hai; isse kuch configuration options retrieve kiye ja sakte hain. OPTIONS = target resource ke communication options ka description maangna; server ko supported HTTP methods ki list ke saath respond karna chahiye. PUT = POST ke alawa server ko content bhejne ka ek aur method; POST web pages par zyada common hai, PUT APIs me zyada common hai. DELETE = web server ko specific resource ya content delete karne ka instruction.
qs.b: GET requests a specific resource, POST posts content to the server, HEAD requests only the headers without the response body, OPTIONS asks for the communication options of the target resource and the server should reply with the supported methods, PUT also sends content to the server and is more common in APIs while POST is more common on web pages, and DELETE tells the server to delete a specific resource.
qs.t: GP-HOPD: Get, Post, Head, Options, Put, Delete.

qs.q: What is the difference between the HEAD and OPTIONS methods?
qs.s: HEAD: request ke sirf HTTP headers maangta hai, response message body omit ho jaati hai. Iska use certain configuration options retrieve karne me ho sakta hai. OPTIONS: target resource ke communication options ka description maangta hai, aur server ko supported HTTP methods ki list ke saath respond karna chahiye.
qs.b: HEAD returns only the HTTP headers of a request and omits the response body, which can be used to retrieve certain configuration options. OPTIONS requests a description of the communication options for the target resource, and the server should respond with a list of supported HTTP methods.
qs.t: HEAD = sirf sar (headers); OPTIONS = menu of methods.

qs.q: What does the HTTP response status line contain, and what do 200, 302, 400 and 501 mean?
qs.s: Status line batati hai request successful thi ya nahi, HTTP version dikhati hai, aur ek http status code include karti hai. Examples: 200 OK = request successful. 302 Found = client ko doosre URL par dekhne (browse karne) ko kehta hai. 400 Bad Request = server client error ki wajah se request process nahi kar sakta ya nahi karega (jaise syntax error, size, message format). 501 Not Implemented = server request fulfil nahi kar sakta ya request method recognize nahi karta.
qs.b: The status line shows the HTTP version, a status code, and whether the request succeeded. 200 OK means success, 302 Found tells the client to go to another URL, 400 Bad Request means the server will not process the request because of a client error such as syntax, size or message format, and 501 Not Implemented means the server cannot fulfil the request or does not recognize the method.
qs.t: 200 haan, 302 udhar jao, 400 tumhari galti, 501 mujhe nahi aata.

qs.q: What are the five classes of HTTP status codes?
qs.s: Status code ka pehla digit response ki class define karta hai. Paanch categories: 1xx = Informational, 2xx = Successful, 3xx = Redirection, 4xx = Client Error, 5xx = Server Error.
qs.b: The first digit of a status code defines its class. There are five: 1xx Informational, 2xx Successful, 3xx Redirection, 4xx Client Error and 5xx Server Error.
qs.t: 1 Info, 2 Success, 3 Redirect, 4 Client galti, 5 Server galti.

qs.q: What are HTTP headers and which common request headers did the course list?
qs.s: HTTP header fields request aur response messages ke header section ka part hote hain aur HTTP transaction ke kai operating parameters define karte hain. Headers colon-separated key-value pairs hote hain, jaise "Connection: close" me 'Connection' key hai aur 'close' value. Request headers examples: Host = server ka domain name. User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 = browser ka user agent string. Accept: text/html,*/* = content negotiation ka part; response ke acceptable media types. Accept-Language: en-US, en = response ke liye acceptable human languages (content negotiation). Connection: close = current connection ke control options.
qs.b: HTTP headers are colon-separated key-value pairs in the header section of requests and responses that define the operating parameters of the transaction. Common request headers are Host for the server's domain, User-Agent for the browser's user agent string, Accept for acceptable media types, Accept-Language for acceptable human languages, and Connection for the connection control options.
qs.t: Header = key: value. Request me HUAAC: Host, User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Connection.

qs.q: Explain the common response headers Date, Content-Type, Expires and Content-Length.
qs.s: Date: Fri, 06 Sep 2019 06:42:56 GMT = HTTP-date jo batata hai message kab bheja gaya (yaani server time). Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 = response message body ke content ka MIME type. Expires: Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT = wo HTTP-date jiske baad response stale maana jaata hai. Content-Length: 3761 = response body ki length bytes me. Saath me Connection aur Cache-Control bhi the (alag card). Notes kehte hain darjano aur headers bhi hote hain; kuch self-explanatory hain, baaki look up karne padte hain.
qs.b: Date is the HTTP-date when the message was sent, which is server time. Content-Type gives the MIME type of the response body, for example text/html with UTF-8. Expires is the date after which the response is considered stale, and Content-Length is the length of the response body in bytes.
qs.t: Date = kab bheja, Type = kya bheja, Expires = kab baasi, Length = kitna bheja.

qs.q: What do the Connection values close and keep-alive mean?
qs.s: Connection header current connection ke control options deta hai. "close" ka matlab response complete hone ke baad connection band ho jaayega. Doosra hi possible option "keep-alive" hai, jo batata hai ki aur messages aa sakte hain, isliye client ko persistent connection maintain karna chahiye.
qs.b: Connection: close means the connection is closed after the response is complete. The only other option, keep-alive, indicates that more messages may follow, so the client should keep a persistent connection open.
qs.t: close = phone rakh do; keep-alive = line on rakho.

qs.q: What does the Cache-Control header do? Give examples of its values.
qs.s: Cache-Control server se client tak saare caching mechanisms ko batata hai ki ye message cache kar sakte hain ya nahi. Example: "Cache-Control: no-cache". Ek aur possible value: "Cache-Control: max-age=3600", jo seconds me measure hota hai, matlab object x seconds se zyada cache nahi kiya ja sakta.
qs.b: Cache-Control tells every caching mechanism between server and client whether the message may be cached. no-cache is one value, and max-age=3600 is another, meaning the object may not be cached for longer than 3600 seconds.
qs.t: max-age seconds me ginti karta hai: 3600 = ek ghanta.

qs.q: What are the common ways to transmit data to a web server in HTTP requests?
qs.s: Websites me sabse common tareeke: (1) Query strings, (2) JSON in background-requests (page reload ke bina), (3) Multipart POST requests. APIs me data aksar forms ki jagah XML ya JSON se transmit hota hai.
qs.b: On websites, data is most commonly sent through query strings, JSON in background requests without reloading the page, and multipart POST requests. In APIs, data is often transmitted as XML or JSON instead of forms.
qs.t: Q-J-M: Query, JSON, Multipart.

qs.q: How are form values transmitted in a GET request versus a POST request?
qs.s: GET example: simple HTML form, do input fields aur submit button, form ka method "GET" (attribute omit karo to default bhi GET hi hota hai). Submit karne par input form ke "action" parameter wali location ("/test/demo_form.php") par jaata hai: https://www.example.com/test/demo_form.php?name1=value1&name2=value2. Form-contents URL me query-string ke roop me jaate hain: name/value pairs ki string, target page ke baad question mark (?) ke baad, aur pairs ampersand (&) se separate. POST me: wahi key/value pair "name1=value1&name2=value2" request message body me jaata hai, request ke bottom me, message header se ek blank line ke neeche.
qs.b: With GET, which is also the default form method, the values are appended to the target URL as a query string after a question mark, with name=value pairs separated by ampersands. With POST, the same name1=value1&name2=value2 string is sent in the request body, below the blank line that separates it from the headers.
qs.t: GET = URL pe chipka (? aur &), POST = body me chhupa.

qs.q: What does Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded mean?
qs.s: Ye content-type header server ko batata hai ki data url-encoded hai. Matlab saare non-ASCII characters convert ho jaate hain. Example: space character + ban jaata hai, "@" ban jaata hai "%40", aur aise hi baaki.
qs.b: It tells the server that the data is URL-encoded, which means non-ASCII characters are converted. For example, a space becomes a plus sign and the @ sign becomes %40.
qs.t: urlencoded: space = +, @ = %40.

qs.q: What is multipart/form-data and when is it used?
qs.s: Form ko "enctype" attribute define karke multipart/form-data ke roop me bhejte hain (form ke source-code me enctype attribute add hota hai). Values ab "boundary" se separate hoti hain, jo browser automatically set karta hai. Har value ke ek ya zyada additional attributes hote hain. Ye method typically web sites ke file-upload forms me use hota hai.
qs.b: multipart/form-data is selected with the form's enctype attribute. The values are separated by a boundary that the browser sets automatically, and each value can carry additional attributes. It is typically used for file-upload forms.
qs.t: Multipart = file upload, boundary se kaata hua.

qs.q: What is Postman and why is it a good choice for API testing?
qs.s: Postman (getpostman.com) ek widely used aur sophisticated API Development Environment hai, zyada tar API testing ke liye ideal. Reasons: basic version free hai; Windows, MacOS ya Linux par available; neat aur clean interface; zyada setup steps nahi chahiye.
qs.b: Postman is a widely used, sophisticated API development environment that suits most API testing. The basic version is free, it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, it has a clean interface, and it needs very little setup.
qs.t: Postman = Free, 3 OS, Clean, Kam setup.

qs.q: How do you create a collection and send your first GET request in Postman?
qs.s: Collection: Postman install karke run karo; left side par "Create Collection" button click karo, naam do jaise "First collection" aur enter dabao. Request: collection ke andar request do tareeke se banti hai: collection dropdown expand karke "Add a request" link, ya collection name ke right wale three dot button par click karke "Add request". Phir Request name enter karo. "Enter request URL" field me full URL daalo (try https://example.com) aur Send click karo. View do hisson me hota hai: upar request area jisme Params, Authorization, Headers aur baaki tabs; neeche response area jisme Cookies, Headers aur baaki tabs. Default me response body neeche thodi beautified form me dikhti hai. Request ko top right ke Save button se collection me save karo. Naya request banane ke liye + icon click karo.
qs.b: Click Create Collection on the left and name it. Add a request either from the collection dropdown with Add a request or from the three-dot menu with Add request, give it a name, enter the URL in the Enter request URL field and click Send. The request area at the top has tabs like Params, Authorization and Headers, and the response area at the bottom has Cookies, Headers and the body. Save the request into the collection with Save, and use the plus icon for a new request.
qs.t: Collection banao, request add karo, URL daalo, Send, Save, + for next.

qs.q: What is CRUD and how does it map to HTTP methods?
qs.s: CRUD computer programming me persistent storage ke chaar basic operations hain. HTTP me mapping: Create = PUT, POST. Read = GET. Update = PUT, POST, PATCH. Delete = DELETE. PUT, POST aur PATCH ke beech kaafi ambivalence hai; real world me ye API (ya web service) par depend karta hai ki kab kaun sa method use hoga.
qs.b: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update and Delete, the four basic operations of persistent storage. Create maps to PUT or POST, Read to GET, Update to PUT, POST or PATCH, and Delete to DELETE. Which of PUT, POST or PATCH is used in practice depends on the API.
qs.t: C = Put/Post, R = Get, U = Put/Post/Patch, D = Delete.

qs.q: Ideally, how do PUT, GET, POST and PATCH behave in terms of idempotency?
qs.s: Ideally: PUT resource ko idempotent tareeke se update karta hai, yaani multiple identical requests ka result hamesha same hona chahiye, bilkul GET ki tarah. Same GET request hamesha same result, same response deni chahiye. POST resource create karta hai aur same result nahi deta; multiple baar call karo to multiple resources ban jaate hain (agar allowed ho). PATCH resource par partial update apply karta hai, lekin sirf tab jab resource pehle se exist karta ho; PUT ke unlike, agar specified resource exist nahi karta to PATCH naya entry create nahi karega.
qs.b: Ideally PUT updates a resource idempotently, so repeating the same request gives the same result, just like GET. POST creates a resource and repeated calls create multiple resources if allowed. PATCH applies a partial update only to a resource that already exists and, unlike PUT, does not create a new entry.
qs.t: PUT/GET = jitni baar bhi, same result; POST = har baar naya; PATCH = sirf thoda, sirf existing pe.

qs.q: What is a safe HTTP method, and what common HTTP-method mistake should you report?
qs.s: Safe HTTP method ka matlab: safe method use karne wali koi bhi request resource ko modify ya change nahi kar sakti. Common mistake: agar testing ke dauraan aapko koi aisi GET request dikhe jo authentication require karti ho aur resource ko update karti ho, to wo most likely ek issue hai jo report karna chahiye. Iska significant security impact ho sakta hai, kyunki HTTP Protocol ke specification ke hisaab se GET requests idempotent aur safe honi chahiye. Web browsers aisa hi expect karte hain aur isliye kam restrictive hote hain.
qs.b: A safe method is one whose requests cannot modify a resource. If you see an authenticated GET request that updates a resource, it is most likely a reportable issue with a possible security impact, because the HTTP specification says GET must be idempotent and safe, and browsers are less restrictive with it for that reason.
qs.t: GET se data badla? Bug report karo.

qs.q: How do you send and inspect a GET request for a file in Postman?
qs.s: Naya request banao (top par + button), by default GET hota hai. Simple text file ke contents maangne ke liye full URL daalo aur Send click karo. File ke contents neeche Response section me dikhte hain. "Headers" tab response headers ki full list dikhata hai. Response section me Postman HTTP status code (200 OK), uske paas request ka execution time (example me 773 milliseconds) aur response size (746 Bytes) bhi dikhata hai. Example response plain text one,two,three,four tha, yaani CSV format me chaar words ki list. CSV = "comma-separated values", individual values ki list store karne ke liye, beech me single comma. Is request ko collection me "GET file example" naam se save karna tha.
qs.b: Create a new request, which defaults to GET, enter the full URL and click Send. The response section shows the body, a Headers tab with all response headers, the status code such as 200 OK, the execution time and the response size. In the course example the body was one,two,three,four in CSV format, which means comma-separated values.
qs.t: Response bar me teen cheez: Status, Time, Size.

qs.q: How do you send a PUT request in Postman and verify it worked?
qs.s: Saara input dobara bina daale naya request banane ka tareeka: existing request ke tab par right-click karke "Duplicate tab" choose karo, method "PUT" kar do. Save button ke paas wale dropdown se "Save As..." choose karke naya request collection me save karo. Jahan data post karna hai wo URL daalo; ise "endpoint" ya "API endpoint" kehte hain. Request section me "Body" tab select karo; ye content-type choose karne deta hai. Default "none" hota hai kyunki message body nahi hai. "raw" choose karo aur naye text field me CSV-data a,b,c,d type karo. Send click karo. Phir purani "GET file example" request dobara submit karke verify karo ki data update hua; response me abhi bheja hua CSV-data dikhna chahiye. Agar poori CSV list nahi, sirf ek entry badalni ho (jaise "c" ko "three" karna), to PATCH method use karo.
qs.b: Duplicate an existing tab, change the method to PUT and use Save As to store it as a new request. Enter the API endpoint URL, open the Body tab, switch from none to raw and enter the data, for example a,b,c,d, then click Send. Re-run the earlier GET request to verify that the data was updated. To change only one entry, use PATCH instead.
qs.t: Duplicate tab, PUT, Body raw, Send, GET se verify.

qs.q: How does the course's PATCH example work?
qs.s: Patching ka syntax APIs ya web services ke beech bahut vary karta hai; APIs JSON, XML ya proprietary formats use kar sakti hain. Example me PATCH bhi PUT ki tarah plain text Body use karta hai. Steps: pichli "PUT data" request duplicate karo, path patchdata.php karo, HTTP method "PATCH" karo, body text 2=Charlie karo, Send click karo. Phir "Save as..." se naye request ke roop me save karo, original overwrite mat karo. Ye endpoint CSV list ki specific entries update karta hai; parameters me index aur new value expect karta hai. 0=Text = pehli entry (counting 0 se shuru) ko "Text" set karo; list a,b,c,d se Text,b,c,d ban jaati hai. 2=Charlie = index 2 yaani teesri entry ko Charlie karo; data a,b,Charlie,d ban jaata hai. Indexes usually zero se count hote hain. Baad me "GET file example" se verify karo.
qs.b: In the example, the PATCH endpoint updates a single entry of the CSV list. You duplicate the PUT request, change the path to patchdata.php and the method to PATCH, and send a plain-text body of index=value, such as 2=Charlie. Indexes start at zero, so 2=Charlie turns a,b,c,d into a,b,Charlie,d. Then save it with Save As so the original is not overwritten.
qs.t: Index zero se: 0 = pehla, 2 = teesra.

qs.q: How does the course's POST example work, and what extra Postman features does it show?
qs.s: POST method ke saath naya request banao aur request body ke liye "form-data" format use karo. Do keys daalo: "firstname" aur "city", values apni marzi ki. Send click karne par response me confirmation dikhta hai, aur is example me response me submitted data bhi hota hai. Console kholne par aapki saari requests ke logs dikhte hain; har request ka detail expand karke dekh sakte ho; raw logs ke liye console ke top right par "Show raw log" click karo. Postman APIs call karne ke liye example code bhi deta hai, kai languages aur libraries ke support ke saath; code snippet section me language/library choose karke example code dekh sakte ho.
qs.b: Create a POST request with a form-data body and add keys such as firstname and city with any values. On Send, the response confirms the submission and echoes the data. The Postman Console shows logs of every request, expandable, with a Show raw log option, and the code snippet section generates example code in several languages and libraries.
qs.t: POST form-data; Console = logs; Code snippet = ready code.

qs.q: How does the course's DELETE example work?
qs.s: Is case me DELETE endpoint ko do tareeke se call kar sakte ho: index ke saath, ek specific entry delete karne ke liye; ya bina parameters ke, poori list delete karne ke liye. Steps: naya request banao, collection me "DELETE data" naam se save karo. Raw Body use karo aur jis list-entry ko delete karna hai uska index daalo. Pichle example se data a,b,Charlie,d hona chahiye. Index 1 ke saath DELETE submit karo to doosri entry hat jaati hai, result a,Charlie,d. Agar result alag aaye to pehle pichli PUT request submit karke original values restore karo. Success verify karne ke liye pichli GET request dobara call karo.
qs.b: The DELETE endpoint either removes one entry when given an index or deletes the whole list when called without parameters. With a raw body of 1 on the list a,b,Charlie,d, the second entry is removed and the list becomes a,Charlie,d. If the data differs, re-run the PUT to restore it, and verify the deletion with the GET request.
qs.t: DELETE 1 = doosra gaya (index zero se).

qs.q: How do you set authorization at the collection level in Postman?
qs.s: Pichle examples me bina authentication ke data request/post ho raha tha, jo web services ya websites ke liye kaafi uncommon hai. Postman me auth variables aur settings har request ke liye individually set kar sakte ho, lekin jab collection ke saath API test kar rahe ho to usually saari requests ke liye global settings banana sensible hai. Steps: Postman sidebar kholo, stored collection par cursor hover karo, "..." button aayega, click karke Edit select karo. Request ke Authorization tab me default value "Inherit auth from parent" hoti hai, yaani collection ki setting use hoti hai.
qs.b: Authorization can be set per request, but for a collection it usually makes sense to set it globally. Hover over the collection in the sidebar, click the three-dot button and choose Edit to configure auth. Requests then use the default Inherit auth from parent setting.
qs.t: Collection pe auth ek baar, requests me 'Inherit auth from parent'.

qs.q: How does Basic Auth work, and how do you test it in Postman?
qs.s: Collection edit me list se "Basic Auth" select karo. Basic access authentication ek authorization method hai; browser me kisi Basic Auth protected page/directory ko call karne par login form wala popup aata hai. Username aur password daalo aur top right ka Save button click karo. Test: collection ke andar protected page ke liye GET request banao aur send karo. Configuration kaam kar raha hai ye verify karne ke liye Basic Auth off karke wahi page dobara request karo: request ke Authorization tab me dropdown se "No Auth" select karo. Ab web server error dikhayega kyunki request authenticated nahi hai aur folder ko Basic Auth chahiye. Authorization type wapas default "Inherit auth from parent" karke code dekho: ye method ek naya request header submit karta hai jisme username aur password Base64-encoded form me hote hain.
qs.b: Basic Auth sends the username and password in a request header, Base64-encoded. In Postman you set it on the collection, save, and send a GET to a protected page. To prove it works, switch the request to No Auth and the server returns an error, then switch back to Inherit auth from parent.
qs.t: Basic = username:password Base64 me; No Auth se negative check.

qs.q: What is a Bearer token and how do you test Bearer token authorization in Postman?
qs.s: Bearer token Basic Auth jaisa hi hai kyunki ye bhi request header me jaata hai, lekin "Authorization: Basic" ki jagah "Authorization: Bearer EXAMPLETOKEN" use hota hai. Bearer token ek security token hai jiska matlab: jis party ke paas ye hai ("bearer") use protected resource ka access hai. Normally login request ke response me server ise generate karta hai. Test steps: pehle collection ki authorization settings undo karo, warna server saari directories par Basic Auth apply karne ki koshish karega aur fail hoga, kyunki doosre folders par wahi username/password combination enabled nahi hai. Phir Bearer token maangne ke liye POST login request banao. Send karne par response me token "EXAMPLETOKEN" dikhna chahiye. Invalid username/password bhejo to server login form dikhata hai. Returned token ko naye GET request me use karo, collection me save karo, aur response batayega request successful thi ya nahi.
qs.b: A bearer token is a security token that gives access to whoever holds it. It is usually generated by the server after a login request and sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. To test it, remove the collection's Basic Auth, send a POST login request to get the token, then use the token in a GET request and check the response. Invalid credentials should not return a token.
qs.t: Jiske haath token, uske haath access.

qs.q: How do you do input validation (negative testing) on an API?
qs.s: Website ke functional testing ke zyada tar methods API functional testing par bhi apply hote hain. Pehle expected result test karo, phir request me alag-alag values try karo: date-field me random text submit karke response inspect karo; koi unexpected error aaya? Kya web service failed attempt handle kar paati hai? Missing required fields ya bahut bade numbers ke saath request submit karo.
qs.b: After confirming the expected result, I try invalid values: random text in a date field, missing required fields or very large numbers. Then I check whether the API returns an unexpected error or handles the failed attempt gracefully.
qs.t: Pehle happy path, phir galat date, missing field, bada number.

qs.q: What should you check about authentication when testing an API?
qs.s: Jab aap properly authenticated nahi ho to API requests ko kaise handle karti hai? Kya koi unexpected error aata hai, ya stack trace output bhi dikh jaata hai?
qs.b: I check how the API handles requests that are not properly authenticated, and whether it returns an unexpected error or even exposes a stack trace.
qs.t: Bina login request bhejo, stack trace dikhe to bug.

qs.q: How do you verify that an API is correctly updating data structures?
qs.s: Jab data POST karo aur updated data inspect karo (corresponding GET request me ya returned response message me): kya saara input pahuncha? Kya kuch truncated ya missing hai? Resource delete karne ke baad verify karo ki wo ab exist nahi karta aur properly delete hua hai.
qs.b: After a POST, I inspect the data through a GET or the response and check that all input arrived without truncation or missing parts. After a delete, I confirm the resource no longer exists.
qs.t: POST ke baad GET, DELETE ke baad bhi GET.

qs.q: What does it mean to verify all limitations of an API? Give examples.
qs.s: Kai actions sirf ek baar perform karne allowed hote hain. Ensure karo ki limits circumvent na ho sakein aur attempt karne par bhi kuch toote nahi. Examples: online shop me usually ek time par sirf ek shipping address active mark kar sakte ho; final order completion sirf ek baar submit kar sakte ho.
qs.b: Many actions are allowed only once, so I check that limits cannot be bypassed and that nothing breaks if I try. For example, only one shipping address can be active at a time, and a final order can be completed only once.
